2026-09-21-com-pfss-tms-55000-menages-mo.summary: Comoros began a new phase of its World Bank-funded social cash transfers on 20 September 2026, reaching 55,000 households, 15,000 of them new, with USD 11 million in additional financing. Payments go through the mobile-banking operators Mvula and Huri Money, and households are selected from the unified social registry.

2026-09-21-cpv-ccip-afdb-reoi-sgit-nomad.summary: Cabo Verde's integrated project coordination centre, CCIP, invited expressions of interest on 21 September 2026 from firms to build a statistics and data module for the National Digital Nomads Programme within the SGIT system, interoperable with other state platforms. The 12-month contract is financed from an African Development Bank credit to the Morabeza Innovation Project. No contract value is given.

2026-09-21-dza-interfil-conseil-ministre.summary: Algeria's Council of Ministers, meeting under President Tebboune on 20 September 2026, called for a presidential decree setting up a secure plan for data exchange between state bodies, overseen by the High Commissioner for Digitalisation. The president asked for the plan to reach the wilayas too, with strong protection of citizens' data. He also ordered that payments to farmers at the state cereals office be digitised immediately.

2026-09-21-egy-dailynewsegypt-fra-movabl.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority surveyed creditors on the services and electronic system of the Egyptian Movable Collateral Registry and met them with the registry's operator, E-Finance, to review the findings, Daily News Egypt reported on 21 September 2026. The proposals will undergo technical and legal review before priorities are set. No timetable is given.

2026-09-21-egy-mubadala-paymob-35m-pre-s.summary: Egyptian payments company Paymob raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round co-led by Abu Dhabi's Mubadala and the EBRD, with BII, Global Ventures and DPI Ventures also taking part (21 September 2026). The money will fund expansion across the Middle East and North Africa. Paymob says revenue from the Gulf grew sevenfold in 18 months and now makes up close to half the total.

2026-09-21-egy-newkerala-india-egypt-ict.summary: India's ambassador to Egypt, Suresh Reddy, met communications minister Raafat Hindy to discuss closer cooperation on ICT. According to the Indian embassy, the talks covered India's digital public infrastructure and how it could be used elsewhere, cooperation between institutions, and links between the two countries' tech companies. No outcome was announced.

2026-09-21-egy-zawya-orange-egypt-marake.summary: Orange Egypt will design, install and operate telecoms networks at four Marakez developments: Ramla, District 5, Aeon Towers and Mall of Arabia. The deal covers fibre to the home, bundled broadband, TV and voice, public Wi-Fi and a smart CCTV system for the mall's first phase. No value was disclosed.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonmediatime-dgdinc-ani.summary: Gabon's Council of Ministers appointed Anicet Claude Andjouat on 18 September 2026 to head a new Directorate-General for digital infrastructure and cybersecurity, created in December 2025. Gabon Media Time reports that the directorate's remit over spectrum, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity overlaps with that of the existing agency ANINF, and that no public division of responsibilities has been set out.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonreview-cemac-systeme.summary: Experts from six CEMAC member states met in Libreville on 21 September 2026 to prepare national energy information systems and a common regional system, with support from the African Energy Commission. They examined a draft community regulation on collecting, validating and disseminating energy data ahead of a ministerial meeting on 25 September.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonreview-permis-condui.summary: Gabon's transport minister Ulrich Manfoumbi Manfoumbi suspended enrolment for the digitalised driving licence on 21 September 2026, six months after launch, to review the scheme; no resumption date was given. 6,993 printed licences await collection in Libreville, and unnamed sources linked the pause to production problems under heavy demand and power cuts.

2026-09-21-gamtel-company-profile-ace-25.summary: The Gambian state operator's undated company profile. It says Gamtel has four international gateways on the ACE submarine cable giving 25 Gbps, and a 28 Gbps backup link through Senegal's Free that traffic switches to if ACE fails.

2026-09-21-gin-agenceecofin-donnees-agri.summary: Guinea's agriculture ministry presented on 16 September 2026 the pilot results of its national agricultural data services programme, run with the Kenyan start-up Pula: 20,463 producers registered and 23,507 farms mapped in Kindia, Kankan and Mamou. Each producer receives a card with a QR code and NFC chip giving authorised users access to verified data on a secure portal.

2026-09-21-gin-mediaguinee-hac-interdit-.summary: Guinea's media regulator, the Haute Autorité de la Communication, on 21 September 2026 banned ten web TV channels and two news sites nationwide and on all digital platforms for broadcasting online without authorisation. Those named include Dabola TV, Coyah TV and Siguiri 24 Star TV. The regulator said earlier warnings to regularise had been ignored.

2026-09-21-gmb-gnnliberia-lra-gra-revenu.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority signed a memorandum of engagement to help the Gambia Revenue Authority build a dashboard that tracks revenue collection; it was announced from Accra on 20 September 2026 and signed during meetings of the West African Tax Administration Forum. The help covers a review of GRA's data sources, choice of indicators, design, a prototype, integration and staff training. The LRA will send the developer of its own dashboard to Banjul for an initial three weeks.

2026-09-21-gmb-thepoint-gra-lra-digital-.summary: The Gambian account of the Liberia–Gambia revenue dashboard agreement, summarised under the GNN Liberia report. It adds that the LRA pays the expert's airfare while the GRA covers lodging and local transport.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-advancing-digital-c.summary: The report behind the GSMA and PDAA roadmap, summarised under the launch. It counts 550 million internet users in Africa in 2025 (36% of the population) and projects about 700 million by 2030 on current trends. Halving the coverage and usage gaps could add some 514 million people and take the total past 1 billion.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-roadmap-1-billion-c.summary: The GSMA and the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa launched a roadmap in New York on 21 September 2026 on how to reach 1 billion connected Africans by 2030. Based on 11 markets, it finds about 906 million people living within mobile broadband coverage but not using the mobile internet, against 122 million with no coverage at all. Its three priorities are moving over 600 million 2G and 3G connections to 4G or 5G, investing in energy and connectivity together, and reaching rural areas more cheaply.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-kenya-hoover-ins.summary: Kenya's foreign ministry signed a five-year memorandum of understanding with the Emerging Markets Working Group at Stanford's Hoover Institution during the UN General Assembly in New York. The signing date was not given. The first project is an El Niño monitoring and response system that brings climate, geospatial, water, farming and infrastructure data together by county. Later work is to include a digital trade readiness index and a tracker for public-private partnerships.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-malawi-india-tec.summary: India's High Commission and the mHub innovation hub held a workshop in Lilongwe on AI, digital skills and technology investment, attended by more than 70 companies. India's high commissioner pointed to openings in agriculture, digital public infrastructure and financial inclusion. No agreement or commitment came out of it.

2026-09-21-itweb-fpb-ai-oversight-stream.summary: South Africa's Film and Publication Board has approved a strategy on digitisation and AI and plans to try generative AI for monitoring, classifying content and managing cases over the next three to five years. None of it is yet in use. Its enforcement committee fined 21 content distributors a total of R16.175 million in September 2026.

2026-09-21-ken-cbk-draft-nps-policy-and-.summary: Kenya's National Treasury and central bank published a draft National Payment System Policy and a draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 for public comment on 21 September 2026. The bill would replace the current Act and license payment providers and system operators by category, with minimum capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million. It also requires interoperability, allows open-finance data sharing with consent and brings virtual asset providers that offer payments under the law, while the policy commits the government to a national instant payment switch.

2026-09-21-ken-diaspora-go-ke-kenya-dias.summary: Kenya's government, the United Nations in Kenya and Equity Group Holdings signed a joint declaration of intent in New York on 20 September 2026 to work on the Kenya Diaspora Impact Platform, a digital gateway linking diaspora investors to verified investment and development projects in Kenya. No budget, operator or launch date is given.

2026-09-21-ken-kenyans-ardhisasa-outage-.summary: Kenya's ArdhiSasa land platform announced an outage on 21 September 2026 affecting searches, transfers, title and lease registration, and stamp duty and land-rent payments, with no time given for restoring service. The Law Society of Kenya had already complained that the platform was unavailable from 1 September.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-draft-national-p.summary: Kenya's draft National Payment System Policy, dated August 2026, which identifies ten gaps in the current system. It commits to a national instant payment switch, requires open APIs and gives non-banks access to settlement. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-national-payment.summary: The full draft text of Kenya's National Payment System Bill, 2026, which runs to 79 clauses. It sets licence capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million, requires interoperability, provides for open finance, brings virtual asset providers into scope and sets fines of up to Ksh20 million. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-lbr-frontpageafrica-cybercrim.summary: A second account of the Wrotto arrest, summarised under the New Dawn report. It adds a justice ministry prosecutor's view that the state, not the vice-president, decides whether a prosecution goes ahead, and notes that the Act does not mention AI or deepfakes.

2026-09-21-lbr-newdawn-koung-seeks-relea.summary: Liberia's vice-president Jeremiah Koung asked for the release of Jerry Nyantee Wrotto, whom police detained under the Cybercrime Act over AI-made images and videos of Koung, and said he would not press charges. It is one of the first high-profile uses of the Act, signed on 19 August 2026 with the Data Protection Act. The head of the Executive Protection Service defended the arrest, while critics including former finance minister Samuel Tweah said the Act's cyberbullying clauses cover protected speech.

2026-09-21-lby-alwasat-cbl-unified-datab.summary: Libya's central bank governor, Naji Issa, put forward an electronic system and a single national database for recording and following up international grants, projects and support. He made the proposal on 21 September 2026 at the second meeting of the committee set up under prime-ministerial decision 422 of 2026. The idea is still under discussion and has not been adopted.

2026-09-21-mdg-newsmada-gasy-money-bgfib.summary: BGFIBank Madagascar launched Gasy Money, a mobile banking app open to people without an account at the bank, including those with no bank account at all, on any mobile network. The launch date was not given. It handles deposits and withdrawals through agents, branches and ATMs, merchant and bill payments, top-ups of prepaid Visa cards, and transfers to bank accounts and Airtel Money.

2026-09-21-mli-burkina24-centre-ia-robot.summary: Transition president Assimi Goïta opened Mali's artificial intelligence and robotics centre, CIAR-Mali, at Kati on 21 September 2026. He had laid its foundation stone on 7 June 2023. The 50-hectare site has six buildings, including teaching space, dormitories and a workshop for building intelligent systems, and cost FCFA 3.3 billion, all from the national budget.

2026-09-21-mli-mali-benin-data-protectio.summary: Mali's data protection authority hosted the First Rapporteur of Benin's data protection authority on 4 September 2026 to compare compliance tools, regulatory standards and institutional communication, TechGriot reported on 21 September. The Benin delegation looked at Mali's regional offices in Kayes, Sikasso, Ségou and Mopti, which take local complaints and run awareness campaigns.

2026-09-21-moz-aim-transformacao-digital.summary: Mozambique is drafting a three-year operational plan to speed up the digitisation of public services to 2029. At a meeting of the technical commission on digital transformation in Maputo on 21 September 2026, the head of the digital transformation agency said the Citizen Portal already offered about 26 services and had over 3,000 users before its official launch. An interoperability portal, a payments platform for state services, a government cloud and a government data centre are to follow. The commission expects to harmonise and cost the plan within two to three months, with funding spread across many donor projects.

2026-09-21-moz-diarioeconomico-soberania.summary: A second account of the Mozambique digital transformation meeting, summarised under the AIM report. It leads on the state administration minister, Inocêncio Impissa, saying that data produced by public bodies must belong to the state. The plan has not yet been costed.

2026-09-21-mrt-rfi-restriction-reseaux-s.summary: Reactions in Nouakchott to the government's plan, presented to cabinet on 16 September 2026, to bar under-16s from social media without parental consent. A blogger supports protecting children but fears the measure could be used to restrict free expression, and a cybersecurity expert argues for education rather than bans.

2026-09-21-mtnima-etablissements-sous-tu.summary: Mauritania's digital ministry lists the bodies under its supervision: a distance-learning centre, the postal operator, and the state company that owns the national fibre backbone, created by decree in 2014, alongside the regional connectivity projects it runs. The page states each body's mandate but gives no budget, staffing or performance figures.

2026-09-21-nam-newera-fintech-jobs-namfi.summary: The head of Namibia's financial regulator, Kenneth Matomola, said fintech could help with jobs and financial inclusion now that the Financial Institutions and Markets Act and a new Namfisa Act are in force. Both took effect on 1 May 2026. He cited youth unemployment of 44.4% in the 2023 labour force survey.

2026-09-21-nam-smart-water-meters-househ.summary: Innovate4Water, a research project led by the Namibia University of Science and Technology, surveyed 692 households in Windhoek, Rundu and Ongwediva and found only 25% reported uninterrupted water supply. In Ongwediva the team fitted 69 pulse readers to household meters to produce time-stamped consumption data, with AI to flag possible leaks and unauthorised use. No verified reduction in water losses is reported.

2026-09-21-nga-boi-idice-tor-kpo-it-enab.summary: The terms of reference, dated 21 September 2026, for the iDICE consultancy to build a knowledge-process outsourcing industry under the Outsource to Nigeria Initiative. They set five workstreams and a target of paid placement for 80% of trainees within six months. The procurement is summarised under the Premium Times notice.

2026-09-21-nga-businessday-national-broa.summary: Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020–2025 ended short of its main target: broadband penetration was 51.97% in December 2025 against 70%, according to NCC figures. 4G made up 52.95% of mobile subscriptions at the end of 2025, also short of its 70% target. The analysis traces penetration through the plan period, when it fell as low as 40.88% in 2021.

2026-09-21-nga-idice-reoi-kpo-it-enabled.summary: Nigeria's Bank of Industry, which runs the iDICE programme, is seeking consultants for a 16-month assignment to build a knowledge-process outsourcing industry under the Outsource to Nigeria Initiative. The brief includes an academy for 1,000 graduates, 200 paid residency places a year, a target of 80% placement within six months of certification, and a framework of rules and tax incentives for delivery centres. iDICE is co-financed by the AfDB, AFD and IsDB; expressions of interest close on 5 October 2026.

2026-09-21-nga-naltf-kankia-rural-digita.summary: A research summary from the National Assembly Library Trust Fund arguing that Nigeria's rural digital divide comes from weak funding, coordination and oversight, not from a lack of policy. It reviews the digital economy strategy, the 2020–2025 broadband plan, the Universal Service Provision Fund and the Digital Nigeria programme.

2026-09-21-pti-angola-telecom-fibra-lobi.summary: Angola Telecom launched its Tudo Nosso fibre network at the Baía Farta housing development in Benguela province, and the national fibre trunk of about 400 Gb was completed to Lobito, PTI reported on 21 September 2026. Telecoms minister Mário Oliveira also opened a free Angola Online internet point at a primary school there. No cost is given.

2026-09-21-rwa-taarifa-ingabire-cross-bo.summary: Speaking in New York ahead of the UN General Assembly, Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire said African countries need digital systems that work across borders if they are to benefit from technology and AI. She argued that separate national systems limit how far data, services and businesses can move across the continent.

2026-09-21-sdn-dabanga-cbos-strategy-dig.summary: An analysis of the Central Bank of Sudan's 2026–2030 strategic plan, published in December 2025, which includes speeding up digital transformation in the banking system. Banker Omar Sid Ahmed argues that with about 98% of the money supply outside the banks and branches lost to the war, the plan needs a 12-month emergency programme with budgets and measurable targets. He adds that digital projects depend on infrastructure that is not yet in place.

2026-09-21-sen-ecofin-civil-registry-77-.summary: Senegal's National Civil Registry Agency (ANEC) has digitised 77% of the country's 629 civil registry centres, its director general Matar Ndao said in September 2026. As of August the Sama État Civil platform for requesting certificates online ran in 189 municipalities and the management software in 74% of centres. ANEC plans authenticity checks, and the data are hosted on government-owned sites in Senegal.

2026-09-21-sle-calabash-ai-strategy-auth.summary: An opinion column by Gleb Tsipursky arguing that Sierra Leone's first national AI strategy, which the communications ministry is drafting with the World Bank, should limit what AI agents are allowed to do. He proposes minimum access rights, identities for machines, human approval before consequential actions, and testing before deployment.

2026-09-21-sle-truthmedia-ag-no-ai-speci.summary: Sierra Leone's attorney-general told a UNESCO forum on AI ethics in Riyadh that the country has no AI-specific law and that its data-protection bill has not yet passed. He said the government would put that legal foundation in place before deploying AI, after an AI readiness diagnostic done with the World Bank.

2026-09-21-sle-truthmedia-procurement-re.summary: Sierra Leone's Independent Procurement Review Panel opened an investigation into alleged irregularities in the Digital Transformation Project's contract for government network systems (GWAN and GLANS), after a complaint by Tiwai Memory Masters Ltd against the communications ministry. The panel said the outcome will be published once the review is complete. No contract value is given.

2026-09-21-som-sonna-id-control-training.summary: Officers from Somalia's identity authority, immigration agency and criminal investigation department are taking part in a joint course with Kenyan immigration in Nairobi from 21 to 25 September 2026. It is the third such course and covers document examination, identity checks and facial comparison. Norway's migration partnership supports it.

2026-09-21-subtelforum-ace-cable-ciena-3.summary: The consortium behind the 17,000 km Africa Coast to Europe submarine cable has chosen Ciena's WaveLogic 6 Extreme optics to raise its total capacity above 30 Tb/s, Ciena said on 21 September 2026. The upgrade keeps the existing equipment at ACE's 18 landing stations, which serve more than 20 countries, and adds new transmission gear. No completion date was given.

2026-09-21-swz-esnews-bika-transport-rep.summary: Eswatini's government has launched BIKA, a real-time platform for the public to report corruption, abuse and unsafe practice on public and freight transport. It is run by the transport ministry with the road transport council, police, emergency services and the Anti-Corruption Commission; reports can be anonymous and are tracked by a reference number.

2026-09-21-swz-independent-eptc-loan-tax.summary: Eswatini's House of Assembly took the second reading of three bills on 21 September 2026 financing the US$65 million World Bank Digital Eswatini Project. MPs focused on the US$26 million (about E455 million) loan to the state telecoms company EPTC, which the government would guarantee. The finance minister said that loan pays for EPTC's financial stabilisation and a change in its pension scheme, repayable from 2034 to 2051; the other two facilities fund broadband to Tinkhundla centres, schools and clinics, online government services, digital ID, payments and skills training. The bills now go to committee.

2026-09-21-swz-observer-eswatini-payment.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini says the fast-payments service of the Eswatini Payment Switch now links banks and mobile-money providers in real time at any hour, with QR-code payments to merchants being built next. Speaking at Tourism Nkwe 2026 in Mbabane, a deputy director said open banking and a domestic card switch will follow. Links to other countries come at a later stage.

2026-09-21-swz-positivenews-mps-back-dig.summary: Eswatini MPs spoke in support of the three World Bank facilities, together worth US$65 million (about E1.14 billion), that fund the Digital Eswatini Project, at the bills' second reading. The debate is summarised under the Eswatini Independent's report.

2026-09-21-techafricanews-egypt-nti-4dt.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunications Institute agreed with digital-twin and automation firm 4DT.io, in Cairo on 19 September 2026, to train young people in digital transformation and automation. The programmes will mix classroom teaching, hands-on training and project work. No intake, length, cost or certification was stated.

2026-09-21-techafricanews-sa-online-shop.summary: The Online Retail in South Africa 2026 report finds 79.1% of adults online but only 34.2% shopping online in 2025, down from 36.6% in 2024, while online retail turnover rose to about R130 billion. The gap is widest among lower-income consumers and women. Delivery costs, weak last-mile service outside the cities and worries about payment security are named as barriers.

2026-09-21-techcabal-local-stablecoins-u.summary: An analysis arguing that stablecoins tied to African currencies have a weak case for retail use, because mobile money and bank transfers already work at home. It sees more promise in wholesale use and currency exchange on the blockchain. It gives supply as of 21 September 2026: about R74.6 million of ZARP in circulation and more than ₦3.75 billion of cNGN.

2026-09-21-techcabal-nigeria-device-mana.summary: A feature on how the NCC's Device Management System, which requires every SIM-enabled phone to be registered by IMEI before sale or connection, could raise phone prices. Importers, traders and repair shops fear the validation fee and compliance costs will be passed to buyers. The NCC says the registry records device data but gives it no access to the contents of phones.

2026-09-21-telecomreview-ericsson-vodafo.summary: Vodafone Egypt has started commercial rollout of Ericsson's AI-capable RAN Processor 6672, making Egypt one of the first markets after Japan. The unit runs AI at each radio site rather than centrally, and Ericsson claims it gives up to four times the processing capacity for less than half the energy. No number of sites, contract value or timetable was given.

2026-09-21-tgo-togofirst-ceet-smart-mete.summary: Togo's energy ministry launched an international tender for 5,200 smart-metering devices for the state power utility CEET, reported on 21 September 2026: 1,200 modems for medium-voltage meters and 4,000 data concentrators for low-voltage meters. It is financed under the World Bank's US$200m IDA-backed IDEA project, and bids are due on 28 October 2026. CEET's losses are put at nearly 16%.

2026-09-21-tun-chourouk-onctad-strategie.summary: UNCTAD is helping Tunisia's trade and export development ministry draft a national e-commerce strategy, with initial planning meetings held from 31 March to 2 April 2026, according to Ramzi Louati of Tunisia's mission in Geneva. No adoption date or drafting timetable is given.

2026-09-21-tza-uga-sen-enabel-aedib2-wit.summary: Enabel, the Belgian development agency, issued tender specifications for a consultancy to build a Women in Tech community platform and source 12 EU-Africa ventures under its AEDIB 2.0 programme in Tanzania, Uganda and Senegal for 2026 to 2028. The procedure is negotiated without prior publication; bids close on 23 October 2026. No contract value is stated.

2026-09-21-uga-kiryandongo-emr-health-fa.summary: Health workers in Uganda's Kiryandongo district told a public meeting on 19 September 2026 that the Ministry of Health's electronic medical record system is slowing care, citing poor connectivity, unstable power and too few computers. Nyakadoti Health Centre III, serving about 40,000 people including refugees, reported long queues, and the district hospital said services stop when power fails.

2026-09-21-wearetech-sonar-orange-money-.summary: Insurer SONAR Assurance and Orange Money Burkina Faso signed a partnership in Ouagadougou on 18 September 2026 so clients can take out policies, pay premiums and check their contracts by phone. Orange Money says it has about 100,000 points of sale in the country. The exact terms of access have not yet been set.

2026-09-21-xgl-fortune-un-dialogue-safe-.summary: An opinion piece by the two co-leads on safe and secure AI at the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance, held in Geneva in July. They ask the UN to take steps with no downside now: a formal link between its scientific panel on AI and the negotiations before next May, and a common safety baseline built on existing frameworks such as the OECD principles and the Hiroshima code.

2026-09-21-zaf-africatechsummit-vea-capi.summary: VEA Capital Partners, the investment arm of VEA Group, has bought a stake of undisclosed size in Bonisa Applied Insights. Bonisa is a South African data science and AI firm that combines credit bureau data with other data sources for credit scoring, fraud modelling and lending decisions. The stated plan is to sell decisioning as a service and take it into new markets.

2026-09-21-zaf-businessday-sita-boss-reb.summary: An interview with Magatho Mello, managing director of South Africa's State Information Technology Agency since April and its first permanent head since late 2023. He wants to retire old systems, build shared platforms that serve several departments, and simplify tendering for start-ups. A ministerial report in July had set out governance and procurement failures at the agency over 2020–25.

2026-09-21-zaf-govza-malatsi-national-di.summary: Opening GovTech 2026 in Durban on 21 September 2026, South Africa's communications minister Solly Malatsi said government digital systems are still fragmented and that the first phase of the Digital Transformation Roadmap ends in February 2027. He presented digital sovereignty as a matter of development rather than security. He also said he had discussed with Operation Vulindlela and the Digital Council making the country a hub for submarine cables and digital infrastructure.

2026-09-21-zaf-itweb-mission-mobile-r500.summary: Johannesburg start-up Mission Mobile, which finances smartphones and connectivity through operators' stores, says it has secured R500 million from DN Invest, drawn from DNI's own funds and dedicated debt facilities. The date of the commitment was not given. Its Beam platform uses data on how people earn and spend to offer phones to prepaid customers, who account for over 80% of South African mobile connections.

2026-09-21-zmb-airtel-fibre-optic-networ.summary: Airtel Zambia is acquiring about 1,300 km of fibre-optic infrastructure from its related company Airtel Telesonic Zambia for K324.9 million, the Zambian Business Times reported on 21 September 2026. The deal is classed as a small related-party transaction, equal to 1.40% of Airtel Zambia's market value.

2026-09-22-afreximbank-bsmart-technology.summary: Afreximbank issued a US$29 million guarantee to BSMART Technology Ltd, announced on 22 September 2026, to support the EAC Customs Bond, a digital platform that lets clearing agents obtain customs bonds online instead of lodging paper bonds at each border. Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi are named as onboarded. No tenor is stated.

2026-09-22-afreximbank-eac-customs-bond-.summary: Afreximbank issued a US$29m guarantee to BSMART Technology on 22 September 2026 to scale the EAC Customs Bond, a digital regional customs guarantee that removes the need to post paper bonds at each border. The bond was piloted from August 2025 and launched at the East African Community heads of state summit in March 2026.

2026-09-22-african-development-bank-syc-.summary: The African Development Bank's board approved a US$34 million loan to Seychelles on 22 September 2026 for the third and final phase of its Economic Resilience and Green Recovery Support Programme. Reforms include electronic invoicing for tax compliance, a national e-procurement system and a one-stop investment portal; the bank's financing across the three phases totals US$84 million.

2026-09-22-atu-unga81-critical-infrastru.summary: The African Telecommunications Union's secretary general, John Omo, called for stronger protection of critical civilian digital infrastructure at a UN Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies roundtable during the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. He cited domestic data centres, cross-border fibre and internet exchange points, and a July 2026 partnership with the UN office on digital public infrastructure and AI.

2026-09-22-bdi-l-interfacage-des-systeme.summary: Tanzanian and Burundian revenue officials met at the OBR on 22 September 2026 to work on linking their electronic cargo tracking systems on the Northern Corridor. Burundi's system, in use since 2014, can track goods only from its own border posts, and the aim is to follow them from Dar es Salaam or Mombasa to destination.

2026-09-22-bfa-sidwaya-carte-sanitaire-d.summary: Burkina Faso's health ministry made its digitised health map the theme of its first 2026 sector council in Ouagadougou on 21 September. The map is a geolocated tool for planning facilities, staff, medicines and equipment. The minister, Robert Kargougou, said 67.8% of 8,759 activities planned for the first half of the year were completed or under way.

2026-09-22-bujeti-financial-management-t.summary: Nigerian finance-software company Bujeti launched more than 15 integrations with banking, payment and accounting tools, among them Stripe, Paystack and QuickBooks, to automate invoicing, collections and bookkeeping.

2026-09-22-civ-aip-comite-pilotage-parae.summary: The steering committee of Côte d'Ivoire's PARAE e-government project met on 18 September 2026 and called for closer coordination to speed up works on the Yamoussoukro administration data centre, which are running late. It also approved the project's revised 2026 work plan and procurement plan.

2026-09-22-civ-sikafinance-datacenter-ya.summary: A delegation led by the African Development Bank visited the Yamoussoukro site of Côte d'Ivoire's planned Tier 3 administration data centre in September 2026. The centre sits within the PARAE e-government project, budgeted at FCFA 60bn and scheduled to run from January 2025 to 2028.

2026-09-22-cog-la-republique-du-congo-s-.summary: Congo's procurement regulator ARMP reports that a tender file for recruiting the firm to build and deploy an electronic procurement (e-GP) system was drafted by a consultant, reworked by a commission in June 2026 and adopted at a workshop in Brazzaville on 21-22 July. The World Bank-supported file now awaits validation by the project steering committee.

2026-09-22-dza-dzwatch-ai-strategy-imple.summary: A follow-up meeting on Algeria's national AI strategy approved an updated draft decree creating a National Research Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Data, which now goes through legal procedures. Committees set 17 infrastructure and 14 data operations for 2026 and 85 training operations. The meeting date and chair are not stated.

2026-09-22-dza-jeune-independant-dzair-d.summary: Algeria's national portal for government digital services, Dzair Digital Services, passed one million registered users and five million visitors two and a half months after its launch on 5 July 2026, the High Commission for Digitalisation said, reported on 22 September. The figures are the commission's own.

2026-09-22-dza-lejourdalgerie-guichet-el.summary: Algeria's justice minister, Lotfi Boudjemaa, announced in Oran on 22 September 2026 that the national electronic window for administrative courts now covers the administrative courts of appeal and the Council of State. Litigants and lawyers can track cases, read the operative parts of judgments and obtain ordinary copies of rulings online.

2026-09-22-egy-ahramonline-fdc-summit-di.summary: Egyptian officials at the FDC Summit in Cairo on 22 September 2026 said the communications ministry aims to offer more than 100 government services on the Digital Egypt platform by 2026. The investment and foreign trade ministry said it will launch TradeTech, a regulatory sandbox for trade technology, in October 2026, and cited a digital capital-increase service linking eight agencies; the industry ministry offered incentives for factories adopting AI.

2026-09-22-egy-youm7-investment-platform.summary: Egypt's assistant investment minister for digital transformation, Sherif Yehia, said a platform for company capital increases now links eight government bodies digitally. Investors and their agents log in with digital ID and sign documents remotely through a service run with ITIDA, and the ministry is using e-passports to verify foreign investors. He spoke at the FDC Summit on 22 September 2026.

2026-09-22-egypt-nti-al-riyada-universit.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunication Institute signed a protocol with Al-Riyada University for Science and Technology to train its students and graduates in NTI's technology programmes and to cooperate on research.

2026-09-22-egypt-nvidia-ai-cooperation-s.summary: Egypt's communications minister Raafat Hendy met an NVIDIA delegation to discuss cooperation on AI, data science, training-of-trainers programmes and support for start-ups. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-22-egyptian-gazette-ict-minister.summary: Egypt's communications minister Raafat Hendy said a national data centre strategy will be launched by the end of 2026, opening the FDC Summit in Cairo. He also set a target of 400 services on the Digital Egypt platform by 2030, through wider digital identity, e-signature and digital mail.

2026-09-22-geopol-usembassy-australia-on.summary: The US government's submission to Australia's consultation on its Digital Duty of Care online-safety bill argues against rules that would restrict protected speech, mandate product design or widen litigation risk for American platforms. It is a direct statement of the US position on how far other states may regulate US technology companies.

2026-09-22-gha-ecofinagency-denmark-stat.summary: Ghana's statistical service and Statistics Denmark agreed the design of a third, three-year phase of their statistics cooperation, focused on institutional capacity and on integrating administrative data held by ministries and agencies. The service signed data-sharing agreements with 25 ministries, departments and agencies in March 2026. No start date or funding figure is given.

2026-09-22-gha-gna-ai-regulation-without.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George said the government will regulate the risks and harms of AI rather than experimentation, separating low-risk student use from high-risk systems such as credit decisions. He spoke at the Pan African AI and Innovation Summit in Accra.

2026-09-22-gha-graphic-gta-digital-reset.summary: The chief executive of the Ghana Tourism Authority, Maame Efua Houadjeto, said on 18 September 2026 that its Ghana Tourism Information System will put registration, licensing and renewal, tourism levy filing and payment, establishment records and public verification into one digital system. No launch date, cost or supplier is given.

2026-09-22-gha-graphic-masterkey-digital.summary: Kenya's President William Ruto announced Masterkey, a digital wallet holding verifiable records of qualifications and work experience that individuals control and can share across African borders, at an Accra Reset event during the UN General Assembly. Ghana, Rwanda and Kenya are in the first phase, which targets 150,000 placements; Kenya's wallet runs through eCitizen.

2026-09-22-gha-presidency-ops308-hate-sp.summary: Ghana's presidency asked the Media Foundation for West Africa and the Ghana Journalists Association, in a letter dated 22 September 2026, to convene a national stakeholder engagement on hate speech and harmful online content. It asks for guidelines for law enforcement, alternatives to arrest for non-criminal speech, and a roadmap with a timetable for the President.

2026-09-22-itweb-africa-kenya-targets-ai.summary: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Broadcasting and Telecommunications, Steven Isaboke, said at a forum held with the World Bank that the government's focus is shifting from AI policy to measurable gains in jobs, productivity and public services.

2026-09-22-itweb-africa-us-backs-african.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation said it intends to invest US$155 million in WIOCC Group, joining Africa Finance Corporation and Vision Invest as investors. The announcement followed an AFC roundtable in New York during the UN General Assembly; WIOCC operates in more than 30 African countries.

2026-09-22-ken-cbk-bank-supervision-annu.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya's Bank Supervision Annual Report 2025, published on 22 September 2026, reports a March 2025 survey in which 50% of supervised institutions had adopted artificial intelligence, including 66% of commercial banks, and 30% had formal AI strategies. Credit risk assessment was the commonest use. The bank plans an AI guidance note for the sector.

2026-09-22-ken-kenyans-co-ke-sha-nssf-so.summary: Kenya's State Department for Social Protection is seeking a consultant to upgrade the Enhanced Single Registry and the Community Development Management Information System so they exchange data with the Social Health Authority, NSSF, the population register IPRS, civil registration and cash-transfer programmes, Kenyans.co.ke reported on 22 September 2026. The work falls under the World Bank-funded second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project. No cost is given.

2026-09-22-ken-nakuru-go-ke-gbv-pwd-digi.summary: Kenya's Nakuru County government announced on 22 September 2026 a digital case-management platform for gender-based violence cases and disability services, funded by Lithuania's development cooperation fund and built by Lithuanian firm Erobotai with the Vilnius Chamber of Commerce. So far 54 GBV cases and 216 disability-service applications have been registered. No cost is given.

2026-09-22-ken-tenderyetu-kfw-d4tvet-imp.summary: Kenya's State Department for Technical, Vocational Education and Training opened international prequalification for a five-year implementation consultant on its Digitalization for TVET project, listed on 22 September 2026. KfW, AFD and the EU co-finance the project with loans and grants totalling some EUR 50m. No date is given for the financing agreements.

2026-09-22-kenya-ca-finalise-commercial-.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority invited stakeholders to validate its draft guidelines for commercial internet telephony services, after reviewing responses to an earlier consultation. The guidelines set the technical and operational terms for rolling out such services.

2026-09-22-kenya-ict-authority-digital-l.summary: The ICT Authority's account of the same Nyeri rollout adds that more than 62,000 teachers nationally have already been trained under the Digital Literacy Programme.

2026-09-22-kenya-intel-ai-literacy-publi.summary: Kenya's State Department of ICT signed a partnership with Intel at the UN General Assembly to teach AI literacy through public libraries. It will run through the Kenya National Library Service and the Mandela AI Hub Foundation under Intel's AI for Citizens programme.

2026-09-22-kenya-smart-boards-178-junior.summary: Kenya began delivering smart boards and teacher laptops to 178 public junior schools in Nyeri County on 21 September, under phase II of the Digital Literacy Programme. The programme is funded through the World Bank-supported Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project and is to reach all 377 junior schools in the county.

2026-09-22-kredete-acquires-gravv-nigeri.summary: Nigerian financial platform Kredete acquired Gravv, bringing in stablecoin-based technology that connects banks and local payment systems. Kredete says the aim is cheaper and faster international transfers; no price was given.

2026-09-22-lbr-newdawn-gongloe-national-.summary: Liberian lawyer and politician Tiawan Gongloe urged the legislature to scrutinise the proposed concession for the National Identification System before ratifying it. He asked whether Austria's OeSD would provide only technical support or take over state functions, and raised jobs, revenue and the protection of biometric data.

2026-09-22-mdg-alalana-plateforme-export.summary: Madagascar's Ministry of Commerce and Consumption began two days of training for its regional directorates on Alalana, a platform for handling export authorisation requests, at Mahamasina on 21 September 2026. Minister Andriamadison Haingotiana said it speeds up processing and makes it more transparent; vanilla and cloves are among the products covered. No launch date, cost or supplier is given.

2026-09-22-mdg-midimadagasikara-gasy-mon.summary: BGFIBank Madagasikara presented its Gasy Money mobile banking app at the Carlton Anosy hotel in Antananarivo, open to the bank's customers, users of other banks and people without bank accounts. The app currently allows national money transfers through partnerships with mobile operators, and manages the bank's Karatro prepaid card for international use. No fees or user targets are given.

2026-09-22-mdg-rcbe-operational-phase.summary: Madagascar's tax directorate signed four agreements on 18 September 2026 to cross-check its central register of beneficial owners against data held by the companies register, the Bianco anti-corruption bureau, the Economic Development Board and the chamber of notaries. The finance ministry said the register, launched on 16 June 2026, now moves from build to operation.

2026-09-22-mus-waste-carrier-licence-onl.summary: Mauritius's environment ministry announced on 21 September 2026 that applications for a Waste Carrier Licence must be made online through the Economic Development Board platform from October. The rule covers individuals, companies, parastatals, local authorities and ministries, who must upload scanned identity and vehicle documents.

2026-09-22-nam-national-ai-institute-lau.summary: Namibia's National Commission on Research, Science and Technology said on 22 September 2026 that it would launch the National Artificial Intelligence Institute of Namibia the next day. The institute will run four centres, including one to curate Namibian datasets, and its youth AI fellowship is training about 2,000 tertiary students. No budget is given.

2026-09-22-ner-digital-citizenship-disin.summary: Niger's first national campaign against disinformation, under the slogan 'Check before you share', was launched in Tillabéry on 19 September 2026. It was organised by the NGO Jeunesse Plus with the support of the communication ministry, whose secretary-general presided. The campaign combines online awareness with media and information literacy workshops for local communities.

2026-09-22-newzimbabwe-zimbabwe-drone-de.summary: The Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe approved Drone Solutions Zimbabwe to fly beyond-visual-line-of-sight medical deliveries using Kite Aero's KITE aircraft, moving from demonstration flights completed in August 2026 to daily operations. The service carries vaccines, blood, pathology samples and medicines, with deliveries taking about 30 minutes. The date of the approval is not given.

2026-09-22-nga-independent-efina-a2f-202.summary: EFInA's ninth Access to Financial Services in Nigeria survey, released on 16 September 2026, found that 79% of adults, about 94.2 million people, use a financial product or service. Formal inclusion reached 73%, above the 70% target of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy. The Central Bank of Nigeria said the focus now shifts to usage, affordability, trust and financial health.

2026-09-22-nga-ngcert-ransomware-phobos-.summary: Nigeria's national CERT warned of rising Phobos ransomware attacks on cloud service providers whose clients include government agencies, banks and telecoms operators. It rates the damage critical and the probability high, and sets out mitigations.

2026-09-22-nga-tribune-nbs-ilo-unicef-so.summary: Nigeria's National Bureau of Statistics, the ILO and UNICEF convened about 160 stakeholders in Abuja from 22 to 24 September 2026 to harmonise fragmented social protection data, under the EU-funded SUSI programme. The meeting was to introduce a Social Protection Management Information System and inaugurate a committee to produce an annual social protection statistics bulletin.

2026-09-22-pin-digital-inclusion-africa-.summary: Paradigm Initiative published a baseline study on 22 September 2026 of digital inclusion in Ethiopia, Algeria, Namibia, Côte d'Ivoire, Mozambique and DR Congo. It compares the six countries' policy commitments, funding, governance and private-sector involvement, and notes that access remains uneven for young people, women and rural populations.

2026-09-22-rwa-ktpress-bank-kigali-cips.summary: Bank of Kigali has joined China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System as a direct participant, the first bank in Rwanda and the first headquartered in East and Central Africa to do so, under an agreement signed in Xiamen on 8 September 2026. It gives the bank direct renminbi clearing and settlement without intermediary banks.

2026-09-22-rwa-radiotv10-un-world-data-f.summary: Rwanda was chosen on 21 September 2026 to host the seventh UN World Data Forum, expected in the fourth quarter of 2028. It is the second African host after South Africa, which held the first forum in Cape Town in 2017. The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda welcomed the selection.

2026-09-22-rwanda-mou-chipmango-semicond.summary: Rwanda's Ministry of ICT and Innovation signed a memorandum of understanding with ChipMango to build local semiconductor design skills. It followed talks between Minister of State Yves Iradukunda and the company on a national chip-design talent pipeline.

2026-09-22-sen-paens-tdr-pins-infrastruc.summary: Senegal's digital economy acceleration project, PAENS, financed by the World Bank, posted terms of reference on 22 September 2026 for a consultancy firm to study the technical infrastructure needed by the X-Road-based national interoperability platform, PINS. The four-month study covers hosting at the state digital infrastructure company SENUM or sectoral sites and integration with the national PKI. PAENS totals EUR 144.9 million over 2023-2028.

2026-09-22-sita-recovery-mode-comms-mini.summary: Communications minister Solly Malatsi told GovTech 2026 in Durban that the State IT Agency is recovering under stable leadership and must now deliver on digitising government services and ending fragmented systems. The conference ran under the theme of South African digital sovereignty.

2026-09-22-south-africa-zaru-stablecoin-.summary: A second report of the ZARU launch on Arc adds how trades settle: the ZARU/USDC pair clears through StableFX's request-for-quote engine, with both legs settling together or not at all, which is meant to remove counterparty risk from rand foreign exchange.

2026-09-22-ssd-jubaecho-ssra-digital-tax.summary: The South Sudan Revenue Authority launched an electronic tax audit module in Juba on 21 September 2026 to replace paper-based audits, backed by a directive from Commissioner General Moun Deng Ajuet banning manual audits. The platform, supported by the company Crawford Capital Pay, centralises audit cases, findings, correspondence and taxpayer records.

2026-09-22-standard-bank-stellenbosch-re.summary: Standard Bank and Stellenbosch University's School for Data Science and Computational Thinking are developing a framework for responsible AI use in business, announced at a panel in Cape Town.

2026-09-22-swz-times-data-recovery-site-.summary: Eswatini's Finance Minister Neal Rijkenberg told Parliament that the Treasury has asked Exim Bank of India to cancel an undrawn US$10.4 million loan, about E182 million, for a government data recovery site in the Lubombo Region. The project stalled and no work has taken place, while commitment fees continue to accrue. The bank has not yet confirmed the cancellation.

2026-09-22-techafricanews-mastercard-wal.summary: Mastercard launched Wallet Pay, a set of services letting digital wallets accept contactless, QR and online payments across its network. MTN and AXIAN are among the launch partners, alongside Alipay+ and others.

2026-09-22-techcabal-safaricom-hits-1-mi.summary: Safaricom became the first Kenyan provider to pass one million fixed broadband subscribers, with 1,024,950 at the end of June 2026 according to the Communications Authority, a 36.1% market share. The report argues that the volume-led growth is straining margins.

2026-09-22-techcabal-south-africas-bank-.summary: App-only Bank Zero recorded its first break-even month in August 2026, five years after opening, with 275,000 direct customers and about 500,000 more through partner platforms. Its CEO put the cost of building its own platform at under R300 million, against an estimated R3 billion to buy one.

2026-09-22-techcabal-tanzania-regulator-.summary: Tanzania's Fair Competition Commission put KCB Group's stake in Kenyan payments firm Pesapal at 22.23%, the first public figure for a deal KCB announced in 2025 without terms. The stake gives KCB indirect control of Pesapal Tanzania and is under the commission's review; its value is undisclosed.

2026-09-22-tgo-etfp-dual-atelier-regiona.summary: Togo's education minister, Mama Omorou, opened a regional workshop in Lomé on 21 September 2026 on dual technical and vocational training in the digital era, attended by six countries. Its planned outputs are a private-sector engagement guide, operating scenarios for the InserJeune graduate-tracking tool and an expanded national policy on AI in vocational training.

2026-09-22-tgo-togopresse-harc-regulatio.summary: Togo's communication regulator HARC held its first official meeting with content creators, bloggers and influencers in Lomé on 22 September 2026, citing its remit over social-media content under article 78 of the 2024 Constitution. HARC's president said social-media advertising should in principle need its prior approval, and the communication ministry said the 2020 press and communication code will be revised to cover these actors.

2026-09-22-tun-cybersecurite-circulaire-.summary: An analysis of Tunisia's circular of 2 September 2026 on public-sector cybersecurity says it obliges public enterprises to adopt multi-factor authentication, DDoS protection, regular audits, backups and business continuity measures, creating recurring costs. The national cybersecurity agency's list of 17 September names only six qualified N-Cloud providers. New continuity and recovery requirements are announced from 1 January 2027.

2026-09-22-tza-citizen-budget-2026-27-co.summary: Tanzania's finance ministry published its Citizen Budget for 2026/27, a 34-page plain-language account of spending of TZS 54.50 trillion, revenue sources, deficit and financing. Its revenue measures include raising the digital service tax on foreign digital service providers from 2% to 3%. The document carries no issue date.

2026-09-22-uga-pride-bank-interswitch-pa.summary: Uganda's Pride Bank launched a partnership with Interswitch that offers selected banking services through Interswitch's network of more than 21,000 Quickteller agents and issues Pride Bank Verve debit cards. Agents will handle deposits, withdrawals, loan repayments and bill payments. No financial terms are given.

2026-09-22-unitel-revenue-rises-17-perce.summary: Angolan operator UNITEL reported first-half 2026 revenue of 274 billion kwanzas, up 17%, with EBITDA of 91 billion kwanzas and net income of 66.3 billion. Subscribers passed 21.2 million, data use rose 43% and the network reached 12,302 base stations.

2026-09-22-verto-visa-multi-currency-cor.summary: Payments platform Verto and Visa launched the Verto Card, a corporate card for African businesses that funds and settles in 11 currencies with no FX markup on eligible ones and indirect access to 160 more. It runs on Visa's commercial rails rather than prepaid rails, which Verto blames for declined cross-border payments.

2026-09-22-zambia-mytochondria-ai-satell.summary: Zambian start-up Mytochondria, co-founded in 2023 by data scientist Thomas Fred Lungu, uses satellite imagery and AI to assess soil quality, moisture and temperature for farmers. The profile presents it as a response to climate shocks hitting harvests in southern Africa.

2026-09-22-zaru-goes-live-circle-arc-blo.summary: ZAR Universal (ZARU), a rand stablecoin issued by BlockTower under a Financial Sector Conduct Authority licence, went live on Circle's Arc blockchain and opened as a founding currency pair on Circle StableFX. Each token is backed by one rand held in South Africa, with reserves managed by Sanlam Specialised Asset Management; Luno, EasyEquities and Lesaka are partners in its development.

2026-09-22-zwe-technomag-africa-data-pro.summary: Zimbabwe's regulator POTRAZ, which acts as the country's data protection authority, marked the first Africa Data Protection Day on 21 September. The day commemorates the 2016 founding of the Network of African Data Protection Authorities, which now has 34 members and in which POTRAZ is second vice-president.

2026-09-23-afdb-seychelles-ergrsp3-loan.summary: The African Development Bank approved a US$34 million loan to Seychelles on 22 September 2026 for the third and final phase of its Economic Resilience and Green Recovery Support Programme. The phase supports electronic invoicing for tax, a national e-procurement system and a one-stop investment portal, and brings the bank's financing across the three phases to US$84 million.

2026-09-23-ago-forum-lusophone-gouvernan.summary: Angola's information-society institute is hosting the Lusophone Internet Governance Forum in Luanda on 23 and 24 September, bringing together experts from Portuguese-speaking countries on digital transformation, online safety and the digital divide.

2026-09-23-ago-novojornal-tribunal-const.summary: Angola's Constitutional Court opened a limited tender on 22 September 2026, valued at Kz 20 billion (about US$21 million), to upgrade its technology platform for registering candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections, including migrating records from earlier electoral cycles. The Ministry of Territorial Administration said more than two million adults have updated their voter data since June.

2026-09-23-bdi-pafen-ddp-e-gp-deploiemen.summary: Burundi's World Bank-funded digital foundations project has issued an international tender for a custom electronic government procurement system covering the whole contract cycle. It is to be open source, built over 18 months with the procurement regulator's staff, installed first at the finance ministry, and owned outright by the government; bids close on 13 November 2026.

2026-09-23-ben-lanation-anip-cartes-egal.summary: Benin's identification agency ANIP handed 1,422 equal-opportunity cards for persons with disabilities to the Ministry of Family and Social Action in Cotonou on 18 September 2026. The cards, provided for under a 2017 law, give access to rights in health, education, employment and transport. ANIP issued 4,718 cards in 2024 and 2025 and has about 4,000 applications for 2026.

2026-09-23-ben-rwa-explorent-cooperation.summary: Benin's digital minister Mahuna Akplogan and Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire discussed AI cooperation in agriculture, health and education on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, including infrastructure, data access, skills and joint research. No agreement or specific project was announced.

2026-09-23-bfa-lefaso-arcep-aes-conventi.summary: The telecoms regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are to sign a cooperation agreement in Ouagadougou on 25 September creating a Sahel Regulators' Council. It covers roaming within the Alliance of Sahel States, consumer protection, cybersecurity, spectrum, mutual recognition of type-approved equipment and joint positions in international bodies.

2026-09-23-bfa-lefaso-ecole-langue-ia-so.summary: In an opinion piece timed to the SIST 2026 science symposium in Ouagadougou, sociolinguist Mamadou Lamine Sanogo of Burkina Faso's CNRST argues that schooling and AI must be built on African languages, data and indigenous knowledge. He presents this as the condition for scientific and digital sovereignty.

2026-09-23-botswana-bofinet-internationa.summary: Botswana Fibre Networks signed a long-term international capacity lease with an unnamed South African partner, raising capacity through the Ramatlabama and Pioneer Gate border crossings from 300 Gbit/s to 1 Tbit/s.

2026-09-23-bwa-dailynews-smartbots-unep-.summary: Botswana's President Duma Boko told UN Economic Commission for Africa head Claver Gatete in New York that the SmartBots digital transformation strategy will be formally launched in November 2026. Boko asked the commission to remain a partner in it as a flagship project. The meeting date is not stated.

2026-09-23-caf-centrafrique-rgph-4-l-ica.summary: The Central African Republic's statistics institute, ICASEES, put the provisional global and preliminary results of the fourth general population and housing census (RGPH-4) before the intersectoral census technical committee in Bangui on 23 September 2026. It is the country's first count since 2003; the operation mapped 7,591 enumeration areas and mobilised more than eleven thousand people, and seven of them died during it.

2026-09-23-cedeao-aip-adapt-data-protect.summary: At the same Dakar conference, digital-governance expert Janet Gbam said the 2010 ECOWAS Supplementary Act on personal data no longer covers AI, algorithmic decision-making or the right to erasure. She named Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria and Cabo Verde as ahead on legislation and regulators, with other member states constrained by capacity.

2026-09-23-cedeao-court-justice-digital-.summary: At a Dakar conference, law lecturer Jake Okechukwu Effoduh argued that the ECOWAS Court already has the legal basis to hear digital-rights cases, from internet shutdowns to biometric surveillance, without a new treaty. A Bissau law professor noted that Guinea-Bissau still has no data-protection law or authority, though a bill would create one.

2026-09-23-citizen-za-iec-glitch-free-el.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission said on 23 September 2026 it has completed end-to-end testing of its results system for the 4 November elections, and parties may test it with their own experts from 5 to 12 October. Chairperson Mosotho Moepya cited reworked voter management devices after results-centre screens failed in 2024. More than 60,000 staff have been trained.

2026-09-23-cod-claude-assistant-ia-anthr.summary: DR Congo's Ministry of Digital Economy announced on 22 September that Anthropic's Claude is now officially available in the country, both the consumer service and commercial API access. Users had previously reached it through VPNs; the communiqué gave no terms.

2026-09-23-cog-adiac-sifec-etat-civil-op.summary: The Republic of Congo's information systems agency ACSI handed the interior ministry's territorial administration directorate, on 22 September 2026 in Kintélé, the technical documents for SIFEC, a civil registration software it designed and built. Next steps include an inventory, data centralisation, user training, finalising the civil-status law and deployment. No cost or deployment date is given.

2026-09-23-dza-algerie-eco-djezzy-paymen.summary: The Bank of Algeria's Monetary and Banking Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services, a subsidiary of Optimum Telecom Algérie, to be set up as a payment service provider under regulation 25-02. The company must apply for a full licence within 12 months of notification.

2026-09-23-dza-bank-of-algeria-cmb-commu.summary: The Bank of Algeria's Monetary and Banking Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services, a subsidiary of the mobile operator Optimum Telecom Algérie, to be set up as a payment service provider, its communiqué of 23 September 2026 states. The firm must apply for the bank's approval to operate within twelve months.

2026-09-23-dza-echorouk-prodnat-industri.summary: Algeria's provincial industry directorates kept registration open on the PRODNAT national-production platform after its mid-September 2026 deadline. Goods-producing firms must supply 12 items, including tax and statistical identifiers, the manager's biometric ID card, the geolocation of each production unit, and purchases, stocks and sales for the first half of 2026. Second-half declarations are due between 1 January and 28 February 2027.

2026-09-23-dza-jo-68-cahier-charges-serv.summary: Algeria's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications approved, by order of 4 August 2026 published in the Official Journal on 23 September 2026, a universal-service specification giving ATM Mobilis the task of providing 4G mobile coverage at 201 sites, funded site by site from the universal-service fund. The regulator ARPCE pays a fixed amount per site on acceptance; late delivery draws a penalty of up to 10%. Per-site amounts are in annexed tables.

2026-09-23-dza-radioalgerie-morafikokoum.summary: Algeria's Ministry of National Solidarity launched Morafikokoum, a digital platform for parents of deaf and blind pupils in specialised schools, reported on 23 September 2026. Registered parents can download enrolment certificates, view grades and attendance, and submit transfer, readmission and appeal requests online.

2026-09-23-eac-igad-eardip-regional-digi.summary: The EAC, IGAD and the World Bank are holding a three-day workshop in Nairobi (22 to 24 September) with Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan to align national projects under the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project. It covers cross-border broadband, digital public infrastructure, cybersecurity cooperation and digital trade; Kenya takes part through its own World Bank-funded KDEAP.

2026-09-23-ecowas-ai-working-group-elect.summary: ECOWAS's director of political affairs, Babatunde Afolabi, said in Dakar that the ECOWAS Network of Electoral Commissions has set up a West Africa Working Group on Artificial Intelligence to draft a framework for election bodies' use of AI, naming deepfakes and disinformation as risks. The date the group was established is not given.

2026-09-23-egy-ahramonline-kemet-data-ce.summary: Egypt's communications minister met INTRO Investment Holding to review the Kemet data centre in the Suez Canal Economic Zone's Sokhna industrial zone, planned as the zone's first Tier III facility at 80 MW. The project is put at USD 1.2 billion, with USD 270 million for phase one; no timeline was disclosed.

2026-09-23-egy-youm7-digital-farmland-re.summary: Egypt's agriculture ministry spokesman Khaled Gad said on 23 September 2026 that a digital register of farm holdings, built over several years, links each holding to the crop actually grown across about 4.4 million farmer cards. He said this curbs fictitious holdings and false crop declarations used to obtain subsidised fertiliser.

2026-09-23-egy-youm7-smart-courts-justic.summary: Youm7 surveys Egypt's Ministry of Justice programme to move courts off paper: digitised case files and archives, remote litigation in some circuits, automated queueing, and systems that transcribe audio recordings of hearings into written minutes. It also points to training for judges and staff through the National Center for Judicial Studies and to legislation on electronic procedure and personal-data protection.

2026-09-23-enterpriseam-instapay-papss-e.summary: Afreximbank plans to connect the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) to Egypt's InstaPay, and six unnamed Egyptian banks have applied to the Central Bank of Egypt for integration approval, PAPSS's chief executive said. InstaPay does not yet handle cross-border payments, so a gateway has still to be built; no launch date was given.

2026-09-23-gab-agp-cemac-sie-workshop-re.summary: Energy experts from the Central African Economic and Monetary Community, meeting in Libreville, validated on 23 September 2026 a draft regulation creating a regional energy information system and its roadmap. They recommended that member states give national units a dedicated recurring budget and permanent qualified staff. The proposals go to the energy ministers' meeting of 25 September.

2026-09-23-gab-agp-sie-cemac-recensement.summary: Gabon's energy statistics director, Armand-Colyn Abessolo Nkewele, said on 23 September 2026 that results of the 2026 population census will feed the country's energy information system and indicators, including those for SDG 7. He spoke at a regional workshop on a shared energy information system for CEMAC states. No date for the census results is given.

2026-09-23-gha-bog-summary-economic-fina.summary: The Bank of Ghana's data summary released on 23 September 2026 records 1,046 million mobile money transactions worth GHC518.8bn in August 2026, up from 831 million worth GHC354.1bn a year earlier. Registered mobile money accounts stood at 85.8 million, of which 26.4 million were active.

2026-09-23-gha-gna-data-protection-boss-.summary: Ghana Data Protection Commission head Arnold Kavaarpuo called for African privacy and competition regulators to act together against big-tech concentration, and presented NADPA's draft model policy on cross-border data transfers, which sets six lawful transfer routes. He said 44 of 55 AU member states have data-protection laws, 38 with operational regulators.

2026-09-23-gha-graphic-chipper-cash-virt.summary: Fintech firm Chipper Cash began opening bank-backed virtual accounts for customers in Ghana through an API link with Universal Merchant Bank, reported on 23 September 2026. The bank had received Bank of Ghana and Securities and Exchange Commission approval to offer virtual accounts to businesses in the virtual asset sector; the approval date is not stated.

2026-09-23-gha-knust-signtalk-gh-sign-la.summary: Researchers at Ghana's Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology have developed SignTalk-Gh, an AI system that translates Ghanaian Sign Language into text and audio and back, built for doctor-patient consultations. The work was funded through the Responsible AI Lab's AI4SD project by the French Embassy in Ghana and AFD. No deployment date or hospital count is given.

2026-09-23-gha-modernghana-helping-afric.summary: The US-based Helping Africa Foundation marked its tenth anniversary in Gbawe, Ghana, and called on African governments to expand its youth ICT laboratory model. It has supported more than 19 ICT demonstration labs in Ghana, The Gambia and Liberia, with more planned in Tanzania and Zanzibar. Ghana's education ministry will discuss a scale-up policy; no funding is stated.

2026-09-23-gha-myjoyonline-dvlaverify-ap.summary: Ghana's Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority released its DVLAverify biometric identity-verification app on Apple's App Store and opened a web version usable from any computer with a webcam. Vehicle-registration applicants can now complete identity checks remotely.

2026-09-23-gha-myjoyonline-gra-itas-digi.summary: The Ghana Revenue Authority said its Integrated Tax Administration System is to be linked to customs (ICUMS), the companies registrar, SSNIT, the Bank of Ghana, Ghana.gov, the Lands Commission and the National Identification Authority. Some capabilities are live, with return pre-population and further automation to follow in stages.

2026-09-23-gha-tvet-unesco-kpmg-microsof.summary: Ghana's TVET Service signed a memorandum with UNESCO, KPMG and Microsoft under the AI EmpowerED initiative to train at least 100,000 technical and vocational instructors in AI and digital skills. No cost or timeline was given.

2026-09-23-gin-africaguinee-ande-academi.summary: Guinea's state digitalisation agency ANDE presented the feasibility study for a National Digital Academy for validation at a Conakry workshop on 23 September 2026, with support from the World Bank-financed WARDIP programme. The academy would offer short certified courses in information systems, AI and cybersecurity, first for civil servants. The amended report goes to the authorities before launch.

2026-09-23-gmb-thepoint-land-lease-digit.summary: The Gambia's Lands Minister told the National Assembly that lease documents will be issued within three days once the ministry's World Bank-supported digital system is fully running, with contracts already awarded. The ministry is clearing about 50 lease files a week from a backlog in which some had waited three to five years.

2026-09-23-gnb-ang-transformacao-digital.summary: Bissau's municipal council launched CMB+, its integrated modernisation and digital transformation project, on 22 September, including a municipal portal for access to council services. The territorial administration minister spoke at the launch.

2026-09-23-gnb-unu-egov-welcomes-delegat.summary: A delegation from Guinea-Bissau's Ministry of Territorial Administration and Local Government, including two regional secretaries, visited the UN University's e-governance unit in Guimarães, Portugal, on 9 September 2026. They discussed the unit's project document for implementing Guinea-Bissau's national digital transformation strategy. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-23-herald-zwe-lims-rural-diagnos.summary: Zimbabwe's health ministry said on 23 September 2026 that its Laboratory Information Management System is running at 117 main laboratories and linked to lower-level ones, allowing results to be sent electronically, including by SMS. The national laboratory plan for 2025–2030 aims to extend it to 80% of health facilities, and it is to connect with the Impilo electronic health records platform.

2026-09-23-ictgo-uga-buhadyo-smart-class.summary: Uganda's ICT ministry said a smart classroom at Buhadyo Primary School in Butaleja District, built with Huawei under the Smart Villages pilot, lets pupils join the same e-learning lessons as Nakasero Primary School in Kampala. The pilot adds a telecoms tower and a 120-panel solar system that also powers 25 households. No cost is given.

2026-09-23-internetsociety-au-ai-governa.summary: The African Union Commission is holding an open online consultation on 23 and 24 September on its draft Guidelines on AI Governance and Regulation, which implement the 2024 Continental AI Strategy. Day two covers regulation, security and standards, including the AU Model AI Law; written submissions are accepted until 30 September.

2026-09-23-itu-dfs-security-lab-watra-cr.summary: The International Telecommunication Union says its Digital Financial Services Security Lab has assisted more than 20 countries in Africa, the Caribbean and Latin America to test mobile payment apps for security. Its guidelines for regulators have been adopted by the southern and east African regulators' associations, CRASA and EACO; the central African body is considering them and the West African one has a draft.

2026-09-23-ken-ruto-ai-child-safety-unga.summary: Kenya's President William Ruto called for technology that is safe by design for children at a UN meeting of the Coalition for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI, which Kenya launched with France and Spain in July. The coalition unveiled a 2026-2027 roadmap backed by 23 states and eight UN entities. Ruto said Kenya is drafting an AI and emerging technologies policy expected to cover child online safety.

2026-09-23-ken-standard-kenya-anthropic-.summary: Kenya signed a Joint Declaration with Anthropic in New York during UNGA 81, covering AI applications in education and health, research, capacity building, and AI safety and evaluation. The next step is to develop specific pilots and institutional partnerships with government agencies.

2026-09-23-ken-techtrendske-state-plans-.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary John Tanui said, in a speech read for him at WSO2Con Africa in Nairobi on 23 September 2026, that the government is building an Enterprise Platform to link public institutions' systems through secure APIs before deploying AI agents in public services. He said Zero Trust security must be a founding principle for autonomous AI in government. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-23-ken-techweez-manual-backend-i.summary: Kenya's ICT Principal Secretary Mary Kerema told WSO2Con Africa 2026 that the government runs more than 22,000 online services but its back-end processing is still largely manual, so citizens carry documents the state already holds. She said a Government Enterprise Architecture has been launched and an interoperability platform for sharing data between agencies is in development.

2026-09-23-ken-uasingishu-ict-regulation.summary: Kenya's ICT ministry and the Communications Authority held a three-day workshop to validate proposed Kenya Information and Communications Regulations, reported on 23 September 2026. The review covers licensing, spectrum, numbering, interconnection, tariffs, consumer protection, universal service, infrastructure sharing, electronic certification and domain names under the 1998 Act.

2026-09-23-lbr-cybastion-women-digital-b.summary: Liberia's gender ministry signed an agreement with Cybastion, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, for women's technology and business hubs with childcare: a Monrovia campus and regional sites in Voinjama, Gbarnga, Kakata and Buchanan. Training is to run through Cisco's Networking Academy; no cost or timetable was given.

2026-09-23-lbr-elbcnews-cybastion-cisco-.summary: Liberia's gender minister Gbeme Horace-Kollie signed a partnership with Cybastion Institute of Technology and Cisco Systems in New York on 22 September 2026 to build digital skills among women. Cybastion is to build, equip and run five technology and business hubs for women in Lofa, Margibi, Grand Bassa, Bong and Montserrado counties over 36 months. No cost is given.

2026-09-23-lbr-fpa-cdc-cybercrime-law-su.summary: Liberia's opposition CDC says it will ask the Supreme Court to rule on the constitutionality of the Cybercrime Act of 2025. The move follows the court-ordered release on 22 September of commentator Jerry Nyantee Wrato, whom police intended to prosecute under the Act over AI-generated images of the Vice President.

2026-09-23-lbr-gin-owlpress-mariama-bang.summary: The third Mano River Union Internet Governance Forum met in Paynesville, Liberia, on 21–22 September 2026, bringing together participants from Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire. Sierra Leonean MP Mariama Bangura urged the region's parliaments to strengthen laws on personal data, privacy and online safety, and to harmonise legislation on artificial intelligence.

2026-09-23-lbr-thenewdawn-gac-automates-.summary: Liberia's General Auditing Commission has begun automating public-sector audits, with KPMG contracted to build audit software under a World Bank-supported project, deputy information minister Daniel Sanoe said at a press briefing on 22 September 2026. No contract value or timetable is given.

2026-09-23-lby-lana-technical-education-.summary: Libya's Ministry of Technical and Vocational Education said on 23 September 2026 that an upgraded version of its electronic archiving system is close to launch, with testing and approval under way and user training to follow. The ministry said the update adds stronger access controls, backups and security.

2026-09-23-lby-libyaherald-unified-trade.summary: The Libya Trade Network met international shipping agents and the Libyan Ports Company to review the mandatory Unified Trade System (PTS) for vessel arrival notices and cargo manifests. Priorities are finishing testing of XML shipment-data transmission and completing roll-out at Tripoli and Al-Khoms ports.

2026-09-23-lso-govls-cybersecurity-bill-.summary: Lesotho's information and communications ministry, with the Lesotho Communications Authority and UNDP, held a two-day consultation on the Cybersecurity Bill 2026 in Maseru, reported on 23 September 2026. Cabinet split the 2024 Computer Crime and Cybersecurity Bill into separate cybercrime and cybersecurity bills; the new bill proposes a two-tier regulatory regime and registration of cybersecurity professionals.

2026-09-23-lso-govls-first-country-imple.summary: Lesotho's prime minister, Samuel Matekane, told the second UN Digital Cooperation Day in New York that Lesotho is the first country to implement the UN AI Blueprint. He said planning is complete and Phase One of a National Compute Roadmap for 2026 to 2029 has begun, after more than a year of assessing compute, data-centre, connectivity, skills and financing needs. No cost is given.

2026-09-23-lso-govls-ramashamole-safe-dp.summary: Lesotho's ICT ministry has developed safeguards for children in digital public infrastructure with UNICEF Lesotho and is piloting them with the National University of Lesotho across five ministries, Principal Secretary Kanono Ramashamole told side meetings at the 81st UN General Assembly.
