Average fitting time at Kampala bonds fell from 19 days in December 2025 to two days in September 2026; the ministry linked the registration system to a 17% rise in taxes.

2026-09-30-uga-nilepost-ura-nin-tax-reco.summary: The Uganda Revenue Authority is moving to the National Identification Number as individuals' tax identifier, first mapping existing tax numbers to NINs, then taking fingerprint consent at URA service points. Basic biodata such as name, date of birth and photograph is drawn from the national identity authority's servers. Companies receive an entity number from the business registry, URSB.

2026-09-30-uganda-japan-discuss-expandin.summary: Uganda's ICT minister and Japan's ambassador discussed a second phase of the JICA-backed UJ Connect ICT industry project, adding AI, more mentorship and closer links between Ugandan ICT talent and Japanese firms. No budget or start date was given.

2026-09-30-xaf-techreviewafrica-auda-nep.summary: AUDA-NEPAD launched an Africa Semiconductor Technical Advisory Group in South Africa with the CSIR, the African Academy of Sciences and South Africa's science department, to coordinate chip design, packaging, critical minerals and skills across the continent. Its first twelve months cover six work areas including RISC-V adoption and standards.

2026-09-30-xaf-techreviewafrica-day-zero.summary: A pre-FIFAfrica dialogue convened by the Global Center on AI Governance, Digital Action and CIPESA called for African AI governance principles to be turned into concrete commitments on training data, worker participation and community interests.

2026-09-30-zaf-compcom-statement-decisio.summary: South Africa's Competition Commission recommended that the Tribunal approve MTN's acquisition of tower operator IHS, on conditions of fair and non-discriminatory access to IHS towers for rival operators, fair lease renewals, ring-fencing of customer information and an operationally independent IHS. Job protection and ownership conditions are attached.

2026-09-30-zaf-dcdt-oral-reply-no763-usa.summary: South Africa's communications minister told the National Assembly, in an oral reply approved on 30 September 2026, that ICASA collected R1,287,583,749 for the Universal Service and Access Fund over the five years to 2025/26, with about R652 million left unspent at the end of 2025/26. He cited delays in set-top-box installation and broadband projects; 2025/26 spending included a R567 million write-off of digital-migration stock.

2026-09-30-zaf-icasa-gg-55476-withdrawal.summary: South Africa's communications regulator ICASA withdrew its notice of an inquiry into the affordability of telecommunications services (Notice 4130 of 2026) in Government Gazette No. 55476 of 30 September 2026. The same gazette withdrew Notices 4129 and 4148 on an inquiry into over-the-top services, and reprinted a draft notice of intention to hold the affordability inquiry in four phases.

2026-09-30-zaf-itweb-absa-digital-asset-.summary: Absa launched institutional digital-asset custody for South African clients on 21 September on Ripple's technology, the first such service by an African bank. It is for institutional and large corporate clients, not retail crypto.

2026-09-30-zaf-usaasa-discussion-documen.summary: South Africa's Universal Service and Access Agency published a discussion document on 30 September 2026 on which needy persons should receive electronic communications subsidies, who must apply and who may be paid. It sets six provisional propositions with financial inability as the central test, but proposes no income threshold, benefit amount or payment platform. Comments close on 30 October 2026.

2026-09-30-zambia-must-use-digital-platf.summary: President Hichilema told the UAE's cabinet affairs minister in Abu Dhabi that Zambia must use digital platforms to cut the bureaucracy slowing investment and services, treating digital infrastructure as part of service delivery itself. The UAE offered its own bureaucracy-reduction programme as a model.

2026-10-01-africa-cdc-calls-for-stronger.summary: Africa CDC called on member states to strengthen national health data stewardship and adopt interoperable digital standards, at a consultative session at the Africa HealthTech Summit in Kigali.

2026-10-01-afrinic-elections-2026-pdp-co.summary: AFRINIC opened candidate registration for one of its two policy development co-chair seats, closing on 29 October. The seat will be filled at the public policy meeting on 18 November.

2026-10-01-ago-expansao-financiamento-cu.summary: Angola's higher education ministry has awarded USD 38.7 million under results-based agreements to 13 public universities and institutes to expand science, technology and engineering courses, under a project co-financed by the World Bank and GPE. Only USD 710,000 had been paid out when this was reported on 1 October 2026.

2026-10-01-ago-pti-sepe-online-after-kaz.summary: Angola's public e-services portal SEPE remained online after the Kazu ransomware group claimed an attack on it, Portal de T.I. reported on 1 October 2026. Registration, the service catalogue and services in employment, education, health, transport and business were still available; the intrusion and data theft claimed by the group are unconfirmed.

2026-10-01-airtel-money-sets-ipo-price-a.summary: Airtel Money set the price of its London share offer at GBP1.96, valuing the company at about GBP5.3 billion. Trading is expected to begin on 14 October.

2026-10-01-anambra-launches-digital-gate.summary: Nigeria's Anambra State launched a redesigned website as a single entry point to state services, with grievance and freedom-of-information channels. An open-government section gives budgets, audit reports, procurement plans, contract awards and open data.

2026-10-01-auda-nepad-launches-atlas-umo.summary: The African Union's development agency launched and chairs an AI policy workstream, ATLAS Umoja, on AI governance and African-language AI. A mobile industry official said at the launch that fewer than 2% of African languages are meaningfully supported by today's AI models.

2026-10-01-businessday-meta-appeals-nige.summary: Meta filed a notice of appeal on 30 September against a Lagos High Court judgment of 25 September that held its processing of Nigerian users' data for behavioural advertising unlawful. The court ordered it to stop, comply with the data protection Act within eight weeks and pay the naira equivalent of US$100,000 in damages.

2026-10-01-cenfri-award-winner-ngirinshu.summary: The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda built a model that assigns industry, occupation and education codes to Labour Force Survey answers in Kinyarwanda, English or French, auto-coding 96% of records in one test. Work that took about four analysts a week now needs one person. The project, which grew from an AIMS and Cenfri training course, won an ITU Innovate for Impact award; a field app awaits further testing.

2026-10-01-civ-forfait-internet-cote-d-i.summary: Tech-Tools Afrique published a price comparison of mobile and home internet plans in Côte d'Ivoire on 1 October 2026. Moov plans cost about 250 FCFA per gigabyte. MTN monthly packs start at 2,000 FCFA for 3 GB. Orange or Moov fibre starts at 15,000 FCFA a month. The site says offers change and prices need checking.

2026-10-01-cmr-comment-internet-arrive-a.summary: The Cameroonian civil-society group OBS-CC published an explainer on 1 October 2026 on how Cameroon connects to the global internet. It lists five submarine cables landing in three coastal towns, Limbe, Douala and Kribi, and a national fibre backbone run by Camtel. OBS-CC puts the backbone at 12,000 to nearly 16,000 km, citing published estimates.

2026-10-01-cod-ceni-denis-kadima-lance-l.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's electoral commission, CENI, launched a programme in Kinshasa on 28 September 2026 to digitise electoral archives produced since 2005 into a single secure document repository. Its president, Denis Kadima, also launched training in four phases for 762 staff, including AI applied to elections. No cost or funder is stated.

2026-10-01-cod-drc-moves-to-expand-publi.summary: The DRC government adopted on 30 September 2026 a bill to replace the 2010 public procurement law (Law No. 10/010), presented by Budget Minister Adolphe Muzito. It would widen the use of paperless procedures and open public contracts to small businesses and start-ups, and responds to heavy use of direct awards and weak contract monitoring.

2026-10-01-cod-recensement-identificatio.summary: Two DRC ministers, Patrick Muyaya and Guylain Nyembo, said on 30 September 2026 that the second population and housing census counts people but does not identify them, unlike the separate identification process that is to issue national identity cards. Census mapping began on 28 September; enumeration starts in July 2027, and the operation is costed at US$192m.

2026-10-01-cod-retour-sur-la-matinee-fis.summary: The Fédération des Entreprises du Congo held a tax briefing for its Kinshasa members (reported 1 October 2026). Two new provincial revenue bodies, DGIPK and DGTK, presented their duties beside the provincial finance minister. The federation wanted members to know which bodies may collect taxes and run audits. A provincial order of 17 September 2026 sets the transition.

2026-10-01-digital-society-governing-ai-.summary: A systematic review of 30 peer-reviewed articles from 2020 to 2026 finds that evidence on AI for sustainability goals in the global south is concentrated in environmental uses such as climate-risk assessment and land-use monitoring. Reported benefits depend on AI tools being combined with data infrastructure, institutional capacity and accountability safeguards.

2026-10-01-drc-senate-social-media-ban-u.summary: The DR Congo Senate declared admissible on 28 September 2026 a bill by Senator Yvan Kazadi Kankonde amending the 2023 Digital Code to bar children under 13 from opening social media accounts. Those aged 13 to 15 would need verifiable parental consent, and platforms would have to verify age. The bill has gone to committee and is not law.

2026-10-01-dza-algerie-eco-gie-monetique.summary: Algeria's interbank card body, GIE Monétique, said on 1 October 2026 that about 23 million payment cards were in circulation at the end of August 2026, including 19 million Algérie Poste Edahabia cards, with over 62% active. Payment terminals rose from 78,000 in December 2025 to 126,000, and active online merchants from 644 to 1,034.

2026-10-01-dza-lasentinelle-gigacity-202.summary: Algeria's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications said on 30 September 2026 that Algiers ranked first in Africa and 34th of 50 cities worldwide in Omdia's Gigacity Index 2026, with 36 points, 11 places ahead of Cape Town. The ministry cited fibre-to-the-home coverage of nearly 100% in the capital and 90% of subscribers on speeds above 100 Mbps.

2026-10-01-dza-maghrebemergent-permis-pa.summary: Applicants in Algiers and Béjaïa reported waiting at least three months, and in some cases five to six, for biometric driving licences, and six to eight weeks for biometric passports. The interior ministry says applicants are notified by SMS when a licence is ready and can track requests online. No official explanation for the delays has been published.

2026-10-01-e-panic-button-security-flaw-.summary: A Gauteng legislature committee said it will examine whether the provincial e-government department's earlier assurances about the e-Panic Button's security were accurate. The department says an attempted breach was identified and fixed and that no personal information was compromised.

2026-10-01-egy-760-2025.summary: Egypt's communications ministry said it carried out more than 760 cyber-defence operations across the country in 2025. It made the statement during Cybersecurity Awareness Month. The statement also describes the national CERT, a youth cybersecurity academy and an awareness drive by the telecoms regulator.

2026-10-01-egy-smart-legislation-crimina.summary: Mohamed Hegazy, former head of the legislation committee at Egypt's communications ministry, wrote in Al-Ahram that the proposal by parliament's legislative committee to defer the new Criminal Procedure Law by a year reflects missing impact assessment. He argues the extra year should address the legal standing of electronic notification and remote trials, court and prison infrastructure, and training.

2026-10-01-egypts-ipn-records-147-bln-tr.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt's governor, Hassan Abdalla, told the Council of Arab Central Banks in Abu Dhabi on 29 September 2026 that Egypt's Instant Payment Network had recorded 1.47 billion transactions worth about EGP 4.33tn by the end of the second quarter of 2026, with about 22 million registered customers. The report does not say whether the figures cover the quarter or the network's life to date.

2026-10-01-eth-ena-web-eng-w-eng-9654453.summary: Ethiopia recorded digital financial transactions worth 33 trillion birr in the 2025/26 fiscal year, Gemechis Dugasa, regulation and licensing director at the National Bank of Ethiopia, told the Ethiopia Finance Forum on 30 September 2026. He linked the growth to mobile money and digital banking and called for stronger cybersecurity, data protection and governance.

2026-10-01-ethswitch-unveils-unified-gov.summary: Ethiopia's national payment switch presented a unified government payment platform at the Ethiopia Finance Forum. It would give government bill payments one interoperable route across mobile apps, ATMs, USSD, branches and agents.

2026-10-01-gabonreview-gabon-ai-strategy.summary: Preparatory work for Gabon's national AI strategy closed in Libreville on 30 September with 22 challenges and 36 recommendations from six working groups supported by UNDP. The ministry and UNDP will now draft the strategy, its action plan and financing for government validation.

2026-10-01-gabonreview-gabon-data-govern.summary: Gabon's data protection authority took part in a study visit on personal-data governance in Dakar on 7 to 10 September, run by the African Union's development agency with German cooperation. Participants cited the Gabonese authority's funding model as a reference.

2026-10-01-gates-foundation-ken-2026-ibr.summary: The Gates Foundation committed US$50,000 in October 2026 to the World Bank's lending arm. The nine-month grant supports Kenya in drafting open-finance policy and guidance on data sharing, consumer protection and inclusive access to financial services.

2026-10-01-gates-foundation-xaf-2026-cen.summary: The Gates Foundation committed US$1,285,123 in October 2026 to Cenfri in Cape Town. The grant runs over 36 months. It funds a tool for central banks and financial providers that identifies arbitrage transactions. The aim is to improve the measurement of digital merchant payments and the accuracy of credit scores.

2026-10-01-gha-bog-to-strengthen-fraud-c.summary: The Bank of Ghana said on 1 October 2026 that it is building a fraud intelligence hub for financial institutions to share emerging fraud patterns, and has revised its Cyber and Information Security Directive for AI, cloud and data-security risks. Its information security director put mobile money flows above GH¢40 billion in June 2026.

2026-10-01-gha-myjoyonline-csa-no-digita.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority opened the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month on securing digital finance. Its director-general asked banks, telecoms operators, fintechs and regulators to share threat intelligence quickly enough to stop attacks before losses occur.

2026-10-01-gin-wardip-ami-scheme-nationa.summary: Guinea's WARDIP project, under the digital economy ministry, invited expressions of interest on 1 October 2026, due by 23 October, from firms to design and implement a national payment scheme. The nine-month assignment supports the national switch GuiM and the central bank, BCRG, on governance, rules, security and a business model through to a pilot. It is paid from a US$60 million IDA financing.

2026-10-01-iati-xm-dac-47066-da0113-stre.summary: IOM committed US$300,000 from its Development Fund on 1 October 2026 to a project on migration data governance in Malawi, running to September 2028. It supports the National Statistical Office and other government bodies. Planned outputs are a technical working group, a governance framework, common administrative data standards and a compendium of migration indicators.

2026-10-01-independentnews-minister-sava.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister launched National Cybersecurity Awareness Month and said a review of the National Cybersecurity Strategy has begun. The Director of Public Prosecutions said her office has set up a Cybercrime Unit and trained prosecutors on the 2022 cybercrime Act.

2026-10-01-internet-society-fair-share-p.summary: An Internet Society paper argues that proposals to make large content providers pay telecoms operators for carrying traffic would raise costs, weaken local traffic exchange and increase market concentration in Africa.

2026-10-01-ken-2026-27-q1-cyber-security.summary: The 43rd edition covers July to September 2026. It records more than 2.6 billion threat events, up 14.45%, mainly exploitation of vulnerabilities, and over 20 million advisories issued.

2026-10-01-ken-duale-grants-one-month-ex.summary: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale extended to 30 October 2026 the deadline for public Level 5 and 6, faith-based and private facilities to move from the Social Health Authority provider portal to hospital management information systems, KBC reported on 1 October 2026. Of 518 contracted faith-based facilities, 38 have moved; the Digital Health Agency will support the rest, and no patient is to be refused care meanwhile.

2026-10-01-ken-revealed-counties-made-sh.summary: Kenya's Controller of Budget reported that county governments paid at least Sh8.3 billion in salaries through manual payrolls outside the Human Resource Information System in the year to 30 June 2026, despite a directive to migrate by June 2025. Nakuru County paid Sh1.86 billion, 21.8% of its personnel costs, manually; Wajir, Nairobi, Siaya and Mandera also had high shares.

2026-10-01-ken-sdsri-draft-national-ai-p.summary: Kenya's State Department for Science, Research and Innovation invited public comment on a draft National AI Policy for Science, Research and Innovation and a draft Science Diplomacy Policy, with a deadline of 14 October 2026. The drafts are posted on the department's website. The notice is undated.

2026-10-01-ken-techcabal-safaricom-pesap.summary: Safaricom and Pesapal put M-PESA tap-to-pay and QR payment on Pesapal's 30,000 point-of-sale terminals in Kenya, with no extra fee. Safaricom says scan-to-pay is live at more than 60,000 merchant outlets and targets 500,000 within a year.

2026-10-01-kenya-advances-digital-public.summary: Kenyan principal secretaries and private-sector leaders discussed the country's digital public infrastructure roadmap at a public sector forum, naming access, trust and interoperability as its three priorities. No document or timetable was published.

2026-10-01-lby-libyaherald-noc-officials.summary: Libya's Attorney General's Office ordered two National Oil Corporation officials, one of them its director of information and digital transformation, into pre-trial detention over leaked oil-sector data. Data on fields, production, reserves and exploration passed to a foreign company contracted in 2023 for a sector study.

2026-10-01-liberian-observer-liberia-ins.summary: Liberia's instant payment system has processed more than 5.3 million transactions between the two mobile money operators since its December 2025 launch, the central bank governor said. About 4.2 million were in Liberian dollars and 1.1 million in US dollars.

2026-10-01-moz-360mz-sadc-real-time-paym.summary: Mozambique plans to join the SADC RTGS regional payment system, hosted by the South African Reserve Bank, in the first quarter of 2027, Banco de Moçambique governor Felisberto Navalha said after the Monetary Policy Committee meeting. Customers would settle South African invoices directly from metical accounts; the system already carries the rand and, since July, Angola's kwanza.

2026-10-01-moz-plano-nacional-geoespacia.summary: Mozambique's energy ministry, MIREME, published the National Geospatial Least-Cost Electrification Plan for 2026-2030 in October 2026. The plan carries a foreword from minister Estevão Pale and sets out how to guide investment in electricity access. The plan was launched at an event on 6 November 2026, covered in the Estevão Pale item.

2026-10-01-mrt-ecofin-mauritania-digital.summary: Mauritania's Ministry of Digital Transformation presented a national digital addressing system in Nouakchott on 29 September 2026, financed by the World Bank under the WARDIP programme. It is to locate every plot and building, divide the country into postal code zones and include mapping and address management portals. A pilot is expected by the end of 2026, but no detailed timetable has been announced.

2026-10-01-mrt-tawassoul-facturation-pai.summary: Mauritania's tax directorate said public establishments must use an electronic platform for invoicing, tax declarations and tax payments from 1 November 2026, reported on 1 October. No invoice may be paid unless first registered and validated on the platform. Training and technical support run through October.

2026-10-01-mwi-mwnation-macra-data-bundl.summary: The Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority opened an investigation, by notice dated 29 September 2026, into complaints that mobile data bundles on TNM and Airtel Malawi run out too fast. It will examine billing systems and usage records and run controlled tests of data used against data deducted, with a deadline of mid-November.

2026-10-01-ncc-launches-zero-rated-data-.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator and the operators' association launched zero-rated access to approved educational platforms, giving eligible learners up to 100MB of free data a day. The association put the industry's commitment at almost N200 billion for an initial pilot of 5,000 learners.

2026-10-01-nga-fmcide-national-digital-a.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry announced on 1 October 2026 that the postal service, NIPOST, has launched a National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System giving every addressable building an 11-character GIS-based postcode. Postcodes can be looked up at postcode.gov.ng, and a NIPOST GIS lab manages the map.

2026-10-01-nga-freedom-on-the-net-2026-n.summary: Freedom House's Freedom on the Net 2026, released in October 2026, rates Nigeria partly free at 56 out of 100. Freedom House cut its score on state control of infrastructure from 6 to 4 over months of disruption in Zamfara State. It also reports an official bid to remove a critic's posts, and DDoS attacks on an investigative outlet.

2026-10-01-nga-sokoto-mide-amadun-alu-2-.summary: The permanent secretary of Nigeria's Sokoto State Ministry of Innovation and Digital Economy describes the state's digital programme in a signed essay. It records the law creating a state ICT development agency, passed in April 2025, and a 10,000-person digital skills programme launched in November 2024. The ministry's 2027 budget proposals seek investment in connectivity, power and skills; no amounts are given.

2026-10-01-nga-von-digital-postcode-syst.summary: The Nigeria Postal Service launched a National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System to improve location identification and access to services, communications minister Bosun Tijani said. He said accurate postcodes would help businesses reach customers, speed emergency assistance and support government service delivery. No cost or coverage figures are given.

2026-10-01-president-tinubu-approves-nat.summary: President Bola Tinubu has approved a renewed National Strategy on Public Service Reforms, the director general of Nigeria's Bureau of Public Service Reforms, Dasuki Arabi, said in Abuja on 30 September 2026. The three-yearly revision will add government policies on AI and blockchain in the public service. No approval date or text was given.

2026-10-01-sdn-alghad-baladna-new-commer.summary: Sudan's Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications added three services to its Baladna platform: company commercial registration, electronic accounts for law firms to manage client records, and remote renewal of lawyers' practising licences. A legal adviser quoted named weak telecoms infrastructure and low uptake by businesses as obstacles. The launch date is not given.

2026-10-01-sen-agenceecofin-wave-rejoint.summary: Mobile money operator Wave Digital Finance appears on the BCEAO's list of participants in its PI-SPI instant payment platform updated on 30 September 2026, authorised to offer the service in Senegal. Wave was absent when the platform launched a year earlier with 45 participants; the list now has 175 across the eight WAEMU states. The central bank had set 30 September 2026 as the connection deadline.

2026-10-01-sen-aps-bourses-securite-fami.summary: Senegal has resumed its family security cash grants after a two-year interruption, paying CFA140,000 per household for 2026 through mobile-money operators. The number of beneficiaries was increased, but the new total was not given.

2026-10-01-sen-seneweb-new-deal-technolo.summary: A delegation from Senegal's telecoms and digital ministry visited SunuCorp's computer assembly plant at Keur Ndiaye Lo on 1 October 2026 under Sénégal Digital Factory, part of the New Deal Technologique, which pools state equipment purchases for local assemblers. The ministry cites 97% 4G coverage but 54% of people without devices; the plant can make about 7,500 computers a year.

2026-10-01-soff-investment-phase-pipelin.summary: Djibouti's weather agency asks SOFF for US$2.01m for 2027 to 2031. Neither of its two required stations meets the global standard. The airport surface station is to be upgraded. A disused upper-air station is to be rebuilt.

2026-10-01-som-hiiraan-nira-id-flights-p.summary: Somalia's federal government began enforcing a requirement on 1 October 2026 that domestic travellers carry the NIRA national identity card. Passengers at Garowe in Puntland, where the identification authority has no registration offices and the card is not issued, were refused boarding on flights to Mogadishu and Nairobi.

2026-10-01-ssd-radioyei-eaco-working-gro.summary: An East African Communications Organisation working group, meeting in Juba, finalised frameworks for rapid cyber-threat response among national response teams. It also produced guidelines for users of digital financial services, child online protection measures and mobile data quality standards.

2026-10-01-swz-2026-esccom-annual-report.summary: The Eswatini Communications Commission has published its 2026 annual report. It covers telecoms and postal market performance, quality of service, spectrum management and the regulator's work on data protection and cybersecurity rules.

2026-10-01-syc-decisions-from-the-courts.summary: The Judiciary of Seychelles keeps a public list of decisions of the Court of Appeal, Constitutional Court and Supreme Court. The page in October 2026 lists 2026 Constitutional Court judgments in the Valabhji cases, the latest dated 25 June 2026, and Supreme Court criminal bail rulings from January 2026. Each case name links to the decision.

2026-10-01-tcd-visasnews-e-visa-platform.summary: Chad's National Police said on 1 October 2026 that its e-Visa platform receives more than 100 applications a day, against fewer than 10 at its launch on 11 December 2024. Express applications take 24 to 72 hours and standard ones 10 to 15 days. The e-Visa has been mandatory since 11 May 2026, and visas for all African nationals are to be waived from 1 January 2027.

2026-10-01-tgo-actutogo-maeciate-16-dema.summary: Togo's foreign ministry put 10 administrative procedures and six consular services online from 1 October 2026, through the national digital procedures portal and a consular portal that holds a register of Togolese abroad. Consular services include document legalisation, consular cards, birth and marriage certificates and laissez-passer; the work began on 31 March 2026 under the public administration digitalisation programme.

2026-10-01-tun-lechotunisien-int-baromet.summary: Tunisia's telecoms regulator, the Instance Nationale des Télécommunications, puts the national internet access rate at 85.9% in its latest ICT use barometer, reported on 1 October 2026. Use is 99.2% among 18–24 year-olds and 54.1% among 60–70 year-olds, and ranges from 69.1% in the lowest-income households to 95.9% in the highest. The barometer's fieldwork date is not given.

2026-10-01-tza-thecitizen-pdmis-disabili.summary: Tanzania's Prime Minister's Office said its Persons with Disabilities Management Information System is linked to 11 government systems, including student, health and loan systems. Officials said it will match employer reports against the national disability register to check the 3% hiring quota for employers with 20 or more staff.

2026-10-01-uga-annual-communications-sec.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission published its communications sector report for 2025 in October 2026. It puts addressable mobile penetration at 73.7% and the gender parity index for mobile internet at 0.82. It reports 53 of 64 subsidised towers live and 62,941 km of fibre.

2026-10-01-uga-news-nira-to-register-lea.summary: Uganda's National Identification and Registration Authority announced on 1 October 2026 a nationwide exercise in December, run at local council level, to register schoolchildren without National Identification Numbers and correct errors in identity records. At the same event the national IT authority said its UGHub links NIRA's register to more than 150 government bodies, banks and telecoms for real-time verification.

2026-10-01-uga-nilepost-ucu-privacy-moot.summary: Uganda Christian University won a regional privacy moot court competition for law students from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. The ICT minister told the students that innovation must not undermine privacy and data protection.

2026-10-01-uga-uganda-public-procurement.summary: The Open Contracting Partnership's registry lists Uganda's PPDA procurement data, published monthly from July 2015 to October 2026 under ODC-By. As retrieved on 24 October 2026, it held 71,639 tenders and 142,168 contracts from 210 enrolled entities. A December 2022 review found inconsistent organisation identifiers and some filler dates.

2026-10-01-xaf-afriscience-mt-decolonizi.summary: An EMNLP 2026 paper introduces AfriScience-MT, a parallel corpus of plain-language science summaries professionally translated into Amharic, Hausa, Luganda, Northern Sotho, Yoruba and isiZulu across 11 domains, with new terms coined where none existed. In its benchmarks closed-source models outperformed every open-source model.

2026-10-01-xaf-airtel-africa-airtel-mone.summary: Airtel Africa's regulatory announcement gives the terms of the Airtel Money offer: existing shareholders sell 270 million shares, with up to 27 million more under an over-allotment option, leaving about 16.5% of the company in public hands. Airtel Africa sells only through the over-allotment option.

2026-10-01-xaf-techcabal-kora-adds-stabl.summary: The Nigerian-founded payments company Kora launched One Rail, which lets merchants accept, convert and settle the dollar stablecoins USDT and USDC through its existing network. It is rolling out market by market.

2026-10-01-xaf-techcabal-space-data-cent.summary: Satlyt, a space-technology startup with its African headquarters in Nairobi, raised US$8 million in seed funding. Its software runs data processing and AI applications on the computers aboard other operators' satellites.

2026-10-01-xaf-techreviewafrica-atu-sg-s.summary: The African Telecommunications Union's secretary general told the 42nd meeting of the International Telecommunications Satellite Organization in Washington that satellite resources remain central to connectivity in Africa.

2026-10-01-xea-comesa-idea-half-year-pro.summary: COMESA's half-year progress report on the World Bank-financed Inclusive Digitalisation in Eastern and Southern Africa programme, a US$2.48 billion envelope, covers January to June 2026 in Angola, the DRC, Malawi, Zambia and Eswatini. The COMESA secretariat had spent 9% of its US$3.71 million 2026 budget by June, and moved its AI and regional digital inclusion consultancies from procurement to implementation.

2026-10-01-xgl-bcg-ai-maturity-matrix-20.summary: The October 2026 report rates more than 75 economies on 33 indicators of exposure to AI and readiness for it. Eleven African economies are rated, and Nigeria moves up to a higher readiness group.

2026-10-01-xss-world-bank-africa-economi.summary: The World Bank's Africa Economic Update for October 2026 focuses on readiness for artificial intelligence. It puts Sub-Saharan Africa's share of global data-centre capacity at 0.6%, counts 39 countries with data-protection laws, and scores the region at 41.6 on AI governance against 52.6 globally. It forecasts 2026 growth of 4.3%.

2026-10-01-zaf-citizen-gauteng-e-panic-b.summary: The Gauteng legislature's e-government committee rejected the provincial department's assurance that no personal information was compromised by the e-Panic Button exposure, and gave it seven days to report. It wants an incident timeline, proof of notification to the Information Regulator and residents, and the contract's data-protection clauses.

2026-10-01-zaf-citizen-green-id-book-end.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said production of the green ID book will end on 31 March 2027. He showed the first working digital identity credential and put smart ID replacements at more than 515 bank branches and 822,000 users.

2026-10-01-zaf-icasa-media-release-withd.summary: South Africa's communications regulator, ICASA, withdrew on 1 October 2026 its notices launching inquiries into telecommunications affordability and the impact of over-the-top services, citing administrative and procedural matters. The affordability notice will be republished with a draft questionnaire and the OTT notice later; earlier submissions can be resubmitted.

2026-10-01-zaf-usaasa-gn-7985-discussion.summary: The Universal Service and Access Agency of South Africa published a discussion document on universal access and universal service in the Government Gazette on 1 October 2026, reviewing the 2010 determination. It sets out three options and favours a targeted revision; comments close on 30 October 2026.

2026-10-01-zmb-itweb-zamportal-revenue-c.summary: Zambia's finance minister said the national services portal has collected about K9.8 billion across 572 services and 52 providers since 2019. The 2027-2029 budget call circular names the Government Service Bus and payment gateway as the state's centralised revenue-collection system.

2026-10-01-zwe-econet-infraco-interim-re.summary: Econet InfraCo, the tower, power and property arm of Econet Wireless Zimbabwe listed on the Victoria Falls Stock Exchange, reported unaudited revenue of US$70.1 million and profit of US$13.7 million for the six months to 31 August 2026, with no interim dividend. It said solar power and AI-based fuel management cut fuel use by 30%, and construction began on a planned 100MW solar farm.

2026-10-02-africa-needs-to-take-charge-o.summary: Rwanda's Minister of State for ICT and Innovation Yves Iradukunda told the Africa HealthTech Summit in Kigali on 1 October 2026 that reliance on external funding and procurement leaves health systems vulnerable, and called for aligned data-exchange policies across Africa. He set out Rwanda's data governance roles: the statistics institute as custodian, the ICT ministry for policy and the Rwanda Information Society Authority for platforms.

2026-10-02-ago-nova-lei-da-ciberseguranc.summary: Angola's cybersecurity law has been published as Lei n.º 9/26 of 28 September and is in force, revoking the 2017 law. Operators of critical infrastructure, essential services, electronic communications, data centres and cloud services must register with the National Cybersecurity Centre within 180 days, set up incident response teams and notify significant incidents to CERT.ao.

2026-10-02-ben-certificats-de-perte-deli.summary: Benin's Republican Police moved loss certificates fully online from 1 October 2026, under a service note signed that day by Director General Kokou Brice Allowanou. Certificates are now issued only through the CDSP platform at certificatdeperte.bj, with electronic payment, and police stations no longer issue them on paper.

2026-10-02-ben-haac-89-medias-en-ligne-c.summary: Benin's media regulator HAAC signed conventions with 89 online media outlets in Cotonou on 1 October 2026, completing its authorisation process for websites offering online audiovisual and written-press services. The outlets now operate under the information and communication code and the digital code.

2026-10-02-burundi-sim-registration-scam.summary: Burundi's mandatory SIM and eSIM registration, begun in mid-June, was about 70 per cent complete on the regulator's count. Users report long queues, few service points and slow systems, and scams continue; operators must keep customer data for at least five years.

2026-10-02-ccima-certificat-origine-elec.summary: Cameroon's chamber of commerce (CCIMA) trained its staff and trade bodies in Douala on 29 September 2026, with China's embassy and customs administration, on China's electronic platform for preferential certificates of origin. Exporters apply online, the chamber issues the certificate and it is sent to Chinese customs, a condition of the zero-duty access China has granted 53 African states since 1 May 2026.

2026-10-02-com-alwatwan-ram-diagnostic-i.summary: Comoros presented its UNESCO AI readiness assessment, RAM 2.0, prepared with UNESCO and Japan, at the fourth forum on AI ethics in Riyadh on 14–17 September 2026. It places the country at an emerging stage, with no national AI strategy, no AI-specific law and no independent ethics body, and makes 23 recommendations to 2030.

2026-10-02-ecofin-cemac-beac-money-marke.summary: The Bank of Central African States (BEAC) published an international tender on 30 September 2026 for a single platform to run the CEMAC money market and the Single Central Depository for securities. The tender does not disclose the platform's settlement or processing features, and no budget is given.

2026-10-02-egy-alpheratz-bayanat-al-misr.summary: An Al-Pheratz investigation found no documented construction start, operating licence or Egyptian operator for the Benya–Khazna data centre at Maadi. The project was announced in May 2023 at 25 MW and over US$250m. The reporter traced the partners to a holding company registered in the Abu Dhabi Global Market.

2026-10-02-gabon-validation-digital-tran.summary: Gabon began a validation review of draft legal texts for digital transformation at Nkok on 1 October, to run about ten days. The texts cover digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, digital services and the institutional framework, under the World Bank-financed Gabon Digital programme.

2026-10-02-gha-mtn-ghana-gse-notice-spec.summary: MTN Ghana (Scancom PLC) told the Ghana Stock Exchange on 2 October 2026 that the National Communications Authority had notified it of 15-year spectrum awards: 2 x 20 MHz in the 700 MHz band for US$100.9 million and 150 MHz in the 3 GHz band for US$101.1 million. The company said it will use the spectrum for 5G once the licences are issued.

2026-10-02-ghana-public-sector-ai-procur.summary: Ghana's communications minister announced that every AI system bought by a public institution will go through a centralised technical review. The national information technology agency will scope deployments against interoperability, data-protection, cybersecurity and local skills-transfer requirements, alongside procurement law.

2026-10-02-icasa-withdraws-affordability.summary: South Africa's communications regulator withdrew the notices for its telecommunications affordability inquiry and its inquiry into over-the-top services, citing administrative and procedural matters. The affordability notice is to be republished with a draft questionnaire and the other at a later date; those who have commented may resubmit.

2026-10-02-itweb-sa-eta-machine-learning.summary: South Africa's home affairs department said its Electronic Travel Authorisation uses machine learning to make automated, risk-based decisions on short-stay visa applications, with a human brought in where the system flags an anomaly. The system is live at four airports.

2026-10-02-ken-why-sha-is-shifting-hospi.summary: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale said hospitals are being moved from the Social Health Authority provider portal to their own management information systems because running both created duplicate work and longer waits, The Standard reported on 2 October 2026. All 6,427 public Level 2 to 4 facilities have moved, four of the Level 5 hospitals have migrated, and the Digital Health Agency has certified 28 private systems; the deadline is 30 October.

2026-10-02-lbr-liberia-advances-developm.summary: Liberia's education ministry closed a two-day consultation on 28 and 29 September on a policy for its education management information system, supported by the African Union. The policy covers how education data is collected, secured, shared and used.

2026-10-02-mar-digital-payment-the-faile.summary: TelQuel reports that Moroccan social assistance paid into payment accounts is withdrawn as cash within hours. Currency in circulation reached 540 billion dirhams by July 2026. In 2024, withdrawals made up 68% of card transactions, and merchants took 8% of wallet transactions.

2026-10-02-mdg-ecofin-4g-coverage-intern.summary: Madagascar's bill on electronic communications and digital infrastructure, submitted on 28 August, still waits for examination by the National Assembly. The article sets it against a market where 4G covers about 80 per cent of the population while mobile internet use stays low.

2026-10-02-meta-a-maurice-securite-en-li.summary: A Meta team is due in Mauritius on 6 and 7 October 2026 for meetings on moderating content in Mauritian Creole, child protection online, identity verification, faster takedowns and whether platforms should have a local presence. Mauritius' ICT ministry and Meta will also discuss a framework agreement on online safety.

2026-10-02-moz-aim-uem-directrizes-ia.summary: Mozambique's Universidade Eduardo Mondlane has approved a directive on the responsible and transparent use of AI in teaching, research and administration. It was presented at a workshop on 30 September and 1 October that also shared a draft institutional AI roadmap.

2026-10-02-moz-clubofmozambique-parliame.summary: Mozambique's parliamentary Standing Commission on 1 October 2026 placed a Personal Data Protection draft law among 35 initial agenda items for the Assembly of the Republic's fourth ordinary session, opening on 28 October. The agenda also includes a framework law on public administration and revisions to the customs and tax procedure codes.

2026-10-02-moz-oam-destaca-importancia-d.summary: The Mozambique Bar Association (OAM) welcomed the Supreme Court's launch of a legislation portal and a case-law portal, in a statement of 2 October 2026. Its president, Thera Tobias Dai, attended the public presentation. The association called the portals a step in modernising justice and widening access to legal information, and said they help lawyers consult the law.

2026-10-02-mus-defimedia-maupass-korek-a.summary: Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency staff will help citizens register on MauPass and reach their digital driving licence in the KOREK app from the coming week. The 883,700 licence holders have three months before the digital licence takes legal effect on 1 January 2027.

2026-10-02-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet agreed on 2 October 2026 to regulations allowing traffic fines without penalty points to be paid online from 30 October, through the Supreme Court portal with MauPass login and MauCAS QR or card payment. It also noted a Meta visit on 6–7 October on platform representation, take-down requests and age assurance, and Statistics Mauritius's rebasing of GDP to 2023, which adds about Rs58 billion.

2026-10-02-nam-iafrica-national-ai-insti.summary: Namibia's research commission opened a National Artificial Intelligence Institute on 23 September with four centres, for datasets, research and development, software development and AI innovation. Each answers a gap named in the country's 2025 AI readiness assessment; that assessment's other findings, including no AI regulatory framework, are not addressed by the institute.

2026-10-02-nam-nampa-fnb-judiciary-court.summary: First National Bank of Namibia handed 42 card payment devices to the Office of the Judiciary on 30 September, so that court-related payments at Magistrates' Courts can be made electronically.

2026-10-02-ner-actuniger-soniloga-airtel.summary: The operator of Niger's vehicle one-stop shop began accepting Airtel Money for some of its services on 1 October, through an app or an offline USSD code. The transport ministry presented it as a way to trace public revenue.

2026-10-02-nga-gtco-h1-2026-investor-pre.summary: Guaranty Trust Holding Company's investor presentation for the half-year to June 2026 reports transactions through its GTWorld mobile app of ₦26.70 trillion, up from ₦21.87 trillion a year earlier. Pay-with-Transfer value rose to ₦1.11 trillion from ₦70.05 billion. The deck carries no date of its own.

2026-10-02-nga-nairametrics-digital-post.summary: Nigeria's National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System, launched through the Nigerian Postal Service on 1 October 2026, gives buildings an 11-character code. Early users reported accurate locations but also duplicate codes, missing houses and no coverage in one Oyo State town, reported on 2 October. NIPOST said corrections would be made within 48 hours.

2026-10-02-nga-thecable-nipost-postcode-.summary: The Nigerian Postal Service launched a national digital postcode system on 1 October 2026, assigning an 11-character code to each addressable building. TheCable reported the next day that the system's app shows homeowners' names against building postcodes and lets users search for an address by a person's name. The report carries no response from NIPOST or the data protection regulator.

2026-10-02-nigeria-digital-postcode-syst.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry asked businesses and developers to build services on the new national digital postcode system. An API is open to organisations that pass business verification, with testing alongside the postal service before production access.

2026-10-02-nigeria-tiktok-disruption-cso.summary: Twelve Nigerian civil-society groups asked for an investigation into disruptions to TikTok access in Kaduna, Kebbi, Kano and Sokoto, first reported around 14 September. They asked the communications regulator to facilitate independent network testing and said their findings do not establish a government-ordered block.

2026-10-02-paradigm-joint-statement-tikt.summary: Nigerian civil society groups including Paradigm Initiative, Media Rights Agenda, CJID and Accountability Lab said on 2 October 2026 that TikTok access in Kaduna, Kebbi, Kano and Sokoto had been disrupted since about 14 September, with no public explanation. They asked the Nigerian Communications Commission and other agencies to investigate and publish findings, to disclose any government directive and its legal basis, and to allow independent network testing.

2026-10-02-permis-de-conduire-digitalise.summary: Rengus Digital, which runs Gabon's digitised driving licence launched on 24 March 2026, has moved the system onto Gabon Poste's infrastructure under a new agreement. Hosting capacity rises from about 1 terabyte at launch to about 10, after enrolment and issuing delays. The postal network is to support a rollout beyond Libreville, for which no dates are given.

2026-10-02-plateforme-numerique-proxigab.summary: Gabon's digital infrastructure agency ANINF presented PROXIGAB, a free online platform linking small businesses with investors, suppliers and incubators, at its Libreville headquarters on 2 October 2026, before the commerce and digital economy ministers. ANINF signed a minute handing the platform to the directorate-general of SMEs. It is open to formal and informal operators and individuals.

2026-10-02-regional-sciencenigeria-afric.summary: Africa CDC said more than 150 internet devices, including Starlink systems, have been deployed to Ebola-affected health zones in the Democratic Republic of Congo to replace paper-based reporting, with 142 more due within two weeks and 600 being procured. Outbreak data run on DHIS2, and a second response plan mobilises 71,000 community health workers.

2026-10-02-rwa-ktpress-mastercard-founda.summary: Eight Rwandan education-technology companies are in the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship, an 18-month acceleration programme launched in June 2026 and run through the Rwanda ICT Chamber. Their products range from identifying learners at risk of dropping out to robotics for schools with few resources.

2026-10-02-sdn-ssmo-iso-annual-meeting-p.summary: Sudan News Agency reported on 2 October 2026 that the Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organisation attended the 48th ISO General Assembly in Paris. The meeting ran from 28 September to 2 October 2026. The organisation's director general led a delegation that included its head of international relations.

2026-10-02-sen-techafricanews-stellarix-.summary: STELLARIX Senegal, part of the AXIAN Group, said it has expanded its data-centre capacity in Senegal for cloud, AI and hosting demand. It named three contractors and gave no capacity or cost figure.

2026-10-02-seychelles-tourism-ai-data.summary: Seychelles' tourism minister Amanda Bernstein told the Seychelles Tourism Forum on 1 October 2026 that the country plans to use AI and real-time data to forecast pressures from tourism, with attention to small locally owned businesses. The forum presented Lazio HRM, a tourism workforce platform built for the tourism department by Cloudbay Solutions.

2026-10-02-soff-investment-phase-pipelin.summary: A World Bank-led request asks SOFF for US$3.3m for 2027 to 2031. It rebuilds the surface and upper-air stations at Mahé airport. It also restores the automatic stations on the outer islands. An upper-air station on Aldabra waits for a second phase.

2026-10-02-syc-27-civil-servants-head-to.summary: A second cohort of 27 Seychelles civil servants was sent off at the Indian High Commission ahead of a two-week executive course in Delhi and Mussoorie from 5 to 16 October, focused on technology and its use in governance. The rest of the article is behind a paywall.

2026-10-02-tun-tunisienumerique-pacte-na.summary: Tunisia's health and communication technologies ministers signed a National Health Pact on 1 October to speed universal health coverage through digital transformation. Its six axes include sovereign governance of health data, modernised digital platforms and medicine supply-chain security; it is backed by the World Bank and WHO.

2026-10-02-tza-dailynews-who-protects-yo.summary: A Daily News feature sets out how personal data is collected across Tanzania's identity, health and financial services as the country implements its Dira 2050 development vision. It describes the role of the Personal Data Protection Commission in protecting that information.

2026-10-02-tza-mwananchi-sh5-bilioni-kam.summary: Tanzania's ICT minister, Angellah Kairuki, launched a TZS 5bn loan programme for youth-owned ICT start-ups in Dodoma on 2 October 2026, run with Azania Bank. Loans come in three tiers from TZS 1m to TZS 100m, and applicants register on the Jamii Hunt system.

2026-10-02-xaf-gsma-undp-partner-african.summary: UNDP and the GSMA announced a partnership to support African-led AI, including AI in African languages. Through UNDP's timbuktoo initiative they will work on access to compute for priority AI pilots and on connecting African talent to applied AI work.

2026-10-02-xwa-bceao-communique-pi-spi-e.summary: The West African central bank BCEAO revised fees for person-to-person e-money transfers on its instant payment platform PI-SPI from 2 November 2026. National transfers up to FCFA 8,000 a day are free, larger ones may cost up to 0.8%, and receiving is free; cross-border transfers within WAEMU get the same terms from 1 June 2027. PI-SPI has 175 connected participants.

2026-10-02-xwa-bceao-uemoa-council-commu.summary: The WAEMU Council of Ministers, meeting in Dakar on 2 October 2026, gave a favourable opinion on the BCEAO and the union's commercial banks joining PAPSS, the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System.

2026-10-02-xwa-bceao-uemoa-council-of-mi.summary: The WAEMU Council of Ministers, meeting in Dakar on 2 October 2026, gave an opinion on the participation of the BCEAO and the union's commercial banks in the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS); the communiqué does not say what the opinion was. The council also adopted a public procurement directive and a 2026-2035 regional social protection strategy.

2026-10-02-zaf-biometricupdate-digital-i.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said a working prototype of the smartphone-based digital ID has been built and demonstrated his own credential. A pilot and wider rollout are being prepared, with no public release date.

2026-10-02-zaf-citizen-tshwane-data-plat.summary: South Africa's City of Tshwane launched an Enterprise Data and Analytics Platform with the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) to support its Service Delivery War Room. It follows a memorandum of understanding signed in June 2023 and a collaboration agreement of August 2026 covering July 2026 to June 2028, during which the platform is to extend to all seven regions. No cost is given.

2026-10-02-zaf-ncc-draft-opt-out-registr.summary: South Africa's National Consumer Commission published draft guidelines on compliance with the opt-out registry regulations on 2 October 2026 (GN 7981), inviting comment within 15 days. Every direct marketer must register on the registry, renew annually and check its contact list against it each month it markets, at 12 cents per blocked entry.

2026-10-02-zaf-polity-schreiber-home-aff.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber announced at Constitution Hill on 1 October 2026 that the department will stop producing the green ID book by 31 March 2027, and that it will cease to be valid identification on 31 March 2028. The 14.7 million people who hold only a green ID book will have 12 months after production ends to switch to the Smart ID card.

2026-10-02-zmb-techreviewafrica-auc-zamb.summary: The African Union's infrastructure commissioner and Zambia's ambassador to the United Nations discussed implementing the Global Digital Compact in New York. They covered regional approaches to compute, including GPU capacity for each of Africa's five regions and a proposed SADC data centre.

2026-10-02-zwe-herald-cyber-strong-zimba.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT ministry said it is still advancing the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030, which would set up a National Cybersecurity Authority and a stronger national incident response team. The statement came at the launch of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

2026-10-03-africa-cdc-official-continent.summary: The head of digital health at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said most health AI models presented to her are hosted on a foreign cloud, because the continent lacks the infrastructure to run them. The agency is drafting a continental health data governance framework with more than 40 member states, setting who may access health data, for what purpose and for how long.

2026-10-03-ai-policy-gets-a-second-chanc.summary: South Africa's deputy communications minister, Mondli Gungubele, said the redrafted national AI policy goes to the minister before the end of November 2026 and to cabinet by the end of the 2026/27 financial year. The earlier draft, released this year, was withdrawn after it was found to contain AI-generated, invented citations.

2026-10-03-banks-baulk-at-a-bill-from-pu.summary: FaydaVerse, the new state enterprise running Ethiopia's Fayda digital ID, has begun charging banks for identity checks they once got free: 10 to 20 birr per KYC record retrieval and 20 to 40 birr per biometric authentication, by volume. Its contract bars banks from passing the cost to customers and bills failed attempts; the Ethiopian Bankers Association has asked for a joint consultation with the central bank.

2026-10-03-ben-beninwebtv-cnin-trois-poi.summary: Benin's National Centre for Digital Investigations, CNIN, which reports to the Presidency, opened three complaint desks outside Cotonou, in police premises at Porto-Novo, Abomey and Parakou. They take complaints about personal data breaches and digital offences, alongside the Cotonou office and the existing email route.

2026-10-03-ben-gouv-preuve-de-vie-biomet.summary: Benin's Ministry of Economy and Finance announced on 3 October 2026 that pensioners can complete their annual proof of life from a smartphone. After identifying with their personal identification number (NPI) and pension booklet number, they verify their fingerprints in an app and receive confirmation by SMS or email. Biometric kiosks in some public places offer an alternative.

2026-10-03-ben-gouv-semo-plus-preuve-de-.summary: Benin's government announced on 3 October 2026 that public servants on official missions now prove their presence through the SEMO+ mobile app. They log in with their personal identification number, select the mission, share their location and confirm by fingerprint; biometric kiosks in some public places offer an alternative.

2026-10-03-bfa-jeppc-2026-le-ministre-sa.summary: Burkina Faso's security minister, Mahamadou Sana, presented his ministry's record for 2022–2026 at a government exhibition on 2 October 2026. Alongside recruitment and new specialised units, he cited digitised police occurrence records, regional offices of the anti-cybercrime unit and electronic traffic fines. He put the ratio of officers to population at one per 537 people in June 2026.

2026-10-03-bungoma-id-registration-hampe.summary: Kenya's National Assembly committee on administration and internal security inspected registration offices in Bungoma County on 2 October 2026 and heard that ID and civil registration are held back by shortages of staff, vehicles, equipment and office space. The county has two ageing vehicles. It recorded 19,361 registrations between July and September 2026.

2026-10-03-cab-corridor-la-spin-et-camte.summary: Gabon's digital infrastructure holding SPIN and Cameroon's operator CAMTEL have signed a memorandum of understanding and a confidentiality agreement on CAB-CORRIDOR, a terrestrial link between Cameroon, Gabon and the Republic of Congo over the Central African Backbone, SPIN said on 3 October 2026. Implementation terms are expected in October 2026; signing dates are not given.

2026-10-03-caf-icasees-retraite-apuremen.summary: The Central African Republic's statistics institute ICASEES held a retreat in Boali from 2 to 5 October 2026 to clean, quality-check and tabulate data from the fourth general population and housing census (RGPH-4), following a review of provisional results by the census technical committee on 23 to 25 September. More than 40 demographers, statisticians and programmers worked on inconsistencies, outliers, non-response and imputation rules, coded in Stata, SPSS and CSPro, with attention to variables on employment, occupation, income and ethnicity.

2026-10-03-cod-ap-ofac-bank-of-kigali-ci.summary: A Congolese civic platform has asked the United States Treasury's sanctions office to examine Bank of Kigali's direct participation in China's cross-border renminbi payment system, signed on 8 September. It argues the channel could be used to get round American sanctions on the Rwandan army and on networks trading Congolese minerals.

2026-10-03-cod-frpc-droit-acces-informat.summary: A federation of community radio stations held a press meeting in the Democratic Republic of Congo on the access-to-information bill, declared admissible by the National Assembly in March. The government spokesman said finishing the law is among the government's priorities; no date for a vote was given.

2026-10-03-cod-rdc-lannuaire-statistique.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's education ministry put its school statistics yearbook for 2023-2024 online on 3 October 2026, after validating it on 5 June 2026. It covers schools, classes, pupils, teachers, staff and infrastructure for pre-primary, primary and secondary education, and applies only to that school year.

2026-10-03-egypt-telecom-industry-commit.summary: Egypt's communications minister, Raafat Hendy, met the regulator NTRA's reconstituted Telecom Industry Committee, which recommended expanding local manufacture of telecoms equipment and studying data-centre and cloud development. Hendy said Digital Egypt offers about 250 services, with 270 targeted by end-2026. NTRA said the biometric digital identity system is in trial with the four mobile operators.

2026-10-03-eth-reporter-digital-transact.summary: An assessment of Ethiopia's second financial inclusion strategy found adult account ownership at 66 per cent in 2025 against a 70 per cent target, with some banks charging up to 11 per cent for transfers to mobile wallets. Only 29.56 per cent of 157.6 million mobile money accounts were active in June 2026; a third strategy, for 2026 to 2030, was launched alongside it.

2026-10-03-gha-lbr-ghanaguardian-bog-cbl.summary: A Central Bank of Liberia delegation led by Executive Governor Henry Saamoi visited the Bank of Ghana in Accra on 1 October 2026 to learn how Ghana set up its interbank payment and settlement system, GhIPSS, to inform Liberia's own payment-systems work. The visit falls under a capacity-building memorandum the two central banks signed earlier in 2026.

2026-10-03-gha-myjoyonline-mtn-ghana-5g-.summary: MTN Ghana says it will roll out 5G once the regulator issues the spectrum licences it has been awarded in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands, at a cost of about US$202 million. The company told investors the payments are already in its cash-flow outlook.

2026-10-03-lptic-subsidiary-reviews-prog.summary: Al-Bunya Investment and Services Company, a subsidiary of Libya's state telecoms holding company LPTIC, discussed its project for 7,000 telecommunications towers at its general assembly, reported on 3 October 2026. The company says the project aims to cut infrastructure operating costs, diversify revenue and use engineers from LPTIC's own companies. No progress figures, cost or timetable are given.

2026-10-03-mdg-lexpress-inclusion-financ.summary: Madagascar's Mvola has made merchant payments free for customers, with the merchant bearing the fee. The mobile money operator reports close to 4 million users, more than 60,000 cashpoints and more than 50,000 merchants accepting payment.

2026-10-03-nam-technews-cran-appoints-na.summary: Cornelia Shipindo became Executive of the Namibia Cyber Security Incident Response Team on 1 October 2026, the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia, which houses the team, announced. She will lead national incident response, threat preparedness and protection of critical information infrastructure.

2026-10-03-new-sha-payment-system-why-ho.summary: Kenya's health secretary, Aden Duale, met private hospital owners on 2 October 2026 over the forced move from the Savannah Informatics-run Social Health Authority claims portal to certified hospital information systems bought from accredited vendors. Owners put the cost at up to Sh1 million a year; the ministry extended the deadline to 30 October and agreed a facility-by-facility transition plan.

2026-10-03-nga-spaceinafrica-digital-pos.summary: The Nigerian Postal Service switched on the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode on 1 October 2026, giving each captured building an 11-character code from state down to building. Space in Africa describes how it was built from satellite imagery, a field campaign with Milsat and 25,000 agents, and GIS processing. The outlet's own trace found the lookup hosted on Amazon Web Services in the US.

2026-10-03-nga-techtv-ixpn-at-20-interne.summary: The Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria, founded in 2006, is marking its 20th anniversary with a month-long programme; it says more than 130 networks use it, with points of presence in Lagos data centres, Abuja and Enugu. The programme includes a visit scheme for about 100 students, an IPv6 training programme with AFRINIC and the Nigeria IPv6 Council, and an awards dinner in Lagos on 30 October 2026.

2026-10-03-permis-de-conduire-numerique-.summary: Mauritius's digital driving licence takes legal effect on 1 January 2027, after a transition period that began on 29 September. A driver may show either the digital licence on the KOREK app or the original physical licence, and the ICT minister said 500,000 people have registered on MauPass, the account needed to reach it.

2026-10-03-tgo-republicoftogo-srmt-2027-.summary: Togo's medium-term revenue mobilisation strategy for 2027–2031 allocates nearly FCFA 6 billion of its FCFA 10.5 billion budget to digitising the tax administration. Plans include e-invoicing, linking government information systems, risk-scoring of taxpayers, national hosting of tax data and possible use of artificial intelligence. The strategy targets FCFA 481 billion in additional revenue over the period.

2026-10-03-tun-assabah-ordre-medecins-fa.summary: Tunisia's National Council of the Order of Physicians said on 3 October 2026 that it maintains its objection to applying electronic invoicing to doctors in its current form. It argues that a 2026 tax note extended Article 53 of the Finance Law to non-commercial professions without legal basis, and cites medical secrecy and patient data protection. A proposed amendment it helped draft is still awaited.

2026-10-03-tza-mwananchi-smz-sh53-bilion.summary: Zanzibar's government has set aside more than TZS 53 billion for three ICT infrastructure projects, chiefly a data centre and public internet, communication minister Mudrik Ramadhan Soraga said on 2 October 2026. He said a draft startups bill creating a fund of grants and low-cost loans is due for first reading in November or December 2026.

2026-10-03-uga-nilepost-digital-number-p.summary: Uganda's parliamentary Committee on Physical Infrastructure watched police track four Parliament vehicles live through the Digital Number Plate System at the Naguru command centre. Police said 337 of 375 stolen vehicles had been tracked and recovered. MPs asked for faster response to tamper alerts, and the Ministry of Works and Transport is linking the registration database to owners' contact details.

2026-10-03-xaf-techreviewafrica-auc-mata.summary: The African Union's infrastructure and energy commissioner called for artificial intelligence built around African languages and priorities rather than adopted from elsewhere. Figures cited by the African Union put the continent at 1 per cent of global AI compute capacity and about 3 per cent of AI talent.

2026-10-04-african-diplomats-in-cairo-ag.summary: Representatives of 11 African diplomatic missions in Cairo agreed to draft a joint Cairo Document for Trust and African Digital Integration. It is to set shared priorities on digital investment, digital trade, cybersecurity, data governance and emerging technologies.

2026-10-04-bceao-makes-pi-spi-mandatory-.summary: The Central Bank of West African States said on 2 October 2026 that its PI-SPI instant payment platform becomes mandatory for all interoperable e-money transactions in the eight WAEMU countries from 2 November. Domestic transfers of XOF 8,000 or less a day per user become free; cross-border transfers follow from 1 June 2027. Economist Youssaou Koanda notes the bank names new uses as an aim for the first time.

2026-10-04-ben-beninwebtv-anip-50109-act.summary: Benin's identification agency said 50,109 children received a first birth certificate free of charge in September 2026. The campaign ran from 16 to 30 September for children under 14 who had never had one.

2026-10-04-bfa-burkina-faso-le-droit-des.summary: Burkina Faso adopted two data protection laws on 3 August 2026, Jupiter Info reported. Organic law 038-2026/ALP, promulgated on 22 September, creates a joint media and data regulator, ARCOD. Law 037-2026/ALP repeals the 2021 law, adds impact assessments and data protection officers, and gives controllers six months to comply.

2026-10-04-cote-divoire-seeks-responsibl.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's digital transition minister told an international seminar that the government wants blockchain and digital assets developed inside a secure regulatory framework. He named agriculture, financial transactions, land administration and the creative sector as possible uses and announced no instrument.

2026-10-04-dza-dzwatch-akbou-i-cloud-sov.summary: Algeria inaugurated I-Cloud, described as its first wholly sovereign data centre, in the Akbou industrial zone in Bejaia. The knowledge economy minister presided, and agreements were signed with local industrialists and Algeria Venture on small firms' access to it; the inauguration date and capacity are not stated.

2026-10-04-dza-radioalgerie-tebboune-dig.summary: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune told his periodic media briefing that digitisation has sharply reduced corruption in Algeria by exposing manipulation across sectors, the foreign-currency allowance procedures among them. He gave no figures.

2026-10-04-egy-sis-planning-minister-202.summary: Egypt's planning minister Ahmed Rostom met the head of CAPMAS on 4 October 2026 to review preparations for the 2028 general census of population, housing and establishments, and pledged the ministry's logistical and institutional support. The results are to guide the Hayah Karima initiative, the national population strategy and housing policy.

2026-10-04-egy-youm7-digital-safety-law-.summary: Ahmed Badawi, newly elected chair of the Egyptian House of Representatives' ICT committee, said a digital safety law tops the committee's agenda for the new session. He said parliament and government coordinated the bill over nine sessions with 14 ministers and that most of its articles regulate children's use of social media. Amendments to the information technology law are also planned.

2026-10-04-egypt-electricity-ministry-on.summary: Egypt's electricity distribution companies lost sight of citizens' service requests after the holding company's systems sector replaced the unified e-services platform with an untested system and switched the old one off, a ministry source told Youm7. The minister ordered the fault fixed and those responsible held to account.

2026-10-04-gha-citinewsroom-attobrah-qua.summary: An opinion piece examines the Ghanaian cabinet's rejection of a proposed United States health compact worth about US$109 million over five years. President Mahama said it would have required Ghana to hand over pathogen data and medical records; the author argues that refusing is only the start of the work of data sovereignty.

2026-10-04-gha-gna-dpc-spot-checks-enfor.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission said it would begin spot checks and enforcement from 5 October against organisations that process personal data without registering or meeting the Data Protection Act, 2012. Its executive director said prosecution would follow where necessary.

2026-10-04-gha-gna-telecel-double-fibre-.summary: Two fibre cuts caused by road construction, on the Accra-Winneba and Winneba-Cape Coast routes, disrupted service to an estimated 72,754 Telecel Ghana subscribers on about 181 sites in the Central Region. The communications minister reported it on 3 October and said engineers were restoring service.

2026-10-04-gha-myjoyonline-traffitech-sm.summary: In a MyJoyOnline opinion piece, Bright Simons examines Ghana's Traffitech-GH system, under which police will fine motorists by text message from 1 November 2026. He reports that the operator, NTMEL, is 60 per cent owned by Frank Osei and 40 per cent by Sensys Gatso, and that fine revenue is split 40 per cent to the operator and 60 per cent to government. He calls for the PPP contract to be published.

2026-10-04-liberia-studies-ghanas-paymen.summary: The governor of the Central Bank of Liberia led a delegation to the Bank of Ghana on 1 October to study how Ghana set up its interbank payment and settlement company. Liberia is working to connect its banks to the instant payment system it switched on in December 2025.

2026-10-04-mar-eyeofriyadh-cbuae-bank-al.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib and the Central Bank of the UAE signed two memoranda in Abu Dhabi. One covers supervisory information exchange and Islamic finance; the other is to explore linking the two countries' instant payment platforms, card switches and financial messaging systems, and to exchange expertise on central bank digital currencies.

2026-10-04-mar-laverite-bo-7548-world-ba.summary: Morocco's Bulletin officiel of 1 October 2026 published decrees approving two World Bank loans: €218.2 million, signed on 25 June, for the Digital Transformation Acceleration Program, and €349.1 million, signed on 30 June, for climate and risk finance. The digital programme plans a single public services portal and a digital wallet linked to the electronic ID card, with results expected by 2031.

2026-10-04-mobile-money-wallets-set-to-l.summary: Ethiopia's non-bank mobile-money operators and payment-service providers are preparing to connect to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System. Each needs a letter of no objection from the National Bank of Ethiopia first, and operators are weighing a direct connection against routing through EthSwitch or partner banks.

2026-10-04-nam-marketwatch-namibia-stren.summary: Namibia's communications regulator launched DigiNam in Windhoek on 31 August as the public face of the national public key infrastructure, for which the regulator is root certification authority. It is meant to support electronic signatures, digital identity and authenticated online transactions under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019.

2026-10-04-nga-businessday-split-cloud-b.summary: Nigerian banks and large fintechs face the central bank's 1 January 2027 deadline for storing payment transaction data in the country. Cloud providers say some may keep applications on foreign clouds and host the regulated data locally, an arrangement the central bank has not ruled on.

2026-10-04-nga-gentechnews-ncc-communiqu.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator issued the communique of its Digital Connectivity Investment Forum, held in Abuja on 29 and 30 September with Swedfund and Ookla. It sets actions on timelines of six to twenty-four months, among them open-access and wholesale regulation, a wholesale rate card, completed broadband mapping and a first national connectivity index report. It records broadband penetration at 57.4% against a 70% target.

2026-10-04-nga-nitda-warns-organisations.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency NITDA warned organisations and staff, in an advisory posted on X through its emergency response team CERRT.NG, not to enter personal, classified or confidential information into public AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Copilot. It said such data may be retained or used for training, and that exposing personal data could breach data protection law.

2026-10-04-rwa-taarifa-digital-payments-.summary: Rwanda's prime minister said reported financial fraud complaints fell by about 30% in the second quarter of 2026 from 4,128 a year earlier. Digital transactions rose from about 256 million in 2017 to 3.1 billion in 2025, and he said phone-based fraud remains a problem.

2026-10-04-sdn-sudanews-un-desa-e-govern.summary: Sudan's foreign ministry undersecretary met the UN under-secretary-general for economic and social affairs in New York and briefed him on the economy, financial reform and reconstruction. The report names support for Sudan's digital transformation as a subject of cooperation and states no agreement or programme.

2026-10-04-sdn-sudanhorizon-mof-zain-eis.summary: Sudan's finance ministry signed an agreement with Zain in Khartoum on 4 October for text-message services on Eisali, the state electronic collection and payment system. Users are to be told the status of each transaction as it is registered, updated or completed.

2026-10-04-sha-to-hmis-how-kenyas-rushed.summary: A commentary argues that Kenya is moving health facilities from the health insurer's provider portal to facility-owned information systems before the arrangement has been tested. It questions the pace, the cost to hospitals and the handling of patient data during the switch.

2026-10-04-swz-standard-bank-revives-ins.summary: Standard Bank Eswatini has told customers by SMS that its Instant Money service will return as it prepares to close the Unayo digital platform on 31 December 2026. No relaunch date, fees or limits had been announced as of 4 October. Unayo users were advised to withdraw stored funds before the closure.

2026-10-04-technologies-spatiales-le-tog.summary: Togo's digital minister Cina Lawson announced on 1 October 2026 a space cooperation with Kyrgyzstan, which is to supply earth-observation data for agriculture, strategic-minerals exploration and green energy, train local staff and transfer the technology to use it. Joint development and launch of future spacecraft is under consideration. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-10-04-tgo-ipdcp-apdp-benin-seance-t.summary: Togo's data-protection authority hosted its Beninese counterpart in Lome on 2 and 3 October for a working session on sharing experience and building skills. It follows the Togolese authority's mission to Benin on 18 August and the two bodies' cooperation agreement.

2026-10-04-tun-businessnews-forum-chawki.summary: Tunisia's Forum Chawki Gaddes for digital rights condemned the spread on social media of personal and sensitive data, including leaked judicial documents and images of child victims. It says the national data-protection authority has stopped working although its law remains in force, and calls for it to be reactivated.

2026-10-04-xca-gep-beac-jornadas-banquer.summary: The governor of the Bank of Central African States, closing the CEMAC Bankers' Days in Bangui on 3 October, set a goal that by the end of 2027 every transfer under CFA 5 million settles in under ten seconds on the region's interoperable instant payment system. He also cited a regional switch project and a central bank sovereign cloud to keep payment data in the region, and a 35% financial inclusion target for 2028.

2026-10-04-zwe-herald-econet-infraco-mai.summary: Econet InfraCo, the tower, power and property company listed in Victoria Falls, reported revenue of US$70.1 million and EBITDA of US$29.0 million for the six months to 31 August 2026, its first half-year results since listing.
