2026-10-05-africa-needs-120m-au-law-to-f.summary: The African Union Commission and the AfricaNenda Foundation presented a framework in Nairobi on 5 October 2026 to harmonise cross-border payment rules across Africa. It would need a binding AU legal instrument, a supervisory body anchored in the Association of African Central Banks and a US$120m implementation fund. The 10-year plan names five regional blocs as pathfinders and Nigeria–Ghana as a pilot corridor.

2026-10-05-ahram-egypt-parliament-ict-co.summary: Egypt's parliamentary ICT committee chair Ahmed Badawi said the committee will open its new session with the digital safety bill and expects it finished within a month. The bill protects children on social media and adds rules for adults on online betting, defamation and disinformation; the committee held six hearings with 14 ministers and agency heads.

2026-10-05-camtel-minesec-sic-connectivi.summary: Cameroon's state operator CAMTEL says it will sign two framework agreements on 7 October: one with the secondary education ministry on connectivity for schools, the other with the state housing company on connectivity in housing estates.

2026-10-05-capitalfm-african-ict-regulat.summary: Opening the same Nairobi session, the head of Kenya's communications regulator urged African regulators to pool their efforts against fraud, cyber threats and cable disruptions that cross borders. He said Kenya has promulgated a new market structure for telecommunications and postal services and is reviewing its sector laws.

2026-10-05-cbk-raises-compliance-costs-a.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya's final regulations for non-deposit-taking credit providers set a Sh100,000 licence application fee and annual fees of Sh500,000 for licensed and Sh250,000 for registered providers, against Sh5,000 and Sh20,000 under the earlier digital credit regime. A new Sh1 million penalty applies to annual fees unpaid by 31 December.

2026-10-05-cbl-electronic-transactions-8.summary: Libya's central bank said electronic transactions reached about 865 billion dinars by the end of September 2026. The figure came from a meeting between the governor, commercial bank heads and the state payments company on cash liquidity, wider electronic payment and cyber-risk readiness.

2026-10-05-civ-aip-parae-confiance-servi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire launched a feasibility study on 5 October 2026 for a national digital authentication platform and digital identity access point, under the e-administration support project PARAE, co-financed by the African Development Bank. The national identity office, ONECI, carries the project on the basis of the national population register. The study is due by January 2027.

2026-10-05-cod-minecon-communique-163-lo.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of National Economy launched LOBA, a national consumer-protection platform, from 6 October 2026. Run through the Competition Commission (COMCO) with sector regulators covering telecoms, banking, insurance, electricity and health, it lets consumers report abuses, learn their rights and track complaints via a WhatsApp chatbot and a mobile app.

2026-10-05-cote-ivoire-plateforme-nation.summary: Côte d'Ivoire launched a feasibility study in Abidjan on 5 October 2026 for a national authentication platform and digital identity wallet, run by the PARAE project with African Development Bank support. The study will first assess existing assets, including the national population register and ONECI systems, and may extend to verifying digital credentials such as diplomas and permits. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-10-05-csa-ghana-opens-ncsam-2026.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority opened its 2026 awareness month with a call for banks, fintechs and telecoms operators to share threat information as routine. The national response team recorded 3,876 incidents between January and July 2026, about 47% of them online fraud.

2026-10-05-dcd-continent-8-johannesburg-.summary: Continent 8 Technologies, which hosts online gaming and betting operators, announced its first African data centre, in Johannesburg. It did not disclose the site or any colocation partner.

2026-10-05-duale-and-governors-set-14-oc.summary: Kenya's health ministry and the Council of Governors' health committee agreed that current Social Health Authority facility contracts will not be extended again, and that the authority will run HAKIKA contracting clinics in every county until 14 October 2026. Facilities meeting other requirements get 30 days to submit outstanding documents, including data protection compliance.

2026-10-05-gha-myjoyonline-nia-ghana-car.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority, with the National Health Insurance Authority, began school-based Ghana Card registration of children aged 6 to 14 in the North East and Upper East regions on 5 October 2026. Children need a birth certificate, passport or citizenship certificate, or an oath of identity by a parent or guardian; those registered in the 2024 pilot should not re-register.

2026-10-05-gin-mediaguinee-orange-unicef.summary: Fondation Orange Guinée and UNICEF signed a protocol at Conakry on 5 October to equip 50 schools across six regions with digital learning hubs. It also provides for training 500 adolescents in science and digital skills and for 100 scholarships and prizes; no budget is stated.

2026-10-05-gin-ucep-attribution-informat.summary: Guinea has awarded a 12-month, USD 26,400 consultancy, signed on 7 September 2026, to continue computerising the Commercial Court of Conakry. The work covers the court's case-management, archiving and communication system, its website, a case-law database and its IT equipment.

2026-10-05-gmb-standard-udp-supplementar.summary: The Gambia's United Democratic Party asked the electoral commission to explain a gap of 28,932 between the 212,095 supplementary registrations it announced and the 183,163 in the dataset given to the party. It wants the figures before and after de-duplication, the records deleted and the method used, and says it is not alleging malpractice.

2026-10-05-google-for-startups-accelerat.summary: Google named 15 South African-led, revenue-generating AI startups to its 2026 Google for Startups Accelerator: South Africa on 5 October 2026, chosen from 1,057 applications. Each gets up to R1 million in equity-free funding, access to Google's AI models and cloud, and mentorship over three months ending in a December Demo Day.

2026-10-05-gtco-payments-business-five-n.summary: An analysis of Guaranty Trust Holding Company's half-year results shows its payments subsidiary HabariPay earning ₦7.81 billion in profit, close to double a year earlier, on ₦74.72 trillion switched. Transfers through its Pay-with-Transfer service reached ₦1.11 trillion while USSD use fell.

2026-10-05-how-much-collected-digital-mi.summary: South Africa's communications minister told Parliament that about R1.29 billion was collected for the Universal Service and Access Fund over five years and about R652 million was unspent at the end of 2025/26. Spending that year included a R567 million write-off of set-top-box inventory, and there is still no analogue switch-off date.

2026-10-05-ifc-and-bot-sign-agreement-to.summary: The International Finance Corporation and the Bank of Tanzania signed an agreement to strengthen Tanzania's credit reporting system, reported on 5 October 2026. IFC will give technical help on credit information systems and the use of alternative data in credit assessment, to widen lending to small businesses. No signing date or value is given.

2026-10-05-ipris-african-telecom-regulat.summary: A European-funded regulatory capacity programme is holding its eighth cohort in Nairobi from 5 to 9 October. Regulators from Liberia, Mauritius, Namibia, Sierra Leone, Tanzania and Zimbabwe are taking part with three regional regulators' associations.

2026-10-05-itweb-tlou-kala-data-centre-e.summary: Tlou Energy's annual report says Botswana's gas-powered Kala Data Centre ran well below its design of about 1MW in the year to June 2026, for lack of gas from the one connected well. The company has begun planning a pipeline from a second well, and any expansion depends on gas supply and funding.

2026-10-05-kcb-zanzibar-health-fund-expa.summary: KCB Bank Tanzania and the Zanzibar Health Service Fund signed a memorandum of understanding on 5 October 2026. It covers member registration and enrolment, payment collection, banking and settlement services, and technology integration for the fund. No financial terms are given.

2026-10-05-ken-kehc-marsabit-petition-e0.summary: Kenya's High Court at Marsabit on 5 October 2026 dismissed a constitutional petition against mandatory travel health insurance for foreign visitors under Gazette Notice No. 11492 of 30 July 2026. The court held the notice valid and found the petitioners' claim that insurance data collected through the Electronic Travel Authorisation system was insecure to be general and unproven. No costs were awarded.

2026-10-05-kenyas-health-system-has-a-gh.summary: A newspaper column asks what Kenya's Sh104.8 billion health digitisation contract of 2024 paid for, now that hospitals are being moved from one Social Health Authority system to another. It cites a 2025 patient-group survey in which six in ten respondents said they had been denied care at least once over system failures.

2026-10-05-koica-ghana-digital-basic-edu.summary: South Korea's ambassador to Ghana, Kyongsig Park, told the Ghanaian Times that the Korea International Cooperation Agency is launching a Digital Basic Education Capacity-Building Programme for 2026 to 2032 with a budget of US$28 million. He said Korea also supports an ICT innovation centre at the University of Ghana, and more than 1,800 Ghanaians have taken part in KOICA programmes.

2026-10-05-mar-bo-7549-arrete-218-26-don.summary: Joint arrêté n° 218.26 of 29 January 2026, published in Morocco's Bulletin officiel n° 7549 on 5 October 2026, lists the data airlines must send on passengers, commercial flights, crew and general-aviation flights. It applies decree 2.21.624 of 21 July 2022 and covers identity, contact, payment, frequent-flyer, baggage and travel-document details, with a catch-all for other useful information.

2026-10-05-minette-libom-li-likeng-patnu.summary: Cameroon's posts and telecommunications minister handed four platforms built under the World Bank-financed digital transformation project to the agriculture ministry on 1 October. They cover e-learning for training schools, a soil-fertility map and agro-pastoral statistics, and soil sampling was launched the same day.

2026-10-05-mli-statistiques-du-commerce-.summary: On a page dated 5 October 2026, Mali's statistics institute INSTAT lists quarterly trade bulletins from 2013 to early 2026. Annual trade yearbooks for 2017 to 2025 are also free to download. The list shows no bulletin for the fourth quarter of 2023 or the first quarter of 2020.

2026-10-05-moz-camaramen-atdi-coordenaca.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency ATDI held its first Design Lab for digital public service delivery at Macaneta, Maputo province, with the World Bank and the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change. Representatives of the transport institute INATRO, the civil identification directorate, the justice ministry and the one-stop service counters mapped the citizen's route through state services. It falls under the World Bank-funded EDGE project.

2026-10-05-mus-appleby-electronic-transa.summary: Law firm Appleby reviews Mauritius's Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act 2026. The Act accepts any reliable electronic signature that identifies the signer and shows intent, gives legal effect to electronic transferable records, and recognises contracts formed by automated systems without human review of each action. Under section 15A, where a certificate or signature originates does not by itself decide its effectiveness.

2026-10-05-namibia-digital-trade-afcfta-.summary: Namibia's assessment of its laws and institutions against the African free-trade area's Protocol on Digital Trade went to a validation workshop in Windhoek. It will feed a National Digital Trade Action Plan; no findings are published.

2026-10-05-nga-fg-turns-to-blended-fundi.summary: Nigeria plans to finance community-owned telecom towers in unconnected areas through the Universal Service Provision Fund for telecom equipment, the Rural Electrification Agency for solar power and state governments for land and rights of way, a resolution of the communications regulator's investment forum. Community cooperatives would own the sites. A rollout of about 3,700 towers is due to start in October, with 200 by December 2026.

2026-10-05-nga-nigeria-hits-73-financial.summary: The 2026 Access to Financial Services survey by EFInA and Nigeria's statistics bureau found formal financial inclusion at 73% of adults, above the 70% national target, and use of digital financial services at 64.4%, up from 45% in 2023. Only 30.7% of formally included adults are financially healthy, leaving about 60.4 million adults vulnerable. The survey covered 18,679 adults between April and June 2026.

2026-10-05-nga-nimc-s-ninauth-mandate-an.summary: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has ordered every ministry, department and agency to use the identity commission's NINAuth service as its default identity check. NIMC says enrolment has passed 136 million against a year-end target of 180 million, while its fee for correcting a date of birth rose from ₦16,340 to ₦28,574.

2026-10-05-nga-nitda-warns-nigerians-aga.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency, NITDA, published an advisory on 5 October 2026 warning people not to enter identity numbers, bank verification numbers, bank details, photographs or medical results into public AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. It tells organisations to adopt AI governance policies naming approved tools and data-handling rules.

2026-10-05-nga-vanguard-inec-voter-regis.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission chairman said the national register of voters stands at more than 103 million after the final biometric clean-up. Three phases of continuous registration added 10,772,421 voters, and card collection begins nationwide on 9 October.

2026-10-05-parliament-probes-delays-in-i.summary: Kenya's National Assembly committee on administration and internal security heard on 5 October 2026 that national ID cards in Elgeyo Marakwet County take one to two months to issue against a two-week standard. Officials blamed processing in Nairobi, poor connectivity, too few staff and vehicles, and some sub-counties receiving as little as Sh10,000 for fuel a quarter.

2026-10-05-question-to-the-minister-of-c.summary: South Africa's communications minister told Parliament in a written reply that the State Information Technology Agency (SITA) moved from a qualified audit opinion in 2024/25 to an unqualified one for 2025/26, after Cabinet approved an interim board in February 2025 and a permanent board on 6 May 2026. SITA delivered 117 e-services through 35 digital products to more than 30 public bodies and met 80.66% of procurement requests on time.

2026-10-05-regional-afreximbank-eabc-afr.summary: Afreximbank made the East African Business Council a trade corridor partner of its Africa Trade Gateway, to bring the region's firms onto its matchmaking, trade finance and payment services. The bank puts the gateway in more than 45 countries with 110 banks and 25,000 verified companies.

2026-10-05-sa-land-availability-edge-dat.summary: A market study by DC Byte puts Africa at 3% of the 93GW of data-centre capacity built or planned across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. It names available land as South Africa's advantage and the time taken to deliver power as its constraint.

2026-10-05-sdn-northern-state-wafi-finan.summary: Sudan's Northern State met the National Technology Company on 5 October 2026 to restore the finance ministry's Wafi resource-management system, in use since 2017 and stopped by the war in 2023. The state says next year's budget will run through the system, with procurement, stores and budget modules to follow.

2026-10-05-sle-slmonitor-slrsa-cyber-int.summary: The Sierra Leone Road Safety Authority said in a public notice dated 2 October 2026 that an intrusion into its IT systems was used to produce fake vehicle licences. Police arrested five people who are not SLRSA staff. The number of fake licences in circulation was not disclosed, and owners are asked to verify licences at SLRSA offices.

2026-10-05-sle-techreview-ai-roadmap-jus.summary: Sierra Leone's judiciary and the attorney-general's office are to draft a national artificial-intelligence roadmap for the justice sector with UNESCO, beginning with the security sector. Participants at the convening pointed to electronic filing and digital case management; no timetable is given.

2026-10-05-smart-africa-to-test-gender-i.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry is validating three gender impact assessment tools ahead of a Smart Africa workshop in Mbabane from 6 to 8 October 2026, where participants will adapt and pilot them for local digital development programmes. The article does not describe what the tools measure.

2026-10-05-som-itweb-mobile-money-silos.summary: The chief executive of Somalia's SomLink Telecom says voice calls now interconnect across six operators while mobile-money wallets remain closed to one another. He calls for cost-based pricing and shared rails, and says the largest operators have little commercial reason to open up.

2026-10-05-swz-system-glitch-stalls-civi.summary: An outage of Eswatini government digital services has stopped new loans to civil servants because lenders cannot reach the Integrated Financial Management Information System to check applicants against the 33% salary-deduction limit, reported on 5 October 2026. Instalments on existing loans are still being received. Other platforms affected include e-Visa, the deeds registry and the government website.

2026-10-05-swz-times-e182m-data-centre-l.summary: Eswatini's finance ministry says the E182 million India Exim Bank loan for a disaster recovery site at Siteki has not been cancelled. What the minister meant in Parliament was the commitment fee on the undrawn balance, which the lender has agreed to stop; 1% of the loan has been drawn.

2026-10-05-tariq-malik-export-dpi-mistak.summary: Tariq Malik, a World Bank identity adviser, argues that countries sharing digital public infrastructure should export their mistakes as well as their expertise. He proposes an exit test for partnerships and a published time-to-redress, and cites Malawi's enrolment of about nine million adults in roughly 180 days.

2026-10-05-tgo-lenouveaureporter-ipdcp-c.summary: Togo's personal data protection authority, IPDCP, opened its first evaluation and certification session for data protection officers in Atakpamé on 30 September 2026. Thirty-two professionals from banking, insurance, telecoms, public administration and other sectors were assessed under Law 2019-014, and only those reaching the required level may hold the title.

2026-10-05-tgo-undp-voix-du-togo-infrast.summary: UNDP Togo reports on the launch of the national local-languages challenge under the Voix du Togo programme, run by the Togo AI Lab for the digital transformation ministry, whose pilot phase targets AI models for Kabiyè, Ewe and Moba. UNDP is supporting the lab with GPU-based computing infrastructure, presented as a supercomputer, to train the models, and minister Cina Lawson described language models as essential public infrastructure. A contribution platform will gather voice recordings, texts and translations, and the challenge's results are still to come.

2026-10-05-the-system-is-down-not-the-ro.summary: Botswana's Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure announced interim manual measures on 29 September 2026 after a government systems outage at the Department of Road Transport and Safety. Expired transport permits are extended by hand with an official stamp, and vehicles with expired roadworthiness certificates are tested and given manual receipts, which police will accept until systems are restored.

2026-10-05-tun-chourouk-ministere-tic-pr.summary: Tunisia's communications ministry announced child-protection measures resting on a telecommunications regulator's decision of 10 June 2026. Internet providers must offer parental controls covering site blacklists, device management and access-time limits, tell subscribers about them and write a child-protection clause into contracts.

2026-10-05-tza-the-electricity-sub-secto.summary: EWURA's review for FY2025/26 reports that TANESCO's average interruptions per customer fell from 17.69 to 12.09. Average outage duration fell from 1,692.73 to 1,044.77 minutes. Both are within target. At transmission level, the review gives 7.4 interruptions and 2.7 hours against targets of 10.0 and 6.5 hours.

2026-10-05-usaasa-usaf-manual-approved.summary: South Africa's universal service agency says the communications minister has approved the manual for the Universal Service and Access Fund, setting its objectives, governance, funding instruments and accountability. An earlier draft was withdrawn in November 2025 and a revised one went out for comment in February 2026.

2026-10-05-wave-joins-pi-spi-as-bceao-re.summary: The West African central bank (BCEAO) is changing fees on its PI-SPI instant payment system from 2 November 2026: sending electronic money stays free up to 8,000 CFA francs a day, with fees above that capped at 0.8%, and receiving stays free. Previously receipts were free only for the first 30 operations a month. The mobile money operator Wave has joined the system.

2026-10-05-wearetech-burundi-e-justice-c.summary: Burundi is preparing an E-Justice platform to link the penal chain from the judicial police to the prisons, with online complaints and case tracking for citizens. An earlier programme digitised more than 15,000 case files, and the article sets the plan against an internet use rate of about 11%.

2026-10-05-xaf-techreviewafrica-au-eu-in.summary: The African Union's infrastructure and energy commissioner and the European Union's ambassador to the AU reviewed cooperation after their seventh summit. On digital infrastructure they covered the continental digital transformation and artificial-intelligence strategies and European support for regulation and data governance.

2026-10-05-xgl-rand-emerging-digital-bat.summary: A RAND study of the contest between the United States and China over third countries' digital networks finds that cost, bundled offers and presence on the ground give China structural advantages. The authors set out five priorities for the United States to close the gap.

2026-10-05-xwa-biometricupdate-ecowas-bi.summary: ECOWAS is running public campaigns in Ghana and Nigeria ahead of its December 2026 target for all member states to accept its biometric identity card at air, land and sea borders. Seven member states have issued the card so far.

2026-10-05-zaf-proparco-invests-us20m-fr.summary: Proparco, the French development finance institution, said on 5 October 2026 that it is investing US$20 million in South African fibre and connectivity companies Frogfoot, Vox and Hypa, in a consortium led by Metier with BII, BIO, DEG, Ke Nako Capital, Nedbank and Standard Bank. The funds are for extending fibre into lower-income and township areas. No signing date is given.

2026-10-05-zaf-question-nw4395-to-the-ac.summary: In a reply to a parliamentary question tabled on 5 October 2026, the police service reported eight cyber-extortion, ransomware and related cases registered over three years. One suspect was arrested, for extortion. The attack on the Weather Service remains unsolved.

2026-10-05-zamtel-myzamtel-super-app.summary: Zambia's Zamtel launched a self-care application with a build-your-own-bundle option, and Kongola Malaiti, a digital financial service reached by short code. No user figures are given.

2026-10-05-zarc-15m-za-domains.summary: South Africa's domain registry reports 1.5 million active registrations across its four commercial second-level namespaces. It says that makes .ZA the first African country-code domain to reach the mark.

2026-10-06-bfa-cfinance-222-procedures-d.summary: Burkina Faso's digital ministry reports 46.70% average physical execution of its minister's 20-action objectives contract at 30 June 2026. In the half year it described 222 administrative procedures for moving online, connected 10 more sites to the government network, counted 120 official platforms hosted abroad for repatriation and drafted nine implementing texts for the information-systems security law.

2026-10-06-cert-sc-takes-the-lead-in-thi.summary: Seychelles' national computer emergency response team designed and delivered the country's third national cyberdrill itself for the first time. The two-day exercise tests how organisations detect, respond to and recover from cyberattacks.

2026-10-06-cmr-businesstechafrica-reasy-.summary: Cameroonian fintech REasy and Africa Global Logistics presented to Douala traders on 1 October 2026 a pilot service for small businesses importing from China. REasy converts CFA francs to yuan to pay suppliers through Alipay, WeChat Pay or Chinese bank accounts, while AGL consolidates and ships goods. The first shared container reached Douala on 29 April; no pricing has been published.

2026-10-06-cod-adn-snia-draft-technique.summary: DR Congo's digital economy ministry has published a technical draft of a national AI strategy to 2030, with 4 pillars and 176 actions. It plans an annual report on AI in the country from 2027 and a minimum of 15% local content in public AI purchases; the text is a draft, not an adopted strategy.

2026-10-06-cod-electricite-presentation-.summary: The electricity regulator ARE presented an online complaints platform in Kinshasa on 5 October 2026. Consumers and operators can file complaints and follow their progress on it.

2026-10-06-cod-globalnewsrdc-ia-rdc-enqu.summary: A survey by the DR Congo consultancy Target Sarl of 2,280 adults in the 26 provincial capitals, conducted from 16 to 22 March 2026, found awareness of artificial intelligence rose from 54% in 2025 to 61%, and use from 24% to 47%. Use stands at 54% among men and 41% among women, and ChatGPT is the most used tool.

2026-10-06-cod-rdc-la-diffamation-dans-l.summary: A Kinshasa lawyer spoke to the press agency on 6 October 2026. He said the 2023 digital code punishes online defamation, with no immunity for journalists or influencers. He cited the September 2026 arrest of a TikTok chronicler. The arrest followed a broadcast about a singer's private life.

2026-10-06-cog-brazzavillois-ins-commerc.summary: Congo's statistics institute held a workshop in Brazzaville on 2 October to set up a permanent statistical system for informal cross-border trade. A mapping of border crossings is under way, a baseline survey is planned for 2027 and quarterly collection is to feed the balance of payments, with World Bank support.

2026-10-06-cs-duale-calls-for-timely-tra.summary: Kenya's health cabinet secretary urged providers to meet the timelines for moving from the insurer's provider portal to the health management information system and for completing the 2026-2029 contracting cycle. The ministry puts migration at 6,427 public facilities, 38 certified private facilities and 38 of 518 faith-based ones, and says correctly submitted claims will still be paid during the change.

2026-10-06-dza-algerieeco-aps-assamaka-e.summary: The Algerian account of the Assamaka ceremony, summarised above, says the link was built by Algerie Telecom and Niger Telecom, starts at 100 Gbps and can be expanded as traffic grows.

2026-10-06-egy-eg-ix-strengthening-regio.summary: AMS-IX reports that the EG-IX exchange in Cairo had 19 connected networks in the third quarter of 2026, against 4 at its launch in April 2022. It lists 37 ports and 3.2 Tb/s of capacity, with traffic peaking at 945 Gb/s. Telecom Egypt hosts the exchange.

2026-10-06-egy-youm7-hrc-first-ai-human-.summary: Egypt, with Bangladesh and a cross-regional group, led the UN Human Rights Council to adopt by consensus its first resolution on the implications of AI for human rights. It stresses the right to development, decent work, linguistic diversity and technology transfer to developing countries, and mandates a Council meeting and a report on AI, human rights and the capacity gap. The adoption date is not stated.

2026-10-06-foundation-sues-as-tiktok-res.summary: The Foundation for Digital Justice filed a fundamental-rights suit against TikTok at the Federal High Court in Abuja on 5 October. It alleges that users in Kaduna, Kano, Kebbi and Sokoto states have been restricted since mid-September while the rest of Nigeria keeps full access, and asks for an order restoring it.

2026-10-06-gab-gabonmailinfos-porte-paro.summary: Gabon's presidential spokesman said on radio that he uses a VPN, outside the law, to get round the social-media suspension the communications authority imposed in February 2026. The outlet reports the suspension still in force and the authority silent on any sanction.

2026-10-06-gab-infosgabon-douanes-contro.summary: IKA Technologie presented on 29 September 2026 the integrated customs operations management system it is building for Gabon under the Gabon Connect project. Its first lot covers customs clearance of minerals and the special hydrocarbons warehouse. No cost or go-live date is given.

2026-10-06-gauteng-transport-department-.summary: Gauteng's transport department launched a digital system to clear its backlog of public-transport operating licences, after six to eight months of testing with e-hailing, taxi and bus operators, municipalities and law enforcement. E-hailing operators are first in line to regularise.

2026-10-06-gha-bog-notice-36-unlicensed-.summary: The Bank of Ghana named 20 mobile loan apps, including Agile Loan, KudiNow, SikaNow and Susu Loan, operating without its licence in a notice dated 6 October 2026. It said they breach its September 2025 directive on digital credit providers and customers' data privacy, and warned banks and payment service providers not to process their transactions.

2026-10-06-gha-myjoyonline-bog-fraud-uni.summary: The Bank of Ghana directed banks to give their fraud units direct and unrestricted access to the managing director or chief executive, Governor Johnson Asiama told heads of banks. He said fraud staff must hold the right skills and certifications, and that the central bank will tighten supervision of technology, customer-fund safeguarding and third-party risk. The meeting date is not given.

2026-10-06-ghana-telecel-huawei-200m-net.summary: Telecel Group signed a $200 million, three-year memorandum of understanding with Huawei Ghana at HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 in Shanghai to expand and modernise Telecel Ghana's network, including mobile broadband. It follows a $70 million agreement signed in Shenzhen the previous November. The signing date is not stated.

2026-10-06-gin-mediaguinee-guichet-uniqu.summary: Guinea's minister of administrative modernisation and the civil service, Faya François Bourouno, presented the government's one-stop public service counter project to the mayors of Conakry's 13 communes on 6 October 2026. The next step is to choose the first pilot sites with the communes. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-10-06-gmb-observer-gid-court-cannot.summary: A Gambia Immigration Department officer told a court on 6 October that the department can no longer reach data generated under the former Semlex biometric ID system, its access having ended with the contract. That leaves open who holds the historical identity records, although Semlex says it handed the system to the government in March 2024.

2026-10-06-gnb-dhis2-hisp-saudigitus-ina.summary: The HISP Centre at the University of Oslo and Saudigitus (HISP Mozambique) signed an agreement, announced on 6 October 2026, to help Guinea-Bissau's National Institute of Public Health (INASA) strengthen its DHIS2-based national health information system. The work, coordinated by the UN Development Programme and financed by the Global Fund, covers data quality, dashboards and new HIV and tuberculosis patient-tracking tools. No amount or duration is given.

2026-10-06-gnq-gqpress-boletin-oficial-d.summary: Equatorial Guinea's government announced a digital edition of its official gazette at boe.gob.gq, giving free online access to laws, decrees, ministerial orders and circulars with search of past publications.

2026-10-06-government-institutions-urged.summary: Opening Kenya's National Customer Service Week, the public service principal secretary told government institutions that good service is a standard citizens are entitled to and that the week's exhibitions should be used to listen to them.

2026-10-06-ict-minister-mavetera-directs.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister asked the telecommunications regulator to consider a dedicated unit to oversee operators' commercial arrangements, mediate disputes and enforce active infrastructure sharing. She also wants the Universal Service Fund to reach every marginalised ward and the regulator's sharing and tower-relocation directives evaluated in 2027.

2026-10-06-ipdcp-togo-universite-de-kara.summary: Togo's personal data protection authority (IPDCP) and the University of Kara signed a partnership agreement on 6 October 2026. It provides for a hybrid professional master's degree in digital law, cybersecurity, cyberdefence and data protection, developed with IPDCP technical and financial support, as well as joint research, workshops and internships. No cost is given.

2026-10-06-itweb-bofinet-launches-digita.summary: Botswana's state fibre operator BoFiNet announced the launch of the Digital Delta Internet Exchange Point, where service providers, mobile operators and content and cloud providers can exchange local traffic inside the country. It builds on the operator's Tier III-certified data centre.

2026-10-06-iucea-eac-ai-foundational-mod.summary: The East African Community, the Inter-University Council for East Africa and the East African Science and Technology Commission, with Germany, validated a draft EAC AI Foundational Module at a two-day workshop in Dar es Salaam, announced on 6 October 2026. The course aims to teach AI literacy to university students in all disciplines, and institutions in the EAC Regional AI Network may pilot it.

2026-10-06-ken-kenyans-e-notification-bi.summary: Kenya will extend electronic birth notification to every hospital contracted by the Social Health Authority within three months, by December 2026, the immigration principal secretary said. Newborns notified this way receive a Unique Personal Identifier, and talks with the health ministry on linking civil registration to hospital systems are complete.

2026-10-06-ken-techafricanews-kcb-stima-.summary: KCB Bank Kenya and Stima Sacco launched a link that lets the Sacco's members deposit straight into their accounts through the bank's mobile application. KCB says its digital Sacco products have grown from 345 to 407, without dating either count.

2026-10-06-ken-techcabal-equity-finserve.summary: Equity Bank's fintech arm, Finserve Africa, has launched a wallet called EMMA, reached by Android application, short code or the Equitel SIM toolkit and opened with an identity document and a facial check. Users can send money to M-PESA merchants, Airtel Money and bank accounts; the analysis reads it as the bank's bid to keep everyday payments, and the data behind them, on its own platform.

2026-10-06-kzn-launches-the-public-works.summary: KwaZulu-Natal is launching a portal listing its public works properties, after an audit of all 10,067 assets and the release of a first batch of 81 unused buildings and land parcels. Organisations and developers can identify assets to lease or reuse, and residents can log complaints about them.

2026-10-06-lbr-fpa-lisgis-ecowas-statist.summary: A week-long ECOWAS training for managers of member states' national statistical systems opened in Monrovia on 5 October. The head of Liberia's statistics office said statisticians need training to use AI in data collection properly, and warned that it can harm the data as well as help.

2026-10-06-local-government-election-res.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission opened its Election Results System, which captures and collates results and assigns seats, to audit by ICT experts from the ACDP, ANC, DA and MK Party from 5 to 12 October 2026. The commission said it had already completed an independent external audit of the system ahead of the 2026 local government elections.

2026-10-06-maroc-ma-cyber-academy-rabat.summary: Morocco's General Directorate of Information Systems Security and the World Bank, with the Smart Africa Digital Academy, opened the Cyber Academy executive training programme in Rabat on 5 October 2026 for leaders of African cybersecurity authorities. It covers strategic leadership, AI-driven threats and cyber crisis response. No participant numbers are given.

2026-10-06-mashrou-mizaniyya-2027-istrat.summary: A Tunisian finance ministry document on the 2027 draft budget plans to fight tax evasion using artificial intelligence, data analysis and linked databases across public bodies, reported on 6 October 2026. It also aims to reduce external borrowing, widen the tax base and expand digital tax services. The document itself is undated and not published.

2026-10-06-mli-fichier-electoral-l-heure.summary: Mali's annual revision of the electoral lists runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026, Le Pays reported. Voters apply at town halls, or at embassies and consulates abroad. The territorial administration ministry runs it, with the election management body AIGE supervising. By law the lists are drawn from the biometric civil-status database, with the national identification number (NINA) as each voter's key.

2026-10-06-moz-clubofmozambique-atdi-des.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency held the country's first Digital Service Delivery Design Lab, bringing public bodies and partners together to pick priority services, map how citizens use them now and redesign them. The process runs in five stages, ending in assigned responsibilities and action plans.

2026-10-06-nam-economist-parliament-brie.summary: Namibia's home affairs and ICT ministries briefed members of parliament on the rollout of a new electronic identity card. MPs asked about system security, cyberattacks, backups and who owns and controls the technology where private providers are involved, and about a proposed Resident Identity Card for long-term foreign residents. The briefing date is not given.

2026-10-06-ner-anp-assamaka-dorsale-tran.summary: Niger and Algeria launched operation of the fibre link between In Guezzam and the Arlit-Agadez region at a ceremony at Assamaka, on the border, on 6 October, chaired by the two communications ministers. Algeria's account gives a starting capacity of 100 Gbps.

2026-10-06-ner-anp-caravane-wuri-niamey.summary: The Niamey stage of Niger's national awareness caravan on civil registration and identification opened on 6 October under the World Bank-supported WURI project. The two-day session is to take stock of the caravan's regional stages; the project has been restructured to speed up civil registration and biometric identification.

2026-10-06-ner-mcnti-niger-algerie-inter.summary: Niger's communications ministry reported its minister's arrival at Agadez on 5 October with an Algerian delegation, describing the mission as the launch of fibre interconnection works between the two countries; the ceremony itself is summarised above.

2026-10-06-nigerias-ncc-to-leverage-itu-.summary: Nigeria's Digital Bridge Institute has been designated an ITU Digital Transformation Centre, and the communications regulator says it will use the status to widen digital skills training for underserved groups. The work is tied to the national target of 95% digital literacy by 2030.

2026-10-06-nigerias-ndpc-noa-sign-mou-to.summary: Nigeria's data protection commission and the National Orientation Agency signed a memorandum on joint public awareness work. It covers training for the agency's staff, coordinated campaigns across traditional and digital media, and guidance on applying the 2023 data-protection Act to the agency's own mandate.

2026-10-06-paperless-courts-spread-to-mi.summary: Zimbabwe's Judicial Service Commission took its electronic case management system live in Midlands and Mashonaland West provinces on 1 October, after installing recording and transcription machines and issuing computers to court staff. Litigants and lawyers can file and follow cases online.

2026-10-06-parliament-media-statement-se.summary: South Africa's Department of Transport told Parliament's Select Committee on Public Infrastructure on 6 October 2026 that draft regulations would extend light-vehicle driving licence cards from five to ten years, because of card-production delays and printer breakdowns. A Presidency-led working group with the Road Traffic Management Corporation and Home Affairs is exploring digital licences linked to the government's digital identity framework.

2026-10-06-problem-with-plan-for-digital.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs missed its first-quarter target to sign a work order starting procurement of digital ID hosting infrastructure, its quarterly report to Parliament's committee says. It also missed revising the National Identification Registration Bill for public comment, and now aims to finalise the procurement in the second quarter.

2026-10-06-rwa-minecofin-ifmis-upgraded-.summary: Rwanda's finance ministry has finished upgrading its Integrated Financial Management Information System, replacing legacy components that had reached the end of support. It plans to use the same approach on the schools data management system and the SACCO core banking system.

2026-10-06-sdn-akhbaralsudan-khartoum-st.summary: Sudan's Khartoum State Supreme Council for Strategy and Information launched the restoration of the state's digital systems and signed partnerships supporting its 2026-2036 recovery and reconstruction plan. Its secretary-general, Issam Batran, said the work covers recovering data and systems, completing telecoms networks, and managing information through a secure cloud system. No cost is given.

Sudan's Khartoum State government signed six partnership memoranda, including with Sudatel and the Central Bureau of Statistics, to support its ten-year recovery and reconstruction strategy. At the same event it restarted its standard systems, connected a government fibre and internet network to 36 state units including the state presidency, and moved all state data to the cloud. No amounts are stated.

2026-10-06-sdn-alwijha24-albalad-bank-mt.summary: Sudan's Albalad Bank launched "Baladna Bibasata" in Khartoum, a USSD banking service built with MTN Sudan that needs neither internet nor a smartphone. It is aimed in particular at letting humanitarian organisations pay beneficiaries. Its technical partner, Smart Solutions, said it is the first step towards a services platform modelled on M-Pesa. The launch date is not stated.

2026-10-06-sdn-sudanese-banks-and-the-po.summary: An opinion piece argues that Sudan's banks are investing too slowly in electronic services at a moment when war and high inflation have made cash costly and risky and disrupted branch networks. The author presents the post-war period as a chance to build an economy less dependent on cash.

2026-10-06-sen-apanews-ai-judicial-archi.summary: A high court in the Dakar suburbs has begun piloting a locally deployed AI application to digitise, manage and analyse judicial archives, with UNDP and Korean funding. Computing and digitisation equipment was handed to the justice ministry's dematerialisation directorate, and a phased national rollout is planned with no cost or timetable stated.

2026-10-06-sen-aps-senegal-digital-facto.summary: Senegal's telecommunications ministry signed a US$150 million partnership convention, nearly CFA 88 billion, with an Africa investment council and the Indian firm Blue Cloud Softech Solutions under the Senegal Digital Factory project. It covers local assembly of electronic devices, quality control, certification and intellectual property; the ministry puts computer hardware imports at CFA 419 billion a year.

2026-10-06-sen-aps-senum-smtd-backbone-i.summary: Senegal's and Mali's state fibre operators inaugurated the interconnection of their national backbones at the Kidira-Diboli border crossing on 5 October, to secure and diversify routes between the two countries. No capacity or cost is given.

2026-10-06-sle-sierraloaded-nra-asycuda-.summary: Sierra Leone's revenue authority has begun consultations with security agencies and local stakeholders at the Jendema border crossing as it prepares to launch the ASYCUDA World customs system there. The system will automate import, export and transit procedures; no launch date is given.

2026-10-06-som-somalia-moves-to-link-nat.summary: Somalia's identity authority is moving to link its registration services to HALMEEL, the national unified public service delivery centre, where an area has been set aside for it. The aim is one national identity across several government services; the integration is planned and not yet in place.

2026-10-06-swz-who-was-held-accountable-.summary: Eswatini senators asked on 5 October whether anyone had been held to account for the pension crisis at the state posts and telecommunications corporation, after Parliament approved the government guarantee for its US$26 million World Bank loan under the Digital Eswatini Project. The ICT minister said E26 million of the loan goes to the post office pension fund, affecting about 500 employees, and that the bank will manage and audit the loan.

2026-10-06-tanesco-modernizes-its-custom.summary: Tanzania's energy minister launched new customer service systems for the state power utility on 6 October: an AI-powered assistant available round the clock, a portal and a dedicated unit for large customers, and a 185 hotline, with a revised service charter.

2026-10-06-techcabal-airtel-money-ipo-ni.summary: Airtel Money's London listing leaves out its Nigerian business. Its prospectus, as reported, says a Central Bank of Nigeria directive required it to transfer its 25% stake in SmartCash back to Airtel's Nigerian network company, for US$3 million; Nigeria made up 1.24% of the unit's quarterly revenue and 6.02% of its customers at June 2026.

2026-10-06-techcabal-south-africans-bypa.summary: Half of 903 South Africans surveyed had got round their employer's restrictions on AI tools in the past year, an Oliver Wyman partner told a cybersecurity roundtable in Johannesburg, citing a report due in November. He said 35% had seen AI-generated work passed off as human, and that consumer trust in AI rose from 11% in 2023 to 44% in 2026.

2026-10-06-tgo-republicoftogo-voix-du-to.summary: Togo's Voix du Togo pilot, backed by UNDP, is collecting voice and text in Kabiye, Ewe and Moba to train AI models for public services in local languages. Contributors are paid through a dedicated platform, linguists and communities validate the data, and field agents collect it where phones and internet are scarce.

2026-10-06-tiktok-sued-over-nigeria-blac.summary: A second report of the suit over TikTok access in four northern Nigerian states, summarised above, frames it as a test of platform accountability and digital rights.

2026-10-06-tomorrownow-how-zambia-is-bui.summary: Zambia's meteorological department and Ministry of Agriculture began building a Digital Climate Advisory Service in late 2025 with TomorrowNow, sending farmers SMS advice tuned to four-by-four-kilometre squares. The department's director said it reached about 35,000 farmers last season in seven local languages and aims for one million next season, adding three crops and livestock.

2026-10-06-tun-lapresse-douane-ia-circui.summary: Tunisian Customs said on 6 October 2026 that it has used AI in its risk analysis of declarations since May 2026. The share of declarations sent to the red channel for full inspection fell from 4.7% in 2025 to 2.6% in 2026. An official said customs could be paperless within 12 to 18 months.

2026-10-06-tun-techafricanews-orange-foc.summary: Orange Tunisie and Focus Tunisie announced a partnership to offer companies cloud and infrastructure resources hosted and operated in Tunisia, pitched on control over where data sits. No value, capacity or start date is given.

2026-10-06-tun-tuniscope-interieur-casie.summary: Tunisia's interior ministry, answering a deputy's written question, said its plan for the criminal-record extract rests on digitising the record through interconnection with the justice ministry, to update judgments, and the finance ministry, to enter fines automatically. The aim is faster issue of the extract.

2026-10-06-tza-ucsaf-250-ict-laboratorie.summary: Tanzania's Universal Communications Service Access Fund said on 5 October 2026 it will build 250 ICT laboratories of 20 computers each in public schools this financial year, instead of its earlier provision of about five computers per school. It reports more than 1,121 schools equipped so far and 2,166 subsidised towers completed in 2,306 wards.

2026-10-06-uga-monitor-ag-2021-digital-n.summary: Uganda's Attorney General told a parliamentary committee that the supplier of the digital number plate system has consistently failed the core obligations of its 2021 contract, which the newspaper reports him declaring null and illegal. Defaults cited include no training of Ugandan staff and no transfer of the system's technology to the state enterprise.

2026-10-06-uga-nilepost-fitspa-fintech-c.summary: Fintech firms, regulators and development partners at Uganda's eighth annual fintech conference called for interoperable systems, shared digital infrastructure and stronger data standards, to move from separate products towards connected services.

2026-10-06-vodacom-western-cape-invests-.summary: Vodacom says it is investing more than R500 million in its Western Cape network this financial year. About R380 million goes to modernising the radio network at more than 50 sites, with 4G capacity upgrades, new 5G sites and backup power in townships including Khayelitsha, Delft and Mitchells Plain.

2026-10-06-woan-is-dead-but-measurable-i.summary: South Africa's withdrawal of the requirement to reserve high-demand spectrum for a wireless open access network ends a seven-year impasse and frees that spectrum for licensing by the regulator. Commentators in this analysis ask how the competition and transformation aims the network was meant to serve will now be delivered, and press for measurable obligations in its place.

2026-10-06-xaf-connectingafrica-saudi-ai.summary: An analysis asks whether Saudi Arabia's spending on data centres, AI and cloud can reach Africa while the kingdom is under attack from the Houthis. It cites the US$300 million committed to the infrastructure company WIOCC by a Saudi investor with the Africa Finance Corporation, and an investor's view that the conflict does not reduce Saudi capacity to do business.

2026-10-06-xaf-digitnomics-auc-africanen.summary: The African Union Commission, supported by the AfricaNenda Foundation, is developing a regulatory framework for a single African digital payments market without a common currency. It covers licence passporting, interoperability standards, anti-money-laundering rules, consumer protection and data governance under a proposed ten-year roadmap, with Nigeria and Ghana discussed as a first corridor. The consultation's date is not given.

2026-10-06-xaf-ictworks-fcdo-78-question.summary: A commentary notes that across 78 questions at the UK development minister's first parliamentary scrutiny session on 15 September, nobody raised digital development, connectivity or digital public infrastructure. The author reads that as the sector being moved out of the development brief rather than merely short of budget.

2026-10-06-xaf-techcabal-amr-data-gap.summary: A contributed analysis argues that Africa's response to antimicrobial resistance is held back by missing laboratory data. It cites a WHO estimate that one in five laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections in its African Region in 2023 was resistant to antibiotics, a figure that cannot count infections never tested.

2026-10-06-xss-reuters-world-bank-africa.summary: The World Bank's October Africa Economic Update urges Sub-Saharan governments to invest in AI for productivity and jobs, pointing to low-cost applications on affordable devices, shared data centres and stronger data-protection laws. It puts the region's 2026 growth at 4.3%, 0.3 of a point above its April forecast.

2026-10-06-zaf-parliament-broadcasting-d.summary: South Africa's parliamentary committee on communications said on 6 October 2026 that delays to the Broadcasting Digital Migration programme leave the state paying for analogue and digital transmission at once. The analogue switch-off is suspended and before the courts for a second time. The programme began in 2008, with switch-off first due on 1 November 2011.

2026-10-06-zambia-ready-to-sign-us-healt.summary: Zambia's health minister said the five-year health memorandum with the United States is finalised and due for signature this week, after negotiators removed a clause requiring Zambia to share specimens from its disease-surveillance system. The revised text also addresses health data, intellectual property and benefit sharing; this account puts US funding at US$1.5 billion over five years, tapering annually, and an opposition party wants the final text published before signing.

2026-10-06-zambia-us-finalise-3-6-billio.summary: A second account of the Zambian health minister's briefing puts the money to be mobilised for the sector at US$3.6 billion and gives Thursday as the signing day. The minister said the contested clauses on data protection, intellectual property, benefit sharing and specimens have all been reviewed, and that the specimen-sharing obligation is gone entirely.

2026-10-06-zimbabwe-eyes-indias-upi-tech.summary: Zimbabwe's central bank is negotiating with NPCI International to build a real-time payments system on India's UPI technology, linking banks, mobile-money operators and fintechs. The governor told Bloomberg an agreement is possible by 31 October 2026; cross-border payments and remittances are not part of the first deployment.

2026-10-07-10th-afrigeo-symposium-opens-.summary: The tenth symposium of Africa's earth observation community opened at Nigeria's space centre in Abuja. The head of the Nigerian space agency urged participants to turn data into intelligence that feeds decisions.

2026-10-07-africanenda-trains-journalist.summary: AfricaNenda says its payments regulation initiative with the African Union Commission has moved to implementation after a feasibility study found a harmonised framework workable. The study names eight priority areas, licence passporting and interoperability standards among them, and a phased roadmap.

2026-10-07-ago-africa-s-governments-alre.summary: Lawyer Ephraim Percy Kenyanito argues in Global Voices, on 7 October 2026, that internet shutdowns should be litigated as assembly cases. Kenyanito notes that the ECOWAS Court's May 2025 Senegal ruling turned on expression and never decided the assembly claim. Angola cut its internet for the first time in July 2025, during fuel-price protests.

2026-10-07-ai-takes-the-bench-before-the.summary: South Africa's judiciary has not finalised its draft policy on artificial intelligence, which a judges' conference in July sent to a steering committee to complete. Judges have meanwhile used a chatbot in rulings, in one case to reconcile payments and in another to test fabricated citations.

2026-10-07-bceao-ao-054-2026-plateforme-.summary: The Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) announced on 7 October 2026 that it had awarded its tender for the supply and deployment of a unified platform for detecting, analysing and responding to cybersecurity incidents to the Groupement Neurones Technologies. The call ran from 19 March to 29 May 2026. No contract value is given.

2026-10-07-bdi-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Burundi scored 0.70 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 45 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.40) and its weakest is Innovation and Ecosystem (0.20); the profile records an AI strategy validated in April 2026 but not adopted.

2026-10-07-bfa-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Burkina Faso scored 1.10 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and ranked 31 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Governance and Regulation (1.40) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.60).

2026-10-07-btwmedia-afrinic-ratifies-thr.summary: AFRINIC's board ratified three internet number-resource policies on 25 September 2026, all listed as awaiting implementation, btw.media reported on 7 October. They cover a quarantine for recovered IPv4 space (about six months to implement), documented exceptions to the 90% utilisation threshold (within 30 days), and hierarchical names for new AS-SETs, which waits on the MyAFRINIC v2 system.

2026-10-07-bwa-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Botswana scored 1.11 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and ranked joint 29 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its pillar scores are assigned values, and its strongest are Strategy and Vision and Ethics and Inclusion (1.40 each).

2026-10-07-c-te-d-ivoire-terrakora-ai-si.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's environment ministry signed a framework memorandum with an Ivorian company to map land use, monitor environmental change and estimate carbon stocks from satellite data, field observation and AI. The 2021 forest inventory put forest cover at 2.97 million hectares, 9.2% of the territory.

2026-10-07-caf-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: The Central African Republic scored 0.25 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 51 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Governance and Regulation (0.70); four pillars score 0.00.

2026-10-07-camerpressagency-transformati.summary: Chad's telecoms and digital economy minister Haliki Choua Mahamat opened a workshop in N'Djamena to validate the National Data Governance Strategy, reported on 7 October 2026. The strategy runs to 2030 and has seven pillars, including institutional governance, interoperability, personal data protection and skills, with health, education, agriculture, mining and digital finance named as priority sectors. No budget is given.

2026-10-07-cemac-la-beac-annonce-la-crat.summary: Closing a bankers' meeting at Bangui on 3 October, the governor of the Central African regional central bank announced a secondary market for debt, with other work to modernise payments and deepen the regional financial market.

2026-10-07-citizen-za-integrated-justice.summary: South Africa's Auditor-General told Parliament's justice committee on 6 October 2026 that the integrated justice system programme has not achieved its aims after about R4.9bn spent over a decade, citing unclear accountability and fragmented oversight. It found cybersecurity and access control weaknesses, and only 63 of 506 planned network upgrades completed by 31 August 2026.

2026-10-07-civ-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Côte d'Ivoire scored 2.03 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Developing tier and ranked 14 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (3.20) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.89); the profile records the SNIA 2030 strategy as adopted, no AI Act, and an AI agency only planned.

2026-10-07-civ-koaci-identification-beta.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's animal and fisheries ministry said on 7 October 2026 that data from a planned electronic livestock identification system with French firm Vet'tronic will be hosted and secured in the country, replying to press criticism of the agreement. It says hosting and security were referred to the state IT agencies SNDI and ANSUT, and a 12-month pilot at Vet'tronic's cost will cover 20,000 farm animals and 5,000 pets.

2026-10-07-cod-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: DR Congo scored 1.32 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and ranked 21 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (2.00) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.80); the profile notes an AI strategy launched in October 2025 and a data protection authority set up in 2024.

2026-10-07-cog-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: The Republic of the Congo scored 1.75 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and ranked 18 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Infrastructure and Data (2.22) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (1.00).

2026-10-07-cog-aci-artf-transferts-de-fo.summary: The Republic of the Congo's money transfer regulator, ARTF, said on 5 October 2026 it will enforce article 13 of the 2026 finance law, which requires every money transfer operator to register on its digital platform and declare all transfers. Operators refusing to connect face a fine of 20 million FCFA. Electronic terminals will go first to Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

2026-10-07-com-iga-bahrain-anaden-knowle.summary: Bahrain's Information and eGovernment Authority held its first knowledge-exchange session by video with the Comoros' National Digital Development Agency, ANADEN, reported on 7 October 2026, under a memorandum signed in June 2026. Bahrain shared how it governs and approves government IT projects and procurement. The stated aim is to raise the Comoros' score on the UN e-government index.

2026-10-07-cpv-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Cape Verde scored 0.91 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 38 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.70) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.11).

2026-10-07-dji-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Djibouti scored 0.93 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 35 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillars are Strategy and Vision and Infrastructure and Data (1.20 each) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.10).

2026-10-07-dpgs-for-dpi-collection-launc.summary: The Digital Public Goods Alliance launched a collection of 18 digital public goods for digital public infrastructure on 7 October at a regional forum in Santo Domingo. Each was assessed against technical criteria across identity, payments, data exchange, registries and trust systems.

2026-10-07-egy-enterpriseam-data-center-.summary: Egypt has about 15–20 MW of installed data centre IT capacity, and of 400–500 MW announced across four large projects only about 20 MW is committed, Post For Investment's chief executive told the EnterpriseAM Egypt Forum on 5 October 2026. He said his firm is forming a consortium to take an equity stake in a data centre; the four projects would need US$4–5bn.

2026-10-07-egy-mena-efinance-alibaba-clo.summary: Egypt's eFinance Investment Group, Alibaba Cloud and Nuvexa signed a memorandum, reported on 7 October 2026, to explore offering Alibaba Cloud services to Egyptian businesses through eFinance's locally hosted infrastructure, with data kept and processed in Egypt. Small businesses, agriculture and digital commerce come first. No sum is stated.

2026-10-07-egypt-personal-data-protectio.summary: Egypt's Personal Data Protection Center opened its electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications in early October, weeks before the data-protection law's compliance grace period ends on 31 October 2026, on a law firm's account. Applying needs a Digital Egypt login tied to an Egyptian national ID, so foreign controllers and processors must act through an authorised local representative.

2026-10-07-eri-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Eritrea scored 0.08 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, last of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its pillar scores are assigned by the index's fellows rather than built from indicators, with Human Capital highest at 0.30 and four pillars at zero; the profile found no AI strategy, data protection law or authority.

2026-10-07-eth-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Ethiopia scored 2.12 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Developing tier and ranked 11 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (3.70) and its weakest is Innovation and Ecosystem (1.00).

2026-10-07-eth-capital-visa-etta-contact.summary: ETTA Solutions and Visa signed a framework agreement to roll out 148,000 contactless payment devices to Ethiopian merchants, jointly financed by both companies. The devices connect to ETTA's ZooryaPay platform, licensed by the National Bank of Ethiopia, and are certified by the tax authority as cash registers and e-receipt terminals. Merchant transaction data feed credit profiles built by Optasia. No sum is stated.

2026-10-07-finguard-swz-smart-africa-gen.summary: A magazine account of the same Eswatini pilot of Smart Africa's gender impact assessment framework, which is meant to test whether digital programmes narrow the divide facing women. It names the tools differently from the ministry's account.

2026-10-07-gab-gabonreview-huawei-souver.summary: Huawei's Gabon subsidiary was received by the vice-president of the government on 6 October and restated its offer to support the state's digital transformation, in infrastructure, energy, cybersecurity and skills transfer. No agreement is reported.

2026-10-07-gab-union-magt-etat-conventio.summary: Gabon's incumbent operator and the digital-economy ministry signed a convention at Mouila on 6 October ceding to the State the 196 km Fougamou-Mouila fibre section the operator pre-financed and built, with two technical centres. It is the first segment of the first phase of the national backbone extension.

2026-10-07-gender-checks-proposed-for-di.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister, opening the gender impact assessment workshop in Mbabane, said the government wants such assessments built into digital policies and programmes before they are implemented.

2026-10-07-gha-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Ghana scored 2.23 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Developing tier and ranked 8 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (2.80) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (1.60).

2026-10-07-gha-bog-governor-remarks-saop.summary: Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama, launching SaoPay as a dedicated electronic money issuer in Accra on 7 October 2026, said Ghana had about 85.8 million registered mobile money accounts holding nearly GH¢40bn in August 2026, of which about 26.4 million had been used in the previous 90 days. He required issuers to reconcile funds three ways, join the sector's security operations centre and keep fees transparent.

2026-10-07-gin-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Guinea scored 0.76 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 40 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.80) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.00); the profile records an AI roadmap validated in December 2025 and a data protection authority not yet operating.

2026-10-07-gin-renforcement-des-capacite.summary: Guinea's universal service agency ANSUTEN launched the fourth edition of its digital skills programme, R-CUN, on 7 October 2026. Its director general said more than 3,200 people had been trained since 2022, about 40% of them women. He also cited 80 professional ICT certifications and nearly 2,000 computer kits distributed.

2026-10-07-gmb-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: The Gambia scored 0.91 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 37 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.30) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.22).

2026-10-07-gmb-foroyaa-three-year-biomet.summary: The Gambia began issuing a biometric driving licence valid for three years on 7 October 2026, at D2,550, replacing annual renewal under section 27(3) of the Motor Traffic Act. Centres open in Banjul and Kanifing first and in Basse and Janjanbureh last, on 22 October. The issuing agency is not named.

2026-10-07-gnb-aaigi-country-profile-ai-.summary: Guinea-Bissau scored 0.53 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 49 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Regional Integration (1.30) and its weakest is Strategy and Vision (0.10).

2026-10-07-gnq-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Equatorial Guinea scored 0.54 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 48 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.20) and its weakest is Innovation and Ecosystem (0.10); the profile finds no AI strategy and the authority under the 2016 data law not operating.

2026-10-07-gov-national-consumer-commiss.summary: South Africa's National Consumer Commission launched the National Opt-Out Registry on 7 October 2026, letting consumers block unwanted direct-marketing calls, SMSes and other messages free of charge. Direct marketers must register by December 2026 and may cleanse their lists free until April 2027; consumers can register blocks from May 2027.

2026-10-07-govt-steps-up-safety-against-.summary: Kenya's ICT minister told the Senate that the national incident response centre's digital forensics laboratory has received more than 200 investigation requests, most involving online abuse. A working group on online safety, a national referral directory and a review of gaps in the law have been agreed.

2026-10-07-iati-gb-gov-1-400199-411-cros.summary: The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office committed GBP 70,000 on 7 October 2026 through the University of the Witwatersrand, its IATI file shows. The project pairs South African ICT and media regulators with UK peers on AI, online safety and digital platforms. It runs to March 2027.

2026-10-07-lso-esccom-lca-cyber-mou.summary: The Eswatini Communications Commission and the Lesotho Communications Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on 3 October 2026 covering information exchange, joint research, staff development and cybersecurity cooperation, including coordinated incident response, awareness campaigns, training and audits. No budget or timetable is given.

2026-10-07-mar-bkam-document-de-travail-.summary: A Bank Al-Maghrib working paper on central bank digital currency says a proof of concept built with the IMF and World Bank confirmed that a retail CBDC is technically feasible in Morocco. It reports a cross-border CBDC experiment under way with the Central Bank of Egypt and treats any issuance as long-term and gradual. The views are the authors', not the bank's.

2026-10-07-mar-bkam-working-paper-dsge-s.summary: A Bank Al-Maghrib working paper dated 7 October 2026, by Michael Kumhof, Mohammed Mikou and Yassine Slaoui, builds an economic model calibrated on Morocco with banked and unbanked households, which can be run with or without a retail central bank digital currency. Under its baseline assumptions, introducing the currency brings modest output gains and modestly better resilience to financial shocks.

2026-10-07-mar-fivenines-nexus-20mw-ai-d.summary: The UK firm FiveNines Group was appointed to lead design management and procurement strategy for a 20MW AI data centre that Nexus Core Systems plans near Casablanca, Morocco, using Nvidia's Vera Rubin reference architecture. The announcement puts the wider Nexus AI Factory platform's target at 180MW on renewable power. No cost, permit or construction start is given.

2026-10-07-mdg-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Madagascar scored 0.63 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 47 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Infrastructure and Data (1.11) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.00); it takes top marks for its data protection law and Malabo Convention ratification but has no AI strategy.

2026-10-07-mitci-mauritius-meta-online-s.summary: The government and Meta held a full-day workshop at Ebene on 7 October 2026, opened by the Acting Prime Minister, on child safety, disinformation, impersonation and AI-generated content. Cybercrime cases rose from 491 in 2024 to 702 in 2025, and sextortion cases from 178 to 223. About 85% of the population uses Meta platforms.

2026-10-07-mli-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Mali scored 0.68 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 46 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Regional Integration (1.00) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.10); the profile records no AI strategy, an operating data protection authority and the Malabo Convention unsigned.

2026-10-07-mli-koutiala-84-elus-et-agent.summary: Eighty-four councillors and local government staff from 21 communes began a five-day course in office and collaborative software at Koutiala, Mali, on 6 October. The Centre de Formation des Collectivités Territoriales runs it with Koutiala town hall to improve local administration and public service.

2026-10-07-moz-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Mozambique scored 0.96 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 34 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its pillar scores are fellow-assigned, strongest Strategy and Vision (1.60) and weakest Implementation and Impact (0.30); the profile lists a draft AI strategy not yet adopted, an AI commission created and no data protection law.

2026-10-07-moz-timesdetodos-metical-sadc.summary: Mozambique's central bank governor said the metical could be used for payments between Southern African countries from January 2027 through the regional real-time settlement system, which is hosted at South Africa's central bank.

2026-10-07-mrt-are-controle-qualite-serv.summary: Mauritania's regulator ARE published on 7 October 2026 its re-inspection of mobile service quality carried out from 13 February to 22 March 2026, finding that Mattel, Mauritel and Chinguitel still breach their licence obligations. Voice service failed in several towns and on major roads (Chinguitel on nine routes, Mattel on six), and mobile data fell below 3G thresholds in 14 localities for Mauritel and 12 for Chinguitel.

2026-10-07-mrt-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Mauritania scored 0.99 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 33 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (2.22) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.22); the profile notes an AI strategy adopted in March 2024 and a 2017 data protection law still lacking implementing decrees.

2026-10-07-mus-lexpress-mauritius-teleco.summary: Mauritius Telecom and Amazon Web Services brought more than 125 delegates from state-owned enterprises to an executive workshop on cloud, data and AI at Ebene on 6 October, to identify uses in public services.

2026-10-07-mus-services-publics-numeriqu.summary: Information Technology Minister Avinash Ramtohul said on 6 October 2026 that about 500,000 Mauritians had registered on the Korek government services app. Of these, 250,000 had completed KYC checks. He put views of the digital driving licence at about 100,000 and of the pensions service at about 497,000. He said more services would be added.

2026-10-07-mwi-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Malawi scored 1.14 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and ranked 27 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Strategy and Vision (1.80) and its weakest are Innovation and Ecosystem and Implementation and Impact (0.50 each); its 2026-2031 AI strategy is still a draft and the Data Protection Act 2024 is in force.

2026-10-07-mwi-ppda-maneps-world-bank.summary: A World Bank team reviewed progress on Malawi's electronic procurement system MANePS with the procurement authority PPDA in early October 2026 and urged more training so that all public bodies use it by December 2026. As of 5 October the system had 7,417 registered suppliers, 216 of 250 targeted annual procurement plans published and 562 tenders. MANePS is World Bank-funded.

2026-10-07-na-paratus-oneweb-leo.summary: Paratus Namibia launched Eutelsat's OneWeb low-earth-orbit satellite internet service across Namibia on 7 October 2026, with capped and uncapped packages for homes and businesses. It follows a November 2025 agreement between Paratus and Eutelsat covering South Africa, Angola, Namibia, Botswana and Zambia. No prices are given.

2026-10-07-nam-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Namibia scored 1.11 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Emerging tier and joint 29th of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its pillar scores are fellow-assigned, strongest Strategy and Vision (2.20) and weakest Implementation and Impact (0.30); the AI strategy is at validation and AI and data protection bills are in draft.

2026-10-07-ner-country-profile-on-ai-gov.summary: Niger scored 0.73 out of 4 on the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, in the Nascent tier and ranked 42 of 54 states, in a country profile version 1.2 dated 7 October 2026. Its strongest pillar is Regional Integration (1.11) and its weakest is Implementation and Impact (0.10); the profile records no AI strategy and the data protection authority dissolved in June 2026.

2026-10-07-ner-sensibilisation-en-matier.summary: The national civil registration and identification awareness caravan ended in Niamey on 6 and 7 October 2026. It closed with a workshop run by the World Bank-funded WURI programme. The director general of territorial administration said fewer than 3 million people hold a national identity card. About 13 million are obliged to have one.

2026-10-07-nga-cooperative-digitalisatio.summary: Nigeria's supervising minister of cooperative affairs, Aliyu Sabi Abdullahi, told the National Cooperative Summit in Abuja on 7 October 2026 that the National Cooperative Identity Reform has begun at no cost to federal or state governments.
