2026-10-17-nga-nairametrics-cbn-nigeria-.summary: Central Bank of Nigeria governor Olayemi Cardoso said he met People's Bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng at the IMF-World Bank annual meetings to discuss cross-border payments, settlement, fintech and trade finance. He said Nigeria will pursue these on a coming visit to Beijing; no plans or timetable were disclosed.

2026-10-17-nga-nigerian-government-integ.summary: Nigeria's Border Control and Immigration Management System now holds more than 15 million migration records after integrating the earlier MIDAS system, Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo and Immigration Comptroller-General Kemi Nandap said in Abuja. They also described a system linking data across interior agencies and a data centre of more than eight petabytes.

2026-10-17-nga-punchng-nucap-3700-rural-.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani commissioned the first of 3,700 rural sites under the Nigeria Universal Communication Access Project in Bende, Abia State, on 16 October 2026. IHS Towers subsidiary GICL is deploying the towers with public Wi-Fi and Smart Village kits, starting at seven locations across Abia, Delta, Enugu, Plateau, Katsina and Ogun.

2026-10-17-sdn-ozyr-284-arab-monetary-fu.summary: The Arab Monetary Fund agreed to include Sudan in its technical assistance on digital transformation in 2027. It will also support Sudan on securities and sukuk and offer more training places.

2026-10-17-sdn-tpra-universal-service-fu.summary: Sudan's telecommunications and post regulator describes its universal service fund, which pays for telecom and postal services in remote and rural areas to narrow the digital divide. The fund's stated purposes include extending coverage, improving e-services outside cities, and supporting research and capacity building.

2026-10-17-som-national-institute-of-tel.summary: Somalia's National Institute of Telecommunications and Technology, part of the communications ministry, launched a programme to build government employees' digital skills, opening with a workshop on data protection, information security and privacy. The ministry says it wants the institute to take the lead in training civil servants and building public institutions' capacity.

2026-10-17-swz-positivenews-hhukwini-elm.summary: Eswatini's health minister visited Hhukwini Clinic to review the eLMIS and CMIS digital health systems, which the ministry runs in 250 health facilities. The systems are interoperable and use national identity numbers to identify patients, according to Eswatini Positive News.

2026-10-17-tun-servicesgov-finances-serv.summary: Tunisia's national administrative services portal lists the tax and payment services citizens can use online. Among them are paying fines online or by USSD, estimating vehicle registration tax, and calculating and paying Tunis municipal building tax.

2026-10-17-tza-simu-za-mkopo-zilivyo-mat.summary: Tanzania's data protection commission said it is investigating complaints about how lenders selling phones on credit collect and use borrowers' personal data. Its director general called the misuse unlawful.

2026-10-17-uga-more-than-3mn-tax-records.summary: Uganda Revenue Authority had linked 2.13 million of its 5.41 million individual taxpayer records to National Identification Numbers by 30 September 2026, leaving about 3.27 million unmatched, the finance ministry told Parliament. Taxpayers with linked records are due to log in with their NIN from 1 January 2027, and no end date has been set for TIN logins.

2026-10-17-zaf-mps-raise-alarm-after-hom.summary: South African MPs found self-service kiosks that Home Affairs bought under a 2024 project still undeployed, while licence fees keep running. The briefing was postponed after the director-general and chief financial officer did not attend, and no total cost was disclosed.

2026-10-17-zaf-sarb-nps-regulation-page.summary: The South African Reserve Bank explains how its National Payment System Department regulates the payment system for safety, efficiency and stability, including the prevention of fraud and money laundering. It says consumer protection in payments is the job of the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.

2026-10-17-zaf-sars-client-information-s.summary: South Africa's revenue service says its Client Information System, introduced in 2014, lets taxpayers register for and manage all their tax and customs registrations in a single profile. SARS is now merging each client's tax, customs and excise records into one consolidated profile.

2026-10-17-zaf-sars-guide-to-payment-rul.summary: South Africa's revenue service sets out the rules taxpayers must follow when paying it, by each payment channel, so that payments are allocated correctly. It warns that payments that do not follow the rules may be rejected.

2026-10-18-bfa-digitalmagazine-faso-digi.summary: Burkina Faso's virtual Faso Digital 2026 fair opened on 17 October 2026 with 201 solutions, selected from 208 entries in its innovation competition. Rwanda is guest of honour, according to Digital Magazine BF.

2026-10-18-civ-cybersecurite-en-cote-d-i.summary: A profile of Côte d'Ivoire's national information-systems security agency, created by decree in October 2024 to take over the work of the former IT directorate and the national CERT. It sets out the cyber laws the agency applies, the Budapest Convention ratified in July 2024 and the Malabo Convention ratified in April 2023.

2026-10-18-cod-au-beach-ngobila-de-kinsh.summary: WHO's Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, visited passenger screening at Kinshasa's Beach Ngobila river crossing on 18 October 2026, where the WHO-backed Preparedness Data Exchange platform supports Ebola surveillance. He said a similar electronic system would go live in Brazzaville the following week.

2026-10-18-gab-gabon-amendes-jusqu-a-50-.summary: Gabon promulgated by decree on 5 October 2026 a law ratifying its ordinance on social-network use, Gabon Media Time reported. Hosts or editors who fail to fight illicit content face a year in prison and fines of FCFA 5 million to 50 million, deepfakes are banned, and judges may order platform suspensions of up to 72 hours.

2026-10-18-gha-ghana-appoints-ai-focal-p.summary: Ghana's communications minister Sam George said every ministry now has an AI focal person and Cabinet ministers have been through an AI boot camp. A UNESCO-supported readiness assessment has mapped ministries and agencies, UNDP and UNESCO are training chief directors and directors, and cybersecurity and data protection laws are under review.

2026-10-18-gha-people-of-internet-biomet.summary: In an unsigned analysis, the outlet People of Internet argues that Ghana's plan to add biometric checks to SIM registration addresses a real gap but needs data safeguards written into the rules. It calls for purging legacy data, match-only queries, warrants for police access and a fallback when biometric reads fail. It draws on the communications minister's 7 September 2026 statement.

2026-10-18-gmb-undp-launches-e-monitor-p.summary: UNDP and The Gambia's Independent Electoral Commission launched e-Monitor Plus at Kololi on 13-15 October 2026, a platform pairing AI with human checking to track online misinformation, disinformation and hate speech before the 5 December 2026 presidential election. Civil society speakers warned that monitoring must not turn into censorship.

2026-10-18-ken-kna-tanui-iten-17000km-pu.summary: On 18 October 2026 the ICT Principal Secretary said a 17,000 km fibre project linking all public institutions is underway, run with the Communications Authority, ICT Authority and Kenya Power. A KSh13 billion private build of 27,000 km runs alongside it. The Elgeyo Marakwet governor said the county will waive all charges for companies laying fibre.

2026-10-18-ken-mps-probe-ai-classrooms-h.summary: Kenya's National Assembly gave its communication committee one month to report on how AI is used in education, health and the public sector, and on the rules that govern it. MPs said there is no national AI framework and are weighing a standalone AI law.

2026-10-18-lby-opening-of-ozone-telecom-.summary: Ozone (O3) Telecom Group opened in Benghazi and announced that the Medusa submarine cable has reached the city. It plans a 16,000 km fibre network, a Tier III data centre and a 5G trial by the end of 2026.

2026-10-18-ner-audience-du-president-du-.summary: Customs chiefs of the Sahel states confederation (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger) and Togo's revenue office met in Ouagadougou on 15 October 2026 to review progress on interconnecting their customs IT systems and validated a draft decision on certifying confederal origin. They reported to Captain Ibrahim Traoré the next day while finishing the text to create a customs union.

2026-10-18-nga-customs-afreximbank-plan-.summary: Nigeria Customs Service opened talks with Afreximbank on modernising the Sèmè–Kraké and Mfum–Ekok border corridors with Benin and Cameroon. The plans include a system for exchanging customs declarations between the three countries on a common data model; no cost or loan has been agreed.

2026-10-18-nga-jamb-moves-to-rescue-grad.summary: Nigeria's admissions board launched a service that lets candidates correct their records to match their national identity data. It is meant to help graduates who have been barred from national service for years by mismatched records.

2026-10-18-nga-ncc-launches-internet-gov.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission launched an Internet Governance Working Group at its first Internet Governance Symposium, held in Lagos on 15 October 2026. The commission called for wider cooperation on artificial intelligence, online fraud, privacy and child protection, and cited its Internet Code of Practice 2026 and a cyber resilience framework for the sector.

2026-10-18-sdn-sudandawn-commercial-regi.summary: Sudan's commercial registry has been almost entirely stalled for more than a week by a technical fault on the Baladna platform, which handles company and business-name filings, Sudan Dawn reported on 18 October 2026. Lawyers report a backlog of files and are calling for urgent intervention and a permanent fix.

2026-10-18-sen-diante-service-public-mod.summary: Senegal's civil-service minister said the physical and biometric audit of state employees, launched in June 2026, is still under way and has not yet confirmed any anomalies. He named e-Sénégal as the single access point for online procedures under the 2025–2029 public-service reform agenda.

2026-10-18-sle-sierra-leone-establishes-.summary: Sierra Leone has set up a national committee for UNESCO's Information for All Programme to align national policy with it, the Foreign Ministry announced. A UNESCO-government conference on information integrity held in Freetown on 28 September 2026 drew delegates from 41 countries.

2026-10-18-zaf-vodacoms-technology-chief.summary: Vodacom's group technology chief said the company will install its own GPUs first in its new Egypt data centre, then build a GPU-as-a-service node in Kenya, with South Africa last. The Egypt facility, built with Elsewedy Electric and Cassava, is expected to draw about $200m in its first phase.

2026-10-19-bfa-le-faso-digital-2026-l-ar.summary: Burkina Faso's regulator ARCEP reported about 3,514 white zones with no operator, nearly 40% of localities and some 4.7 million people, at the Le Faso Digital conference on 19 October 2026. Its figures at 30 June 2026 show about 30 million mobile subscriptions, nearly 20 million mobile-internet and 328,764 fixed-internet subscriptions.

2026-10-19-caf-developmentaid-pgnsp-mobi.summary: The Central African Republic opened an invitation for bids on 19 October 2026 for goods: kits to set up mobile money agents. The tender falls under the World Bank-financed Public Sector Digital Governance Project. No budget is stated and no award has been made.

2026-10-19-cmr-digitalbusiness-herve-tiw.summary: In an interview with Digital Business Africa, digital transformation and AI expert Hervé Tiwa argues that Cameroon has a legal gap on AI and should fill it. He favours a broader digital law that absorbs the cybercrime law rather than a separate law for each new technology, with clear prohibitions against misuse such as disinformation and deepfakes.

2026-10-19-cmr-itweb-camtel-socadel-infr.summary: Cameroon's Camtel and electricity utility Socadel signed a memorandum of understanding in Yaoundé on 16 October 2026 to study infrastructure sharing. It would pair Camtel's national fibre backbone with Socadel's poles and rights-of-way to extend fibre along overhead power lines. Feasibility studies and pilot sites come next.

2026-10-19-cod-who-deploys-pdx-preparedn.summary: WHO's Africa office has deployed its AI-based Preparedness Data Exchange in the DR Congo, the first country to get it, linking national epidemic intelligence to a regional platform for the 47 states of the WHO African Region during the Ebola response. Dure Technologies and WHO also installed the Voyage Santé digital entry-screening system at N'djili airport and the Nord Bangui border post.

2026-10-19-dza-mesrs-baddari-gpu-calcul-.summary: Algeria's higher-education ministry agreed on 19 October 2026 with public and private companies to set up a joint framework for drafting a 2030 roadmap to finance GPU-based high-performance computing and AI research capacity. Its four aims are company co-funding of GPUs, research steered to economic needs, a stronger national AI and data centre, and recruiting diaspora talent.

2026-10-19-gab-gabon-lidentification-for.summary: Gabon's law 003/2026 of 5 October 2026, published on 9 October, requires individuals and legal entities using social networks and online platforms to formally identify themselves. Gabon Media Time reports that article 4 does not say what documents are needed, how identity will be checked or how existing accounts are treated. It also does not make the personal identification number mandatory for this purpose.

2026-10-19-gab-gabon-securite-alimentair.summary: Gabon's food safety agency AGASA will launch Nexus, a digital platform for food and plant-health operators, on 2 November 2026. Operators will be able to apply remotely for approvals, import authorisations and health certificates, and track their files. Operators are asked to visit AGASA offices from 20 to 29 October with identity documents to update their data and get login details.

2026-10-19-gab-mediation-financiere-le-g.summary: Gabon's Comité national économique et financier (CNEF) was to launch financial mediation in Libreville on 26 October 2026, giving customers of banks, microfinance institutions and payment providers a free, confidential route to settle disputes, with agreements enforceable. The mechanism rests on a 2020 CEMAC consumer-protection regulation, a 2024 decree and two orders of January 2025; a complaint to the institution must come first, and Axcèle Saturnin Kissangou-Mouele was named mediator in June for a three-year term.

2026-10-19-gha-imani-africa-missing-plum.summary: John Sitsofe Mensah, an IMANI associate, argues that Ghana needs a whole-of-government data exchange to connect state databases, now that identity and payment systems are in place. He warns against agencies hosting core records on offshore cloud servers instead of the national government cloud run by NITA, citing legal, sovereignty and vendor lock-in risks. He also says a single exchange would stop citizens being asked for information the state already holds.

2026-10-19-lbr-biometricupdate-mps-scrut.summary: Liberia's House of Representatives referred a proposed $52 million build-operate-transfer concession for a national ID and civil registration system to a joint committee on 16 October 2026, giving it two weeks to report. The system would hold records for up to 10 million people, and civil society groups are asking for scrutiny of the financial terms and data protection. The National Identification Registry says fewer than 800,000 people hold a national ID.

2026-10-19-lby-techafricanews-o3-group-f.summary: Libya's O3 Group, a private telecoms company founded in 2024 and based in Benghazi, set out its infrastructure plans as the Medusa submarine cable made its first Libyan landing at Benghazi on 17 October 2026. The plans include a 12,000 to 13,000 km national fibre network, a Tier III data centre in Benghazi and a mobile service. A second Medusa landing is planned for Tripoli.

2026-10-19-le-gimac-et-papss-card-posent.summary: GIMAC, the Central African interbank card network, and PAPSS Card agreed the practical terms of a partnership at working sessions in Yaoundé on 13 and 14 October 2026, with a convention to be signed in the following days. The plan would let GIMAC cards issued by CEMAC banks be accepted across the PAPSS network and PAPSS cards be used in the CEMAC zone, and the sessions produced a roadmap of priority actions, owners and deadlines. GIMAC's interim director general Guy Noël Londongo tied the move to the BEAC joining the AU-backed PAPSS system.

2026-10-19-mar-programme-gouvernemental-.summary: Morocco's new government presented its 2026–2031 programme to parliament on 19 October 2026. It commits to a platform and legal framework for data exchange between public bodies, and a law barring under-15s from social media. It also promises 5,000 trained AI specialists, fibre to 80% of homes, 4G everywhere and a sovereign national cloud.

2026-10-19-mastercard-moovn-five-year-ea.summary: Mastercard and Moovn Technologies signed a five-year agreement, announced on 19 October 2026, to add Mastercard prepaid cards, tokenisation, online acceptance, Pay Local and cross-border transfers to the MoovnPay wallet. Pay Local is to expand across Kenya and Tanzania, and the Shooga prepaid Mastercard portfolio is to launch next.

2026-10-19-moz-altas-taxas-cobradas-no-n.summary: Fees at Mozambique's new Centro Pronto document centre have drawn public anger, as the private centre adds its own fee and 16% VAT to the state fee. An adult identity-card renewal costs MZN 1,058.12 in total, of which the state fee is MZN 160. A driving-licence renewal costs MZN 5,201.84 and an express passport renewal MZN 10,725.10.

2026-10-19-moz-intic-eleito-comite-de-ge.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC was elected to the management committee of ANCA-CERT, Africa's network of cyber incident-response teams, for Southern Africa at the African Network of Cybersecurity Authorities meeting in Rabat on 12 October 2026. ANCA admitted five new members, taking it from 28 to 33 states, and Mozambique reported its cybersecurity and cybercrime laws in force since 29 September.

2026-10-19-mus-sil-tcs-mou-digital-trans.summary: Mauritius' State Informatics Ltd signed a memorandum of understanding with India's Tata Consultancy Services on digital transformation, technology cooperation and innovation. IT Minister Avinash Ramtohul said it would support knowledge transfer and local digital skills, and he pointed to the planned AI City and the automation of public-sector workflows.

2026-10-19-nga-techcabal-cheaper-fibre-f.summary: A TechCabal analysis of Nigerian Communications Commission portal data from July 2026 finds that state right-of-way fees do not neatly predict where fibre has been built. Ogun charges up to ₦6,600 per metre yet has 4,246 km of fibre, while Jigawa and Zamfara, which waive the fee, have 970 km and 1,101 km. The piece notes that construction costs and other factors are not captured in the portal data.

2026-10-19-nga-techcabal-onafriq-baxi-sa.summary: Onafriq had been negotiating the sale of Baxi, its Nigerian agent-banking business, before it announced a shutdown on 16 October 2026, according to UK-filed accounts approved on 29 July 2026. The accounts record a non-binding memorandum of terms for a full divestment, agency services revenue down 56% to $13.4 million in 2024, and ₦19.9 billion in overdrafts owed to Zenith Bank and Stanbic IBTC.

2026-10-19-sdn-suna-pm-forms-national-cy.summary: Sudan's prime minister issued a decision on 19 October 2026 forming a National Mechanism to Combat Informatics Crimes, chaired by an assistant attorney general. It is tasked with combating cybercrime and publications deemed harmful to the state and society, monitoring media and social platforms, and taking preventive and legal action, including lawsuits on the state's behalf.

2026-10-19-sle-statssl-mock-census-joint.summary: Sierra Leone's planning minister, the Statistician-General and UNFPA's country representative monitored the 2026 mock census enumeration at Hill Station, Freetown, on 19 October 2026. The mock census is testing census methods, the digital data-collection system and quality assurance ahead of the national census scheduled for December 2026, Statistics Sierra Leone said.

2026-10-19-som-biometricupdate-halmeel-u.summary: Somalia's Unified Public Service Delivery Center, known as Halmeel, plans to launch a unified digital government services platform by the end of March 2027, starting with about 70 services. The national ID will be the only accepted credential, its director general told Biometric Update. Halmeel, created by Cabinet resolution on 23 April, is integrating with the national ID agency NIRA, which had about 2 million people registered as of October 2026.

2026-10-19-som-developmentaid-eardip-api.summary: Somalia invited expressions of interest on 19 October 2026 for the design, deployment and operation of a government API gateway, a government single sign-on system and a national digital government portal. The work falls under the World Bank-financed Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project.

2026-10-19-swz-govt-plans-ai-services-at.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry presented a proposed platform for reaching government services and payments by mobile device at the Global AI & Digital Summit in Seoul on 19 October 2026. No implementation date was announced. The ministry also cited digital-skills targets of 300,000 citizens through a UAE partnership and 200,000 through a World Bank-supported initiative.

2026-10-19-swz-senators-back-e5m-fines-1.summary: Eswatini's Senate adopted the ICT portfolio committee's report on the Critical Infrastructure Bill No. 16 of 2025 on 19 October 2026. It backs fines of up to E5 million for companies, and E1 million or up to 10 years' imprisonment for individuals, for offences against telecom towers, fibre and energy lines.

2026-10-19-syc-seychelles-targets-2027-s.summary: Seychelles plans to begin implementing a digital human resource management system in 2027, Vice-President Sebastien Pillay announced after meeting Canadian vendor FreeBalance at State House on 14 October 2026. The system would cover employee records, payroll, performance management and workforce analytics. Pillay said technology alone would not improve efficiency unless administrative procedures are also reviewed.

2026-10-19-tcd-digitalisation-de-leftp-l.summary: Chad's higher-education ministry opened a workshop in N'Djamena on 14 October 2026 to validate a national strategy for digitising technical and vocational training, backed by the Francophonie's education institute IFEF. The strategy has three axes: data-driven governance, digital infrastructure in training centres, and digital skills and teaching quality.

2026-10-19-tgo-togo-signs-huawei-agreeme.summary: Togo and Huawei signed a memorandum of understanding in Shenzhen on 16 October 2026 covering energy, smart transport and smart customs systems. It includes technology transfer and local skills development, and was signed during Council President Faure Gnassingbé's visit to China from 9 to 16 October. No value was given.

2026-10-19-tun-tunisie-moins-de-paperass.summary: Tunisia's government told parliament its 2025-2027 programme to simplify some 2,250 administrative procedures is about 70% done, with around 80% of them to be digitised fully or in part. It opened 34 digital service houses in 21 governorates in 2026 and plans 68 more from 2027 to 2030.

2026-10-19-uga-43-000-elderly-ugandans-l.summary: Uganda's gender ministry said, as reported on 19 October 2026, that about 43,000 eligible older people cannot draw SAGE cash grants because the birth dates on their national ID cards make them appear too young. SAGE reaches about 318,000 of more than 2.4 million potential beneficiaries, and mobile-money payment is being piloted.

2026-10-19-xaf-au-innofest-26-youth-hack.summary: The African Union Commission convened the first African Community of Practice on Technology-Facilitated Violence Against Women and Girls and launched the SafeTech Africa HackLab for innovators aged 18 to 35. Both took place at AU InnoFest'26 in Addis Ababa on 29 and 30 September 2026, with UNDP, UNFPA, UN Women and the Spotlight Initiative.

2026-10-19-xaf-biometricupdate-sadx-ben-.summary: Benin, Ghana and Rwanda have connected their national identity systems through the Smart Africa Data Exchange and are moving toward real-world testing of cross-border ID verification, Biometric Update reported on 19 October 2026. Pilots are planned for Benin-Rwanda air travel and Ghana-Benin land crossings. No date for live testing has been announced.

2026-10-19-xea-mapping-digital-connectiv.summary: The African Development Bank built a digital intelligence platform using Ookla speed-test data to rank district-level connectivity gaps across 11 East African countries, reported on 19 October 2026. It combines 51 months of tests, January 2022 to March 2026, with data on 93,125 health and education facilities in 8,925 administrative areas.

2026-10-19-xgl-govinsider-jargon-problem.summary: Speakers at an Open Government Partnership webinar on 15 October 2026 said the label 'digital public infrastructure' keeps the public out of designing digital ID, payment and data systems, and urged governments to make clear where people can take part. Nigeria's open-government plan carries a DPI commitment led by NITDA, including a pilot of accessibility standards in 10 federal agencies.

2026-10-19-xwa-the-communications-direct.summary: The ECOWAS Commission's Communications Directorate held the second meeting of its Disinformation Working Group in Accra, Ghana, on 15 and 16 October 2026. The meeting brought together ECOWAS institutions and partners to plan a coordinated regional response to information integrity challenges.

2026-10-19-zaf-bma-vehicle-targeting-sys.summary: South Africa's Border Management Authority launched its Vehicle Targeting System at Lebombo Port of Entry on 18 October 2026. It reports 83 vehicles worth R46.6 million recovered in the six months since the system went live at land ports on 1 April 2026, with rollout to eight land ports planned by the end of February 2027.

2026-10-19-zaf-citizen-gauteng-egov-weig.summary: Gauteng's e-Government department said on 19 October 2026 it will decide whether to pursue criminal charges against student Joel Cedras, who exposed a flaw in the e-Panic Button app, once an investigation report due the following week is in. The DA's Michael Waters said the department had sought his prosecution, and that police advised the app's developers would have to open the case.

2026-10-19-zaf-electoral-commission-and-.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission announced on 19 October 2026 a partnership with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa to counter disinformation ahead of the 4 November 2026 local government elections. It follows a similar framework signed with the platforms before the 2024 national and provincial elections.

2026-10-20-bdi-wb-op00476457-pafen-porta.summary: Burundi's IDA-funded PAFEN project issued a request for proposals on 20 October 2026 for the national e-Gouv public services portal. Bids are due on 4 December 2026. The winning firm must put at least eleven priority services fully online, use open-source components and connect the portal to government registries. The work is set at twelve months, with the first phase live by week 36.

2026-10-20-ben-presidence-de-la-republiq.summary: Benin created a National Digital Committee under the President of the Republic by decree n° 2026-579 of 2 September 2026, reported on 20 October 2026. The head of state chairs it and it meets quarterly. It tracks digital projects through a quarterly dashboard from a permanent secretariat, and gives prior opinions on structuring digital projects and on technology partnerships that could affect national digital sovereignty.

2026-10-20-bfa-autorite-de-regulation-de.summary: Burkina Faso appointed W. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, previously president of the Conseil supérieur de la communication, to head the new regulator formed by merging that council with the data-protection commission CIL. The decree is dated 16 October 2026.

2026-10-20-bfa-bulletin-agrometeorologiq.summary: Météo Burkina Faso publishes a ten-day agrometeorological bulletin covering rainfall, temperature and humidity anomalies and vegetation index data. The page seen on 20 October 2026 lists a latest update for 13 to 19 October 2026, describing monsoon winds with some harmattan incursions. Earlier updates cover periods back to early September 2026.

2026-10-20-bfa-les-regulateurs-du-numeri.summary: The second session of the UEMOA national digital regulators' committee (CRNN) opened in Ouagadougou on 20 October 2026 and runs until 22 October. The agenda covers regulation of digital financial services, sharing of telecoms infrastructure and community roaming. Burkina Faso currently chairs the committee, and the first session was held in Cotonou from 28 to 31 October 2025.

2026-10-20-civ-donnees-portail-officiel-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's official open data portal, data.gouv.ci, listed 211 datasets when captured on 12 November 2026. Economy led with 73 datasets and society followed with 39; the newest update was dated 20 October 2026.

2026-10-20-cmr-donnees-modelisation-geom.summary: Cameroon's national climate observatory ONACC lists a library of 11 data, modelling and geomatics products on its website, seen on 20 October 2026. They include a national climate and geospatial database on PostgreSQL/PostGIS, risk maps, Sentinel satellite imagery, drought indices and web services. The page says connection to the database tables will be added later.

2026-10-20-cmr-modernisation-de-la-fonct.summary: Cameroon's public-service ministry MINFOPRA met on 20 October 2026 to validate the national public-services portal servicepublic.gov.cm and plan its rollout, and presented My MINFOPRA, an internal platform for staff to share documents and circulars. The portal is meant to be the single official source of information on administrative procedures, with a mobile app to follow.

2026-10-20-cmr-servicepublic-gov-cm-minf.summary: Cameroon's public-service minister Joseph Le reviewed the servicepublic.gov.cm portal on 20 October 2026 before its launch: it lists 1,250 procedures in 25 categories in French and English, with an app for offline use and a proposed 90-day publicity campaign across the ten regions. He asked for a new name and look for the portal and a review of the contract with its provider, ADWA SARL.

2026-10-20-dza-algerie54-solidarite-plat.summary: Algeria's Ministry of National Solidarity launched a digital platform on 20 October 2026 that tracks the progress and spending of the sector's investment projects nationwide through a dashboard for the central administration. For 2027 it plans an AI-built national map of persons with special needs and an AI system to detect fraud in solidarity schemes.

2026-10-20-dza-m-kamel-baddari-preside-l.summary: Algeria's fifth cross-ministry meeting on its national AI strategy, chaired by higher-education minister Kamel Baddari on 20 October 2026, gave four months to deliver a large language model on Algerian tax law, built with the tax directorate. It also made first estimates of public money for AI infrastructure towards a joint financing fund and proposed a national AI doctoral school with 102 places.

2026-10-20-egy-digital-egypt-13-5m-users.summary: Mahmoud Badawi, Egypt's assistant ICT minister for digital transformation, told Egypt Forum 2026 that the Digital Egypt platform had about 13.5 million users. He put growth at about 30% a year, with about 90% of use on mobile phones. He described a digital-vault prototype holding official documents in electronic form, first applied to work contracts. He also set out plans for generative AI help on the platform.

2026-10-20-egy-launch-of-chat-egypt-plat.summary: Egypt's Cabinet Media Center launched "Chat Egypt" at Egypt Forum 2026, an AI platform for monitoring, verifying and answering rumours, with sections for news, awareness, statistics and citizens' questions. Ministries, agencies and governorates each upload their own verified data, and it held more than 21,000 entries at launch.

2026-10-20-egy-youm7-digital-sovereignty.summary: Egypt's Communications and IT Minister Raafat Hindy presented a digital sovereignty strategy with five pillars at the Digital Egypt session of Egypt Forum 2026, reported on 20 October 2026. The pillars are sovereign digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, AI development, data protection and technology talent. He defined sovereignty as state control over its own infrastructure, data and services, not isolation.

2026-10-20-gab-afrique-centrale-lartac-v.summary: Central African telecoms regulators are meeting in Libreville on 20 and 21 October 2026 to revise the founding texts of ARTAC. Minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba opened the 4th extraordinary session on 20 October. Delegations from DR Congo, Congo, Cameroon, Chad, Equatorial Guinea, the Central African Republic and São Tomé and Príncipe are reviewing revised statutes, rules of procedure and financial regulations.

2026-10-20-gha-data-protection-commissio.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission said, in a statement reported on 20 October 2026, that publishing the names, signatures and financial-assistance records of 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa exposed them to identity theft and fraud. It told the Minority Caucus, the Foreign Affairs Ministry and media houses that registering as data controllers does not exempt them from the Data Protection Act. It urged redaction and announced a review of the legal basis for the disclosures.

2026-10-20-gha-nia-rolls-out-online-ghan.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority opened an online Ghana Card replacement service for citizens living in 11 countries, including the UK, US, Canada and the UAE, so they no longer have to travel home. The service is also available at four Prestige 24/7 centres in Ghana, and an online update service is to follow.

2026-10-20-gha-stanbic-ghana-explores-st.summary: Stanbic Bank Ghana and Hong Kong-based RD Technologies said, as reported on 20 October 2026, that they are exploring a stablecoin-backed cross-border settlement service for Ghanaian importers paying Asian suppliers. Stanbic would handle onboarding, KYC and local-currency settlement, and RD Technologies the digital-asset rails. Next steps are regulatory engagement, technical validation and a controlled pilot, all subject to regulatory no-objection.

2026-10-20-gha-ug-secures-96000-gemini-a.summary: The University of Ghana secured more than 96,000 Google "Gemini for Education" licences for staff and students, announced at a two-day training workshop for faculty and administrators. No cost or term is stated, and use falls under the university's AI policy.

2026-10-20-gnb-26-tecnicos-capacitados-p.summary: The Boa Governação project trained 26 regional planning delegates, regional secretaries and civil-society staff in Bissau on 1-3 September 2026 to enter and update data in Guinea-Bissau's Plans and Projects Information System (SIPP). Anyone can consult the system's public side to see regional development plans, ongoing projects and who runs them.

2026-10-20-iati-xm-dac-7-ppr-260001129-e.summary: The Netherlands foreign ministry committed EUR 450,000 on 20 October 2026 to a digital rights project in Nigeria, running to September 2029. The grant funds a barometer on how the Cybercrimes Act is applied, legal aid and strategic litigation. It also trains lawyers, judges and journalists.

2026-10-20-ispa-urges-free-data-for-poor.summary: South Africa's Internet Service Providers' Association called on 20 October 2026 for a free basic data allowance for people below the poverty line. It said the communications department has listed a cost-to-communicate programme for years without a substantive plan. It also said the Competition Commission's proposed Electronic Communications Act amendments are unlikely to be finalised before the end of 2027.

2026-10-20-lbr-liberia-to-digitalize-16-.summary: Liberia's Office of the Chief Information Officer met ministries and agencies on 17 and 18 October 2026 to validate 16 priority government services for digitalisation with World Bank support. They assessed readiness and procurement for an e-Liberia one-stop portal, a Government Service Bus for real-time data sharing, National Data Center upgrades and digitised County Service Centers.

2026-10-20-legal-aid-sa-resets-all-passw.summary: Legal Aid South Africa ordered a password reset for all staff and compulsory cyber-security training after phishing e-mails posing as National Prosecuting Authority summonses circulated around 8 and 9 October 2026. It said it knew of no successful breach, and the Information Regulator said it had received no security-compromise notification. This was reported on 20 October 2026.

2026-10-20-medusa-submarine-cable-system.summary: The Medusa submarine cable system completed its Pre-Laid Shore End installation in Benghazi, Libya, as reported on 20 October 2026. This is the pre-installed cable section between the landing site and the offshore connection point. No value or completion date was given.

2026-10-20-moz-clubofmozambique-governme.summary: Mozambique's government will track and monitor businesses operating on digital platforms, including online credit providers, under its recently approved decree on electronic transactions and e-commerce. The Council of Ministers' spokesperson said so on 20 October 2026. The Digital Transformation Agency is among the bodies that will supervise operators.

2026-10-20-moz-mocambique-prepara-formad.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC, UNDP and the National Elections Commission are training 26 institutional trainers on AI in election administration at Macaneta on 19-23 October 2026. The course covers AI ethics and governance, data protection, cybersecurity and spotting manipulated content, and INTIC called for oversight against misuse.

2026-10-20-mus-request-for-proposal-supp.summary: The Bank of Mauritius is tendering for the supply and implementation of a threat intelligence sharing platform for the banking sector. Encrypted bids close on 20 November 2026.

2026-10-20-nga-agency-unveils-dashboard-.summary: Voice of Nigeria reports NITDA's launch of a National Digital Literacy Dashboard to track progress towards 70% digital literacy by 2027 and 95% by 2030, with 248 organisations reporting about 2.76 million training achievements since January 2022. Women made up 32.9% of recorded participation, and NITDA's director-general said training counts are not proof of skill.

2026-10-20-nga-ncc-device-verification-q.summary: Nigeria's Communications Commission launched a Device Checker on 7 October 2026 that lets buyers dial *315# to see whether a phone is type approved, using its IMEI. An article on 20 October 2026 notes that 99% of smartphones are imported and about 63 million devices are sold each year, and questions how well the NCC can enforce compliance. Buyers of flagged phones have no standard refund route.

2026-10-20-nga-nitda-moves-to-boost-digi.summary: Nigeria's NITDA began its first IPv6 migration readiness training for federal ministries, departments and agencies, with AFRINIC and the Nigeria IPv6 Council, as reported on 20 October 2026. It runs in two streams, for management and for technical staff, and NITDA is funding certification for the technical staff. The move is tied to online public services and the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative.

2026-10-20-nigcomsat-ceo-highlights-impa.summary: NIGCOMSAT chief executive Jane Egerton-Idehen, with Minister Bosun Tijani and others, visited Nigeria's first NUCAP base station in Bende, Abia State, as reported on 20 October 2026. The solar-powered 45-metre station covers a radius of about eight kilometres and is expected to serve the community school and hospital. NUCAP plans 3,700 base stations in total.

2026-10-20-nigeria-data-protection-commi.summary: Nigeria's Data Protection Commission hosted a delegation from Sri Lanka's Data Protection Authority for a two-day study tour, reported on 20 October 2026. Sri Lanka is the eighteenth country to visit the Commission for knowledge exchange, and the World Bank supported the visit. National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji presented the Commission's roadmap and its public-private partnership model.

2026-10-20-orange-egypt-partners-with-bo.summary: Orange Egypt and the UAE fintech Botim announced on 20 October 2026 a UAE-to-Egypt remittance route that pays directly into Orange Cash wallets. It is Botim's first partnership with an Egyptian mobile operator. Botim has more than 2 million Egyptian users and Orange Cash about 10 million.

2026-10-20-postbank-full-service-banking.summary: Communications Minister Solly Malatsi told Parliament, as reported on 20 October 2026, that South Africa's Postbank has been directed to submit a new application to establish a bank under section 12 of the Banks Act and has not yet done so. Outstanding items are recapitalisation, which is with National Treasury, banking-system modernisation and a Bank Controlling Company. Postbank paid social grants to about 1.9 million beneficiaries in September 2026.

2026-10-20-rwa-rwanda-looks-to-coordinat.summary: Rwanda's ICT minister of state Yves Iradukunda told the Global AI and Digital Summit in South Korea that Rwanda will bring its digital and AI strategies together under one coordinated programme. Its three priorities are digital and AI infrastructure, jobs, and better digital public services.

2026-10-20-sdn-abagnews-com.summary: The secretary-general of Khartoum State's Supreme Council for Strategy and Information told Sudan's federal digital transformation authority that data recovery is about 93% complete and a move to the cloud has begun. The authority's director promoted its Baladna platform as a single portal for government services that could be used nationally.

2026-10-20-sdn-item.summary: A joint meeting of Khartoum locality and two Khartoum State councils agreed that all government transactions in the localities will go digital from 1 January 2027, once staff are trained on the systems. The meeting also reviewed the locality's 2026 development projects and set weekly reporting for 2027.

2026-10-20-sen-note-publique-identite-nu.summary: In an open note to Senegal's prime minister, economist Seydou Bocoum argues that the new digital governance committee (GouvNum) cannot deliver digital identity and e-government until five prerequisites are met: practical access to information under law 2025-15, reliable networks, a working national addressing system, a social data tariff and visible sanctions by the regulator ARTP. He cites ARTP tests in Popenguine in June 2025 where call and data success rates fell well below regulatory thresholds, and proposes a 30-day stocktake followed by an interministerial action plan within 60 to 90 days.

2026-10-20-sen-senegal-columnist-facing-.summary: Senegal's Special Cybersecurity Division detained Sen TV columnist Mamadou 'Momo' Cissé on 15 October 2026, MFWA reports. Cissé had discussed influencer Nourah Ba's arrest on the Sen Téranga YouTube channel, and was charged with spreading false news on 16 October. Cissé was released pending a hearing set for 21 October; MFWA condemned the prosecution.

2026-10-20-sen-sngal-une-nouvelle-instan.summary: Senegal's Prime Minister installed the Comité de gouvernance du numérique (GouVNum) on 16 October 2026 to coordinate state digital projects and rationalise digital spending. The telecoms and digital ministry acts as its permanent secretariat. The 2034 targets under the New Deal technologique are 90% of administrative procedures dematerialised and a digital identity for 90% of citizens.

2026-10-20-sle-deputy-finance-minister-o.summary: Sierra Leone's Financial Intelligence Agency and GIABA opened a three-day consultation on a proposed consolidated anti-money-laundering database that would join financial records now held in separate systems. Deputy finance minister Isata Marah named lawful access, security by design, audit trails and respect for individual rights as safeguards, and asked participants to agree its governance, standards and financing.

2026-10-20-sle-unfpa-stats-sl-train-147-.summary: Statistics Sierra Leone and UNFPA began training 147 master trainers and data-quality managers on 14 October 2026 for the digital census, whose census night is 1 December. The Statistician-General said all 29,000 tablets had arrived and about 22,508 enumeration areas had been mapped; Ireland funds UNFPA's support.

2026-10-20-tcd-tchad-le-plan-de-connexio.summary: Chad's telecoms minister told the Global AI and Digital Summit in Seoul that the country has only one active international internet link, through Cameroon. He named the World Bank-funded PATN digital transformation project and the Central African regional programme CARDIP, still being designed, as the way out.

2026-10-20-tcd-tlcommunications-la-libye.summary: An unnamed Libyan project official said Libya's fibre link to the Chadian border should be finished by the end of 2026; it already reaches the Egyptian border and work with Chadian authorities and operators has started. The route is pitched as a way to Europe through the MEDUSA submarine cable for Chad, Niger, Mali, the Central African Republic and Burkina Faso.

2026-10-20-tgo-mdias-et-protection-des-d.summary: Togo's data protection authority IPDCP has placed a team in the media regulator HARC's monitoring service, under an agreement the two signed on 10 December 2025. The team will check how the press handles personal data and respond with guidance, awareness work or, where needed, legal measures.

2026-10-20-tiktok-launches-election-cent.summary: TikTok announced on 20 October 2026 an in-app election centre built with the Electoral Commission of South Africa for the 4 November 2026 local government elections. It links to an AI media-literacy hub. TikTok said it removed about 90,000 South African videos between January and March 2026 for civic-integrity, misinformation and misleading AI-content violations.

2026-10-20-tza-nalis-digital-transformat.summary: Tanzania's National Legal Information System (NaLIS), built by the constitution and legal affairs ministry, merges three earlier systems into one platform covering six service areas, including legal aid and alternative dispute resolution. The article gives no launch date for it.

2026-10-20-uga-moict-uganda-national-dat.summary: Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance published the National Data Strategy 2026/27–2030/31, costed at UGX 1,662.6 billion over five years, mostly from government budgets with UGX 333.6 billion expected from selling data services. It rests on data governance, data infrastructure and use of data, overseen by a steering committee chaired by the finance ministry and run by a National Data Office in the ICT ministry.

2026-10-20-uga-newvision-uganda-launches.summary: New Vision's account of the National Data Strategy's launch in Kampala on 20 October 2026, giving the spend by area: UGX 684.9 billion for data infrastructure and 553 billion for data governance. The strategy itself is summarised under the ministry's document.

2026-10-20-uga-ucc-tightens-licensing-ru.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission said on 20 October 2026 that commercial Wi-Fi hotspot resellers must be licensed and must stop reselling home internet packages. Its seven-day deadline for unlicensed operators ended on 19 October 2026. It will open a registration system by service category and set up a joint committee with government, security agencies and seven hotspot operators.

2026-10-20-uk-fcdo-zmb-2025-zra-customs-.summary: A US$650,000 grant from the British High Commission, routed through TradeMark Africa, funds UNCTAD technical help for the Zambia Revenue Authority to move its customs system from ASYCUDA World to ASY5. The agreement was signed on 15 December 2025; assessments, pilots and officer training are under way, with no completion date.

2026-10-20-vodacom-south-africa-invests-.summary: Vodacom said on 20 October 2026 that it is investing more than R600 million in Mpumalanga network infrastructure this financial year, after R620 million in 2025/26. Its sites in the province have grown from just over 1,300 to 1,408, and the share connected by fibre from 41% to 45%.

2026-10-20-vodacom-zaf-mpumalanga-networ.summary: Vodacom announced on 20 October 2026 that it will spend more than R600 million of its own funds on network infrastructure in Mpumalanga in the current financial year. It invested R620 million there in 2025/26, and the spending covers all 17 local municipalities.

2026-10-20-xaf-co-creating-with-africa-s.summary: A UNDP blog describes the AI Hub for Sustainable Development, endorsed by the G7 and co-led by Italy and UNDP, and its two programmes for African AI builders: Infrastructure Builder and Compute Accelerator. Partners named include AWS with US$1 million in cloud credits and Microsoft with up to US$150,000 in Azure credits per innovator, across 18 countries in Italy's Mattei Plan.

2026-10-20-xaf-ifc-eyes-75m-for-100m-afr.summary: TechSoma reports IFC's proposed senior loan of up to US$7.5 million to Cauris Finance's Third Wave Fund, which targets US$75 million and may raise up to US$100 million to lend to African fintech lenders. About 60% would go to lenders serving small businesses and 40% to vehicle-finance fintechs; the loan is not yet approved, with a board decision expected on 30 November 2026.

2026-10-20-xca-eccas-validates-regional-.summary: ECCAS member states validated a Regional Data Governance Framework at a workshop in Brazzaville on 19-20 October 2026, organised by ECA with ECCAS. It rests on six pillars, including cross-border data flows and common interoperability standards, with a 36-month roadmap in three phases.

2026-10-20-xca-gabon-artac-six-groupes-d.summary: ARTAC created six permanent technical working groups at its 4th extraordinary Conference of Regulators session in Libreville on 20 October 2026. They cover radiocommunications, technical standards on safety and environmental protection, regulatory governance, postal regulation, digital financial services and consumer protection. The session, hosted by ARCEP Gabon, is also reviewing ARTAC's statutes, rules of procedure and financial regulations.

2026-10-20-xca-gabon-telecommunications-.summary: The Central African telecoms regulators' assembly ARTAC opened its 4th extraordinary session in Libreville on 20 October 2026, running two days and hosted by Gabon's ARCEP. Digital Economy Minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba launched it. Participants are reviewing ARTAC's statutes, rules of procedure and financial regulations, and São Tomé and Príncipe's regulator formally presented its membership application.

2026-10-20-xgl-access-now-deliberately-f.summary: Access Now published a report on 20 October 2026 on internet shutdowns with no announced end, citing Tigray, Sudan and Annobón. It says the number of such shutdowns has risen each year. It asks states, the Freedom Online Coalition and satellite providers to act; the Annobón entry carries its testimonies.

2026-10-20-xgl-world-bank-group-launches.summary: The World Bank Group launched its first digital strategy in Seoul on 20 October 2026, with four priorities: connectivity, affordable devices and data, digital services and skills, and AI readiness. It also announced an AI Infrastructure and Readiness Initiative that gives emerging-market governments shared pay-as-you-go GPU capacity, starting with Africa and Latin America, with Cassava Technologies and NVIDIA as knowledge partners.

2026-10-20-xwa-bceao-indicateurs-inclusi.summary: The BCEAO's report on financial inclusion in the WAEMU for 2025 gives each member state's access, usage and affordability indicators to the end of December 2025, with series from 2015 and a composite inclusion index. Across the union the broad account-ownership rate including microfinance and e-money stands at about 50 per cent of adults, ranging from under 15 per cent in Guinea-Bissau to over 90 per cent in Benin.

2026-10-20-xwa-benin-ghana-and-rwanda-ta.summary: Benin, Ghana and Rwanda completed Phase 1 of the Smart Africa Data Exchange cross-border digital identity pilot, announced on 20 October 2026. The three national systems were connected and verified identities end to end using synthetic data. Phase 2 prepares a controlled operational pilot for border identity checks, subject to national approvals and security assessments.

2026-10-20-zaf-borrowed-trust-africa-and.summary: The University of the Witwatersrand published a research feature on 20 October 2026 featuring Professor Keith Breckenridge of WiSER. It considers whether digital finance tools such as biometric IDs, automated credit scoring and asset registers will reduce Africa's credit exclusion or deepen it, and which institutions of trust would be needed. No figures were given.

2026-10-20-zaf-dcdt-policy-direction-ica.summary: South Africa's communications minister Solly Malatsi signed on 19 October 2026 a policy direction under the Electronic Communications Act, published in Government Gazette 55609 the next day, to implement the 2023 national policy on rapid deployment of networks and facilities. It directs Icasa to consider amending the 2010 Facilities Leasing Regulations and to draft Rapid Deployment Regulations governing access to public and private land for affordable high-speed broadband.

2026-10-20-zaf-iec-receives-over-700-ele.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission said on 20 October 2026 that it has received more than 700 election-misinformation complaints, most about posts on X, ahead of the 4 November 2026 local government elections. It is working with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa against disinformation. Electoral Code breaches carry fines up to R200,000 or five to ten years' imprisonment.

2026-10-20-zaf-ramaphosa-to-meet-silicon.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa said at the Black Wednesday commemoration lunch on Monday 19 October 2026 that he will lead a delegation to Silicon Valley after the local government elections. It will include people from government, universities, business and youth, to meet AI company leaders and learn how the technology works. No travel dates were given.

2026-10-20-zaf-rewiring-payments-open-co.summary: The South African Reserve Bank, opening its 2026 payments conference, set out plans to let non-banks into the payment system under an authorisation framework due by end-November 2026, pilot QR+ interoperable merchant codes in early 2027, and build a single digital ID for payments. Regional payments under R100,000 are to move from SADC-RTGS to TCIB by end-April 2027; PayShap has passed 1 billion transactions since 2023.

2026-10-20-zaf-south-africa-s-ratificati.summary: South Africa's ratification of the AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade was presented to the NCOP Select Committee on Economic Development and Trade on 20 October 2026, after the Protocol was tabled in Parliament on 30 July. Legal opinions found no conflict with domestic law, and both houses must approve before ratification goes to the AU; the briefing also covered the SADC Protocol on Industry.

2026-10-20-zmb-zambia-advances-customs-s.summary: The Zambia Revenue Authority set out on 19 October 2026 the next steps in moving its customs system from ASYCUDA World to ASY5: system assessments, pilot testing and officer training. The UNCTAD project is backed by a US$650,000 British grant through TradeMark Africa, and no go-live date has been set.

2026-10-20-zwe-zim-strengthens-digital-r.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT ministry told its departments to submit validated risk registers by 6 November 2026 and to include risk assessments in every new major project proposal from now on. The instructions came out of an enterprise risk-management workshop the minister opened in Harare on 19 October 2026.

2026-10-21-32-african-markets-tax-digita.summary: PwC's 2026 report on VAT and digital services in Africa finds 32 of 54 countries now tax electronic services supplied by foreign providers, up from 21 in its 2024 edition. The eleven newcomers include Algeria, Botswana, Malawi, Mauritius, Rwanda and Zanzibar, and Namibia and Mozambique have measures awaiting a start date.

2026-10-21-banjul-airport-security-needs.summary: An opinion piece argues that the Gambia's contract with Securiport for civil-aviation and immigration security at Banjul airport needs a public scorecard of which findings of the National Audit Office's November 2022 management letter have been closed. It separates what the auditors found for September 2019 to May 2021 from the responses institutions printed, such as the civil aviation authority's report of a joint collection account.

2026-10-21-bdi-burundi-bujumbura-seeks-s.summary: Burundi's finance and digital economy minister met South Korea's science and ICT ministry in Seoul in October 2026. They discussed cooperation on digital identity, data centres, secure hosting of public data and links between government agencies. Financing through KOICA and Korea's EDCF fund was explored, with training and cybersecurity support.

2026-10-21-bfa-inclusion-financiere-avec.summary: At a talk reported by C'Finance on 21 October 2026, expert Corinne Nikièma put Burkina Faso's financial inclusion at 79.7% at end 2024. That is 6.1 points above the UEMOA rate, while strict bank account ownership stood at 23.4%. Nikièma said half of those included through e-money do not use their accounts.

2026-10-21-burundi-explore-seoul-identit.summary: Burundi's finance and digital economy minister, Alain Ndikumana, discussed cooperation on digital identification and authentication, data centres, secure hosting and linking government systems with South Korea's science and ICT ministry in Seoul. Financing through KOICA and Korea's Economic Development Cooperation Fund was explored. No agreement was reported.

2026-10-21-bwa-botswana-explores-ai-inte.summary: A consultant to Botswana's planned National Health Insurance scheme said authorities are considering digital and AI tools to coordinate public and private providers, now that Parliament has approved the NHI policy and a financing model is being prepared to accompany the bill. The government has allocated P77.8m this year to set up the scheme.

2026-10-21-dji-dj-cert-centre-gouverneme.summary: The alert page lists 511 vulnerability alerts with severity ratings, from 2 January 2023 to 21 October 2026. The newest rows, dated 21 October, rate the PHP2Shell flaws in PHP and a GitLab vulnerability as critical.

2026-10-21-dza-algerie-poste-caci-framew.summary: Algérie Poste signed a framework agreement with the Algerian Chamber of Commerce and Industry on 21 October 2026 to offer artisans and traders its CCP Business Cashless service and other e-payment products. The two will run joint awareness and training sessions.

2026-10-21-dza-aps-base-donnees-unifiee-.summary: Algeria's Ministry of Internal Trade is building a unified price database that links the ministry's platforms to flag unusual price rises early and show which wilayas a supply problem affects, a central director said on national radio. It follows a Council of Ministers instruction for the Interior and Trade ministries and the High Commission for Digitalisation to set up a price-alert mechanism.

2026-10-21-ecofin-equatorial-guinea-telg.summary: Equatorial Guinea's authorities aim to sign an agreement before the end of October 2026 with investor group EGSA LOITA for a new telecom operator, TELGESA. The group has proposed USD 50 million for 260 towers to reach 90% national coverage, while KPMG values the assets of state operator GECOMSA. Launch before the end of 2026 remains uncertain.

2026-10-21-egy-foreign-ministry-launches.summary: Egypt's foreign ministry has started piloting a mobile app for consular services for Egyptians abroad, covering 17 embassies and consulates at launch, with more to follow. Users can complete consular transactions in the app and track their progress.

2026-10-21-egy-minister-ict-egypt-tops-a.summary: At the Egypt Forum's Digital Egypt session, the communications minister set targets for 2030: 400 services on the Digital Egypt platform, fibre to 55% of homes, 5G coverage everywhere and five to seven very large data centres. He also said Egypt has led Africa on fixed internet speed for six years running. The targets are ministerial statements, not a published plan.

2026-10-21-encryption-as-a-digital-right.summary: CIPESA marks Global Encryption Day with a commentary on Global Partners Digital's relaunched World Map of Encryption Laws and Policies, which now covers 100 countries, 40 of them under a new assessment framework. On the map, Ethiopia rates severe for encryption restrictions and weak on safeguards, requiring licences for encryption providers and security clearance for importers of cryptographic hardware and software, while Zimbabwe and Nigeria rate severe for legislative and policy threats.

2026-10-21-eri-building-artificial-intel.summary: A UN Day panel in Asmara on 15 October discussed what Eritrea would need to use AI for development: skills, data systems, local-language tools and infrastructure. No policy or commitment came out of it.

2026-10-21-eth-ethiopia-calls-for-data-d.summary: Opening the Statistical Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa, President Taye Atske Selassie said Ethiopia has reformed its statistics law and set up an independent statistical service. He put the country's mobile-money and mobile-banking accounts at 257 million, handling more than ETB 24 trillion in the first nine months of 2026.

2026-10-21-gab-cooperation-gabonchine-mo.summary: Gabon's civil-service minister asked China's ambassador for Chinese expertise in digitising public administration and training civil servants. The ambassador said China would look at what support it could give; no agreement is reported.

2026-10-21-gab-rgpl-2026-apres-la-procla.summary: Gabon's census counts 3,518,621 residents, 2,318,365 of them Gabonese, figures certified by the Constitutional Court on 27 August 2026, but the detailed report has not been published. A deputy and citizens are asking when the breakdown by province, commune, age and sex will be released.

2026-10-21-gabon-parliament-digital-plat.summary: Gabon's National Assembly launched a Legislative Work Management Platform (GTLAN) on 19 October 2026 and issued tablets to members. The digital infrastructure agency ANINF trained members until 20 October on using it for committee review, government hearings and joint work on amendments.

2026-10-21-gha-knust-google-strengthen-p.summary: Google has given staff and students at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology 95,000 licences for Gemini and NotebookLM and approved 500 places on professional AI courses. Google said data on Gemini for Education stays within the university's environment and is not used to train its models; a memorandum to formalise the partnership was proposed but not signed.

2026-10-21-gha-sam-george-announces-nati.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George announced a national data exchange hub to connect 48 public registries, so that developers can query several institutions in one request while each keeps ownership of its database. NITA will set common data-classification standards, and private firms wanting government data will have to share their own.

2026-10-21-gin-signature-electronique-de.summary: Guinea opened a workshop in Conakry on 21 October 2026 to review nine draft regulations on the state's electronic signature, following an implementing decree adopted on 19 August 2026. The justice ministry is adapting procedure texts to bring e-signatures into a future procedure code, and the digital agency ANDE is building the public-key infrastructure behind them.

2026-10-21-gna-ghana-dpc-evacuee-persona.summary: The Ghana News Agency's account of the Data Protection Commission's warning against publishing the personal details of 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa. The statement is summarised under the Commission's own item of 20 October 2026.

2026-10-21-ken-education-ministry-sued-o.summary: Two petitioners have asked a Kenyan court to stop the education ministry finalising senior-school placements, saying the KEMIS portal shows at most 1,000 schools for any subject combination without saying the list is cut. They say 26 combinations are affected, one of them listing 1,000 of 10,515 schools, and that some combinations show no schools at all.

2026-10-21-ken-mps-want-land-succession-.summary: Kenya's National Assembly Public Petitions committee recommended amending the Law of Succession Act and related laws so that land succession can be handled through e-Citizen and Huduma Centres. It backs a petition to end paper-based trips to land registries and courts.

2026-10-21-lby-aonsrt-mou-digital-econom.summary: Libya's Authority for Scientific Research signed a memorandum with the office of the Minister of State for Digital Economy and AI, launching a national programme of Libyan experts and researchers in the digital economy and AI. It also covers a national database of experts, links with the diaspora, an annual forum to review digital transformation plans and a joint implementation team; the signing date is not stated.

2026-10-21-lso-the-government-of-lesotho.summary: Lesotho's ICT ministry and UNICEF held a workshop in Berea on 20-23 October 2026 to plan an X-Road pilot for the National Data Exchange. It assessed ministries' readiness, picked priority uses for child-focused services and set a roadmap with data-protection and child-rights safeguards.

2026-10-21-mar-bkam-rapport-annuel-imf-m.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib's annual report on financial market infrastructures and means of payment for 2025 covers the activity, development projects and assessment of Morocco's gross settlement system, interbank clearing, card and mobile switch, central securities depository and exchange clearing house. It also reports on cyber-resilience oversight, the RIBAT resilience rating, cash in circulation and electronic means of payment.

2026-10-21-mar-cndp-niiat-partner-to-tra.summary: Morocco's data-protection commission CNDP signed an agreement with the National Institute of Innovation and Advanced Technology on 21 October 2026, bringing it into the CNDP's DATA-TIKA programme. A six-month pilot in Casablanca-Settat is to train at least 20,000 young people in privacy principles, with a national roll-out to follow on no fixed timetable.

2026-10-21-mli-sahel-confederation-togo-.summary: Customs directors of Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Togo, meeting in Ouagadougou on 15-16 October 2026, set 1 January 2027 for national company lists to support a regional identification code and 31 January for a technical unit to supervise interconnected customs data. Nine of the 18 recommendations from their 2025 meeting have been implemented, six are under way and three are outstanding.

2026-10-21-nam-ijg-pitches-mobile-saving.summary: An IJG Investment Managers director proposed a USSD service that would let low-income Namibians put small sums into regulated funds from a basic phone. The service is a prototype, and he asked NAMFISA, the Bank of Namibia and CRAN to let it be tested in a regulatory sandbox.

2026-10-21-nam-namibia-s-first-ai-tutori.summary: Two AI tutoring labs, the first in a Namibian government school, opened at Angra Pequena Senior Secondary School in Lüderitz on 21 September 2026, funded with N$1.15 million from BW Kudu and Namport. Run by YYeni AI, they serve the school's 436 learners and 20 teachers, with six more schools in the ||Kharas region due to get labs in 2027.

2026-10-21-newtimes-rwanda-ncsa-business.summary: Rwanda's National Cyber Security Authority and the Rwanda Development Board held a workshop for businesses in Kigali on 20 October 2026 on recovering from cyber attacks, as part of cybersecurity awareness month. Speakers urged layered defences, monitoring, recovery plans and checks on technology partners.

2026-10-21-nga-businessday-udo-complianc.summary: Lawyer Blessing Udo argues that Nigeria's annual data protection compliance audit return is a model for other countries, because it makes designated organisations report on their compliance before a breach happens. She compares it favourably with the Californian, Indian, Chinese and EU approaches and calls for findings to be published by sector.

2026-10-21-nga-connectingafrica-tiktok-b.summary: TikTok has been hard to reach for more than a month in northern states including Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi and Sokoto, mostly for MTN and Airtel subscribers. TikTok denies restricting access, the operators have not commented and the government has said nothing. Gatefield's chief executive alleges throttling ahead of the 2027 elections.

2026-10-21-nga-fg-moves-to-regulate-ai-u.summary: Nigeria's Minister of State for Health, Iziaq Adekunle Salako, told the AI in Health Summit 2026 in Abuja that the government is drafting sector-specific rules for AI in healthcare, building on the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 to cover health data, secondary use of clinical information, anonymisation and consent. He pointed to the National Digital Health Architecture endorsed by all 36 states and the FCT, a planned Health Information Exchange, and weak infrastructure, power and broadband as obstacles.

2026-10-21-nga-nibss-transactility-s-par.summary: Transactility says NIBSS built Nigeria's National Payment Stack, an ISO 20022 instant payments platform, on its open-source jPOS software and jPTS switch. NIBSS says having the full source code leaves it in control of the platform's design, roadmap and intellectual property.

2026-10-21-nga-undp-cisco-offer-50-000-n.summary: UNDP and Cisco signed a memorandum in Abuja giving up to 50,000 fellows and alumni of the Nigeria Jubilee Fellows Programme free access to Cisco Networking Academy courses. The programme is a federal youth-employability scheme funded by the European Union and run by UNDP; Cisco valued its contribution at more than USD 52.7 million.

2026-10-21-nga-von-build-2026-shared-com.summary: Opening the BUILD 2026 conference on shared compute in Abuja, Nigeria's communications ministry announced plans for a Nigeria–Togo data park and wider fibre connectivity. It also proposed a continental scheme for countries to pool computing power for AI research.

2026-10-21-nitda-digital-literacy-dashbo.summary: Nigeria's NITDA launched a National Digital Literacy Dashboard to track training and coordinate providers. It records about 2.77 million reported training achievements from 252 organisations over three years, across all 774 local government areas, led by Cisco, NITDA and Meta. It supports national targets of 70% digital literacy by 2027 and 95% by 2030.

2026-10-21-rwanda-south-korea-ai-digital.summary: Rwanda's Minister of State for ICT and Innovation, Yves Iradukunda, met South Korea's Vice Minister of Science and ICT to discuss cooperation on AI, digital infrastructure and smart cities. No agreement was reported.

2026-10-21-sa-biometrics-verification-cu.summary: South Africa's National Treasury said in the 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement that better biometric enrolment and beneficiary verification, mostly on the social relief of distress grant, has saved R13.1 billion in social-grant fraud. It will apply similar checks to student bursaries and housing subsidies, and expects grant beneficiaries to fall from 17.8 million in 2026/27 to 17.1 million by 2029/30.

2026-10-21-sa-crypto-assets-regulation-r.summary: South Africa's finance minister said on 21 October 2026, presenting the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, that the draft Capital Flow Management Regulations, which cover cross-border crypto assets, need a different approach after Treasury received thousands of comments. Consultations will produce a revised second draft for further comment; no date was given.

2026-10-21-sa-mymzansi-citizen-services-.summary: South Africa's National Treasury is allocating R150 million to the Presidency's digital services unit to develop MyMzansi, a single platform for government services, according to the adjusted estimates released with the 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement. The first use case will be issuing and verifying digital matric certificates.

2026-10-21-sam-george-outlines-270m-ghan.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George outlined a US$270m AI programme, US$250m for infrastructure and computing and US$20m as seed money for an AI fund, including a national language model he called Ghana Chat. He said analysts in ministers' offices had put classified material into foreign AI platforms, which he said undercut the country's data-residency law.

2026-10-21-sdn-sudaray-provisional-decre.summary: Sudan's official gazette of 19 October 2026 published Provisional Decree 7 of 2026, the Miscellaneous Amendments Act, which changes six laws including the 1998 petroleum law, the 1991 Criminal Act, the companies act and the laws on the justice ministry and public prosecution. Among the criminal-law changes, the offence of publishing false news now explicitly covers publication through electronic or media channels, with the penalty unchanged; the decree also exempts anti-smuggling forces from criminal liability when pursuing smugglers.

2026-10-21-sdpay-sudan-digital-payments.summary: Saudi payments firm EdfaPay and Sudanese IT company GoPravo launched SDPay, an equally owned joint venture based in Khartoum, to run payments infrastructure in Sudan. It plans merchant QR and card-terminal acceptance, wallets, card issuing, government collections, payroll and remittances, with digital ID and eKYC integration.

2026-10-21-sen-avant-le-forum-regional-d.summary: The Global Development Network held a workshop in Dakar on 19 October 2026 to draft a national digital-policy research agenda. The Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs was a partner and IDRC gave support, LASPAD UGB reports. The workshop opened a regional forum on research in francophone Africa, held 20 to 23 October.

2026-10-21-sen-donnees-publiques-jusqu-a.summary: The manager of Senegal's national data centre at Diamniadio said 10% to 20% of the country's public data is still hosted abroad (reported October 2026). Some hosting contracts run for ten years, which delays moving the data home. Paying off the contracts early or waiting for them to expire are both under study, and no date has been set.

2026-10-21-sen-inclusion-financiere-le-s.summary: Le Soleil reports from the BCEAO's 2025 financial inclusion report that Senegal's composite index is 0.651 against a WAEMU average of 0.616. Senegal has 150 service points per 10,000 adults, almost all of them e-money outlets; its strict banking rate is 27.42 per cent, its broad rate 67.13 per cent, and 39.71 per cent of adults use microfinance.

2026-10-21-sen-socialnetlink-wack-ndiaye.summary: Policy analyst Elhadji Wack Ndiaye argues that GouvNum, Senegal's digital government agency, should use data and AI to cut spending and target social programmes under the 2027 finance bill. The budget figures he cites are his own reading of the bill.

2026-10-21-som-moct-house-of-the-people-.summary: Somalia's House of the People passed the Digital Transactions Bill on 21 October 2026 with 137 votes in favour, giving a legal framework to digital transactions and mobile money. The bill was drafted by the communications ministry; the release does not mention the Senate stage or assent.

2026-10-21-som-somali-federal-government.summary: Somalia's civil aviation authority said its dispute with Somaliland over the national eVisa system was resolved and that Hargeisa-based travel agencies could use it. Somaliland's aviation minister denied any agreement, saying travellers arriving at Hargeisa with a Somalia-issued eVisa still need a Somaliland visa.

2026-10-21-tcd-num-rique-le-pastoralisme.summary: Chad's livestock ministry took delivery on 21 October 2026 of seven digital systems built by the PRAPS-2 pastoralism project with technical support from the World Organisation for Animal Health. They include an animal-health information system linked to the health ministry, laboratory systems for two institutes, a school portal and a central HR planning database.

2026-10-21-tnm-engages-meta-on-whatsapp-.summary: Malawian operator TNM said it has engaged Meta over reports of customers' WhatsApp accounts being compromised in Malawi and other countries. It said nothing shows its own systems were breached, and advised customers to turn on two-step verification.

2026-10-21-tun-solecrypt-announces-sover.summary: SoleCrypt announced at NVIDIA GTC Europe in Berlin a planned 40 MW AI data-centre campus in Bizerte, Tunisia, whose 7 MW first phase is to house 1,728 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and come online in early 2028. The site lies about 3.6 km by fibre from the Medusa subsea cable landing and is to be backed by a 60 MW solar and battery project in Tozeur, with Hosted.AI, Schneider Electric, Supermicro and others named as partners.

2026-10-21-tza-dailynews-bunge-committee.summary: Tanzania's Parliamentary Standing Committee on Infrastructure invited public views on ratifying the AU's Malabo Convention on cybersecurity and personal data protection. It holds a public hearing on 26 October 2026 and accepts written submissions before the ratification resolution moves on.

2026-10-21-tza-tanzania-launches-digital.summary: Tanzania's education minister Adolf Mkenda launched the Integrated National Digital Library System, built by the Tanzania Library Services Board with the e-Government Authority, which handles registration, ISBN and ISSN applications, cataloguing, lending and billing on web and mobile. Copyright limits mean not every title will be online in full.

2026-10-21-uga-independent-ubos-rejects-.summary: The Uganda Bureau of Statistics publicly rejected the ICT ministry's National Data Strategy on 21 October 2026, a day after its launch, calling it illegal, irregular and redundant. Its executive director said the strategy breaches the UBOS Act, which makes the Bureau the coordinator of the National Statistical System, and that existing statistics plans already cover its ground.

2026-10-21-whoafro-ethiopia-eaii-ai-heal.summary: A WHO delegation led by its representative to Ethiopia visited the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute to explore a partnership on using AI in health systems, emergency preparedness and health security. The Institute showed locally built tools including language and translation software, disease-prediction models and AI skin-disease diagnostics. No agreement was reported.
