2026-10-21-xaf-afrinic-s-2025-audit-opin.summary: A BTW Media analysis notes that Forvis Mazars signed an unmodified opinion on AFRINIC's 2025 financial statements on 22 May 2026 but drew attention to Note 22, where directors describe ongoing legal proceedings and explain why no provision was recognised. The piece argues the opinion speaks only to whether the accounts are fairly presented, not to the outcome of the litigation or the effectiveness of internal controls, on which the auditor gave no opinion.

2026-10-21-xaf-afrinic-s-2025-surplus-fe.summary: BTW Media's reading of AFRINIC's audited 2025 accounts finds income up 2.8% to US$6.289 million while total expenses nearly doubled to US$5.114 million, cutting the surplus of income over expenditure by 65.1% to US$1.175 million. Election costs of about US$1.04 million and legal fees of about US$878,000, against US$27,322 a year earlier, account for some 80% of the rise, and cash generated from operations fell 75.2% to US$856,407.

2026-10-21-zaf-information-regulator-fnb.summary: The Information Regulator issued an enforcement notice and an infringement notice to First National Bank. Both were signed on 21 October 2026. The infringement notice carries an R1 million administrative fine. The regulator found an offence under section 105 of the data protection act. A 2022 compromise exposed the data of 88 people to 696 unauthorised individuals. The bank must fix its privacy policy, retention and further processing. It must report within 90 days.

2026-10-21-zaf-sabs-publishes-draft-ai-s.summary: The South African Bureau of Standards published draft AI standards for comment, each an unmodified adoption of an ISO/IEC text, covering transparency, data quality, human oversight, and AI's benefits and environmental impact. The standards are voluntary unless a law refers to them, and comments close on 10 November 2026.

2026-10-21-zmb-public-notice-draft-revis.summary: ZICTA, Zambia's ICT regulator, wants comments on revised type approval rules for telecoms equipment by 20 November 2026. The draft splits equipment into high-risk and low-risk classes. Some goods could leave customs before approval.

2026-10-22-ago-executivo-disponibiliza-5.summary: Angola's President authorised USD 50 million for the Programa Conectividade by Presidential Despacho 394/26 of 20 October, to extend broadband to under-served areas with schools and community centres first, through a public tender. The programme falls under the World Bank-financed Angola Digital Acceleration Project, assets bought become state property, and the head of the Institute for Administrative Modernisation runs the procurement.

2026-10-22-ago-joao-lourenco-autoriza-de.summary: Angola's President authorised USD 20 million, by a despacho reported on 22 October 2026, for digital skills training at basic, intermediate and advanced levels for young workers and civil servants, along with awareness of data protection and cybersecurity. Training centres are to be hired by public tender, run by the Institute for Administrative Modernisation.

2026-10-22-ben-benin-15-189-retraites-on.summary: By 21 October 2026, 15,189 pensioners of Benin's national pension fund (FNRB) had completed their annual proof of life remotely through the Preuve de Vie app, according to sources close to the presidency. Pensioners enter their national personal identification number (NPI) and pension book number and scan their fingerprints with the phone camera, or use biometric kiosks with a biometric ID card; the campaign runs to 15 November.

2026-10-22-bfa-compte-rendu-du-conseil-d.summary: Burkina Faso's Council of Ministers adopted a decree on 22 October 2026 on computerised processing of civil-status data, a civil-status identifier and the interoperability of the civil-status system with other systems. Applying the 2025 Persons and Family Code, it provides for electronic archiving of registers and online delivery of certificates, with the identifier as the base of a national digital register.

2026-10-22-bfa-le-faso-digital-2026-ladj.summary: Burkina Faso's central cybercrime brigade recorded 6,477 complaints and FCFA 2.23 billion in losses in the first nine months of 2026, more than in all of 2025, an investigator told the Le Faso Digital fair on 21 October. Complaints have risen from 556 in the brigade's first year, 2020, and mobile-money fraud and fake investment platforms are among the six scam types he named.

2026-10-22-civ-c-te-d-ivoire-promotes-na.summary: A second account of the YIRI launch, adding that it aims to build a voice and text language model for Ivorian languages and that digital transition minister Djibril Ouattara called for national languages to be central to AI development.

2026-10-22-civ-intelligence-artificielle.summary: FuturAfric launched YIRI in Abidjan on 15 October 2026, an AI-based social network and online marketplace working in Ivorian languages, with six covered so far and Baoulé and Dioula 70% complete. Its locally hosted corpus holds about 50,000 translated sentences and 300 annotated audio files, the founders aim to reach 80% of West Africa within three years, and the digital transition ministry was asked to back it.

2026-10-22-cod-actualite-senat-ratifie-o.summary: The DRC Senate on 21 October 2026 ratified ordonnance-loi 26/015 of 7 September 2026 organising statistical activity, by 73 votes to none of its 109 members. The 95-article law gives the national statistics institute the power to issue the statistical visa, puts a council chaired by the Prime Minister at the head of the system, penalises breaches of statistical secrecy and puts the system's budget at about USD 192 million.

2026-10-22-cod-kongo-central-l-adn-kc-fa.summary: Kongo Central's provincial digital development agency (ADN-KC) met on 21 October 2026 to review the provincial data centre, whose operation is held back by internet connectivity, power supply and unfinished works. The agency also worked on a provincial project file it means to put to the authorities for validation.

2026-10-22-cod-rdc-serge-kaozi-lubamba-n.summary: DR Congo's digital economy minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba appointed Serge Kaozi Lubamba, with Tommy Tumba Muana as deputy, to lead the missions of the national electronic certification authority (ANCE) by an order signed on 19 October 2026. The authority was provided for in the 2023 Digital Code but never set up, and its missions had been given to the telecoms regulator ARPTC in August 2024.

2026-10-22-cog-administration-fiscale-le.summary: Officials of the Republic of Congo's tax directorate briefed Pointe-Noire business leaders on 20 October on the certified electronic invoicing system (SFEC), in deployment since 1 August 2026. Project lead Séraphin Ndion said 1,335 companies were connected and warned that sanctions for non-compliance apply from 31 October.

2026-10-22-com-alwatwan-conseil-ministre.summary: Comoros' telecoms minister presented a national data-governance and data-centre strategy for 2027-2031 to the Council of Ministers on 21 October 2026, along with the takeover and hosting of the State data centre. The Council approved the national postal-code booklet in principle, asking that the island governors be involved.

2026-10-22-cpv-assinaturas-de-internet-f.summary: Cabo Verde's fixed broadband subscriptions grew 14.7% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, according to the regulator ARME, within 500,263 internet access subscriptions in total, 85% of them mobile broadband on phones. CVTelecom held 72.6% of internet subscriptions, Unitel T+ 26.5% and Starlink 0.87%, and mobile SIM penetration stood at 114% in June 2026.

2026-10-22-dji-dawan-djibouti-all-public.summary: Djibouti's interim Prime Minister Ali Hassan Bahdon said on 21 October 2026 that all public procurement will move to a digital system, with a tender bulletin and an open-data portal on procurement planned. He gave no timetable, and said the average tendering period fell from 35 days in 2021 to 26 in 2023, with over 71% of contracts going to Djiboutian firms in 2024.

2026-10-22-dji-rtd-colloque-commande-pub.summary: Djibouti's second regional public-procurement colloquium, in Dikhil, heard plans for electronic bid submission, e-signature and digital tracking of payments and guarantees over 2026-2028, and a full e-procurement platform by 2027. The procurement portal launched in May 2023 records 1,300 published tenders and 1,227 awards since 2021.

2026-10-22-dza-aadl-3-electronic-payment.summary: Algeria's housing minister told the National Assembly's finance committee that electronic payments for the first two price tranches of the AADL 3 rent-to-buy programme exceeded DZD 338 billion. AADL rent collected electronically reached DZD 14.02 billion, against DZD 3.46 billion in 2022.

2026-10-22-dza-communique-retrait-defini.summary: Algeria's telecoms regulator ARPCE definitively withdrew, from 22 October 2026, the general authorisation it issued to DATAGIX in February 2024 to provide cloud hosting and data storage. The regulator cited breaches of the rules in force and told the company to contact it without delay.

2026-10-22-dza-la-cnas-examine-l-integra.summary: The acting director-general of Algeria's salaried workers' social insurance fund (CNAS) met the head of the government electronic certification authority (AGCE) to work out the technical and organisational steps for bringing electronic signatures into document handling. The project is meant to move the fund's payment centres gradually from paper to electronic processing, guard against forgery and fraud, and prepare a wider rollout of electronic document management and archiving.

2026-10-22-egy-consumer-protection-agenc.summary: The head of Egypt's Consumer Protection Agency, Ibrahim El-Segini, told Egypt Forum 2026 that the agency uses AI on complaints, inspection data, prices, adverts and online stores to spot violation patterns and high-risk sectors. It is also building a unified electronic inspection system tied to a central database and upgrading its complaints system to sort and route reports automatically.

2026-10-22-egy-egypts-souhoola-secures-f.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority licensed Souhoola to provide fintech-based consumer finance through V-Lens, covering electronic identification and verification, e-KYC, electronic contracts and digital record-keeping. The application was approved because it predated FRA Resolution No. 43 of February 2026, which suspended new fintech consumer-finance licence applications for a year.

2026-10-22-gab-artac-libreville-acte-une.summary: A second account of the ARTAC closing session, adding that São Tomé and Príncipe's admission brings membership from seven countries to eight.

2026-10-22-gab-gabon-connect-tresorpay-d.summary: Gabon's vice-president of the government, Hermann Immongault, presented the next phase of the Gabon Connect single digital window in Libreville on 22 October 2026, deploying the single salary declaration (DUS) and TrésorPay portals. The platform groups eTax, eEmployeur, TrésorPay for non-tax and local-government revenue, eDouane and ePropriété, with full deployment due by December 2027.

2026-10-22-gab-paiement-electronique-des.summary: Four months after Libreville's mayor launched collection of market fees by Airtel Money and Moov Money at Mont-Bouët market on 12 June, traders interviewed say they paid electronically once or twice before going back to cash, or never did. The article gives no figures from the municipality on how much has been collected electronically.

2026-10-22-gha-csa-and-nita-order-govern.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority and NITA issued a joint alert on 22 October 2026 ordering all government institutions to patch two critical PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) within seven days and report what they did. Fixed PHP releases are available, and NITA will coordinate support for government systems under its Government Digital Assurance Programme.

2026-10-22-gha-ghanaian-clinic-stored-pa.summary: A Ghanaian laboratory scientist and journalist argued that the Data Protection Commission's inspections of 12 October 2026 raise questions about national health record systems. The Commission found one clinic with no data protection supervisor, unpaid fees and no privacy impact assessment of its electronic records system, and referred it to the police; two hospitals had expired certificates.

2026-10-22-gha-ghanas-hospitals-are-adop.summary: A Ghanaian journalist, drawing on an investigative documentary, argued that AI diagnostic tools now used in Ghana's health facilities, such as TB screening and smartphone ultrasound, were mostly trained on foreign patients and may err more often on Ghanaians without warning. The piece says adoption has outrun regulation.

2026-10-22-gha-phase-one-of-ghana-s-firs.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George said phase one of the country's first national data centre should be complete within 24 months, with equipment being procured through the Public Procurement Authority. The centre is meant to give researchers, universities and industry computing capacity they now buy from abroad.

2026-10-22-gha-sam-george-urges-africa-t.summary: At Digital Economy Live 2026 in Accra, Ghana's communications minister urged African states to build their own digital technologies rather than depend on foreign ones, citing Ghana's mobile money interoperability and national digital identity. He said his ministry is reviewing the policy, institutional and regulatory frameworks for the digital sector.

2026-10-22-gin-guinee-le-ministere-de-le.summary: Guinea's livestock ministry launched Ngaynaako on 22 October 2026, a one-stop online portal where farmers and others in the sector can request services with set deadlines and without travelling or using intermediaries. Minister Alpha Bacar Barry said it will also give the ministry better data on the sector, including the number of farms.

2026-10-22-gnq-el-proyecto-de-ley-de-com.summary: Equatorial Guinea's draft communication law would ban content inciting violence, hatred or crime, or harming minors, across print, broadcast and digital media, and require streaming, podcast and platform providers to register and answer for what they carry. Broadcast licensees would have to give the regulator free monitoring of their output; the bill's legislative stage is not stated.

2026-10-22-gnq-la-guinee-equatoriale-ass.summary: Equatorial Guinea was elected to chair the UN Statistical Commission for Africa (StatCom-Africa) for 2026-2028 at its tenth session in Addis Ababa on 19 to 23 October 2026, with INEGE director-general Ricardo Nsue Ndemesogo Obono presiding. He set five priorities: turning data into usable evidence for policy, the financial and technical autonomy of national statistical systems, integrating administrative registers, censuses and geospatial data, using new technology while protecting confidentiality, and harmonised regional methods.

2026-10-22-ken-kenya-ict-authority-signs.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority signed a letter of intent in Seoul with the Korea Data Agency (K-DATA) to prepare government data for AI and pilot AI in public services, witnessed by ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo. The cooperation also covers data governance, interoperability, secure data exchange across government, data quality certification and training, within the Data Protection Act 2019.

2026-10-22-ken-kenyas-language-data-hold.summary: Kenyan researchers are calling for more investment in local language data for AI services, pointing to Teknobyte's Kenya Languages Lexicon (KENGLEX), which documents more than 133,000 words of Kenyan English with meanings and pronunciations for use in speech recognition, translation and text-to-speech. Swahili has the most language resources in Kenya, while many indigenous languages have no public models, and NLP researcher Cynthia Amol argued that communities should have a say in how their language data is collected, licensed and paid for.

2026-10-22-ken-ps-oluga-calls-for-accoun.summary: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Ouma Oluga, chaired the steering committee of the Healthcare IT Digitisation Programme with the Safaricom Consortium, the Digital Health Authority, the Social Health Authority and KEMSA to review progress under the UHC digital transformation programme. He set four priorities for the next phase: holding subcontractors to their obligations, tracking project investments more visibly, speeding up delivery of infrastructure, equipment and systems, and making sure facilities and patients see real benefits.

2026-10-22-ken-who-owns-indigenous-data-.summary: Indigenous communities from northern Kenya presented a community-based monitoring and information system at the biodiversity COP17 in Yerevan, developed with the organisation IMPACT, to record traditional knowledge of grazing, water and wildlife digitally. They want that data recognised in national biodiversity reporting while staying under community control.

2026-10-22-lbr-liberia-joins-smart-afric.summary: Liberia became the 43rd member of the Smart Africa Alliance, the admission completed by a delegation led by Minister of State for Presidential Affairs Samuel Stevquoah on the margins of the Global AI and Digital Summit in Seoul. The Executive Mansion presented it as part of President Boakai's digital agenda, pointing to training through the Smart Africa Digital Academy.

2026-10-22-lbr-nec-seeks-us-72m-for-2029.summary: Liberia's National Elections Commission chair, Jonathan Weedor, said on 21 October 2026 that the commission would propose a 2029 election budget of over US$72 million. The proposal was due to the government by 31 October. It includes a fresh biometric voter registration in January–March 2028. That replaces plans to verify and update the 2023 final registration roll. He also asked donors to invest in Liberian staff over foreign consultants.

2026-10-22-lby-libyas-gnu-orders-immedia.summary: Libya's Government of National Unity ordered the immediate temporary shutdown and isolation of all government systems, websites and databases running on PHP, in a circular from the Minister of State for Cabinet Affairs. It cited US NSA warnings of two critical vulnerabilities allowing attackers to take over servers without authentication, and put cybersecurity teams on alert.

2026-10-22-mdg-la-prevention-de-la-cyber.summary: Madagascar's digital development ministry handed computers on 21 October 2026 to the Centre de lutte contre la cybercriminalité, which resumed work in June 2026 after an interruption, for its teams in all 24 regions. Under a responsible cyber-citizenship programme, regional staff are to be trained to detect offences on social media; the centre's coordinator said awareness comes first, with sanctions possible for those who persist.

2026-10-22-moz-mozambique-joins-sadc-reg.summary: Mozambique joined the SADC Regional Working Group on Data Protection through INTIC, naming board chair Lourino Chemane as member and data protection head Rosa Dique as alternate, after SADC ICT ministers meeting in Bulawayo on 26 June 2026 asked states to appoint representatives. The country's personal data protection bill is before the Assembly of the Republic.

2026-10-22-mus-pq-paiement-electronique-.summary: Mauritius received three bids for consultancy on a cashless electronic ticketing system for buses, using a smart card and mobile app and possibly extended to Metro Express and taxis, the land transport minister told parliament. Bids opened on 17 September are being evaluated for award by the end of October, for a six-month assignment; a clearing house is a precondition and no launch date is set.

2026-10-22-nga-fg-proposes-shared-ai-com.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani, speaking through NCAIR's director at BUILD 2026 in Abuja, proposed pooling GPU capacity with Rwanda, Senegal and Kenya so researchers could combine compute to train large models. He said about 20 million Nigerians remain offline and pointed to a proposed Nigeria-Togo data park at Egbe to use unused power capacity.

2026-10-22-nga-foreign-cloud-dependence-.summary: Luminate's chief executive Melanie Hui told the BUILD 2026 conference in Abuja that Nigeria loses an estimated $850 million a year by relying on foreign cloud providers, citing research Luminate commissioned from the Global Centre on AI Governance. She urged African governments to judge foreign tech investment by the jobs, skills and value it keeps at home.

2026-10-22-nga-npc-seeks-unified-system-.summary: Nigeria's National Population Commission opened a North-East zonal consultation in Yola on a draft harmonised protocol for marriage and divorce registration, part of strengthening the civil registration and vital statistics system. Stakeholders from the zone's six states reviewed the draft over two days.

2026-10-22-nga-wb-restructuring-paper-p1.summary: The World Bank proposes a third extension, of 12 months to 31 December 2027, for Nigeria's US$430 million digital identification project. The extension would fund the NIMS 2.0 system, contracted on 15 September 2026. At 30 June 2026, 117.5 million people held a NIN, 65% of the 180 million target. Enrolment partners have gone unpaid since January 2026.

2026-10-22-nga-we-must-build-cybersecuri.summary: NITDA's director general Kachifu Abdulahi used a press conference in Abuja to announce an International Cyber Security Conference there on 27-28 October 2026, themed on cyber resilience in the age of AI. He described the split of responsibility under the Cybercrimes Act, with the National Security Adviser's coordination centre over NITDA for ministries and citizens, the NCC for telecoms and the Central Bank for banks, and called for a national cybersecurity architecture setting minimum standards.

2026-10-22-rwa-mtn-rwanda-signs-cybersec.summary: MTN Rwanda signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Cyber Security Authority to support cybersecurity and data-protection skills training through the CyberHub Academy and Innovation Centre. No value or duration was stated.

2026-10-22-rwa-rwanda-can-be-korea-s-ai-.summary: On his first visit to South Korea, Rwanda's minister of state for ICT and innovation Yves Iradukunda pitched Rwanda as an entry point for Korean technology firms into Africa and sought Korean investment in data centres, proposing that countries share such infrastructure regionally. He said Rwanda's new government-owned AI agency, coming into operation through 2026, will run an 'AI Factory' unit that builds and tests applications with private partners, help firms reach data and computing, and aim to recover part of its costs by charging for development, training and compute.

2026-10-22-rwa-rwanda-ghana-benin-test-c.summary: Rwanda, Ghana and Benin completed the first phase of a Smart Africa pilot linking their national ID systems through the Smart Africa Data Exchange, verifying identities end to end with synthetic data in a test environment. Smart Africa said the exchange passes verification requests between national systems without storing records centrally, and does not change visa or immigration rules.

2026-10-22-sle-dsti-and-social-welfare-v.summary: Sierra Leone's Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation and the Ministry of Social Welfare held a validation exercise for Leh Wi Tok, a communication app for speech- and hearing-impaired people, with members of that community giving feedback. Its first phase is aimed at school pupils with content based on American Sign Language, and Social Welfare minister Melrose Karminty plans to take it to cabinet for approval; the disability commission's chairman urged a codified Sierra Leone Sign Language.

2026-10-22-som-somali-justice-ministry-o.summary: Somalia's justice ministry issued guidelines requiring officiants of Islamic marriages to register with it and be trained, licensed and overseen, so that marriages can be documented and verified. Only a judge or a registered officiant may solemnise a marriage, and marriage records must be kept confidential.

2026-10-22-som-somalia-enrolls-citizens-.summary: Somalia's National Identification and Registration Authority began enrolling citizens returning from Yemen for biometric national ID cards, working with the National Commission for Refugees and IDPs at its reception camp. NIRA puts national enrolment at about two million against a target of 15 million by 2029, and the Halmeel unified government services platform, covering about 70 services, is due by the end of March 2027.

2026-10-22-tgo-digitalisation-agricole-l.summary: Togo's agriculture ministry held a World Bank-supported national consultation on digital public infrastructure for agriculture in Lomé on 12-13 October 2026 and set a first roadmap for its ProDISA-Togo project. The project is to bring the sector onto one central system around subsidies, extension advice, finance and markets, farmer identification and grievances, and goes next to the World Bank for comment.

2026-10-22-tza-nida-produces-23-718-060-.summary: Tanzania's National Identification Authority had issued 23,718,060 identification numbers and produced 21,526,594 ID cards, 21,515,793 of them distributed, the deputy home affairs minister told a parliamentary committee on 22 October 2026. NIDA has also connected 152 public and private institutions to its database and upgraded 24 modules of its registration system.

2026-10-22-uga-ucc-moves-to-tighten-moni.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission agreed with mobile operators and licensed internet providers in ISPAU to tighten tracking of data consumption and billing, aimed at unlicensed resellers of bulk connectivity over public Wi-Fi. Eligible resellers are to be brought into licensing through onboarding guidelines, and illegal access points and routers removed; no date or design for the monitoring was given.

2026-10-22-uga-uganda-denmark-sign-deal-.summary: The Uganda Bureau of Statistics signed a memorandum with Statistics Denmark and the Danish Embassy to modernise Uganda's national statistical system, including green-transition statistics and work with the finance ministry on statistics for macroeconomic modelling. Denmark's foreign ministry funds the cooperation through its Strategic Sector Cooperation programme; no amount is stated.

2026-10-22-uga-uganda-moves-to-make-nati.summary: Uganda's Minister of State for Finance, Amos Lugoloobi, told Parliament the government is proceeding with making the National Identification Number the tax identifier for individuals, under a 2025 amendment to the Tax Procedures Code; companies keep a URSB registration number. The Uganda Revenue Authority has bought 80 biometric fingerprint scanners to link ID details to tax records, deployed first in Kampala and Wakiso with a wider rollout from 26 October. URA counts about 5.4 million individual taxpayers, of whom about 3.3 million are active.

2026-10-22-uga-uganda-s-digital-skills-g.summary: At a dialogue on Uganda's digital skills held by the Uganda Communications Commission with the British Council, information minister of state Nabbosa Sebugwawo called for more affordable devices and access, better recognition of digital skills and measuring whether trainees go on to use them. The 2024 census found 43.3% of Ugandans aged 10 and over owned a mobile phone, 53.7% in towns against 37% in rural areas; UCC said its universal service fund had trained more than 13,000 women and reached over 11,000 people in rural education programmes between 2020 and 2026.

2026-10-22-xaf-africa-must-own-its-digit.summary: A second account of Luminate chief executive Melanie Hui's BUILD 2026 keynote, adding her point from the same commissioned research that Africa's undersea internet cables follow old trade and extraction routes.

2026-10-22-xaf-african-governments-custo.summary: African public agencies are starting to buy locally built AI tools for welfare, health and procurement, partly to keep public data under local control, though tight budgets and limited data access hold startups back. Togo's AI laboratory, which grew out of using phone and satellite data to target Novissi pandemic cash transfers, now works with more than ten agencies on over 70 projects, and Kenya and Rwanda are also looking for local applications. A UN-backed call run with the ITU and Research ICT Africa, which closed on 2 October, is selecting African AI products to present to officials in Accra.

2026-10-22-xaf-afrinic-ixp-sijil-istikhd.summary: BTW Media argued that AFRINIC should disclose how its IPv4 reserve for internet exchange points is being used before the community decides whether to enlarge it from a /16 to a /15. AFRINIC's policy keeps a contiguous /24 beside each peering assignment so an exchange can grow to a /23 without renumbering, but its extended statistics file does not separate reserved blocks, so the remaining contiguous space cannot be seen. Minutes of the AFRINIC-37 policy meeting of 24 June 2026 record staff promising consumption figures and NAPafrica describing two Johannesburg /23 blocks close to needing a /22.

2026-10-22-xaf-au-member-states-validate.summary: AU member states validated the African Continental Health Data Governance Framework in Addis Ababa on 22 October 2026, the first common continental approach to governing health data, proposing a federated model for sharing across borders. Africa CDC will finalise it with the agreed amendments and take it through AU policy processes, with consideration expected in 2027.

2026-10-22-xaf-cybercrime-crackdown-afri.summary: INTERPOL's Operation Serengeti III, run by police in 21 countries from 29 June to 31 August 2026, arrested 1,462 suspects, disrupted 10,909 malicious networks and recovered more than USD 105 million, against identified losses above USD 385 million and 65,929 victims. In Uganda alone, 365 foreign nationals were arrested over investment and pension frauds aimed at victims in Asia; the operation was co-funded by the EU-Council of Europe GLACY-e project.

2026-10-22-xaf-icbc-standard-bank-rmb-pa.summary: ICBC and Standard Bank Group, authorised in June as joint renminbi clearing bank for Africa, announced ten measures in Beijing on 19 October to expand RMB payments, financing and clearing on the continent. They include an interbank financing facility of more than RMB 10 billion for African financial institutions, wider coverage of China's CIPS payment system among African institutions and a guide to using the RMB in 19 African countries; China's central bank said RMB flows tied to China-Africa goods trade rose 40% in 2025.

2026-10-22-xca-afrique-centrale-a-librev.summary: An account of the opening of the ARTAC session in Libreville on 20 October 2026, where Gabon's digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba called regulatory harmonisation a political act and a step toward a single Central African digital market. Delegations came from DR Congo, Congo, Cameroon, Chad, Equatorial Guinea, the Central African Republic and São Tomé and Príncipe, and the six working groups created on 29 May 2026 were formally launched.

2026-10-22-xca-gabon-telecommunications-.summary: The Central African telecoms regulators' assembly ARTAC closed its 4th extraordinary session in Libreville on 21 October 2026 by adopting revised statutes, rules of procedure and financial regulations and admitting São Tomé and Príncipe's regulator. Executive president Christian Katende called for the roadmaps of the six permanent working groups to be put into effect.

2026-10-22-zaf-digital-id-could-change-h.summary: DIDx, a South African digital identity firm with a commercial stake in the outcome, told TechCentral that a credential from home affairs' MyMzansi digital ID app could seed a payment credential under the Reserve Bank's PEMKey programme, sparing users a second onboarding. The Reserve Bank has not said whether MyMzansi credentials will be accepted or published the PEMKey sandbox participants.

2026-10-22-zaf-malatsi-orders-faster-bro.summary: South Africa's communications minister Solly Malatsi issued a policy direction to Icasa under the Electronic Communications Act, gazetted on 20 October 2026, building on the 2023 rapid-deployment policy. It directs a review of the 2010 Facilities Leasing Regulations, new rapid-deployment regulations, a national GIS database of communications infrastructure and a dispute-resolution process between operators and landowners.

2026-10-22-zaf-mzansi-mind-sovereign-ai-.summary: HPE announced that Mzansi Mind, Solcon Capital's enterprise AI platform built on its Siya language model for all official South African languages, chose HPE servers with NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and HPE Juniper switches, hosted at Equinix's Johannesburg data centre. The platform cites local regulatory and data-residency requirements and plans to extend to other African markets.

2026-10-22-zaf-premier-ntuli-launches-fi.summary: KwaZulu-Natal's premier launched a fibre pre-provisioning proof of concept at the Empangeni Phase 1A housing development near Richards Bay, building fibre into 405 new homes as they are constructed, in partnership with Huawei. The province presents it as a model for laying connectivity before settlements are occupied.

2026-10-23-ago-pr-autoriza-50-milhoes-us.summary: A presidential despacho signed on 14 October 2026 authorises USD 50 million to extend broadband to unserved areas of Angola, schools and care homes first, through a public tender run under the director-general of the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa. Polígrafo África sets this against a 2026 state budget line of Kz 62.7 billion, about USD 67 million, for the national broadband network.

2026-10-23-ben-benin-lanip-deploie-des-t.summary: Benin's identification agency ANIP began issuing tablets to arrondissement secretaries in several communes on 19 October 2026, so residents can change the signature and phone number on their record locally instead of at ANIP's main offices. The tablets add to the ANIP BJ app and web portal, which already allow phone numbers to be updated.

2026-10-23-bfa-burkina-securite-numeriqu.summary: Burkina Faso's information systems security agency ANSSI launched a national network of information systems security officers (RSSI) and cyber focal points in Ouagadougou on 23 October 2026. The network is meant to give ministries and public institutions a standing framework for coordination, information sharing and capacity building on cyber risks and incidents, and institutions were asked to designate security officers and give them resources.

2026-10-23-civ-cote-d-ivoire-welcomes-ec.summary: An international seminar on blockchain and digital assets in Abidjan, co-organised by the VITIB technology zone and Valoores Africor and attended by digital transition minister Djibril Ouattara, discussed how the technology could support Côte d'Ivoire's economy. The minister said the government aims both to enable innovation and to build supervisory mechanisms and trust frameworks, and VITIB's director-general said it plans a blockchain centre of excellence to train and assist the state and businesses.

2026-10-23-civ-cote-divoire-loneci-instr.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's civil registration and identification office, ONECI, is training municipal civil registrars in Yamoussoukro from 22 to 24 October on its new platform for requesting and obtaining birth, marriage and death certificates online. Its director general told registrars the platform does not replace their legal role.

2026-10-23-cmr-cameroon-summit-calls-for.summary: A second account of the Yaoundé Declaration, adding its call for interoperable digital identity, payments and data-exchange systems built on open standards, and for a once-only principle under which citizens are not asked again for information an administration already holds.

2026-10-23-cmr-yaounde-declaration-targe.summary: The Yaoundé Declaration on E-Governance and Artificial Intelligence in Africa, adopted when the E-Gov'A conference closed on 17 October 2026, asks African governments to host all classified critical or sovereign public data inside their own borders by 2030, and where domestic capacity is lacking to prefer another African country over providers off the continent. The organisers, Smart Click Africa and Digital Business Africa, are to run an African Observatory for E-Government and AI; the hosting target is a recommendation and binds no government.

2026-10-23-cod-itie-rdc-donnees-et-divul.summary: The data page of EITI DR Congo reports 2023 extractive revenue of USD 5.85 billion, 5.61 billion of it from mining and 234.3 million from oil, from 134 reporting entities. It also publishes the beneficial ownership register set up under Law 25/048 of 1 July 2025 and a ministerial order of 8 July 2026, now listing 202 beneficial owners of 54 companies, two of them politically exposed persons.

2026-10-23-cod-nbsinfos-sekimonyo-etat-n.summary: An opinion piece by economist Jo M. Sekimonyo, chancellor of Université Lumumba, argues that DR Congo still lacks a digitised state almost eight years into Félix Tshisekedi's presidency, despite the 2023 digital code giving electronic documents the same legal value as paper. He holds that scattered platforms and strategies have left core administrative procedures untouched, citing the presidency's correspondence handling, and urges the executive to refocus on digitising the state as a whole.

2026-10-23-cpv-bcv-preve-lancar-projecto.summary: Banco de Cabo Verde governor Óscar Santos said in Mindelo on 23 October 2026 that the central bank plans to pilot its Speed system, which lets people pay by mobile phone even without a balance, on one island or remote locality before the end of the year. The launch still depends on agreement with banks, telecom operators and the regulator over running costs, which the BCV will bear at first; he put the banked share of the population at close to 90%.

2026-10-23-dza-la-cnr-lance-le-projet-du.summary: Algeria's national pension fund, the CNR, launched "Takaoudi All in One", a single digital desk in every local agency where a staff member helps retirees and beneficiaries install the Takaoudi app, open accounts and use online services. The fund has more than 19 e-services and plans more in the last quarter of 2026.

2026-10-23-egy-helping-young-minds-acros.summary: Google announced a US$2.4 million Google.org grant to INJAZ Al-Arab to take its Arabic online-safety curriculum, Abtal Al Internet (Be Internet Awesome), into classrooms in nine Middle East and North African countries over four years, aiming to reach more than 2.3 million students in countries including Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia. The curriculum covers misinformation, scams, cyberbullying and protecting private data; Google also set out default protections for users under 18 on its platforms.

2026-10-23-eth-strengthening-digital-rig.summary: The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission is adding the digital rights of persons with disabilities and older persons to its monitoring mandate. It presented a draft digital-inclusion monitoring toolkit at a CIPESA-facilitated staff workshop on 21-22 September 2026.

2026-10-23-gha-ghana-pledges-to-link-off.summary: Ghana's Government Statistician, writing on the opening of the tenth Statistical Commission for Africa, called for official statistics broken down to community level and tied to maps. He committed the Ghana Statistical Service to five steps, including early preparation for the 2031 census.

2026-10-23-gin-ministere-de-lelevage-alp.summary: Guinea's Ministry of Livestock presented NGAYNAAKO on 22 October 2026, a platform through which farmers and other livestock-sector actors can obtain the ministry's documents, regulations and support schemes without travelling to its offices. Minister Alpha Bacar Barry said it will work in national languages with AI assistance and will count the farms operating in the country; the ministry had already moved its mail handling online.

2026-10-23-iec-chairman-declares-final-v.summary: The Gambia's electoral commission will give parties the final voter register, combining the 2021 register with the 2026 supplementary registration, only after the revising courts finish and names ordered removed are expunged. The opposition UDP had asked why the commission announced 212,095 new registrations when the dataset it received held 183,163.

2026-10-23-ken-kenya-expands-ai-training.summary: A second Kenyan cohort of the UNESCO-Oxford course on AI and Digital Transformation in Government opened on 21 October 2026, aimed at 9,000 national and county public servants, after 1,239 of the first cohort's 2,730 learners graduated at the Kenya School of Government on 8 October. The course belongs to DigiKen, a Joint SDG Fund programme led by UNESCO with EU and donor funding.

2026-10-23-ken-kenya-s-konza-technopolis.summary: A second account of the Konza cloud expansion agreement, naming the counterparty as the PPP Project Facilitation Fund under the National Treasury and listing feasibility work and an investment framework among the costs it covers.

2026-10-23-ken-kenya-s-technopolis-autho.summary: Kenya's Konza Technopolis Development Authority has put live a Digital Telematics Platform for the National Transport and Safety Authority, which registers and certifies vehicle speed limiters and lets the regulator identify non-compliant vehicles. The authority presents the project as a step toward acting as a technology supplier to government beyond its smart-city remit.

2026-10-23-ken-konza-data-centre-set-for.summary: Kenya's Public Private Partnerships Directorate signed a funding agreement on 23 October 2026 to prepare the Konza National Data Centre Cloud Expansion and Smart City Facilities Project, including hiring a transaction adviser to structure it for a private partner. The project joined the PPP pipeline in December 2025 and is presented as strengthening sovereign cloud capacity; no private partner has been chosen, and the agreement does not mean construction has started.

2026-10-23-lbr-orange-liberia-launches-5.summary: Orange Liberia launched 5G and presented itself as the country's first 5G provider. It gave no coverage areas, service packages or rollout scale.

2026-10-23-lso-lesotho-urged-to-turn-inn.summary: Opening Lesotho's third National Science, Technology and Innovation Week, ICT and science minister Nthati Moorosi said research must turn into products, businesses and jobs rather than stopping at publication. She said a Research and Innovation Policy to commercialise research is awaiting approval.

2026-10-23-mli-intelligence-artificielle.summary: In an interview with Mali's national news agency, digital governance specialist Tidiani Togola, founder of Tuwindi, said Mali has made a start on AI, with the CIAR-Mali centre's Kati site opened in September and a Tier III national data centre in service since January, but has published no national AI strategy. He noted that the personal data law dates from 2013, that about 35% of Malians use the internet, and that WIPO's Global Innovation Index 2025 puts Mali 135th of 139.

2026-10-23-moz-governo-prepara-lei-para-.summary: Mozambique's education and culture minister Edson Macuácua said on 22 October 2026 that the government is preparing a law to regulate artificial intelligence in education, centred on ethical and responsible use, fundamental rights and copyright. He spoke at the launch of MAZA IA, a learning tool built by MOZEDUCA with Vodacom Moçambique, and called for national solutions, wider access to digital platforms for poorer students and investment in teacher training.

2026-10-23-moz-works-under-way-at-ressan.summary: Works have begun on a one-stop border post at Ressano Garcia on the Mozambique-South Africa border, at about 980m meticais, with six lanes, joint immigration and customs controls and integrated, automated border systems. The target is to cut transit for mineral trucks from up to an hour to about five minutes.

2026-10-23-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet on 23 October 2026 noted the setting up of a Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency branch in Rodrigues for year-round e-government outreach, after an August session there onboarded some 500 citizens onto the MauPass digital identity and the KOREK! platform. It also noted laptops and assistive equipment for blind and visually impaired secondary pupils with the Mauritius Telecom Foundation and a CERT-MU advisory on critical PHP vulnerabilities, alongside measures following the riots of 12 to 18 October and the water shortage.

2026-10-23-nga-airtel-globacom-mtn-face-.summary: Nigeria's House of Representatives summoned the chief executives of MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria and Globacom to appear before an ad hoc committee on 28 October 2026 over network quality, following an MTN outage in early October across several states and the capital. NCC figures put fibre cuts at 44,678 from January to September 2026, alongside 23,954 cases of denied site access, 73% of them attributed to insecurity.

2026-10-23-nga-nigeria-delegation-to-app.summary: A Nigerian delegation led by communications minister Bosun Tijani attended a KOICA training programme on digital governance in Seoul, run with Sangmyung University and the Korea Productivity Centre. Speaking for the delegates, data protection commissioner Vincent Olatunji credited KOICA's help with Nigeria's eGovernment Masterplans 1.0 and 2.0.

2026-10-23-nga-nigeria-s-first-lady-lays.summary: Nigeria's First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, laid the foundation stone of the Renewed Hope Startup Hub in Wuye, Abuja, funded by a USD 10.4 million grant from Japan through JICA and intended for incubation, hardware prototyping and research. NITDA's director-general said the agency's programmes had supported more than 995 startups and created about 7,596 jobs over three years.

2026-10-23-nga-nigeria-uk-deepen-collabo.summary: The British Standards Institution and Nigeria's National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics ran an executive workshop on AI governance and standards for senior officials and regulators, under the UK's Digital Access Programme, covering ISO/IEC 42001 and ISO/IEC 23894. The British High Commission presented it as part of several years of BSI work with NITDA, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria and the data protection regulator.

2026-10-23-rwa-rwandans-report-lower-sat.summary: The Rwanda Governance Board's 13th Rwanda Governance Scorecard, published on 22 October 2026, scored service delivery at 68.48%, down from 71.73% and the lowest of its eight categories, while security and public order stood at 90.15%. Digitally delivered services scored 60.98% against 77.83% for services from public institutions, businesses and NGOs; satisfaction with the Irembo platform fell 5.60 points to 81.80% and e-court filing 13.60 points to 65.40%, and the report cited ICT ministry data that only 11% of government services were fully online in 2024.

2026-10-23-sdn-sudan-press-syndicate-rej.summary: Sudan's journalists' syndicate and rights groups oppose a justice ministry amendment adding publishing in media and on electronic platforms to Article 51 of the 1991 Criminal Code, on waging war against the state, which carries penalties up to death. They also reject a planned national cybercrime mechanism with powers to monitor media and social platforms; the minister defended both.

2026-10-23-sdn-sudanese-journalists-synd.summary: The Sudanese Journalists Syndicate rejected an amendment made by Temporary Decree No. 7 of 2026 that extends a 1991 Criminal Act provision on undermining the constitutional order, which carries penalties up to death or life imprisonment, to publication through electronic and media platforms. It also opposed the National Mechanism to Combat Cybercrime that the prime minister ordered formed on 19 October, whose remit includes monitoring media and social media content and bringing cases on the state's behalf, and called for both to be withdrawn and the cybercrime law reviewed.

2026-10-23-sen-homologation-des-medicame.summary: Senegal's pharmaceutical regulator, the Agence sénégalaise de réglementation pharmaceutique (ARP), launched an online platform for medicines marketing authorisation on 23 October 2026, on which applicants file CTD-format dossiers and follow their progress on a single portal with each step traced. The module is the first part of an integrated regulatory information system meant to connect imports, clinical trials, licensing, batch release and pharmacovigilance.

2026-10-23-sle-natca-boss-intensifies-na.summary: Sierra Leone's National Communications Authority stepped up a nationwide campaign from 20 October 2026 for mobile subscribers to link their SIM cards to their National Identification Numbers before a 1 November deadline. It is working with the National Civil Registration Authority and the mobile operators, and presents the linkage as a defence against SIM fraud and identity theft.

2026-10-23-swz-govt-plans-2-000km-fibre-.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister Savannah Maziya said on Eswatini TV that the ministry will lay about 2,000 km of fibre to bring free Wi-Fi to more than 800 schools, and aims to build digital skills for about 200,000 people. She gave no timetable or cost.

2026-10-23-tcd-education-le-pareab-lance.summary: Chad's education ministry and the World Bank-funded PARAEB project began distributing 39,000 tablets with power banks to primary teachers, preloaded with curricula, teacher guides and the Teach and Coach classroom tools. The first phase covers four academies and 9,375 teachers.

2026-10-23-tgo-jnpdp-2026-l-ipdcp-mobili.summary: Togo's data protection authority, the IPDCP, will hold the country's first National Personal Data Protection Day in Lomé on 29 October 2026, on personal data and digital sovereignty, with a panel of counterpart authorities from Benin, Burkina Faso, Mali and Senegal. Ahead of it, the authority planned an awareness session for over 250 young people in Dapaong on 24 October and announced a network of more than 500 volunteers to carry its messages locally.

2026-10-23-tgo-togo-adds-building-materi.summary: Togo's Ministry of Territorial Planning and Urban Development put two new services on the Service Public portal: ordering compressed stabilised earth blocks and requesting geospatial maps. The portal lists 155 procedures, according to the national digital observatory, and handled more than 400,000 requests in 2024 against 100,000 in 2023.

2026-10-23-xaf-afrinic-s-four-pool-ipv4-.summary: A draft AFRINIC policy, AFPUB-2026-IPv4-003-DRAFT01, submitted in June 2026 and under discussion, would sort recovered IPv4 space into four pools by origin, cap ordinary requests and open a first-come queue once the two main pools are empty. It is a proposal, not adopted policy.

2026-10-23-xca-centrafriquenews-beac-res.summary: The governor of the central African central bank BEAC, Yvon Sana Bangui, met the Reserve Bank of India's governor in New Delhi on 20 October 2026, and the two agreed to explore technical cooperation on payment systems, financial cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and currency swaps. India's experience with instant payments, interoperability and mass financial inclusion was the focus; nothing was signed, and technical teams are to set priorities in the coming weeks.

2026-10-23-xgl-un-expert-highlights-glob.summary: In a report to the UN General Assembly, the Special Rapporteur on the right to privacy, Ana Brian Nougrères, found that none of the cross-border transfer instruments she reviewed, from adequacy decisions to standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules, protects privacy by itself. She urged States to negotiate a legally binding international instrument on data transfers, and asked for low-cost tools so developing countries and small firms can use transfer mechanisms and for data protection to be written into digital trade agreements.

2026-10-23-xss-africa-emerges-as-d2d-sat.summary: GSMA Intelligence's Q3 2026 satellite tracker finds 13% of mobile operators in sub-Saharan Africa have satellite partnerships, the lowest share of any region against 19% worldwide, and expects broad direct-to-device coverage, Africa included, around 2028 or 2029. Airtel Africa launched Starlink Mobile in DR Congo in August, while early services are limited to messaging and licensing remains the main obstacle, as Starlink's provisional suspension in Senegal shows.

2026-10-23-xwa-signature-des-accords-bil.summary: Burkina Faso signed bilateral roaming agreements with Benin, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal in Ouagadougou on 23 October 2026, after a meeting of WAEMU's committee of national digital regulators. The minister, Aminata Zerbo/Sabane, called for close follow-up so the agreements are put into effect.

2026-10-23-xwa-uemoa-telecommunications-.summary: Burkina Faso's telecoms regulator signed bilateral roaming agreements with its counterparts in Benin, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal in Ouagadougou on 23 October 2026, under the WAEMU framework. The WAEMU Commission and the regulators called for the commitments to be put into effect so users get cheaper, clearer roaming terms.

2026-10-23-zaf-sars-s-expanded-auto-asse.summary: The South African Revenue Service reported more than 6.9 million returns auto-assessed by 30 September 2026, 20% more than a year earlier, after extending auto-assessment to some provisional taxpayers, drawing on more verified third-party data and sending assessment notices by WhatsApp. Between 1 July and 19 October it paid R33 billion in refunds to 3.1 million taxpayers, 85% of them within 72 hours.

2026-10-23-zwe-zimbabwe-approves-nationa.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera told a cybersecurity summit on 21 October 2026 that the Cabinet Committee on National Development had approved a National AI Charter that morning, setting out regulation, ethics and governance for AI adoption. She said a 'Penguin AI' project to build local datasets would launch before December, a National Regulatory Digital Committee was being formed, and the government wants an AI Act in force by late next year.

2026-10-24-benedict-oramah-africa-must-b.summary: In an interview after the IMF and World Bank meetings, former Afreximbank president Benedict Oramah, now running the strategy firm Marob, argued that Africa should build its own AI models rather than supply data to foreign firms. He said data centres need power the continent lacks, proposed technology parks with concentrated energy supply, and said Nigeria's cheap gas lets it sell electricity at prices that would draw investors; he added that only private capital can close an infrastructure gap he puts at about US$100 billion a year.

2026-10-24-bwa-atu-advances-ipv6-testbed.summary: The African Telecommunications Union moved its IPv6 testbed for Botswana forward after a due-diligence visit to the regulator BOCRA, which has picked a university by tender to host it. The testbed is part of an ICANN-funded ATU programme under which 52 specialists from 26 African countries have been trained; the visit coincided with a Smart Africa and CRASA workshop in Gaborone on 20 to 22 October on cutting roaming costs in southern Africa.

2026-10-24-bwa-govt-moves-to-clear-omang.summary: Botswana's labour and home affairs minister Pius Mokgware said the backlog of Omang national identity cards should be cleared within two to three weeks, with nearly half of the 45,000 cards needed already produced. That would bring back the normal 14-day wait after a shortage of blank cards and staff held production up; applicants notified by SMS were urged to collect their cards.

2026-10-24-cod-cybersecurite-felix-tshis.summary: At the 101st Council of Ministers on 23 October 2026, President Félix Tshisekedi ordered an audit of DR Congo's public IT systems to find security flaws, coordinated by the posts and telecommunications ministry with the digital economy ministry. The interior and defence ministries are to tighten protection of sensitive systems, and the finance ministry is to work with the Banque Centrale du Congo on public-finance platforms, payment systems and critical infrastructure; the order came a day after the digital economy ministry warned of two critical PHP vulnerabilities.

2026-10-24-cod-rdc-des-personnes-poursui.summary: The justice minister spoke at a press briefing. He said several people prosecuted for social-media offences are held at Makala prison in Kinshasa. He added that some of them presented themselves as communicators for the presidency. He said nobody is exempt from prosecution on grounds of political affiliation.

2026-10-24-cpv-bcv-volta-a-prometer-proj.summary: Banco de Cabo Verde governor Óscar Santos again promised a pilot of the Speed mobile payment system before the end of 2026, on one island or remote locality; the system was first announced in December 2025 to start in the first quarter of this year. He said the launch still depends on agreement with banks, telecom operators and the regulator over running costs, which the central bank will cover at first.

2026-10-24-cpv-cabo-verde-starlink-tripl.summary: Figures from Cabo Verde's regulator ARME, reported by Lusa, show Starlink's share of national internet traffic rising from 6% in the second quarter of 2025 to 18% a year later, although it held only 0.87% of internet subscriptions at the end of June. Over the same period Cabo Verde Telecom's traffic share fell from 89% to 78% and Unitel's from 6% to 4%; the country had 500,263 internet subscriptions, 85% of them mobile broadband.

2026-10-24-egy-egypt-forum-2026-outlines.summary: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly announced the closing recommendations of Egypt Forum 2026, issued as presidential directives with targets running to 2030, covering wages, housing, health, education and industry. On digital government they aim to digitise all public services within three years and to double the Digital Egypt platform's 250 services to 500 by the close of 2026, and basic fixed-internet packages are to go from 50 GB to 100 GB.

2026-10-24-egy-egypts-tax-authority-taps.summary: The Tax Authority contracted eTax to build and run a platform that analyses electronic-invoice and e-receipt data to select cases for examination. The work covers the data warehouse, integration, hosting and security.

2026-10-24-gab-gabon-digital-interview-n.summary: Ahead of the first Gabon Digital Week, digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba told the national news agency that satellite providers such as Starlink and Eutelsat will be authorised in the coming months to cover more than 200 unconnected villages, alongside a universal service fund. He said the Gabon Fiber programme with SPIN and Gabon Télécom has laid 196 km of fibre, connecting Lambaréné, Fougamou and Mouila, and that ministries are digitising driving licences, payments and revenue collection, digital identity and civil registration.

2026-10-24-gab-gabon-la-hac-leve-la-susp.summary: Gabon's media regulator, the Haute autorité de la communication, lifted on 24 October 2026 the nationwide suspension of social media it had ordered on 17 February. It cited three presidential ordinances of 26 February regulating social-media use and reporting protocols now operating with TikTok, Meta and YouTube that give it access to their tools for flagging illicit content.

2026-10-24-gab-union-gabon-digital-week-.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry announced a Gabon Digital Week at the Palais des Congrès in Libreville from 26 to 30 October 2026, under the president's patronage. The programme includes a government seminar on the national digitalisation strategy, presentation of the Gabon Digital programme, the official start of a 5G pilot with Moov Africa Gabon Telecom and Airtel Gabon, and an African Union specialised technical committee where some fifteen ministers are to draft a Libreville Declaration ahead of ITU meetings in Doha.

2026-10-24-gha-gss-population-housing-ce.summary: The Ghana Statistical Service's census page presents the 2021 Population and Housing Census as the latest national count, with its reports, regional and district profiles and population indicators, beside earlier editions back to 1984. It gives the next census as projected for 2030, with planning under way.

2026-10-24-ken-kenya-statistics-bureau-p.summary: The Kenya National Bureau of Statistics held a first capacity-sharing workshop with the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, under CGIAR programmes, on bringing spatial analytics into official statistics. Sessions covered satellite crop mapping, future food demand against climate hazards, local socioeconomic and food-security indicators and environmental SDG measures such as mountain green cover, with KIPPRA and IFPRI taking part.

2026-10-24-lbr-pul-condemns-governments-.summary: At a Governance Commission policy dialogue, the Press Union of Liberia called for the immediate withdrawal of a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement the Civil Service Agency has introduced for civil servants, saying it overturns the Freedom of Information Act and strips the Independent Information Commission, which opposed it, of its authority. The union also said most agencies the commission assessed had not appointed public information officers and that Liberia lacks an enforceable data-protection framework.

2026-10-24-lby-qanwan-and-huawei-sign-co.summary: The Qanwan investment foundation and Huawei's Libya branch signed a cooperation agreement on investment and technology at the General Union of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture. It aims at innovation, expertise exchange and digital transformation. No value or specific project was stated.

2026-10-24-mar-office-des-changes-e-decl.summary: The Office des changes opened an international tender for an e-declarations platform. It would digitise declarations of property, assets and funds held abroad by resident Moroccans, and the statistical surveys owed by resident companies. The work runs in five phases under a steering committee, within the Office's 2025-2029 digital strategy.

2026-10-24-mdg-liste-electorale-biometri.summary: Madagascar's electoral commission (CENI) received IT equipment worth US$750,000 from Japan and UNDP on 23 October 2026. The kit is for processing and securing voter data ahead of a biometric roll. The roll now being rebuilt is still alphanumeric; over 7.16 million citizens had registered against a target of 14 million. Five local radio stations also received equipment for civic education.

2026-10-24-mdg-lutte-contre-la-cybercrim.summary: Madagascar's 96-article cybercrime bill n° 042/2026, which would replace the 2014 law and was postponed at September's extraordinary session, returns to committee in the National Assembly on 2 November. Contested provisions include article 75, giving a new digital investigation unit (UPIN) permanent direct access to operators' systems with fines of 100 to 500 million ariary for refusal, and article 52 on criminal liability for administrators of pages and groups; the access-to-public-information bill n° 017/2025 is also on the session's agenda.

2026-10-24-mrt-ami-health-and-digital-tr.summary: Mauritania's health minister and minister of digital transformation met in Nouakchott on 24 October 2026 on making the new health centres built under the capital's emergency development programme digitally ready before they open in the coming days. They agreed to form a joint technical team to visit the centres, set out each one's requirements and close the gaps found.

2026-10-24-sdn-new-arab-criminal-code-am.summary: Rights groups and activists warn that a temporary decree issued by army commander Abdel Fattah al-Burhan under Sudan's Miscellaneous Amendments Act of 2026 extends Article 51 of the 1991 criminal code, on inciting war against the state and punishable by death or life imprisonment, to electronic and media publications. They say it is likely to be used against dissent alongside the new cybercrime mechanism, and local reports describe a marked fall in social-media posting from Sudan since the change.

2026-10-24-swz-e15-million-uneswa-unipod.summary: The University of Eswatini is building a E15 million innovation pod at its library, funded by the UN Development Programme. The vice-chancellor announced it at the 44th graduation on 24 October 2026. The pod will give students from the country's institutions space and equipment to start businesses, and the communications commission pledged US$150,000.

2026-10-24-swz-govt-restores-13-online-s.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry said on 23 October 2026 that 13 government online services hit by disruptions had been restored with the Royal Science and Technology Park, among them the Government in Your Hand platform, e-Visa, the Social Registry, the elderly and disability grants system and IFMIS. The government website and other platforms were still being restored, and the statement gave no cause for the outage.

2026-10-24-uga-exim-bank-uganda-launches.summary: Exim Bank Uganda launched Exim Global Pay in Kampala, a cross-border payment service that connects its individual and business customers to TerraPay's international network. It is meant for payments to overseas suppliers and for personal costs abroad such as school fees, health care and family support, and spares the bank from building its own bilateral links; no fees, volumes or corridors were given.

2026-10-24-uga-ngo-bureau-to-automate-re.summary: Uganda's National Bureau for NGOs plans to move registration, document submission and payment online, with online registration expected by the end of the financial year. The interior ministry is preparing a platform for agencies handling NGO matters to share information.

2026-10-24-xea-igad-advances-regional-co.summary: IGAD's World Bank-backed Food Systems Resilience Program held a four-day regional workshop in Arba Minch, Ethiopia, from 21 to 24 October 2026 on digital advice to farmers on weather and climate, and on gender in food systems. Experts from seven member states, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, South Sudan and Uganda, shared national experience and discussed strengthening IGAD's DACAS knowledge network, with calls for regional standards on data quality, interoperability and data sharing.

2026-10-24-zwe-zinara-rolls-out-multi-cu.summary: The road authority launched a self-service e-wallet that takes toll fees, vehicle licensing, radio licences and third-party insurance payments in several currencies. It runs on iOS, Android, web and USSD, and full access requires uploading an identity document.

2026-10-25-bdi-butihinda-la-digitalisati.summary: Butihinda commune in Burundi held a practical session on 24 and 25 October 2026 for its zonal assistant accountants and tax collectors on AK-SOFT, integrated software for communal accounting, budget and financial management, following a Primature workshop for communal finance officers at Buhumuza on 20 to 23 October. Staff are entering the commune's revenue and spending from 1 July 2025 through the first quarter of fiscal 2026-27; participants asked for more training and said they need stable internet and continuing technical support.

2026-10-25-bfa-burkina-faso-vers-la-crea.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition ministry met startups, SMEs, incubators, universities and partners in Ouagadougou on 21 October 2026 to gather their expectations for two projects in preparation: the services of a planned Mini-Technopôle TIC de Ouagadougou and a support fund for digital startups. The fund's amounts, eligibility rules and timetable are still to be set once the consultation ends.

2026-10-25-bfa-burkina-intelligence-arti.summary: The 2026-2030 national AI roadmap was validated on 19 June 2026 but has not been officially published. A ministry official presented it on 23 October with a projected budget of FCFA 30 billion, 23 proofs of concept, 500 experts and 5,000 specialised jobs by 2030. It targets hosting at least 80% of the data concerned inside the country.

2026-10-25-cobac-ai-regulation.summary: Central Africa's banking supervisor, COBAC, said in its 2025 annual report that it will begin applying AI and advanced analytics to banks' prudential returns over 2026 and 2027. The plan falls under its OWALI 2025-2029 strategy. No system in use is reported.

2026-10-25-cod-rdc-le-gouvernement-relan.summary: DR Congo relaunched its e-visa reform with a new competitive selection of a provider, after cancelling a June 2024 concession found gravely deficient. Workshops in mid-November 2026 will revise the specifications and pricing, and bids are to be evaluated in early 2027.

2026-10-25-dji-deux-projets-numeriques-d.summary: Djibouti's minister Mohamed Abdoulkader Moussa reviewed two IDA-funded digital projects with the regulator ARMD and the state information systems agency ANSIE and called for faster implementation. The US$10 million DFN project has completed 26 of 35 activities, with nearly 80% of funds committed and 56% disbursed, before it closes on 30 June 2027; the US$20 million EARDIP's cross-border links, twelve 4G sites and fibre loops to Dikhil, Tadjourah and Obock still await approval of commercial, environmental and social studies.

2026-10-25-gab-gabon-loi-de-finances-202.summary: Gabon's National Assembly examined the 2027 budget requests of the communication and digital economy ministries on 25 October. The digital economy ministry asks for FCFA 37.2 billion in 2027, down about FCFA 16.5 billion from FCFA 53.7 billion in 2026, for connectivity, digital sovereignty and modernising the administration, while the communication ministry's request rises to FCFA 21.5 billion from FCFA 17.5 billion.

2026-10-25-gab-permis-digitalise-apres-p.summary: Gabon's transport ministry said enrolment for the digitalised driving licence would resume on 26 October 2026 at five Greater Libreville sites, after a suspension from 21 September while the platform moved to new infrastructure.

2026-10-25-gha-bright-simons-flags-compu.summary: IMANI's Bright Simons argued that Ghana's national AI strategy misprints its computing targets, giving 10²¹ and 10²⁵ FLOPS as '1021' and '1025', and that the 2027 target read correctly would mean some 200,000 top-end chips and 500 MW of power costing about US$24 billion, about a hundred times what the US$250 million AI data centre under procurement would provide. He questioned the value of GhanaChat, the ministry's planned national AI model, putting the data centre's likely subsidy near US$61 million annually, and suggested starting with a government-hosted AI assistant for civil servants on roughly 144 GPUs, at US$13 million up front.

2026-10-25-mar-le-plf-2027-veut-faire-du.summary: The cabinet adopted draft finance law 60-26 for 2027 on 20 October 2026. The finance minister presented it to Parliament on 23 October. Its digital section provides for a Cloud First circular making cloud the default for new public projects. It also provides for a 50 MW sovereign data centre in Rabat over 2027-2029. It remains a draft that Parliament can amend.

2026-10-25-moz-precos-de-passaporte-cart.summary: A private document-services firm said on 25 October 2026 that official fees are unchanged at the public counters. The fees cover identity cards, residence permits, passports and driving licences. Its own service is an optional paid channel. An express passport costs the state fee of MZN 7,200. It adds a MZN 3,038.89 service fee and 16% VAT on that fee. Delivery takes one working day.

2026-10-25-mus-risque-de-cyberattaque-10.summary: About 70% of government websites, those running on PHP, were taken offline over the PHP2Shell flaw. The ICT minister said 85 to 90% of services were back by 24 October 2026, and that the delay lay with sites built by outside contractors. Mauritius Telecom put a free exposure-check tool online on 23 October.

2026-10-25-nga-citad-tasks-fg-on-indigen.summary: Opening the seventh Kano Social Influencers Summit, the Centre for Information Technology and Development (CITAD) urged Nigeria's federal government to invest in home-grown AI rather than buying foreign products, and to hold foreign technology companies accountable for the data they collect from Nigerians. Its executive director Yunusa Zakari Ya'u said much of the country's data is still analogue and fragmented, and that reliable electricity and water are preconditions for data centres.

2026-10-25-nga-ndpc-urges-responsible-ai.summary: At the Kano Social Influencers Summit organised by CITAD, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission warned influencers, developers and users against misusing personal data, urging them to verify content, disclose AI-generated material and not use people's faces, voices or data without authorisation. It said breaches of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and its implementation directive can draw financial penalties, and set out citizens' rights to access, correct and in some cases delete their data.

2026-10-25-nga-nigerians-recount-frustra.summary: Nigerians describe repeated visits to National Identity Management Commission offices without getting errors in their records corrected, with one applicant who made five trips before paying informal roadside agents to get her record changed. Others report time-outs on NIMC's mobile app and portal and failed NIN-SIM verification that left phone lines unusable, while an NIMC staff member blamed recurring network failures for disrupting service.

2026-10-25-sdn-ebs-general-manager-inter.summary: The general manager of the national payments operator said the account-to-account transfer service has passed 376 million transactions, at about 10 million a month and up 12% in 2026. Operations moved to secured sites outside Khartoum during the war. The next project is an instant payment system with a single national QR code.

2026-10-25-sle-bridging-the-digital-divi.summary: A paper by Alusine Boys Conteh and Peter Jesse Saxo-Decker surveyed 200 people running or planning digital businesses in Freetown, Bo and Makeni on Sierra Leone's digital entrepreneurship ecosystem. Only 12.5% judged the policy and regulatory framework effective, against 35% for digital literacy and 30% for infrastructure, with half unable to describe the policy environment at all; the authors conclude that policy clarity may be the most neglected factor and make recommendations to MoCTI, DSTI and development partners.

2026-10-25-som-somalia-launches-digital-.summary: A digital Ebola travel health pass began on 22 October 2026. Arrivals must file an online health declaration before travel. It was built by the National Institute of Health and starts at Aden Adde International Airport, with extension to other airports, seaports and land borders on no stated timeline.

2026-10-25-tun-le-hub-numerique-the-dot-.summary: The EU-funded hub marked its fifth anniversary on 23 October 2026. It reported support for more than 500 startups since 2021, 37 of them founded by diaspora Tunisians. It has incubated 140 startups from ten governorates. It has hosted over 3,000 events.

2026-10-25-uga-when-smart-cities-turn-me.summary: A researcher at a digital-rights organisation traces Uganda's EPSAuto traffic-fine system. It was switched on in June 2025 and suspended within days after complaints of wrong fines. On 6 October 2026 the Attorney General declared the 2021 contract for the intelligent transport monitoring system void. The author cites a report finding more than US$2 billion of surveillance spending in 11 countries. The author asks for open procurement.

2026-10-25-xna-league-of-arab-states-fou.summary: The League of Arab States held the fourth meeting of a joint expert committee on a Draft Arab Agreement on Personal Data Protection on 25 and 26 October 2026. The draft stems from an Algerian proposal approved by the Council of Arab Ministers of Justice. The results go to that council's session in Algeria in November 2026.

2026-10-25-zaf-south-africa-s-ai-strateg.summary: In an opinion piece, Ravi Naidoo argues that South Africa, with 34% of working-age people and 60% of under-25s unemployed, should steer AI adoption towards augmenting workers rather than replacing them. He proposes treating AI job displacement as a negative externality to be restricted or taxed, with pro-employment uses rewarded, through an AI Skills Augmentation Act and a business code of practice added to the King Codes, and rights for people over their own face, body and voice modelled on Denmark's copyright amendment.

2026-10-25-zwe-zimbabwe-wants-digital-pa.summary: Zimbabwe's central bank is in talks with NPCI International, the overseas arm of the body behind India's instant-payment system, on a real-time payment system meant to cut costs, move money faster between bank accounts and mobile wallets and make the gold-backed ZiG easier to use. The author, a trade policy researcher, argues the technology will only help the currency if Zimbabwean institutions keep control of the system, people can still pick freely between the ZiG and the US dollar, and monetary policy is credible, given the country's history of hyperinflation and failed currencies.

2026-10-26-ago-proposta-de-lei-da-identi.summary: Committees of Angola's National Assembly examined the government's bill on civil and criminal identification on 26 October 2026. The bill makes the Bilhete de Identidade the only valid identity document. It also simplifies issuing that card and the criminal record certificate.

2026-10-26-airtel-money-revenue-rises-34.summary: Airtel Money reported revenue up 34% to $830 million for the half year to 30 September 2026, its first results as a listed company, with customers up 18.7% to 56.7 million. Annualised processed value reached $270 billion in the second quarter.

2026-10-26-ben-2027-professional-electio.summary: The budget and public service ministry decided to hold the March-April 2027 professional elections by electronic vote. The COSI-Benin union confederation demanded an independent technical audit first. It cited 2023 e-elections in education and health. In those votes, third parties voted for registered voters.

2026-10-26-ben-a-abou-dhabi-romuald-wada.summary: Benin and the United Arab Emirates exchanged a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement in Abu Dhabi on 25 October 2026, with seven companion instruments. One is a letter of intent on data hosting and information systems. No amounts, scope or timetable were published for it, and the agreement awaits ratification.

2026-10-26-caf-vers-une-diversification-.summary: The country's international connectivity rests largely on a 935 km fibre segment of the Central African Backbone. Vandalism in March 2026 partly cut telecom services. A ministry official said in late August that a route eastward via South Sudan is under study, with the path and terms still to be set.

2026-10-26-cmr-cameroon-eyes-ai-led-grow.summary: The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications spoke at the World Bank's summit in Seoul on 19-22 October 2026. The Minister said a draft national digital-economy strategy is being finalised. It rests on national AI consultations. Its pillars are digital infrastructure, data governance, skills, research and responsible-AI rules.

2026-10-26-cmr-leadership-numerique-le-c.summary: Central African telecoms regulators set the headquarters of their regional body, ARTAC, in Cameroon at an extraordinary session in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026.
