Cameroon's regulator may designate the executive secretary. The session also adopted a resolution on a Central African ICT Observatory for sector data.

2026-10-26-dza-plateforme-tawassol-comme.summary: The Ministry of Internal Trade opened an online consumer portal at tawassol.commerce.gov.dz. Consumers can report unpriced goods, breaches of capped prices, hygiene failures and stock-outs. A mobile app is announced to follow.

2026-10-26-ebanx-integrates-opay-direct-.summary: EBANX became the first international payments provider to offer OPay Direct Debit, so global subscription merchants can collect recurring payments from Nigerian consumers through the OPay wallet. OPay claims 40 million monthly active users.

2026-10-26-egy-how-i-mapped-a-250-millio.summary: The reporter behind the Al-Pheratz investigation into the Benya–Khazna data centre at Maadi described the method for the Pulitzer Center on 26 October 2026. The reporter mapped brand names to legal entities across Egyptian records and Abu Dhabi Global Market filings. The investigation's findings are summarised under the Al-Pheratz entry.

2026-10-26-egy-planning-finance-nib-elec.summary: The planning minister told the Senate about an integrated electronic link. It joins the planning ministry, the finance ministry and the National Investment Bank. It was activated over the past four months, a first. It is meant to tighten monitoring of public investment and the allocation of project funding.

2026-10-26-eth-ethiopia-delivers-over-1-.summary: The trade ministry reported 1,088,787 business registration and licensing services delivered online over three months. Trade name clearance led with 579,785, and new business registrations numbered 60,409. Oromia accounted for 441,550.

2026-10-26-ethio-telecom-extends-4g-lte-.summary: Ethio telecom extended 4G LTE to 80 more Ethiopian towns. Its 2026/27 plan targets 4G population coverage of 95%, from 82.23%, across 1,500 towns.

2026-10-26-fdc-threatens-court-action-ov.summary: Uganda's Forum for Democratic Change threatened to sue over plans to give the Uganda Revenue Authority wider access to bank accounts. On 15 October 2026 a finance minister told Parliament the government would keep seeking that power. MPs had rejected it. The party also asked the Personal Data Protection Office to audit URA's access to NIRA's national ID records.

2026-10-26-gab-fonction-publique-5-38-mi.summary: Gabon's civil-service ministry asked parliament for FCFA 5.38bn for 2027, excluding staff costs, to digitise five procedures, bring 150 processing stations into service and deploy the SIGRH human-resources system. Only 32% of its 2026 envelope had been executed by end-October.

2026-10-26-gab-gabon-digital-week-la-5g-.summary: 5G networks were launched in Libreville at the opening of Gabon Digital Week. The regulator had given a favourable opinion on assigning frequency bands to Airtel Gabon and Moov Africa Gabon Telecom. Masts are going up in Greater Libreville and Port-Gentil. A gradual national rollout follows.

2026-10-26-gab-gabon-semaine-du-numeriqu.summary: Gabon Digital Week opened with the launch of an online register of the companies in the state's portfolio. The register is built to centralise and secure data on public holdings. The budget minister performed the launch on 26 October 2026. The register runs at www.fup.ga.

2026-10-26-gab-lancement-du-fichier-uniq.summary: Gabon's economy ministry launched the Fichier unique des participations, a digital register of the state's shareholdings, at Gabon Digital Week in Libreville on 26 October 2026. The Direction générale des Participations runs it with the digital economy ministry. It is meant to map state holdings and track their revenues.

2026-10-26-gha-undp-hands-over-90-laptop.summary: The UN Development Programme gave the Ghana Enterprises Agency 90 laptops. They are for the national rollout of the MSME Digital Gateway. Trained Digital Champions will use them to help small businesses reach support, financing information and markets. The work falls under a Joint SDG Fund programme with three other bodies.

2026-10-26-gin-fana-soumah-nomme-ministr.summary: A presidential decree read on 26 October 2026 appointed Fana Soumah as Guinea's Minister of Communication, Digital Economy and Innovation. President Mamadi Doumbouya signed it.

2026-10-26-gin-guinee-nimbapay-traite-7-.summary: Guinea's central bank said on 22 October 2026 that its instant payment system NimbaPay had seven connected institutions by 15 October. It had handled about 67,000 transactions worth over GNF 68bn. The bank is also drafting a payment-systems bill and a 2027–2030 payments strategy with World Bank support.

2026-10-26-gin-lancement-officiel-du-sys.summary: Guinea's fisheries ministry launched KONKÖE, an integrated management system for fishing licences and certificates, in Conakry on 26 October 2026. The first licence was signed through it at the ceremony, which fell under the Simandou 2040 programme.

2026-10-26-gin-peche-la-guinee-lance-le-.summary: The fisheries platform Konkoé, also called SIGPEM, was launched in Conakry on 26 October 2026 at a ceremony chaired by the presidency's chief of staff. Artisanal and industrial fishers can file applications by phone or computer and follow each step of their file. Fishing representatives asked for local-language help for users who cannot read.

2026-10-26-gnq-inege-avanza-en-la-valida.summary: Equatorial Guinea's statistics institute opened a technical validation workshop on 26 October 2026 with UNDP and FAO. Participants review the methods and data-collection tools for the fifth population census and the first agricultural census. It follows a strategy workshop held on 27-29 July 2026.

2026-10-26-government-ai-adoption-financ.summary: TechCabal argues that African governments' demand for AI does not yet make a market for local startups, citing a South African CIPC chatbot tender that pays only after delivery and a GIZ-Briter survey in which 44% of AI businesses target governments. It notes that Nigeria's N-ATLAS project discloses neither the contract's value nor its payment terms.

2026-10-26-lbr-impact-base-forecast.summary: The Liberia Meteorological Service publishes an impact-based forecast that states expected weather and its likely effects on people and infrastructure. Entries listed in October 2026, including those of 7 and 11 October, expected light rainfall across most of the country. The service says the product also gives safety advice for communities and agencies.

2026-10-26-lbr-pul-accuses-boakai-gol-sa.summary: The Press Union of Liberia's president, Julius Kanubah, asked the government on 23 October 2026 to withdraw a non-disclosure agreement imposed on civil servants. He said it overrides the Freedom of Information Act and the Independent Information Commission, which opposed it. He cited 78 of 103 assessed agencies without information officers, and no Data Authority.

2026-10-26-lby-national-council-for-huma.summary: A committee of the House of Representatives and Libya's human rights council began a joint review of a draft personal data protection law on 26 October 2026. The council's committee wrote the draft over two and a half years. It had Council of Europe expert review. It added a chapter on artificial intelligence. It sent the draft to the House as an initial proposal.

2026-10-26-mar-decret-2-26-831-attributi.summary: Morocco's decree 2-26-831 of 26 October 2026 sets the remit of Ahmed Rahhou, Minister of AI, Digital Transformation and Administrative Reform. It charges him with drafting and implementing government AI policy. It makes him the authority for telecoms under law 24.96 and places the Digital Development Agency under him.

2026-10-26-mar-plf-2027-ia-les-donnees-s.summary: Morocco's draft 2027 finance bill includes MAD 1.34 billion for digital sovereignty and artificial intelligence. Earlier bills had no such component. It covers cloud services across administrations and a sovereign data centre in Rabat. It also covers AI adapted to national languages and specialised training.

2026-10-26-maroc-telecom-group-revenue-r.summary: Maroc Telecom's group revenue rose 5.1% to MAD 28.68bn in the nine months to September 2026, with the Moov Africa subsidiaries up 6.9%. Mobile money revenue at the subsidiaries grew 18.8%.

2026-10-26-mdg-wearetech-mpianatra-schoo.summary: Madagascar's digital development ministry launched MPIANATRA, a school-management platform for tracking pupils' progress, on 24 October 2026; its deployment in public schools is still to be studied. It follows the NUIS single pupil identifier, piloted with about 180,000 pupils since May.

2026-10-26-moz-centro-pronto-document-ap.summary: Mozambique plans to open Centro Pronto document-application centres for the diaspora in Cape Town, Porto and England within six months, through its partnership with VFS. The state keeps the technology, data collection and document validation.

2026-10-26-moz-parlamento-alarga-calenda.summary: Mozambique's Assembly of the Republic may sit on Fridays and Saturdays during its session from 28 October to 22 December 2026. The reason is the volume of business. The plenary agenda for 6 November includes the bill on personal data protection. It also includes bills on the Highway Code and aeronautical registration.

2026-10-26-mus-mauritius-managed-entitie.summary: Mauritius's Data Protection Office issued updated guidance in September 2026, as described by an advisory firm. A management company must register as a controller for its own data and separately as a processor for entities it administers. Each managed entity needs its own registration and data protection officer.

2026-10-26-nga-protection-of-personal-pr.summary: In a BusinessDay interview, NDPC chief executive Vincent Olatunji describes building Nigeria's data protection commission since 2022 and the personal and sensitive data it regulates, with trust and accountability for AI as its next concern.

2026-10-26-nga-techcabal-infragora-afrid.summary: Infragora Global Capital plans to start building two AI-ready AFRIDATA data centres in Nigeria in the second and third quarters of 2027, a project it puts at $650 million to $1 billion, with financial close still to come. The centres would run on a dedicated 160-200 MW gas, renewable and battery plant.

2026-10-26-nga-trust-stamp-blip-three-ye.summary: Trust Stamp signed a three-year agreement with BLIP Limited, a Nigerian supplier of registration and certification platforms to government, announced on 26 October 2026. It covers tokenised biometric identity tools hosted in the customer's environment, under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. Trust Stamp expects more than one million enrolments in the first year.

2026-10-26-rwa-connectingafrica-ncsa-air.summary: Rwanda's National Cyber Security Authority partnered with Airtel Rwanda to support the University of Rwanda's CyberHub with student internships, alongside an MoU with MTN Rwanda. No value or term was stated.

2026-10-26-rwa-raia-agentic-workflows-re.summary: In October 2026 the Rwanda AI Agency sought firms for agentic-AI proofs of concept on three government platforms. The lots cover Mbaza complaints, IremboAI licensing and Kubaka building permits. The World Bank-financed work is to run from late March to 8 November 2027.

2026-10-26-tgo-togo-4-consultants-recher.summary: Togo's procurement regulator ARCOP is recruiting four consultants to set up a national e-procurement system, Togo First reported on 26 October 2026. The posts are a functional analyst, a procurement specialist, a change-management expert and a systems administrator. Applications close on 18 November 2026; no go-live date is given.

2026-10-26-tza-kamati-ya-bunge-yasisitiz.summary: Tanzania's parliamentary committee on Lands, Natural Resources and Tourism met in Dodoma on 21 October 2026 and discussed the land survey and titling report of the lands ministry. Deputy minister Kaspar Mmuya presented the report. Committee members asked citizens to be educated on the value of land titles. They also asked the ministry to extend the e-Ardhi land management system to all regions.

2026-10-26-tza-paratus-new-dar-es-salaam.summary: Paratus Tanzania set up a point of presence at the Wingu data centre in Dar es Salaam in September 2026. It sells IP transit, Layer 2 circuits and wholesale capacity. The routes run to Nairobi, Maputo, Johannesburg, Eswatini, Europe and the US. The point of presence is part of its Kigali-Mombasa network strategy.

2026-10-26-tza-tanzania-plans-50m-ventur.summary: The Tanzania Startup Association proposed a $50 million venture capital fund at Tanzania Startup Week 2026 in Dar es Salaam. It wants 15 per cent from government and the rest from private institutional investors. The fund would back 18 local and regional funds and seek $180 million in co-investment.

2026-10-26-uga-kacita-ucc-agree-to-form-.summary: Kampala traders and the Uganda Communications Commission agreed to form a joint committee, led by the commission, to recommend how unlicensed internet resellers are regulated. Resellers will first register for an inventory. The commission is pursuing about 4,000 unlicensed Wi-Fi resellers and puts potential tax losses at Shs148 billion a year.

2026-10-26-xaf-airtel-money-results-half.summary: Airtel Money's own results announcement for the half year to 30 September 2026, its first as a listed company, reports 56.7 million customers, mobile money penetration of 42.9% of Airtel's telecom base and annualised processed value of $270 billion. It declared an interim dividend of 6.4 US cents a share.

2026-10-26-xaf-final-communique-of-the-t.summary: The 25th COMESA Summit in Harare on 22 October 2026 urged member states to support the Digital Retail Payment Platform after its Malawi-Zambia pilot, and noted the electronic certificate of origin live in six states. It called for faster national single windows and trade portals.

2026-10-26-xaf-why-ecobanks-new-moves-in.summary: African Business analysed Ecobank's October 2026 agreement with China's yuan payment system, CIPS, on 26 October 2026. It reports that CIPS has 9 direct and 112 indirect participants in Africa. It presents the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System as a complement.

2026-10-26-xca-nbc-beac-ink-mou-on-finan.summary: BEAC signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Bank of Cambodia in Phnom Penh, with a 2027-2028 action plan on digital transformation, financial inclusion and cybersecurity. It covers interconnecting payment systems, potentially linking Cambodia's Bakong with the CEMAC region.

2026-10-26-xwa-west-africa-struggles-to-.summary: Burkina Faso's roaming agreements with Benin, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal need about three months of operator work before they take effect, nearly nine years after ECOWAS adopted regional roaming rules. WATRA had counted 13 bilateral agreements across eight countries by August 2025.

2026-10-26-zaf-home-affairs-one-million-.summary: Home Affairs says 1,002,773 South Africans have applied for replacement Smart IDs at 669 bank branches in just over seven months, a fully digital, biometric process, with passports, first-time IDs and home delivery to follow. The green ID book stops being produced on 31 March 2027 and loses validity a year later.

2026-10-26-zaf-information-regulator-fin.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator fined Central Johannesburg TVET College R500,000 for not complying with an enforcement notice of 22 May 2026. The notice followed the sharing of three complainants' personal information with third parties. The fine was announced on 26 October 2026 together with a R1 million fine on First National Bank.

2026-10-26-zaf-itweb-steyn-data-centre-i.summary: An ITWeb column argues that the Human Rights Commission's data centre inquiry also binds companies that lease capacity, through the King V governance code in force since January 2026. It notes that Africa Data Centres sought retrospective environmental authorisation at its Midrand campus after an expansion.

2026-10-26-zaf-minister-hails-home-affai.summary: Minister Leon Schreiber hailed more than one million replacement Smart ID applications at bank branches through Home Affairs @home in seven months. Passport and first-time ID applications with home delivery are to follow at over 1,000 branches.

2026-10-26-zaf-saaff-calls-for-customs-i.summary: South Africa's revenue service closed consultation on its Digital VAT Model, built on e-invoicing and near-real-time reporting, on 16 October 2026. The freight forwarders' association asked for customs and VAT records to be linked through the Movement Reference Number. It also asked for a phased rollout and an industry pilot.

2026-10-26-zaf-smart-id-delays-exclusion.summary: A Business Day column warns that about 4 million undocumented South Africans risk being unable to vote on 4 November, while 341,000 Smart IDs lie unclaimed. It weighs the digital ID plan and the MyMzanzi app trial against that exclusion.

2026-10-26-zaf-techcabal-sarb-non-bank-a.summary: The South African Reserve Bank plans to publish by end-November 2026 an authorisation framework letting approved non-banks issue e-money, process merchant payments and reach clearing and settlement directly, without a sponsor bank. TechCabal weighs what that does to the fees banks earn from fintechs.

2026-10-26-zaf-timeslive-imc-migration-b.summary: South Africa's inter-ministerial committee on migration said on 26 October 2026 that ports of entry will register arrivals electronically. Visa details and phone numbers would be recorded, with SMS reminders before visas expire. Fingerprints would feed a wider biometric tracking system. Chair Mmamoloko Kubayi said mobile operators are being consulted on tighter SIM registration; no timetable was given.

2026-10-26-zmb-982-properties-vanish-aft.summary: Zambian Business Times reported on 26 October 2026 that 982 property records in the old ZILMIS land system are missing from its successor, ZILAS. The report cites an official government report and the 2025 Auditor General's report. Property consultant Reuben Chongo said network outages lasting weeks disrupt users. The rest of the article is behind a subscription.

2026-10-26-zwe-paradigm-zimbabwe-14th-di.summary: Paradigm Initiative's Londa 2025 report ranks Zimbabwe 14th of 29 African countries on digital rights and inclusion. That is four places lower than before. It records no internet shutdown in 2025, but continued arrests of journalists and use of sedition and false-news laws. It urges laws on online gender-based violence and rights assessments before surveillance projects.

2026-10-27-accessnow-noexamshutdown-one-.summary: Access Now reviewed exam-related internet shutdowns in the Middle East and North Africa in 2026. Algeria confined restrictions to exam centres, and Syria held exams with no recorded shutdown. Tunisia restricted mobile messaging apps during both baccalaureate sessions in June and July, a first in the campaign's tracking. Sudan ordered 10 shutdowns between 13 and 23 April.

2026-10-27-afrinic-pdp-draft-clocks.summary: BTW Media reviewed version 4 of AFRINIC's proposal to update its policy development process, submitted on 14 October 2026. It sets separate deadlines for impact analysis, list discussion, the chair's decision, Last Call and expiry. The article says the draft does not state how the decision window and Last Call fit together.

2026-10-27-ago-infosi-certifica-e-aprova.summary: Angola's information society agency INFOSI certified and approved the private AngolaID identity-verification platform, built by Tech by Tech, for use nationwide. This followed an October test release. The company says the platform neither issues nor replaces the state identity card.

2026-10-27-aigles-le-ministre-joseph-le-.summary: Cameroon's public service ministry will extend biometric attendance checks to all civil servants after a pilot in three ministries. It announced this in Bafoussam on 22 October 2026. The occasion was the launch of nationwide training on AIGLES, its career and payroll system.

2026-10-27-ben-apdp-cooperation-cybersec.summary: Luciano Hounkponou, who heads Benin's data protection authority, spoke at the 15th One Africa Digital Forum in Cotonou. He called for closer cooperation between the data protection, cybersecurity and communications regulators, and for regional harmonisation of standards. He also argued for national data centres and less offshore hosting.

2026-10-27-bfa-burkina-faso-plus-de-433-.summary: AES Insider reported that Burkina Faso's social registry committee met on 27 October 2026 in Ouagadougou. The family and solidarity minister, Pélagie Kaboré, said the registry held 433,888 households at 30 June 2026, over 2 million people in 110 communes. She put this at 30% of the target and called for faster expansion and links to other systems.

2026-10-27-bfa-semaine-nationale-de-lutt.summary: Burkina Faso's central cybercrime brigade announced the second national week against cybercrime on 23 October 2026. The week is held in Ouagadougou from 26 to 30 October. The brigade's commander said it recorded more than nine billion FCFA in losses from online fraud between 2020 and 2025.

2026-10-27-cameroon-to-host-artac-headqu.summary: Central African telecoms regulators chose Cameroon as the seat of their association, ARTAC. They gave Cameroon's regulatory board the task of appointing its Executive Secretary. They decided this at their fourth extraordinary session in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026. The session also adopted a resolution on running the regional ICT Observatory.

2026-10-27-cassava-technologies-becomes-.summary: Cassava Technologies became an authorised reseller of Anthropic's Claude models through Amazon Bedrock, giving organisations in Africa a local route to the models. The date of the agreement is not stated.

2026-10-27-civ-afd-expertise-france-call.summary: Expertise France opened a tender on 27 October 2026 for an investment readiness programme for tech startups in Côte d'Ivoire. The programme falls under the Africa-Europe Digital Innovation Bridge. It would support four support organisations and 16 startups, at least five women-led, for 17 months from February 2027; bids close on 23 November.

2026-10-27-civ-cybercriminalite-en-cote-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's national cybersecurity agency recorded more than 14,700 cybercrime complaints in 2025, according to the digital minister. Losses came to nearly FCFA 23 billion. His Cybersecurity Month statement places security in the 2026-2028 digital roadmap of seven pillars and 40 projects. It also tells firms to comply with the national security framework.

2026-10-27-civ-digitalisation-trois-outi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's civil identification office has archived the registers of 505 civil-registry centres. It has begun digitising them in 14, about 3.8 million records so far. Up to 62.5% of centres in Moronou were inactive. Network coverage limits nearly 35% of centres. An online platform for requesting civil-status acts was shown to registrars on 22-24 October 2026. It has EU and World Bank backing.

2026-10-27-cmr-artac-le-cameroun-simpose.summary: Cameroon was confirmed as the seat of ARTAC, the assembly of Central African telecoms regulators, at its fourth extraordinary session in Libreville on 20-21 October 2026. Cameroon's regulator was charged with naming the Executive Secretary, under the statutory rotation.

2026-10-27-cod-de-leurope-a-kinshasa-lin.summary: The head of the DR Congo finance inspectorate led a delegation to Paris, Brussels, Bern and Frankfurt to discuss digital data in public audit. Talks covered risk mapping, interconnection of information systems and a planned national hub for state financial data, for which a software firm in Frankfurt was sounded out. The account comes from an opinion piece.

2026-10-27-cod-des-coupures-du-reseau-vo.summary: Vodacom's mobile network at Aba, in Haut-Uélé province, had been down for three weeks, according to local civil society on 26 October 2026. Vodacom is the only operator there, and mobile-money transfers and airtime and data sales stopped. Outages were also reported at Aru, Ariwara and Bunia in Ituri; Vodacom had not responded.

2026-10-27-cod-le-fdsu-presente-la-strat.summary: DR Congo's universal service fund set out a 2026-2035 connectivity strategy, first presented on 12 February 2026, to reach about 68 million rural people. Tower companies finance and build passive infrastructure on open access, and mobile operators run the active equipment, in consortia subsidised by zone. There are five zones and three phases.

2026-10-27-cod-rdc-la-strategie-de-digit.summary: DR Congo's deputy interior minister opened a four-day national workshop in Kinshasa on 26 October 2026. The workshop is to validate a strategy and roadmap for digitalising security governance. The aim is real-time reporting of security information from village to state level. That reporting still relies largely on manual procedures.

2026-10-27-cog-crise-du-carburant-les-re.summary: Congo's telecoms regulator reported voice, internet and mobile-money outages on 27 October 2026. They hit all or part of the country. A diesel shortage caused them by leaving backup generators without fuel. Operators average nine hours of grid power a day against six hours of battery autonomy. Helios Towers needs about 100,000 litres of diesel a week for its 550 sites.

2026-10-27-com-meteo-comores-alertes.summary: Météo Comores, run by ANACM, listed no active weather alert on 27 October 2026. Its most recent alerts were moderate-severity wind warnings issued that day for north-east winds on 28 October. Earlier expired alerts date from July and August 2026.

2026-10-27-cpv-sao-vicente-ucid-denuncia.summary: Cabo Verde's opposition party UCID said recovery of court files has stalled. The files were flooded in São Vicente by storm Erin. It said the justice information system runs there for criminal but not civil cases. It said the system does not connect to the Judiciary Police system. It called for court records to be digitised.

2026-10-27-dji-le-chef-de-letat-preside-.summary: Djibouti's Council of Ministers approved a draft organic law on finance laws with a title on dematerialisation. It provides for an integrated public financial management system, electronic archiving, digital signatures and online publication of budget data.

2026-10-27-dza-retour-a-la-normale-cable.summary: Algeria's posts and telecommunications ministry announced on 27 October 2026 that internet service was back to normal. Maintenance on the Algeria-Spain submarine cable had taken place overnight on 26-27 October. Traffic had been moved to other cables beforehand. The ministry said main services were not affected.

2026-10-27-egy-raya-ventures-venture-cap.summary: Raya Holding conditionally approved up to US$60m to buy an unnamed operating data centre in Egypt, it told the Egyptian Exchange. The money would come through a capital increase at Raya Data Center Services. Al Borsa News reported the disclosure on 27 October 2026.

2026-10-27-eth-ethiopia-prioritises-nati.summary: Ethiopia's Minister of Innovation and Technology told the Space Science and Geospatial Institute to build an integrated national geospatial data foundation and extend digital addressing, so far started in selected cities, nationwide. The work feeds the next five-year plan. A study of a national communications satellite has not yet been done.

2026-10-27-eth-kacha-mastercard-ink-deal.summary: Kacha Digital Financial Service signed a five-year agreement with Mastercard. It is the first privately owned payment-instrument issuer licensed by Ethiopia's central bank. It will issue cards to its customers. It will also offer issuing to banks, microfinance institutions and fintechs. All of this is subject to regulatory approval.

2026-10-27-fnb-issued-with-r1m-fine-for-.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator fined First National Bank R1 million after a fault in its mobile app exposed the personal data of 88 home-loan applicants to 696 unauthorised people. The regulator found the bank's safeguards inadequate and its response to repeated security incidents deficient. It issued the notices on 26 October 2026.

2026-10-27-gab-digitalisation-le-gouvern.summary: The Gabon government set a phased timetable for its Gabon Connect portal, launched in March 2026. The portal groups tax, payroll, customs and land services. Large employers must file the first single payroll declaration by 15 November 2026. All employers must do so from January 2027. Customs and property services follow from September 2027. Full rollout is due by December 2027.

2026-10-27-gabon-and-african-union-sign-.summary: Gabon and the African Union signed a host country agreement for the AU Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT. Gabon's digital economy minister and the AU Commissioner signed it in Libreville at the opening of Digital Week. The signing date is not stated.

2026-10-27-gin-djiba-diakite-un-etat-mod.summary: The head of the President's cabinet launched the Integrated Fisheries and Maritime Economy Management System, named Konkoé, on 26 October 2026. The platform is to trace fishing licences, landings, vessels and revenue, and to support surveillance of territorial waters. It is presented as part of the Simandou 2040 programme.

2026-10-27-gin-donnees-passagers-et-fron.summary: Guinea's transport minister and civil aviation authority held talks in Washington on 17–23 October 2026 on a national passenger-data system. The talks included the border-technology firm Securiport. An order of 25 June 2026 requires airlines to send passenger data, hosted in a state-approved data centre and kept six months before anonymisation.

2026-10-27-gnq-annobon-without-internet-.summary: Access Now's report of 20 October 2026 carries testimonies from Annobón, an island of Equatorial Guinea cut off from internet and communications since July 2024. It attributes the blackout to the government, amid protests over detonations affecting homes and land. It demands full restoration of service.

2026-10-27-ken-germany-digital-transform.summary: Kenya's State Department for ICT and the Digital Economy and GIZ worked on finalising the implementation agreements for the Digital Transformation Centre II programme, after feedback from National Treasury. Tax exemptions for the programme remain unresolved.

2026-10-27-ken-ictworks-ifc-sama-impact-.summary: A commentary argues that the IFC's appraisal of the outsourcing firm Sama did not price the risk of a client leaving. It points to the 16 April 2026 redundancy notices to 1,108 Nairobi staff. Meta had ended one engagement. It cites a randomised study of 1,115 Nairobi youth. In the study, training plus a referral to Sama raised monthly earnings by 37%. Training alone showed no gain.

2026-10-27-ken-kenya-plans-44-000km-fibe.summary: Kenya plans a further 44,000km of fibre. One part is a 17,000km project for public institutions. The other is 27,000km of backbone, middle-mile and cross-border links. Government investment of KES 13 billion backs the plan. The plan sits within a Digital Superhighway target of 100,000km. The ICT Principal Secretary's remarks are the source. An earlier account on file describes the 17,000km as already added since 2022.

2026-10-27-ken-kra-rolls-out-multi-vendo.summary: The Kenya Revenue Authority began rolling out a multi-vendor electronic cargo seal framework on 27 October 2026. It replaces the single-vendor arrangement in place since 2017. All seals connect to the East African Community's regional cargo tracking system.

2026-10-27-ken-nation-mps-scrap-iebc-ele.summary: Kenya's National Assembly adopted MP Peter Kaluma's amendments to the Elections (Amendment) Bill, 2024. They remove clauses giving the IEBC intellectual property in election technology. They also drop a requirement to keep election servers and data centres in Kenya. The technology must instead stay open to scrutiny. The Bill goes back to the Senate.

2026-10-27-ken-strathmore-joins-google-b.summary: Strathmore University is one of six Kenyan universities selected for the Google.org-funded Africa AI Upskilling Programme, through its School of Computing and Engineering Sciences. The programme is to reach 30 universities in four countries by 2028. An educator workshop was held on 12-16 October 2026, and Strathmore's own start is set for January 2027.

2026-10-27-lbr-iic-proposes-regional-hub.summary: A survey of 1,875 people in Grand Gedeh County on 14-17 October 2026 found that 87.6% had never heard of the Freedom of Information Act of 2010. Some 85.3% did not know how to file a request. Some 77.6% said they use the internet regularly. The Independent Information Commission recommended a feasibility assessment for a regional freedom of information hub in the county.

2026-10-27-lby-health-minister-chairs-co.summary: Libya's Health Minister chaired a consultative meeting on a 2026-2030 plan for digitalising the health sector. The Minister of State for Digital Economy and AI and representatives of the WHO and UNDP took part. Participants reviewed the state of digital health, facility readiness, national health information systems and a preliminary digital maturity analysis. The plan is in preparation. Priorities, responsibilities and timetables were still to be set.

2026-10-27-lby-o3-lands-medusa-cable-in-.summary: O3, a Libyan telecoms provider, has landed the Medusa submarine cable in Benghazi. Its data centre, with a Tier III design certificate from the Uptime Institute, is due to operate by March 2027. The company plans further projects from December 2026 through 2027, including a national fibre network, digital services and an education programme.

2026-10-27-le-mozambique-veut-porter-100.summary: Mozambique's Communications and Digital Transformation Minister, Américo Muchanga, gave a radio interview broadcast on 26 October 2026. He said the government aims to connect 1,000 schools to the internet by 2029, up from 418. He added that 19,454 computers have been distributed to higher-education students. He added that 20 digital spaces have been created.

2026-10-27-mdg-acces-a-internet-une-nouv.summary: Madagascar's government filed bill 040/2026 on electronic communications and digital infrastructure on 28 August 2026. Its vote was adjourned in the previous session, and it was not yet on the National Assembly's agenda for the new session. Article 111 would guarantee operators stable legal, tax, customs and financial regimes for the term of their licence.

2026-10-27-moz-mozambique-s-digital-plan.summary: Mozambique's draft National Digital Transformation Strategy of 22 August 2026 still shows a blank Cabinet approval date, BTW Media reported on 27 October 2026. The ITU had scheduled approval for June 2026 and a launch for October. The draft puts financing needs at US$1.5–2.0bn across six pillars.

2026-10-27-moz-revisao-do-quadro-de-inte.summary: Mozambique's INTIC presented a proposed revision of Decree 67/2017, its e-government interoperability framework, in Maputo on 23 October 2026. The proposal raises the guiding principles from 10 to 15. New ones include technical neutrality, reuse, security by design and digital by default.

2026-10-27-mrt-how-many-systems-is-your-.summary: Bluesquare said on 27 October 2026 that the DIGISANTE MRT programme in Mauritania brings together the health and digital ministries, the population registry authority and professional bodies. It listed early lessons. Data access splits into four decisions, and response time drives architecture. A national trust bus such as X-Road suits only a country that has or requires one.

2026-10-27-mus-dossier-m-dical-num-rique.summary: Mauritius's electronic medical record had registered more than 150,000 patients in a pilot across about thirty public health facilities, it was reported on 27 October 2026. Patients are identified by national identity card, and data sit on the government intranet. Phase 1 acceptance is planned by December 2026 under a UNDP-managed contract of USD 4.44m.

2026-10-27-mwi-malawi-pushes-tough-new-l.summary: Malawi's Justice Minister, Charles Mhango, said the government hopes to table a cybercrime bill in the February-April 2027 budget session. Drafted with the ICT Ministry, it is meant to trace fraudulent bank and mobile-money accounts and to address AI-linked threats. He spoke at the National Cyber Drill and Cybersecurity Conference in Lilongwe.

2026-10-27-mwi-minister-chipungu-reveals.summary: Lands Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu said the ministry's Land Information Management System was hacked about two weeks earlier, exposing title deeds and other land data. He alleged the intruders sold title deeds while posing as ministry officials. The ICT Minister announced reviews of two existing acts and three bills: on cybersecurity, cyber crimes and e-evidence, and e-transactions and e-commerce.

2026-10-27-mwi-proposed-acquisition-of-a.summary: Malawi's competition commission approved, with conditions, Telekom Networks Malawi's MK23.5 billion purchase of Open Connect Limited's fibre network, data centre and enterprise contracts. TNM must split wholesale and retail under independent boards. Its fibre must stay open to all on equal terms. The commission accepted the deal as the rescue of a failing firm and set three years of monitoring.

2026-10-27-ner-lancement-de-l-atelier-su.summary: Niger's Ministry of Commerce and Industry opened a three-day pre-validation workshop on 26 October 2026. The workshop concerns its national e-commerce strategy. The strategy aims to use digital means to support financial and social inclusion. It also aims to make Niger a major West African e-commerce actor by 2035.

2026-10-27-nga-meta-google-microsoft-sup.summary: Microsoft, Google and Meta committed to help Nigeria's electoral commission, INEC, counter AI-generated falsehoods before the 2027 elections. Microsoft will load INEC's final candidate list into its systems to block generated images of candidates. Google has opened its SynthID Detector to the public, and Meta will work with INEC on reliable election information.

2026-10-27-nga-naigf-inaugurates-advisor.summary: The Nigeria AI Governance Forum inaugurated a 15-member advisory council chaired by Olusola Teniola, it was reported on 27 October 2026. The council will give policy advice in support of the national AI strategy. It is not a regulator, and its recommendations have no legal force.

2026-10-27-nga-ncc-nitda-agf-national-as.summary: Nigeria's Attorney-General said the Federal Ministry of Justice has advanced a draft executive bill to strengthen the cybercrime legal framework. It covers emerging technologies and the preservation and exchange of electronic evidence. NITDA said it is reviewing cybercrime legislation with the Office of the National Security Adviser and the National Assembly.

2026-10-27-nga-ncc-tasks-telcos-defenses.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission spoke at the second International Cybersecurity Conference in Abuja. It urged telecom operators to adopt zero-trust architecture. It also urged them to test their AI systems regularly for weaknesses. The commission said telecoms infrastructure is designated Critical National Information Infrastructure. It said it runs a computer incident response team with mandatory incident reporting.

2026-10-27-orange-continues-remarkable-m.summary: Orange reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of EUR 2.4 billion in its Middle East and Africa region, up 14.2% on a year earlier, against 5.3% growth in Europe. Orange Money customers rose 21.8% to 54 million by the end of September. The region has 98 million 4G customers and 5.4 million fixed broadband customers. Group revenue was EUR 12.2 billion, and the group raised its 2026 growth target to above 4.5%.

2026-10-27-paratus-expands-its-african-r.summary: Paratus Tanzania launched a point of presence at the Wingu Data Centre in Dar es Salaam. It links customers to Paratus network routes north to Nairobi via Mombasa and south to Maputo, Johannesburg and Eswatini. The company will offer IP transit, Layer 2 circuits and wholesale capacity to carriers, internet service providers and enterprises.

2026-10-27-rand-mutual-probes-alleged-br.summary: Rand Mutual Assurance said it is investigating a possible systems breach after an alert on 23 October 2026. A threat actor claims to hold 366GB of data, including 1,683,810 compensation claims records, and demands US$95,000 by 5 November. The insurer said no unauthorised access had yet been established.

2026-10-27-rwa-rwanda-marks-completion-o.summary: The Ministry of Education, with the Ministry of ICT and Innovation and Huawei, marked the end of Phase I of the Smart Education Project. Phase I connected 1,500 schools to high-speed internet and built two data centres. The DigiTruck, a mobile solar-powered classroom, was launched to give free digital skills training to more than 5,000 people across 30 districts over three years. The page carries no date of its own.

2026-10-27-rwa-why-rwanda-is-unhappy-wit.summary: The latest Rwanda Governance Scorecard finds that 11% of government services are fully digitised from start to finish. Cabinet reviewed the scorecard on 26 October 2026 and directed institutions to take coordinated, measurable action. The report also cites a service inventory that cuts local services from 235 to 60, a consolidation of 22 licences and 12 land services online.

2026-10-27-sdn-cbs-signs-strategic-partn.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan, through its Electronic Banking Services arm, signed a partnership with the telecoms operator Sudani. Sudani prepaid and postpaid subscribers will be able to top up and pay bills through banking and electronic payment channels.

2026-10-27-sdn-democracy-online-can-inte.summary: An unsigned commentary from the Next Century Foundation proposes a phased, hybrid route to internet voting for Sudan's displaced electorate. It makes secure digital identity the precondition, and compares the experience of countries that already use electronic or internet voting. It is analysis and reports no decision.

2026-10-27-sdn-fraud-targeting-sudanese-.summary: A colonel commanding the New Halfa and Atbara River area warned that unknown parties are using his name on WhatsApp. The office of Sovereignty Council member Salma Abdeljabbar Al-Mubarak reported that a phone number in her name was used to defraud other officials. An information security engineer described phishing and other fraud patterns, sometimes run from outside Sudan.

2026-10-27-sle-18-arrested-40-detained-a.summary: Sierra Leone's security forces and communications regulator raided a suspected international cybercrime network in Freetown and Kenema. They arrested 18 people and seized 1,206 phones, over 500 computers and 301 passports. The information ministry announced the raid on 27 October 2026.

2026-10-27-sle-stats-sl-commences-traini.summary: Statistics Sierra Leone began training trainers for the 2026 Population and Housing Census on 26 October 2026. Enumerator training starts on 7 November and census night is 1 December 2026. The Statistician-General said the agency holds 30,000 tablets for digital collection.

2026-10-27-som-dowladda-soomaaliya-oo-an.summary: Somalia's Office of the Prime Minister and communications ministry held a workshop on 27 October 2026 to validate a National Digital Coordination Framework for federal government ICT. Participants reviewed the results of a national ICT baseline assessment.

2026-10-27-som-somalia-opens-fourth-nati.summary: The fourth National Cybersecurity Forum opened in Mogadishu. The National Communications Authority and Mogadishu University organised it over two days under a security-by-design theme. The Minister of Communications and Technology noted that the Somalia Computer Incident Response Team was launched in March 2026. The Minister also noted a planned National Cybersecurity Academy later this year.

2026-10-27-stp-sao-tome-e-principe-defen.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's justice minister, Vera Cravid, called for faster sharing of digital evidence between CPLP states on 27 October 2026. She spoke at the 19th CPLP justice ministers' conference in Dili. She cited her country's 2024 interoperability framework law and a World Bank-financed e-commerce bill.

2026-10-27-swz-finance-minister-warns-of.summary: Eswatini's Senate considered a committee report on the National Payment System Regulations, 2026 on 27 October 2026. The regulations put the 2023 Act into effect. They cover licensing of payment providers, e-money, central bank oversight and consumer protection; the finance minister urged caution on cryptocurrencies.

2026-10-27-swz-sharesha-users-can-send-m.summary: Eswatini Bank trained agents and residents in Nhlangano, Shiselweni, on its ShareSha digital wallet. The wallet lets users send money to any mobile number, including recipients not registered on the platform. Sign-up is by national ID, through the app, USSD or a branch, and no bank account is needed.

2026-10-27-tcd-lendjampost-cdig-geoporta.summary: Chad's Centre de Documentation et d'Information Géographique presented a water-resources geoportal and the SITEAU-APP mobile application on 27 October 2026. The tools are meant to give ministries, projects, NGOs and partners in the water sector a shared data source with checks on data quality. A field test is planned at Bongor in Mayo-Kebbi Est.

2026-10-27-tgo-fibre-a-domicile-larcep-p.summary: Togo's regulator ARCEP opened a tender, number 004/ARCEP/PRMP/2026 of 25 September 2026, for a public portal mapping home fibre networks. Users could compare operators' coverage, speeds and service quality by locality and report faults on the map. Bids are due 30 October 2026, the contract is estimated at FCFA 250 million, and delivery is set within 240 days.

2026-10-27-trust-stamp-targets-nigerian-.summary: Trust Stamp signed a three-year technology services and data sovereignty agreement with BLIP Limited, a Nigerian provider of registration platforms for government. Trust Stamp will supply tokenised biometric identity tools, with data hosted in Nigeria. The company expects more than one million enrolments in the first year.

2026-10-27-tun-tunisie-la-digitalisation.summary: More than 85,000 Tunisian taxpayers had filed employer declarations on the TEJ platform by end-July 2026, saving about 6,000 working days. The figure comes from the report on the 2027 budget bill, Webmanagercenter said on 27 October 2026. More than 270 cash registers in sit-in food and drink outlets are now connected.

2026-10-27-tza-nbs-nm-aist-and-udsm-turn.summary: Tanzania's National Bureau of Statistics signed a three-party memorandum of understanding with NM-AIST and the University of Dar es Salaam on artificial intelligence, statistical modelling and data innovation. The partners will pool researchers, data and computing to support Vision 2050. The signing date is not stated.

2026-10-27-tza-tanzania-moves-to-e-deliv.summary: Tanzania's Deputy Minister for Planning and Investment told Parliament about the e-Delivery System. About 940 public servants have been trained on it. Every ongoing development project must be registered in it. Its dashboards are to let Parliament and the public track projects against Vision 2050 targets.

2026-10-27-uga-new-national-ids-to-be-ac.summary: Parliament heard that Uganda's newly issued national ID cards are failing verification at banks, and that NIRA is synchronising them with the Uganda Communications Commission. An MP questioned the proposal to use national identification numbers in place of tax identification numbers for individual tax registration. The Deputy Speaker directed the ICT committee to oversee the authentication.

2026-10-27-uga-nilepost-kakande-mayanja-.summary: Office of the President Permanent Secretary Yunus Kakande told Parliament's physical infrastructure committee he disputed Attorney General Sam Mayanja's view that the digital number plates contract with Russia's Joint Stock Company Global Security is legally flawed. The committee heard that 1,499 of 5,110 plates made for government vehicles no longer work. MPs questioned the contractor's 80% share of revenue.

2026-10-27-why-ghana-is-mandating-4g-for.summary: Ghana's Communications Minister, Samuel Nartey George, directed that all rural telephony sites be upgraded to at least 4G. A national audit covers the 2,016 community network sites inherited under the Rural Telephony Project, of which about 1,400 carry traffic. Telecel is to add about 350 sites, and GIFEC has allocated GH¢30 million.

2026-10-27-xaf-au-opens-6th-session-stc-.summary: The African Union's Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT opened its 6th Ordinary Session in Libreville. It elected a bureau chaired by Ghana, with Kenya, Gabon and a North African state still to be confirmed as vice-chairs, and Lesotho as rapporteur. Its recommendations go to AU ministers for decision.

2026-10-27-xaf-undp-ebn-partner-quality-.summary: UNDP and the European Business and Innovation Centre Network agreed a partnership to build certification and benchmarking frameworks for incubators in UNDP's timbuktoo Pan-African Incubation Network. The frameworks draw on the network's EU|BIC quality standard. Terms and funding are not stated.

2026-10-27-xwa-ecowas-moves-to-boost-int.summary: ECOWAS opened an E-Commerce Community Forum and the second meeting of its Regional E-Commerce Committee in Abuja to review its E-Commerce Strategy 2023-2027. Delegates are to validate an updated action plan and form an expert group on e-commerce intelligence. Intra-regional trade is below 15% of the bloc's trade, against targets rising towards 35%.

2026-10-27-zaf-planning-monitoring-and-e.summary: South Africa's Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation will convene the first Geospatial Information Management Strategy Coordination Committee on 29 October 2026 in Pretoria. The agenda covers governance arrangements, implementation priorities, data standards, reporting and systems integration.

2026-10-27-zmb-393-taxpayers-owe-zra-k26.summary: Zambia's Auditor General reported that the Zambia Revenue Authority fined 393 taxpayers more than K26 million for not using the Smart Invoicing System. As at 31 August 2026 it had collected none of the amount.

2026-10-27-zmb-zambia-zambia-takes-first.summary: Zambia took the first chair of the SADC Regional Computer Incident Response Team Steering Committee for 2026-2027. The Zambia Cyber Security Agency's director general, Dr Schmidt Chintu, assumed the post on 17 September 2026. The agency says the regional cybersecurity framework adopted in 2019 is now being put into operation.

2026-10-28-ago-afdb-eoi-stdp-national-po.summary: The African Development Bank published a call on 28 October 2026 for consultants to draft two Angolan policies. One is a new science, technology and innovation policy; the other is a national policy on scientific data management. Each comes with an implementation and evaluation plan, under the Science and Technology Development Project.

2026-10-28-cmr-uptime-institute-awards-c.summary: Uptime Institute's register for Cameroon lists two Tier III design certifications. They cover Cameroon Telecommunications' Camtel NBN II data centre and MTN Cameroon's data centre, both in Yaoundé.

2026-10-28-cog-talangai-lancement-de-la-.summary: Congo's health ministry began training community health workers in Brazzaville's Talangaï district on 28 October 2026. The training covers the Système d'Information Communautaire app. The ministry's IT directorate presents the app as part of digitising the health information system.

2026-10-28-cpv-municipios-ganham-novas-f.summary: Cabo Verde began applying the Simpol municipal information system in all 22 municipalities from 28 October 2026. The system supports local finance management. It will support assessment and collection under the new Property Tax Code from 2027.

2026-10-28-democratic-republic-of-congo-.summary: The DRC's telecoms ministry is seeking a firm for an eight-month e-government consultancy, Consultancy Africa reported on 28 October 2026. The work covers a master plan for the 2025–2030 strategy, enterprise architecture and interoperability. The wider programme has US$400m from the World Bank and €100m from the French Development Agency.

2026-10-28-developmentgateway-optimizing.summary: The African Tax Administration Forum and Development Gateway launched a 12-month project, backed by the Hewlett Foundation, on responsible use of AI by African revenue authorities. It will survey AI readiness across ATAF's 45 member states to set a continental benchmark. Three selected authorities will get help to draft AI strategies and roadmaps.

2026-10-28-egy-the-ntra-issues-order-to-.summary: Egypt's telecoms regulator ordered fixed-line providers to double the EGP 150 base internet package from 50 GB to 100 GB at no extra charge. The change takes effect on 1 November 2026. The package was introduced in May 2026 for low-use subscribers.

2026-10-28-ethiopia-orders-telecom-regul.summary: Ethiopia's Minister of Innovation and Technology, Frehiwot Tamru, told the Ethiopian Communications Authority on 27 October 2026 to judge its work by service quality, affordability, consumer protection and access. The ministry asked for measurable rural connectivity targets, firmer spectrum management and enforcement of quality-of-service rules. New postal legislation is to replace a proclamation of 1958 in the Ethiopian calendar.

2026-10-28-gabon-union-africaine-accord-.summary: Gabon's digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba and AU Commissioner Lerato D. Mataboge signed a host country agreement on ICT cooperation in Libreville on 26 October 2026. The signing opened Gabon's Digital Week, which runs to 30 October. The agreement covers digital infrastructure and access to digital tools and services.

2026-10-28-gates-foundation-says-nigeria.summary: Uche Amaonwu, head of the Gates Foundation's Nigeria office, spoke at the Moonshot conference in Lagos. He said Nigeria should measure AI by its effect on health, education, farming and public services. He named reliable connectivity, trusted data and interoperable systems as foundations. The foundation backs the Nigeria AI Building Hub at Lagos Business School.

2026-10-28-gha-26-countries-sign-accra-c.summary: Twenty-six states signed the UN Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents in Accra on 26 October 2026, with Ghana first. Known as the Accra Convention, it gives electronic cargo documents the legal effect of paper. Road, rail and air documents can serve as documents of title. Ghana's trade minister said it will ratify; the Convention needs ten ratifications.

2026-10-28-gha-lands-commission-s-digita.summary: Ghana's Lands Commission plans to spend GH¢1.8 billion by 2030 on its Strategic Land Administration Reform Project, Ghana News Agency reported on 28 October 2026. National coordinator Jones Ofori-Boadu said 67% of the Commission's revenue is ring-fenced for it. The project has eight components, including a land information system. Its management unit was inaugurated on 1 July 2026.

2026-10-28-gha-northern-ghana-fiber-back.summary: CSquared Ghana invited US firms to bid for a feasibility study on fibre strung along NEDCo's electricity network in northern Ghana. A US$660,000 USTDA grant pays for the study. Proposals are due on 1 December 2026.

2026-10-28-gin-guinee-le-matd-lance-via-.summary: Guinea's territorial administration ministry launched RENEC, a national civil-status register, through its agency ONECI on 28 October 2026. The firm Digitech will build it to 2028, with national budget funding. It will give each citizen a unique identifier from birth, with first centres opening in 2026.

2026-10-28-gin-le-gouvernement-lance-la-.summary: Guinea's public service ministry presented digitised organisational frameworks for the administration and a new jobs and skills framework on 28 October 2026. The framework replaces one dating from 1965. Officials said biometric checks had removed 64,000 fictitious payroll numbers, leaving 128,000 staff, and that performance evaluation of civil servants starts in 2027.

2026-10-28-guin-e-la-num-risation-s-tend.summary: Guinea launched KONKÖE, a platform for fisheries and maritime administration also called SIGPEM, in Conakry on 26 October 2026, with public use from 1 November. Its first phase covers vessel owners, the national vessel register, fishing licences and access to the exclusive economic zone. A fishing professionals' body asked for help at landing sites and explanations in national languages.

2026-10-28-guinee-lfr-medias-publics-ris.summary: Guinea's digital economy ministry told a National Assembly commission on 27 October 2026 that the country relies on one submarine cable. The cable is near the end of its life and at risk of saturation. Damage to it would take the whole country offline, Secretary General Souleymane Thianguel Bah said. He asked MPs for more weight for the sector in the supplementary budget.

2026-10-28-internal-affairs-ministry-exp.summary: Uganda's Ministry of Internal Affairs held exploratory talks with Aratek Biometrics on a possible partnership in biometric technology and digital systems. State Minister Juma Witonze Kisekka chaired the meeting. No scope, technology or implementation plan was agreed.

2026-10-28-ken-cipesa-kenya-2027-electio.summary: CIPESA argues that Kenya's August 2027 elections will test its record on digital and media rights. It cites the Kenya Information and Communications Act and the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act. The Media Council of Kenya counts more than 20 laws with provisions that threaten journalists. CIPESA also cites the risk of internet shutdowns and AI-made disinformation.

2026-10-28-ken-kra-eyes-m-pesa-invoices-.summary: The Kenya Revenue Authority and Safaricom are in talks to let M-Pesa issue electronic tax invoices for small traders. The plan was reported on 28 October 2026. The invoices would come under eTIMS. They would cover traders paid through M-Pesa tills and paybills.

2026-10-28-ken-national-treasury-pushes-.summary: Kenya's Treasury told the National Assembly Finance Committee on 27 October 2026 that a parliamentary committee had approved the eCitizen regulations. The regulations put the Treasury in charge of the platform. It plans to separate revenue collection from services and cites a revenue assurance system against the Auditor-General's ownership concerns.

2026-10-28-kremlin-russia-africa-forum.summary: President Vladimir Putin addressed the third Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow. He offered African states Russian e-government systems and digital know-how. He said Russia has two large language models of its own. He proposed the Bank of Russia's Financial Messaging System alongside PAPSS for settlements. Over 200 African civil servants have joined a Russian digitalisation training programme.

2026-10-28-ktpress-rwanda-seeks-386-mill.summary: Rwanda filed a $386 million counterclaim against South Korea's KT Corporation at the Permanent Court of Arbitration on 20 October 2026. The dispute concerns their 4G joint venture, KT Rwanda Networks. KT had sought about $152 million in March 2026 to exit the venture. RURA ended the venture's 4G wholesale exclusivity in 2023; neither claim has been decided.

2026-10-28-la-mauritanie-explore-l-exp-r.summary: Mauritania's state digital agency AN-ETAT visited Morocco's Digital Development Agency in Rabat to study its interoperability work, catalogue of shared solutions and open-data portal. The visit falls under a partnership between the two agencies as Mauritania links up its administrations' systems. No schedule for joint projects was announced.

2026-10-28-lby-lana-communications-autho.summary: The head of Libya's General Authority for Communications and Informatics, Abdel Basset Al-Baour, met an AFRINIC delegation in Tripoli on 28 October 2026. They discussed IP address and autonomous system number allocation, network security, internet exchange points and national training. No agreement was reported.

2026-10-28-linfodrome-cyber-ex-2026-anss.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's cybersecurity agency ANSSI opened CYBER.EX 2026, the country's first national cyber-crisis exercise, on 28 October 2026. It tests how government bodies, companies and the defence and security forces respond to a simulated cyberattack and work together.

2026-10-28-mar-medias24-decret-2-26-831-.summary: Médias24 reported on 28 October 2026 on Morocco's decree giving Ahmed Rahhou the AI policy mandate. It adds that minister-delegate Aïcha Guellaa takes administrative reform. Rahhou also inherits the Maroc Digital 2030 roadmap and the Nouaceur AI Factory project; the decree is summarised under its own entry.

2026-10-28-moz-governor-felisberto-naval.summary: The governor of Banco de Moçambique said on 28 October 2026 that the METIX instant payment system handles about 12,000 transactions a day. It handled about 3,000 a day at its launch in March 2026. He also said a central foreign-exchange platform will operate by December 2026, alongside a digital transformation strategy and an internal AI policy.

2026-10-28-mus-undp-and-statistics-mauri.summary: Statistics Mauritius trained staff on Phase 2 of its MauStats platform, built with UNDP, from 19 to 28 October 2026. Phase 2 adds 14 modules, among them prices, tourism, SDG monitoring and AI-assisted coding. It also adds data exchange through APIs.

2026-10-28-namibia-engages-meta-microsof.summary: Namibia's ICT minister Emma Theofelus met Meta, Microsoft and Google, including YouTube, online to discuss what local creators need to earn money from content on their platforms. The US ambassador hosted the meeting. No agreement was announced.

2026-10-28-nga-afridata-agency-sign-1-87.summary: USTDA and AFRIDATA signed a US$1.87m grant for a Nigerian data centre feasibility study, the News Agency of Nigeria reported on 28 October 2026. The signing marked AFRIDATA Nigeria's launch in Abuja. The study covers a flagship site in Lagos, possibly in the Lagos Free Zone, and a backup site in Delta.

2026-10-28-nga-cbn-warns-banks-on-cybers.summary: CBN deputy governor Lamido Abubakar Yuguda spoke at a CBN-NITDA dialogue in Lagos on the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative. He told banks that keeping data in Nigeria does not by itself make it secure. Regulated institutions stay responsible for risks from cloud providers. They must hold critical payment data in Nigeria by 1 January 2027.

2026-10-28-nga-nitda-woos-us-tech-firms-.summary: NITDA director general Kashifu Inuwa met a US business delegation that included Microsoft and Flutterwave. He asked them to invest in Nigeria's data centres and cloud infrastructure. He said the sovereign cloud initiative seeks national control of critical infrastructure and does not shut out foreign firms. Federal IT spending exceeded ₦4.5 trillion from June 2023 to June 2026, he said.

2026-10-28-nigeria-tests-upgraded-biomet.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission scheduled a six-day stress test of its upgraded voter accreditation devices for 23–28 October 2026. It is preparing 57,000 more devices for the general elections of 16 January 2027. The upgrade authenticates polling-unit result sheets before upload to the results portal.

2026-10-28-novojornal-31-mil-funcionario.summary: Angola's Ministry of Public Administration, Labour and Social Security launched SINGERH, a single human-resources database for the civil service, on 28 October 2026. Minister Teresa Rodrigues Dias said more than 31,000 staff listed as active could not be validated and are suspected of being 'ghost' workers. Over 300,000 public servants were registered between January and September 2026.

2026-10-28-sajim-sme-ai-governance-toe-r.summary: A scoping review in the South African Journal of Information Management covers 72 studies published from 2021 to 2025 on how small and medium firms adopt AI. It finds that responsible AI governance helps such firms turn pilots into repeatable value while keeping customers' trust. The authors apply the findings to Cape Town and the Western Cape.

2026-10-28-south-africa-plans-biometric-.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs plans an online booking system for asylum seekers by 10 November 2026. It will collect biometric and identity data. The step follows a July Constitutional Court ruling that struck down Refugees Act barriers to asylum procedures. The government is also building electronic border systems and weighing stricter SIM registration for foreign nationals.

2026-10-28-ssd-south-sudan-s-first-dedic.summary: UNESCO profiled South Sudan's first media and information literacy centre, at Juba Day Secondary School, on 28 October 2026. UNESCO set it up in 2024 with the Central Equatoria education ministry. It offers computers, internet and verification training; the head teacher estimates about 500 users.

2026-10-28-t-l-coms-le-liberia-identifie.summary: The Liberia Telecommunications Authority said on 26 October 2026 that it had chosen sites for 15 new towers under the Universal Access Fund. It had reviewed coverage gaps in 14 of the 15 counties. The fund already supports 15 towers. 4G covered 93% of the population in 2025.

2026-10-28-talent-pipelines-versus-compu.summary: Rwanda's ICT ministry signed a memorandum with the AI Skills and Compute Africa Foundation in Kigali in October 2026. It covers AI skills, research and local solutions, and commits no new public money or computing capacity. By September 2026 the foundation had made 42 grants in 14 countries. It uses 50 NVIDIA H200 GPUs given by Cassava Technologies.

2026-10-28-tap-pay-go-mastercard-and-int.summary: Mastercard and Interswitch launched Google Pay contactless payments for eligible Mastercard holders in Nigeria, using Mastercard tokenisation and Interswitch links to issuing banks. Supported cards include those of FirstBank, GTBank, UBA and Zenith. On 26 October 2026 Interswitch announced tap-to-pay tokenisation with five banks.

2026-10-28-ucc-seeks-digital-upgrade-of-.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission is seeking technical help from the Universal Postal Union for a National Addressing System and a digital upgrade of Posta Uganda. Executive director Nyombi Thembo said so after attending Uganda's first UPU Administrative Council meeting in Berne. The addressing system is to be delivered under the fourth National Development Plan.

2026-10-28-uga-government-seeks-two-week.summary: Uganda's ICT minister told Parliament the government needs two weeks to settle a licensing dispute over local Wi-Fi hotspot operators, it was reported on 28 October 2026. The ministry is consulting telecoms firms, internet providers, regulators and operators on a legal framework. The report notes concern that compliance costs could force small operators out.

2026-10-28-vanguard-22-financial-institu.summary: A NITDA survey of 44 financial institutions found 22 had not begun meeting Nigeria's payment data localisation rules. The deadline is 1 January 2027. The survey was presented at a NITDA-CBN dialogue in Lagos. On their own answers, 59% of firms were on track and 34% at risk. Most asked for a definition of payment transaction data.

2026-10-28-xaf-au-russia-action-plan-202.summary: The AU Commission and Russia signed a non-binding Action Plan for 2027-2029 in Moscow on 28 October 2026, at the third Russia-Africa Summit. It spans 19 areas of cooperation. Its science and technology priorities include AI, digital transformation, cybersecurity and space technology, with joint work on AI-based early-warning systems.

2026-10-28-xaf-iss-africa-has-its-ai-str.summary: An Institute for Security Studies analysis reviews the AU Continental AI Strategy, adopted in July 2024. It says the strategy depends on connectivity, electricity and regulators that most member states lack. The strategy sets 15 action areas under five focus areas. Rwanda, Ghana and Zimbabwe are among the countries with national AI policies or strategies.

2026-10-28-xaf-kenya-calls-to-boost-ai-d.summary: Opening Cyberweek Africa 2026 in Nairobi, Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo called for closer African cooperation and intelligence sharing against AI-enabled cybercrime. His speech said the national KE-CIRT/CC recorded more than 11 billion threat events against Kenyan systems in the last financial year. It also said Parliament is considering accession to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime.

2026-10-28-youm7-egypt-justice-property-.summary: Egypt's Ministry of Justice said it has linked the real estate registry by network to the communications, planning, housing and awqaf ministries and survey bodies (reported October 2026). A unified platform lets owners complete property registration remotely, from application through payment to electronic signature. The ministry gave no launch date.

2026-10-28-zim-to-launch-a-third-satelli.summary: Zimbabwe is preparing to launch a third satellite, said Fanuel Tagwira, permanent secretary of the higher education, innovation, science and technology ministry. He spoke at the AARSE International Conference in Harare, which opened on 26 October 2026. No launch date was given.

2026-10-28-zimbabwe-to-fully-operational.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera said the national AI and data platform, Pangolin AI, will be fully operational in the first quarter of 2027. The platform pools public health, agriculture and education data, while sensitive ministry data stays on local servers behind privacy-preserving interfaces. Her address was read at the POTRAZ-NUST Research and Innovation Symposium in Bulawayo.

2026-10-28-zmb-paradigm-zambia-6th-digit.summary: Paradigm Initiative's Londa 2025 report ranks Zambia 6th of 29 African countries on digital rights and inclusion, two places lower than before. Its score fell from 40 to 37 out of 60. The report cites an energy crisis and high sector taxes as limits on access, and new cyber laws that risk rights violations.

2026-10-28-zwe-zimbabwe-moves-to-strengt.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister ordered a 90-day implementation plan for the National Cyber Security Strategy, still before a Cabinet committee, in Harare on 28 October 2026. The plan must name priorities, institutions, resources and indicators, with quarterly reviews. She also asked critical-infrastructure bodies to join a national incident simulation within six months.

2026-10-29-ago-pti-homologacao-diplomas-.summary: Angola's Council of Ministers assessed a presidential decree on recognising higher-education studies on 27 October 2026. Institutions would send records directly to the accreditation institute INAAREES, and diplomas would carry a verification QR code. Earlier graduates keep the current procedure through the SEPE portal for a three-year transition.

2026-10-29-ago-pti-ima-concurso-internac.summary: Angola's Institute for Administrative Modernisation (IMA) opened an international tender for a new platform for the SIMPLIFICA public-services portal. A US$300 million World Bank loan for the Angola Digital Acceleration Project pays for it. Bids close on 27 November 2026.

2026-10-29-au-media-and-information-lite.summary: The African Union Commission's Media and Information Literacy Framework was reported at validation stage on 29 October 2026. Begun in 2025 with UNESCO support, it would set a continental standard for teaching media, information and AI literacy. A Zimbabwean official said about nine of 54 African states include such literacy in national curricula.

2026-10-29-bdi-consulting-digitale-verwa.summary: Germany Trade & Invest listed the World Bank-financed PAFEN tender for Burundi's national e-Gouv portal (OP00476457) on 29 October 2026. Bids are due on 4 December 2026. The Burundi Digital Foundations Project notice entry covers the terms.

2026-10-29-ben-promotion-du-droit-a-lide.summary: Benin's interior ministry began issuing about 8,500 free birth certificates to primary pupils in ten communes of the Centre and South on 28 October 2026. The pilot also enrols the children in the national register of natural persons. The OIF provided technical and financial support.

2026-10-29-cameroon-looks-to-cote-divoir.summary: Cameroon's civil-registration office, BUNEC, sent a study mission to Côte d'Ivoire's ONECI on 26–30 October 2026 on digitisation and interoperability. Cameroon has computerised 60 of its 432 principal civil-registration centres. It aims to computerise all of them by 2029.

2026-10-29-cameroons-ai-data-centre-five.summary: A CLG Global analysis sets out five legal questions for Cybastion's planned US$75 million AI data centre in Douala. Cybastion announced the project in August 2026. The analysis notes that the data protection authority, which must authorise transfers abroad, awaits a presidential decree and is not yet operational.

2026-10-29-cmr-cameroun-coupures-d-elect.summary: The regulator ARSEL and the distributor Socadel did not agree on 2025 outage figures. ARSEL puts the average at 125.77 hours per customer, and Socadel at 45.59 hours. The minutes record a methodological disagreement. ARSEL's annual report gives 147.83 hours, up from 114.39 in 2024, and 249.42 hours in rural areas.

2026-10-29-cpv-parlamento-governo-aponta.summary: Cabo Verde's Justice Minister Clóvis Silva opened the parliamentary State of Justice debate on 29 October 2026. He named faster digital handling of court processes, and modernised registry and identification services, among the government's justice priorities.

2026-10-29-device-checker-nigeria-introd.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator, the NCC, announced a Device Checker app on 29 October 2026. Authorised manufacturers, importers, distributors and dealers use it to scan handset IMEIs and upload device data. The NCC is also licensing phone dealers in Kano State.

2026-10-29-dza-numerisation-du-secteur-d.summary: Algeria's health ministry said on 28 October 2026 that more than 2,355 health facilities had been connected to fibre, working with Algérie Télécom. It said all university hospital centres are due to be digitised by 15 November 2026. A national telemedicine system and teleradiology are being rolled out with the electronic medical record.

2026-10-29-dza-visa-et-mastercard-l-enca.summary: Algeria's card operator SATIM received Visa and Mastercard certification to personalise and process their cards locally in October 2026. A pilot with two public banks aims to cut card issuance from weeks to 48 hours. Online merchants accepting international cards through BDL still pay 1.01 million dinars in fixed fees in year one, plus 5% a transaction.

2026-10-29-en-cote-divoire-une-simulatio.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's information-systems security agency, ANSSI, ran a national cyberattack simulation, Cyber.Ex, in Abidjan on 28–29 October 2026. ANSSI names energy, finance and telecommunications as the most targeted sectors. It says it has recorded 147 major vulnerabilities since January 2026, leading to data leaks, outages and ransom demands.

2026-10-29-etat-civil-le-cameroun-sinspi.summary: Cameroon's civil registration bureau BUNEC visited Côte d'Ivoire's ONECI in Abidjan from 26 to 30 October 2026. Cameroon plans to computerise and interconnect 432 main registry centres by 2029. ONECI reported its CityWeb software in every centre, online e-certified birth extracts, and weak connectivity in some centres.

2026-10-29-eth-comesa-workshop-seeks-fin.summary: COMESA held a workshop in Addis Ababa on 27–30 October 2026 on financing affordable digital infrastructure. Salience Consulting leads the related regional work on least-cost planning and financing models. Citing ITU figures, an Ethiopian official said 36% of Africans use the internet: 21% in rural areas and 55% in towns.

2026-10-29-eth-dsrv-signs-mou-with-ethio.summary: Faydaverse, the state enterprise created from Ethiopia's national digital ID programme, signed a memorandum with South Korean blockchain firm DSRV on 26 October 2026. A joint working group will study turning its digital wallet into a verifiable-credentials wallet with a blockchain layer. The two also plan to explore public assistance based on digital ID, such as e-vouchers.

2026-10-29-from-informal-landmarks-to-so.summary: Nigeria launched its National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System on 1 October 2026. Each addressable building gets an 11-character code. The National Addressing Council approved links to the NIMC identity database and the CAC business registry, Tech Africa News reported on 29 October 2026. Public lookups run through Amazon Web Services. Where the database itself is held is not shown.

2026-10-29-gab-gabon-connect-le-minister.summary: Gabon's economy ministry asked the data protection authority, APDPVP, for technical support on the Gabon Connect e-services platform (reported 29 October 2026). The aim is to bring the platform into line with data protection law. Its next modules, the single payroll declaration (DUS) and TrésorPay, have yet to go live.

2026-10-29-gab-gabon-digitalisation-des-.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry began a national mission on 26 October 2026 to inventory the IT equipment of local administrations, starting in Haut-Ogooué. Arnaud Ona Ndong leads the team, which visits town halls, prefectures and the governorate. This is phase 2 of a national diagnosis. Phase 1 ran from 22 April to 6 May 2026 in the nine provincial capitals.

2026-10-29-gab-gsma-calls-for-more-affor.summary: A GSMA report on Gabon, reported on 28 October 2026, finds four in ten Gabonese use mobile internet, though 4G reaches 95%. The report proposes removing the 18% VAT on entry-level smartphones and cutting operator charges from 11% to 3% of gross revenue. It estimates these steps could bring about 190,000 more people online by 2031.

2026-10-29-gha-africas-data-must-benefit.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, spoke in Libreville on taking the chair of the AU's ICT committee (reported 29 October 2026). He said African data should serve Africans and not be extracted and sold back to them. He said 55 countries negotiating as one market would have more bargaining power on AI and digital trade.

2026-10-29-gha-bog-to-introduce-ai-direc.summary: The Bank of Ghana is setting up a Data Analytics and AI Department, Governor Johnson Asiama said on 29 October 2026. It is also drafting an AI directive for the financial sector. Speaking in Accra at the launch of the Ghana Statistical Service's Ghana in Numbers 2025, he asked for its data in machine-readable formats.

2026-10-29-ghanas-communications-ministe.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, was confirmed as chair of the AU Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT at its session in Libreville (reported 29 October 2026). George named connectivity, data governance, cybersecurity and AI as priorities for his two-year term. He called on member states to implement the continental frameworks already adopted.

2026-10-29-gin-fratel-2026-a-conakry-la-.summary: Guinea hosted the 24th annual meeting of FRATEL, the network of French-speaking telecoms regulators, in Conakry on 29–30 October 2026. Mamady Doumbouya, head of the regulator ARPT, said Guinea has 13 million mobile subscribers and about 12,000 km of fibre. More than 600 localities still lack coverage.
