2026-10-29-gnq-el-gobierno-analiza-el-co.summary: Equatorial Guinea's vice-presidency reviewed the VFS Global e-visa contract before formalising it (reported 29 October 2026). About 35,127 e-visas have been processed since launch on 1 July 2023, against an expected 200,000 a year. VFS proposed automated applicant assistance and document data-extraction tools.

2026-10-29-guinea-launches-ai-open-days-.summary: Guinea's universal-service agency ANSUTEN launched AI Open Days on 28 October 2026 with training for 160 officials from four ministries on AI in public administration. The programme runs under R-CUN with Africa Digital Academy.

2026-10-29-iati-xm-dac-6-4-013531-01-0-a.summary: Italy's development agency AICS committed EUR 20 million through UNDP on 29 October 2026 to digital agriculture in Ghana, running from 2026 to 2029. The project sets up physical and digital service hubs in the Bono, Volta and Savannah regions. It offers smallholders and agribusinesses digital advisory services, traceability, training and market links.

2026-10-29-kagame-pledges-to-champion-di.summary: President Kagame pledged to champion digital public infrastructure at African Union level when he received the new Private Sector CEOs DPI Coalition in Kigali, reported on 29 October 2026. AfricaNenda and Equity Group co-lead the coalition. The talks covered interoperable continental payments, financial inclusion and AfCFTA integration.

2026-10-29-ken-online-safety-bill-2026.summary: The Kenya Gazette published the Online Safety Bill, 2026 on 29 October 2026 as National Assembly Bill No. 69. It sets duties of care on illegal and harmful content, and requires age verification and parental consent for children. Penalties reach KES 500 million or 10 per cent of global turnover.

2026-10-29-kenyas-data-protection-commis.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner hosted a delegation from an EU call-centre operators' association, with GIZ's support, to discuss outsourcing investment. The talks covered cross-border data transfers under the Data Protection Act. The office described adequacy discussions between Kenya and the EU as ongoing.

2026-10-29-lby-lana-passports-authority-.summary: Libya's Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority received 773 e-visa applications from 78 nationalities between 23 and 29 October 2026. It approved 610 and refused 65, and 98 were still pending.

2026-10-29-lso-afdb-egov-infrastructure-.summary: An AfDB supervision report of 29 October 2026 rated Lesotho's eGovernment Infrastructure Phase II satisfactory, with 85.21% of the loan disbursed. Its 17 eGovernment services were not yet public and were due to go live from 15 November to 1 December. Broadband penetration reached 70.8% against a 57.54% target; financial management stayed unsatisfactory.

2026-10-29-mli-mali-l-intelligence-artif.summary: Mali's telecoms regulator AMRTP opened the 4th national cybersecurity days in Bamako on 27 October 2026, on AI and cybersecurity. Mali approved its 2026-2030 cybersecurity strategy by decree on 25 February 2026, and a security agency's founding texts on 10 June. APA reports 1,338 cybercrime cases recorded in 2025.

2026-10-29-momo-and-ubipharm-partner-to-.summary: MTN Congo's mobile money service MoMo signed a partnership with drug distributor UbiPharm in Pointe-Noire (reported October 2026). Pharmacies can pay UbiPharm, and customers can pay pharmacies, by mobile money. No volumes, fees or number of pharmacies were published.

2026-10-29-moz-jornalnoticias-detidos-fr.summary: Mozambique's criminal investigation service detained five mobile operator staff in Zambézia province on 29 October 2026. They are accused of registering SIM cards with other people's voter cards, and the SIM cards were then used for cybercrime. One suspect said he did it to meet monthly registration targets and earn commission.

2026-10-29-moz-us-and-mozambican-governm.summary: The US Embassy in Maputo and Mozambique's communications and digital transformation ministry held a one-day Google training course for civil servants on 29 October 2026. It covered AI, data policy and cloud computing in public administration. It was Google's second training activity in Mozambique that month, after a virtual session for 100 entrepreneurs.

2026-10-29-mus-financial-sector-urged-to.summary: Mauritius launched a guide on data protection in the financial sector on 29 October 2026. The ICT minister said only about 23,000 of an estimated 60,000 entities had registered as data controllers or processors. He called for better training and certification of data protection officers.

2026-10-29-mus-lexpress-pq-reseaux-socia.summary: Mauritius's ICT minister told the National Assembly in October 2026 that draft amendments to the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 are ready. They cover cyberharassment, doxxing, fake profiles, deepfakes and disinformation, and create a national cybersecurity agency. Platforms such as Facebook and TikTok would carry duties to take down content, keep evidence and report.

2026-10-29-mwi-how-can-education-systems.summary: The Unlocking Data Initiative reported in October 2026 on a session about education data systems held on 14 October. Malawi presented an education management information system governance framework with five pillars. In Rwanda, exam assessment dashboards moved from a commercial platform to open-source Apache Superset on government servers.

2026-10-29-mwi-msaka-discloses-plans-to-.summary: Malawi's Education Minister Bright Msaka said on 29 October 2026 that 2,000 primary and secondary schools will be connected to the internet. The work falls under the World Bank-supported Digital Malawi Acceleration Project, with the Malawi Research and Education Network central to delivery. He gave no timeline or cost.

2026-10-29-nam-paratus-namibia-continues.summary: Paratus Namibia says its fibre network now exceeds 5,000 km after about 600 km was added in the past year. It reports investing N$600m in its mobile network over 24 months, and it is the Namibian landing partner for the Equiano submarine cable. Its next phase includes more mobile and fibre coverage and a second data hall.

2026-10-29-ner-visite-technique-du-chant.summary: Niger's national information society agency ANSI inspected the site of the national data centre on 29 October 2026, which was still under construction. ANSI says the centre will host and secure the public administration's data and applications. No completion date, cost or contractor was published.

2026-10-29-nga-326-mdas-spend-n3-8trn-on.summary: NITDA's director-general, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, spoke at the Lagos data localisation dialogue on 28 October 2026. He said 326 government bodies spent more than N3.8 trillion on technology between June 2023 and October 2026. NITDA will set a localisation deadline for them after the financial sector's of 1 January 2027.

2026-10-29-nga-cbn-nitda-allay-banks-fea.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria and NITDA met the financial industry in Lagos on 28 October 2026 about the 1 January 2027 payment-data localisation deadline. They said sanctions would not be the first response to a missed deadline, only to deliberate breaches. A NITDA survey found 59% of 44 financial institutions expected to finish migrating on time.

2026-10-29-nga-mtn-plans-large-data-cent.summary: MTN Group chief executive Ralph Mupita told journalists in Lagos on 28 October 2026 that MTN aspires to build a large data centre in Nigeria for sovereign data needs. He gave no site, capacity, cost or date. He also named fibre to homes and businesses as MTN's main Nigerian priority for the next five to ten years.

2026-10-29-sen-senegal-joj-videosurveill.summary: The president of Senegal's data protection commission, the CDP, said the state's video surveillance for the Youth Olympic Games had the commission's prior authorisation and complies with the law. The state had widened its existing camera network in Dakar, its suburbs and Saly ahead of the games. The stated aim is the security of people and property.

2026-10-29-sen-validation-de-la-snao-l-i.summary: Senegal began technical validation of its national strategy for receiving and directing users of public services in October 2026. The strategy simplifies procedures before digitising them and has administrations exchange civil status, court and police records directly. Health and security are the pilot sectors.

2026-10-29-sle-natca-unveils-state-of-th.summary: Sierra Leone's National Communications Authority unveiled new systems on 28 October 2026 for spectrum monitoring, quality of service, spectrum management and broadcast monitoring. The World Bank funded them under the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project.

2026-10-29-som-somalia-parliament-suspen.summary: Somalia's House of the People will suspend sessions for two weeks from 31 October 2026 to install an E-Parliament system. The Speaker said it would take members' requests online and bring digital attendance and electronic voting.

2026-10-29-stablecoins-drive-africas-gro.summary: Chainalysis's 2026 Geography of Crypto Report, as reported by ITWeb Africa, puts Sub-Saharan Africa's crypto economy at USD 101bn, up 13.4% and the fastest growth of any region. South Africa grew 52% to USD 39.3bn and Nigeria fell 3% to USD 38.1bn. Stablecoins received through peer-to-peer channels rose from USD 2.3bn in 2022 to USD 14.6bn in 2026.

2026-10-29-stp-sociedade-civil-sai-a-rua.summary: A civil-society movement in São Tomé and Príncipe called a street protest for 30 October 2026 over the prices and service quality of CST, the telecoms operator that is 49% state-owned. CST replied that tariff changes need approval from the regulator AGER. It said it had waited 22 months for approval of proposed improvements.

2026-10-29-swz-eswatini-s-cybersecurity-.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister told a cybersecurity conference in Sandton in October 2026 that parliament is considering ratification of the AU Malabo Convention. The minister cited a cybercrime law, a data protection law and an operational national CIRT. Eswatini's ITU Global Cybersecurity Index score rose from 18.23 to 79.43 in the 2024 edition.

2026-10-29-syc-cabinet-business-wednesda.summary: Seychelles' Cabinet approved the Seychelles Digital & AI Strategy 2026–2031 on 28 October 2026. It also approved a Government Cloud and Datacenter Project on two in-country datacentres, to reduce reliance on overseas infrastructure. The ICT minister will chair a new inter-ministerial digital and AI committee.

2026-10-29-talent-nation-raises-pre-seed.summary: Talent Nation, which trains AI engineers, announced pre-seed funding of an undisclosed amount from investors including Enza Capital, LocalGlobe and Future Africa. It aims to train one million AI engineers in Africa over ten years. The company reports about 1,400 fellows on nine campuses and more than 63,000 applicants.

2026-10-29-tcd-conseil-des-ministres-fon.summary: Chad's Council of Ministers examined a draft decree on electronic court procedures on 29 October 2026. It covers electronic communication and the digitisation of civil, commercial, social and administrative cases. The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights submitted it.

2026-10-29-tgo-journee-nationale-de-la-p.summary: Togo's data-protection authority IPDCP held the country's first national data-protection day in Lomé on 29 October 2026. Its peers from Benin, Mali, Burkina Faso and Senegal attended. IPDCP named three priorities: enforcing the rules, including on biometrics and data transfers abroad; national and regional hosting, including sovereign cloud; and training data-protection correspondents.

2026-10-29-tgo-quest-ce-que-la-journee-n.summary: Togo's data-protection authority IPDCP set its national data-protection day on 29 October, the date of Law 2019-014 on personal data protection. The first edition, in 2026, took data governance and digital sovereignty as its theme. The day itself is summarised under the Le Visionnaire report of the same date.

2026-10-29-tun-adel-chouari-dici-2027-fi.summary: Tunisia's business registry, the RNE, aims to end requests for certified copies in public administrations by 2027. Its director-general, Adel Chouari, said so at an RNE colloquium (reported 29 October 2026). Authenticated electronic documents would carry the same legal value as paper, so firms could complete procedures remotely.

2026-10-29-tun-thomas-denfer-un-registre.summary: At the colloquium for the centenary of Tunisia's national business register (RNE), Thomas Denfer spoke for the Alliance francophone des registres du commerce. He said its review of about fifteen registers found a common model built on legibility, interoperability and digitised data. The alliance was founded four years ago and has about 20 member countries.

2026-10-29-tza-bot-instructs-institution.summary: Bank of Tanzania Governor Emmanuel Tutuba said the bank has set up an AI and Data Innovation Hub (reported 29 October 2026). The bank has approved policies on AI adoption with safeguards for privacy and human oversight. It has signed cooperation agreements with five Tanzanian higher-learning and research institutions.

2026-10-29-tza-digital-driver-identifica.summary: Officials and motorcycle-taxi associations met in Dodoma to discuss Jamii Wezeshi, a government platform registering drivers for health insurance, social security and loans (reported 29 October 2026). Permanent Secretary Eliakim Chacha Maswi said the data should guide support for drivers. The association CHAMWAPITA proposed a unified database of drivers and loan recipients.

2026-10-29-tza-zanzibar-to-link-identity.summary: Zanzibar plans to link Zan ID card details to land ownership records through LARIS, a land registration system being built by the French firm IGN FI. The project coordinator said on 29 October 2026 that the project runs from June 2026 to May 2028. Its nine components include digitising land documents.

2026-10-29-uga-egypt-uganda-discuss-coop.summary: Uganda's State Minister for ICT, Joyce Ssebugwawo, held talks in Cairo with Egypt's ICT minister, Raafat Hindi (reported 29 October 2026). They discussed digital transformation, training and Egyptian support for Uganda's national AI strategy. The two sides agreed to sign a memorandum of understanding later.

2026-10-29-uga-police-pdpo-raid-synclend.summary: Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office and the police raided SyncLend Uganda's Kampala call centre on 29 October 2026 and arrested 13 people. The firm's lending apps are alleged to have harassed borrowers' relatives and friends. The charges are failure to register with the office and unlawful disclosure of personal data.

2026-10-29-xaf-kremlin-russia-africa-act.summary: Russia and African states adopted the Russia–Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan for 2027–2029 at the third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow on 29 October 2026. Its ICT and security chapters cover personal and biometric data protection, an AI capacity programme, compute and data-centre infrastructure, and sovereign communications platforms. The plan states what the parties intend to do.

2026-10-29-xaf-kremlin-russia-africa-ai-.summary: Russia and African states adopted an 18-point declaration on civil uses of AI at the third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow on 29 October 2026. It affirms each state's right to set its own AI rules and calls for non-discriminatory access to data and compute. It also calls for common rules on labelling AI-generated content, and excludes military AI.

2026-10-29-xaf-opening-remarks-lerato-ma.summary: AU Commissioner Lerato Mataboge opened the ministerial session of the AU's 6th technical committee on communication and ICT in Libreville on 29 October 2026. She asked for a common African voice at the ITU's PP-26 conference in Doha. She also presented the Algiers Declaration on digital platforms in Africa.

2026-10-29-xgl-supporting-responsible-ai.summary: British International Investment published a Responsible AI Due Diligence Toolkit for investors in emerging markets, developed with Reframe Venture. It sets due-diligence questions on discrimination, privacy, security and accountability risks in companies that build or use AI.

2026-10-29-xss-chainalysis-sub-saharan-a.summary: Chainalysis reported on 29 October 2026 that Sub-Saharan Africa's crypto economy grew 13.4% to USD 101 billion between July 2025 and June 2026. South Africa's grew 52% to USD 39.3 billion, and Nigeria recorded USD 38.1 billion, down 3%. The two countries account for more than three-quarters of regional activity.

2026-10-29-zaf-icasa-publishes-draft-num.summary: ICASA published draft Numbering Plan Fifth Amendment Regulations for 30 days' public comment on 29 October 2026. They would require biometric verification of new and existing mobile subscribers when numbers are activated or reactivated and at every SIM swap. They would also cap numbers per subscriber and limit how long visitors' numbers stay active.

2026-10-29-zaf-itweb-gotyme-targets-thir.summary: GoTyme Bank, the South African digital bank formerly branded TymeBank, reported more than 13 million customers on 29 October 2026. Chief executive Cheslyn Jacobs said it expects to become the country's third-largest bank in the last quarter of 2026. The bank plans a credit card and wider lending through Sanlam in 2027.

2026-10-29-zaf-itweb-iec-national-result.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission opened its National Results Operations Centre at Gallagher Convention Centre on 28 October 2026. It declared its results system ready after an independent audit. Five political parties audited it on 8–12 October 2026, and 29.2 million voters are registered for the local government elections.

2026-10-29-zaf-put-the-woan-s-spectrum-i.summary: Vodacom asked ICASA to assign the spectrum once reserved for the defunct wholesale open-access network (Woan) to mobile operators for satellite-to-phone coverage. It asked for a price below the spectrum's terrestrial value, its group CTO Dejan Kastelic told TechCentral. ICASA has committed to a high-demand spectrum auction in 2026/27 but has set no date.

2026-10-29-zmb-techafricanews-mutati-rea.summary: Felix Mutati has been reappointed as Zambia's Minister of Technology and Science, the ministry announced on its Facebook page. The appointment was reported on 29 October 2026.

2026-10-29-zwe-30-day-ultimatum-to-tackl.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister gave POTRAZ, operators, police and platforms 30 days to agree a protocol on WhatsApp account takeovers and digital fraud. She set the deadline in Harare on 28 October 2026. She also said the National Cyber Security Strategy is before a Cabinet committee.

2026-10-29-zwe-potraz-says-it-is-now-a-g.summary: Zimbabwe's regulator POTRAZ now licenses services, not technologies, and uses its Universal Service Fund to fund early-stage ventures, director-general Gift Machengete said in Harare on 29 October 2026. He said the fund's Innovation Drive Programme has backed more than 100 innovations. Its AI for Impact programme drew over 700 applications in 2026 and advanced 16.

2026-10-29-zwe-zimstat-targets-household.summary: ZIMSTAT is listing households and businesses across all ten provinces, from 19 October to 13 November 2026, to select samples for the FinScope Consumer and MSME surveys. The surveys will measure use of banking, savings, credit, insurance and digital payments. The agency said responses stay confidential under the Census and Statistics Act.

2026-10-30-africa-seeks-control-of-ai-sa.summary: The Eswatini Standards Authority and AICE Africa launched an AI Safety and Standards Centre of Excellence on 27 October 2026. It will train standards officers, auditors and regulators, and work towards an AI testing laboratory and an African AI standards baseline report. An AI safety summit is planned for Mbabane in July 2027.

2026-10-30-ago-deputados-aprovam-regras-.summary: Angola's National Assembly approved in detail on 30 October 2026 two chapters of the civil and criminal identification bill. They set purpose-specific criminal record certificates valid for 90 days and a confidential register for minors. The justice minister said access to identification data must serve defined legal purposes, with no open access for the President or the Executive.

2026-10-30-ai-exacerbates-election-disin.summary: The CSIR and GCIS held an online media roundtable on AI and elections in the week of 26 October 2026, ahead of South Africa's municipal elections. A Centre for Analytics and Behavioural Change researcher said its monitoring had found AI-generated videos, including one of Nelson Mandela. The CSIR asked partners to join a network against misinformation.

2026-10-30-airtel-uganda-840-sites-starl.summary: Airtel Uganda's managing director, Soumendra Sahu, said the company has built 840 new sites in two years, enlarging its network by about 25%. Starlink's direct-to-phone service went live through Airtel in September 2026. Sahu put smartphone penetration at 42–43% and asked for duty and VAT relief on low-cost phones.

2026-10-30-ben-e-gouvernance-le-benin-et.summary: Benin and Mauritania compared their digital government programmes at Estonia's embassy in Paris on 28 October 2026. Benin reported more than 210 end-to-end online services, up from five at launch in March 2020, and digital identity for over 99% of the population. Mauritania reported about 40 transactional services out of nearly 900 targeted.

2026-10-30-civ-la-cote-d-ivoire-teste-sa.summary: Côte d'Ivoire held its first national cyber-crisis exercise, CYBER.EX 2026, in Abidjan over two days in October 2026. The scenario was an attack on energy, telecommunications and payment systems at once. The head of the national security agency, ANSSI-CI, named AI-assisted ransomware as a main threat.

2026-10-30-civ-oneci-se-deploie-aux-etat.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's identification office ONECI began a pilot of national identity card enrolment at the Ivorian embassy in the United States on 30 October 2026. It installed equipment and trained embassy staff first. The aim is to serve the diaspora.

2026-10-30-cmr-itweb-cameroon-warns-of-r.summary: Cameroon's ICT agency ANTIC said it has audited 108 fintech companies and found 3,914 vulnerabilities. Its director-general spoke at the Digitize Cameroon forum in Mbankomo, which opened on 28 October 2026. Since an April 2025 ministry decision, platforms need ANTIC-verified security compliance to reach the national aggregation platform.

2026-10-30-cmr-techafricanews-cameroon-1.summary: About 100 fintech firms met in Mbankomo for a three-day forum on security and regulation, opened on 28 October 2026 by ANTIC's director-general. The forum is part of Digitise Cameroon 2026, run by ANTIC and The Change Engine. Digital payment services earned over FCFA 1,022 billion in 2024, 3.16% of GDP.

2026-10-30-cod-rdc-le-senat-examine-une-.summary: A joint committee of the DRC Senate finished examining a bill amending the 2023 digital code on 28 October 2026. The bill bars children under 13 from social platforms and requires age verification and stronger parental controls. It goes to the Senate plenary, then to the National Assembly.

2026-10-30-cod-rdc-pass-les-agents-denre.summary: The director general of RDC-Pass, the DRC's unique digital identifier, said on 29 October 2026 that trained enrolment agents will go into Kinshasa neighbourhoods from early November. Kinshasa is the pilot city. President Tshisekedi launched RDC-Pass on 13 June 2026, and the first agents were trained in September.

2026-10-30-com-lagazette-sante-et-numeri.summary: Comoros's health statistics directorate said on 27 October 2026 that only one of eleven projects in the 2022 digital health plan has been substantially implemented. It cited lack of funds. DHIS2 is in use with an electronic vaccination register, and malaria forecasting is being piloted in five Ngazidja districts.

2026-10-30-eac-states-pursue-unified-ai-.summary: The 21st EAC Sectoral Council on Education, Science, Technology, Culture and Sports, meeting in Uganda, took up the draft EAC AI Strategy. The strategy has been through national consultations in all partner states and a regional validation in Kampala in 2026. No council decision on it has been reported.

2026-10-30-ecowas-coywa-second-cohort-ac.summary: ECOWAS, AUDA-NEPAD and the Spanish development agency AECID held the second COYWA training session in Accra from 26 to 30 October 2026. Young and women entrepreneurs were trained in digital tools, online security, financial skills and the use of AI. The session followed an online phase that began on 23 September.

2026-10-30-ecowas-e-commerce-forum-abuja.summary: The ECOWAS Commission and the West African Regional Digital Integration Project held an e-commerce forum in Abuja on 27 and 28 October 2026. It worked on implementing the ECOWAS E-Commerce Strategy 2023–2027 and a draft action plan. The plan covers women, young people, people with disabilities and small cross-border traders.

2026-10-30-gab-digitalisation-identityse.summary: On 29 October 2026 the police inspectorate and Group IDENTITY signed an agreement for a pilot of the Identitysecu app. Users would file complaints online about police conduct. The pilot is to run for six months to a year.

2026-10-30-gambia-eco-papss-finance-mini.summary: The Gambia's finance minister told the National Assembly on 28 October 2026 that the central bank has committed to implementing PAPSS. He said the bank is integrating the country's payment systems with it. He also said The Gambia should meet three of the four ECOWAS convergence criteria in 2026 and all four in 2027.

2026-10-30-gcis-warns-of-information-bre.summary: South Africa's GCIS told applicants that its e-recruitment system had been compromised, possibly exposing ID numbers, phone numbers and e-mail addresses. Suspicious activity on its web systems was identified on 24 October 2026. GCIS reported the incident to the Information Regulator, the police and the State Security Agency.

2026-10-30-gha-nia-arrests-6-sacks-7-oth.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority arrested six staff and dismissed seven over alleged extortion of parents at the Galaka Ghana Card centre in the Upper East Region. The demands were made during the free registration of children aged 6 to 14. The seven dismissed had known of them and not reported them.

2026-10-30-gnb-arn-consulta-publica-regu.summary: Guinea-Bissau's ICT regulator ARN-TIC opened a public consultation on a draft regulation of satellite communications networks and services in October 2026. It sets licensing for satellite networks, gateways, earth stations and terminals, with a decision within 60 working days. Responses are due by 29 November 2026.

2026-10-30-itu-ai-transforming-our-futur.summary: ITU Deputy Secretary-General Tomas Lamanauskas wrote on 30 October 2026 on who gains from AI investment, drawing on his World Investment Forum remarks. He cited World Bank figures giving Latin America and Africa 3.3% of data-centre capacity. He said ITU, UNCTAD and eight development banks had launched a Digital Infrastructure Investment Catalyser.

2026-10-30-kenya-rolls-out-30-000-kilome.summary: ICT Principal Secretary John Tanui said Kenya has laid more than 30,000 km of fibre since 2022. He spoke at the second national-county ICT consultative forum in Naivasha. The forum took up a proposed County Digital Maturity Index, the National AI Agenda and the draft National DPI Roadmap.

2026-10-30-lbr-house-halts-review-of-us-.summary: A committee of Liberia's House suspended its review of a US$52 million concession with OeSD International for a national digital ID and civil registry system on 28 October 2026. The agreement before it lacked the signatures of OeSD's chief executive and the telecoms regulator's chairman. Three government agencies sent no one, and the hearing moved to 4 November.

2026-10-30-lbr-louisville-group-helps-li.summary: Liberia's national water, sanitation and hygiene commission signed a memorandum with US nonprofit WaterStep and the Kijani Group in October 2026. They will build a management information system cataloguing the country's water points and the ministries responsible for them. WaterStep's pump diagnosis app will feed data from several agencies into one national system.

2026-10-30-lso-movable-assets-unlock-loa.summary: The Central Bank of Lesotho and the CAFI project launched campaigns urging small businesses to pledge movable assets as loan collateral. Assets worth M3.7bn have been registered on LERIMA, the electronic registry of interests in movable assets. CAFI also named an electronic data reporting and supervision system among the partnership's results.

2026-10-30-mli-recouvrement-digital-des-.summary: Commune V of Bamako signed an agreement with mobile payment operator Sama Money on 29 October 2026 to collect municipal taxes and fees digitally. Residents can pay through the Sama Money app or a USSD code. The commune says this will make revenue easier to trace.

2026-10-30-mus-lexpress-protection-des-d.summary: Mauritius launched a guide on data protection in the financial sector on 29 October 2026. The ICT minister said about 23,000 of some 60,000 entities required to register under the Data Protection Act 2017 had done so. He announced training for data protection officers and a review of the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021.

2026-10-30-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet noted on 30 October 2026 that fines for minor offences could now be paid online through the Supreme Court website. A unified government web portal is in development, and an AI training programme for 50,000 people is being designed. The World Bank discussed helping Mauritius draft an AI Act.

2026-10-30-mwi-eeas-ubuntunet-connect-20.summary: The EU took part in UbuntuNet Connect 2026 in Lilongwe on 29 and 30 October, marking the UbuntuNet Alliance's 20th year. The EU says AfricaConnect has connected over 3,000 institutions and reached over 9 million students and researchers. It also funds Malawi work on digital identity, governance, skills and ICT regulation.

2026-10-30-nga-how-nigeria-borrowed-over.summary: Ripples Nigeria published an investigation in October 2026 into Chinese loans for Nigerian telecoms between 2002 and 2010. It reports that the rural telephony project funded by China Exim Bank never delivered, and that the NigComSat-1 satellite failed in orbit. Nigeria repaid the loans, according to debt office records and a ministry response to a freedom of information request.

2026-10-30-nga-sangmyung-univ-nigeria-di.summary: A Sangmyung University consortium ran a study visit to Korea for Nigerian senior officials from 19 to 26 October 2026. It was part of a KOICA-funded digital governance project. About 20 people took part, among them the communications minister, the data protection commissioner and the head of Galaxy Backbone. The aim was to help put Nigeria's e-Government Master Plan 2.0 into practice.

2026-10-30-sen-le-senegal-se-dote-d-un-h.summary: Senegal and the Gates Foundation launched the Senegal AI Scaling Hub in Dakar on 29 October 2026. It is to take AI pilots into use in health, agriculture and education. The hub implements a September 2025 agreement worth over USD 10 million, which also covers digital identity and a delivery unit.

2026-10-30-sen-senegal-and-brazil-streng.summary: Senegal's digital minister, Samba Diouf, met Brazil's ambassador, Daniella Xavier Cesar, on 26 October 2026. They discussed Brazil's experience digitising public services and skills transfer under Senegal's New Deal Technologique. Brazil's part in the next Dakar International Fair was also discussed.

2026-10-30-sen-visa-et-le-sngal-sallient.summary: Visa and Senegal's ministry of telecommunications and digital affairs signed a two-year memorandum of understanding in October 2026. It covers payments between people and government, financial innovation, cybersecurity and regulation. The release calls it Visa's first partnership framework with a Senegalese government institution.

2026-10-30-syc-ai-to-support-permits-hea.summary: Seychelles' Cabinet approved the Digital and AI Strategy 2026–2031 on 28 October 2026. It is costed at US$50 million over five years, from government and international funding. The principal secretary for ICT said its first project is a government cloud and data centre.

2026-10-30-tcd-lendjampost-education-nat.summary: Chad's education ministry gave biometric staff cards to academy rectors on 30 October 2026. It ordered its HR directorate to have the Mirador staff-management platform running by the end of November 2026. Personnel acts are to require the card, and deceased, retired and absent staff are to be removed from the active list.

2026-10-30-thales-cyshield-join-forces-o.summary: Thales and the Egyptian firm Cyshield signed a memorandum on biometric border management and electronic passports for Egypt, reported on 30 October 2026. It covers biometric e-gates across more than 32 air, land and sea border points. It also covers issuance systems for a planned national e-passport rollout.

2026-10-30-tun-justice-budget-digitalisa.summary: Two parliamentary committees reviewed the 2027 budget of Tunisia's Provisional Supreme Council of the Judiciary on 29 October 2026. The Council proposed keeping its 2026 level of 1.525 million dinars. MPs asked for a permanent council, faster digitalisation of judicial services and ways to enforce court rulings.

2026-10-30-tza-digital-shift-boosts-acce.summary: Tanzania's procurement regulator said on 29 October 2026 that the NeST e-procurement system has handled 430,643 tenders worth TZS 42.6 trillion since September 2023. Compliance with procurement law reached 79% in 2025/26. A portal opened on 1 October 2026 links more than 36 banks to issue tender securities through NeST.

2026-10-30-tza-mobile-money-transaction-.summary: Tanzania's deputy finance minister told Parliament on 29 October 2026 that the Bank of Tanzania is assessing whether to raise mobile money transaction limits. An MP had said the daily limit of Sh5 million is too low. The minister said the central bank sets limits by customer category and risk, and warned against raising them without safeguards.

2026-10-30-tza-tanzania-targets-nationwi.summary: The Guardian reported on 30 October 2026 that Tanzania aims to roll out the e-Ardhi land system nationwide by June 2027. Under e-Ardhi, applications are processed electronically and records sit in a central digital register. Anthony Sanga briefed editors on the system, the review of the 1995 National Land Policy and the Mtumba Government City project in Dodoma.

2026-10-30-uga-state-house-meeting-shs57.summary: Uganda's President questioned a US$134 million (Shs578 billion) item in the digital number plate deal at a State House meeting on 29 October 2026. He also questioned the plates' security features. He summoned the directors of the contractor, Joint Stock Company Global Security.

2026-10-30-vanguardngr-inec-blames-regis.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission said some registration officers used their own logins to add suspected AI-generated photos to the preliminary voters' register. Its biometric identification system found the records. ICT director Lawrence Bayode said the register, uploaded on 26 October 2026, is being cleaned within the 90-day statutory period.

2026-10-30-workonline-communications-bri.summary: Workonline Communications opened a point of presence at iXAfrica's NBOX1 data-centre campus in Nairobi, reported on 30 October 2026. It offers IP transit, Ethernet and remote peering to networks in the facility. The company already had a presence in Nairobi and Mombasa.

2026-10-30-xaf-africanenda-mensah-regula.summary: AfricaNenda deputy CEO Sabine F. Mensah told Business in Cameroon that differing identity, compliance and licensing rules slow cross-border payments in Africa. She called for an African Union framework and licence passporting for fintechs. AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2026 report is due on 19 November 2026.

2026-10-30-xaf-airtel-africa-results-hal.summary: Airtel Africa reported results for the half year to 30 September 2026. Its customer base grew 11.6% to 193.9 million, and mobile money customers grew 22.4% to 60.9 million. The report also records the Kenya 3500 MHz spectrum purchase, 100 MHz for US$65 million over 25 years.

2026-10-30-xaf-au-ministers-digital-stra.summary: The African Union's ICT ministerial committee opened its sixth session in Libreville on 29 October 2026, with Ghana taking the chair from Lesotho. AU Commissioner Lerato Mataboge asked ministers for financing and implementation, not new strategies. She called for investment in cross-border fibre, data centres and internet exchange points.

2026-10-30-xaf-brusselstimes-au-eu-ai-in.summary: The AU and EU held an online high-level event on AI in science on 26 October 2026, the EEAS said. Participants named shared datasets, computing capacity and data governance as priorities. The European Commission said AU–EU research cooperation had supported about EUR 6 billion of activity.

2026-10-30-xea-comesa-idea-national-cons.summary: COMESA's IDEA programme is holding four-day national workshops on least-cost digital infrastructure planning and financing. Tanzania and Ethiopia held theirs in October 2026. Madagascar, Uganda and Eswatini follow in November.

2026-10-30-xss-path-digital-records-inte.summary: PATH reported in October 2026 on a Gates Foundation convening on electronic medical records held in Johannesburg in August. Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, Zambia and Zimbabwe took part. Malawi has designated 11 core national systems for government stewardship, and Mozambique is replacing a donor-funded HIV records system with a national platform.

2026-10-30-zaf-operation-vulindlela-impl.summary: Operation Vulindlela's progress report for the second quarter of 2026, released on 30 October, put South Africa's MyMzansi digital ID at a working prototype in testing. The Gov.za shared website platform opened for departmental testing. The MzansiXchange data-sharing pilot is due to finish in December 2026.

2026-10-30-zmb-comesa-idea-pre-event-pre.summary: COMESA announced on 30 October 2026 a regional meeting in Chongwe, Zambia, from 3 to 5 November. Member states will review a draft regional digital inclusion strategy, action plan and situational analysis. The work is funded by the World Bank under the IDEA programme.

2026-10-30-zmb-techafricanews-smart-zamb.summary: SMART Zambia Institute and Huawei announced a five-day AI training programme for government officials, opening on 2 November 2026. Huawei will provide it free, with trainers from China. It covers national AI strategy, large language models, AI data centres and AI agents.

2026-10-30-zwe-funding-gaps-could-underm.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister said in October 2026 that her ministry was allocated ZWG1.03 billion for 2027 against a bid of ZWG12.72 billion, or 8.09%. She said the ministry's share of the national budget fell from 0.46% in 2021 to a proposed 0.28% in 2027. The 2027 allocation is 34.7% above the revised 2026 budget.

2026-10-31-ago-law-on-false-information-.summary: Angola's National Assembly adopted Law 6/26 against false information online on 21 May 2026, CIVICUS Monitor reported. The law took effect on 4 August and sets fines and criminal penalties; media report prison terms of up to ten years. The update also records a 14-month defamation sentence passed on editor Daniel Frederico on 2 October 2026.

2026-10-31-civ-statistiques-du-marche-de.summary: The regulator ARTCI published Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms market statistics for the third quarter of 2026. Fixed internet subscriptions passed 1 million, up 59.9%. Mobile internet stood at 41.4 million subscriptions and active mobile money accounts at 32.5 million. Starlink was licensed in July 2026.

2026-10-31-cod-rdc-lancement-dun-numero-.summary: DR Congo's telecom regulator ARPTC put the short code 1515 into service nationwide on 30 October 2026 to reach the customer service of any mobile operator. The operators' own short codes stay in use. ARPTC said the number is part of a mechanism to monitor customer-service quality.

2026-10-31-eth-authorities-bid-for-digit.summary: The Institute of Ethiopian Standards is building scannable digital marks, with the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, to replace manual watermarks on essential products. The marks will become mandatory for those products. Revised fees reach up to 0.5% of revenue, and businesses have pushed back.

2026-10-31-eth-ethiopia-moves-to-deepen-.summary: Ethiopia's Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh and Eric Yuan, the new chief executive of Huawei Ethiopia, agreed to deepen cooperation on ICT infrastructure and the digital economy (reported October 2026). Temesgen stressed national ownership, security and local value creation under the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy. No agreement, value or project was named.

2026-10-31-gab-gabon-libreville-digitali.summary: Libreville city hall officially presented e-Taxe municipale, a platform for declaring and paying municipal taxes and fees online, on 30 October 2026. It was prototyped in January 2026 and put into service on 12 June 2026. The municipality described it as 95% operational.

2026-10-31-gha-everything-is-ready-mttd-.summary: Ghana's Motor Traffic and Transport Department said on 31 October 2026 that its TraffiTech-GH enforcement system would start on 1 November. Cameras will detect speeding and owners will receive electronic notices by text message. Owners have 14 days to pay the fine or contest it in court, and transport operators have threatened a strike.

2026-10-31-gin-plateforme-de-la-dgecs-de.summary: Parents in Koundara, Conakry, Gaoual and Léro reported missing marks, unregistered pupils and registration numbers at the wrong grade on Guinea's DGECS school-records platform (reported October 2026). They fear pupils will have to repeat years. DGECS director general Mamady 49 Keïta defended the platform, in use since 2024, and told schools how to correct files.

2026-10-31-gmb-senegalese-fintech-intouc.summary: The Gambia's finance ministry and the Gambia Revenue Authority signed a 10-year agreement with Senegalese fintech InTouch on 30 October 2026, after an international tender with three bidders. InTouch will run a platform that monitors transactions and processes government payments, giving the state real-time revenue data. Online gaming is the first sector targeted.

2026-10-31-iati-xm-dac-41301-766180-ugan.summary: FAO reported a USD 250,000 grant to Uganda in its IATI file, committed on 31 October 2026. It is to update and digitalise the 2019 National Risk and Vulnerability Atlas by June 2027. USD 39,622 had been disbursed.

2026-10-31-iati-xm-dac-41301-766203-rwan.summary: FAO reported a USD 100,000 grant to Rwanda in its IATI file, committed on 31 October 2026. It funds a digital monitoring system for the fruit tree value chain. The system serves planning, extension services and market links, from October 2026 to October 2028.

2026-10-31-ken-airtel-kenya-pays-sh8-4-b.summary: Airtel Kenya acquired 100 MHz in the 3500 MHz band for US$65 million (Sh8.4 billion) on a 25-year term. The Communications Authority of Kenya approved the purchase subject to standard conditions. It follows a new 25-year operating licence the operator obtained in August 2026 for an undisclosed fee.

2026-10-31-ken-government-to-partner-wit.summary: Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo said at a forum in Naivasha that the national government will work with county governors on ICT projects (reported October 2026). These include a cybersecurity policy, a review of the Digital Master Plan and monitoring of the national fibre backbone. The ministry will present a draft policy to harmonise wayleave charges across counties.

2026-10-31-ken-public-notice-validation-.summary: Kenya's information and communications ministry has published a revised draft of the Kenya Information and Communication (Amendment) Bill, 2026, for comment. Written comments are due by 17 November 2026, and a virtual validation forum is set for 25 November.

2026-10-31-ken-state-plans-digital-acces.summary: Kenya's Cabinet Secretary for Gender, Hannah Cheptumo, said public institutions are to audit their websites and online platforms and plan to remove barriers for persons with disabilities. She spoke on 30 October 2026 at a forum validating a roadmap on digital and ICT accessibility. The Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights is drafting inclusive communication guidelines.

2026-10-31-mdg-justice-595-arrets-select.summary: Madagascar's Court of Cassation selected 595 of its 3,104 rulings from 2019 to 2022 for its online case-law platform, on 29 October 2026. The work was supported by UNDP. The platform, jurisprudence.justice.gov.mg, has held 1,003 rulings since its launch on 30 May 2025.

2026-10-31-mdg-lutte-contre-la-corruptio.summary: Madagascar's anti-corruption bureau BIANCO launched i-Fanagna, a platform for filing asset and economic-interest declarations remotely (reported October 2026). BIANCO will also use it to track illicit financial flows. The African Development Bank financed it through the PREGODI governance-by-digitalisation project.

2026-10-31-mus-afrinic-official-statemen.summary: AFRINIC's receiver served a notice on Mauritius's Registrar of Companies on 29 October 2026, demanding that Cloud Innovation be removed from AFRINIC's register of members. AFRINIC relies on a Supreme Court ruling of 19 June 2025. Cloud Innovation cites an order of 11 June 2025 to include it as a member.

2026-10-31-mwi-cama-takes-airtel-and-tnm.summary: The Consumers Association of Malawi (CAMA) complained to the regulator MACRA about network quality on Airtel Malawi and TNM (reported October 2026). It cited dropped calls, poor data connections, unexplained data losses and delays on Mo626, Airtel Money and Mpamba transfers. It asked MACRA to publish operator performance reports, run independent drive tests and impose penalties.

2026-10-31-nga-verve-plans-phone-tap-to-.summary: Verve, Nigeria's largest card scheme, plans phone tap-to-pay and later payments made by AI assistants, its chief executive said on 29 October 2026. He said Verve now has 130 million cards. No launch date was given.

2026-10-31-recensement-numerique-beni.summary: North Kivu's Provincial Digital Development and Archives Unit (CPDA) restarted its digitised population census in Beni in the fourth quarter of 2026, ACTUALITE.CD reported. Ebola had halted it. Agents visit households in the city's 30 neighbourhoods. They record births, deaths, moves and address changes in a population file on a provincial server. Butembo and other areas are to follow.

2026-10-31-rwa-irembo-appoints-ceo-and-c.summary: Irembo, which runs Rwanda's government-services platform, appointed Noella Dushime chief executive and Ngabe Rutagarama chief technical officer (reported October 2026). Dushime was formerly its Director of Business and Partnerships. She succeeds Israel Bimpe.

2026-10-31-rwa-rwandas-first-voice-ai-co.summary: MTN Rwanda and Viamo launched Miss Baza on 29 October 2026, a voice AI assistant reached by dialling 845 on an ordinary phone without internet. It answers in Kinyarwanda, English, French and Kiswahili, with 30 free minutes a month and Rwf45 a minute after that. MTN said it had more than 500,000 users.

2026-10-31-ssd-juba-city-council-launche.summary: Juba City Council's caretaker mayor said on 30 October 2026 that all revenue collection had moved from paper forms to a digital payment system. The council also launched a website, jccgov.ss, with its budget, tax schedules and bylaws. An investigation had found half of council resources lost to malpractice, and 32 rate collectors were arrested.

2026-10-31-tun-lotfi-gabsi-sans-data-cen.summary: Lotfi Gabsi, president of the Tunisian IT group Advences, said in an October 2026 interview that Tunisia's data centres remain small. He said telecom operators have blocked carrier-neutral sites since an attempt in 2005, and that power cuts raise hosting costs. He named heat recovery, energy and water savings and cybersecurity as conditions for an AI industry.

2026-10-31-tza-tanzania-expresses-intere.summary: Angola and Tanzania signed a memorandum of understanding on telecommunications and ICT in Dar es Salaam during Angolan President João Lourenço's state visit (reported October 2026). Tanzania seeks access to ANGOSAT-2 satellite services and to Angolan Earth-observation and geospatial applications for mining, agriculture and logistics. No value was published.

2026-10-31-uga-exim-bank-terrapay-cross-.summary: Exim Bank Uganda launched Exim Global Pay, a cross-border payment platform built on TerraPay's network (reported October 2026). The bank said it had cut prices on individual corridors to keep fees low. TerraPay said its fees are disclosed upfront, so recipients get the full amount sent.

2026-10-31-xea-eac-ministers-adopt-ai-an.summary: East African Community ministers adopted regional strategies on artificial intelligence, digital transformation and biotechnology at a sectoral council in Kampala, 27 to 31 October 2026. They approved an AI foundational module for undergraduates in all disciplines and a regional AI network of universities. They also directed that AI certification benchmarks be developed for Kiswahili.

2026-10-31-zmb-judiciary-rolls-out-natio.summary: Zambia's Judiciary launched its nationwide Electronic Case Management System, Times of Zambia reported on 31 October 2026. The first phase is a pilot in four registries at the Lusaka and Kitwe High Courts. Supreme Court judge Nigel Mutuna told a media briefing that the paper filing system had slowed the administration of justice.

2026-11-01-bruno-kone-digitalisation-agr.summary: Côte d'Ivoire opened a Digital Farmer School at the INP-HB technopole in Yamoussoukro on 31 October 2026. Agriculture Minister Bruno Nabagné Koné said the country has too few technicians trained in both farming and digital tools. He called for data on rainfall, vegetation, production, infrastructure and yields to be linked to guide decisions.

2026-11-01-civ-linfodrome-ia-entreprise-.summary: An official of Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Digital Transition said on 27 October 2026 that the ministry is drafting a text to regulate the use of artificial intelligence. He said it would complement the existing personal-data protection rules. No draft or timetable was given.

2026-11-01-cod-digitizing-health-campaig.summary: The Clinton Health Access Initiative reports on digitising health campaigns in Benin, the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria between 2021 and 2025. It says 24 million people were reached, and that in Kano the cost per person fell from US$0.20 to US$0.12. The report closes with five lessons.

2026-11-01-cog-ixp-tracker-congo.summary: Internet Society Pulse lists one active internet exchange point in Congo in November 2026, with nine members. It gives the country a resilience score of 49 out of 100.

2026-11-01-com-telco-money-mvola-conditi.summary: Telco Money, the operator of the MVola mobile money service in the Comoros, published its general terms of use dated 1 November 2026. Checks scale with risk. Individuals provide an identity document and a phone check, and firms declare their beneficial owners. Records are kept for 10 years.

2026-11-01-cvtelecom-ceo-cabos-cibersegu.summary: In an interview printed on 28 October 2026, outgoing CVTelecom chief executive João Domingos said three international submarine cables land in Cabo Verde. At least three more investors want to land cables, he said. He put turnover near 7 million contos, against about 4.5 million in 2020. Investment over his six years came to about 12 million contos. The operator is waiting for the regulator's 5G roadmap.

2026-11-01-egy-egypt-launches-digital-en.summary: Egypt made its digital environmental impact assessment system, IDEIA, mandatory from 1 November 2026. Paper applications have ended, and all files must be submitted and tracked on the platform. Minister Manal Awad presented it as the response to investor complaints about delays and about not knowing a file's status.

2026-11-01-egy-youm7-parliament-committe.summary: Ahmed Badawi chairs the House communications committee. He said on 1 November 2026 that parliament is preparing a digital safety bill with heavier penalties for online crimes. He said one large platform had removed 80 million items of content in three months at the state's request. The media regulator now requires global apps to keep a legal representative in Egypt. TikTok has complied, he said.

2026-11-01-eth-eservices-portal-landing.summary: Ethiopia's government eServices portal, captured in November 2026, offers public services through a single account. Users sign in with national ID authentication. They can pay online and download certificates.

2026-11-01-eth-faydaverse-expands-beyond.summary: Ethiopia's national ID programme has renamed itself FaydaVerse and joined Ethiopian Investment Holdings, its stakeholder engagement director told Capital on 1 November 2026. He said more than 52 million citizens have registered, registration machines have grown from under 100 to 15,000, and 150 institutions work with the programme. Other countries have asked it for digital public infrastructure services.

2026-11-01-gab-e-tax-la-mairie-de-librev.summary: Libreville's town hall reviewed its E-Tax market tax platform on 30 October 2026, more than three months after launch on 12 June 2026. Mayor Eugène M'ba chaired the session. Nearly 2,000 traders are enrolled, 15 markets are covered and over 4,000 transactions are recorded. Gabonreview reports about 200 million FCFA collected through Airtel Money and 10 million through Moov.

2026-11-01-gha-nia-taskforce-launches-na.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority began nationwide enforcement of L.I. 2523 on 2 November 2026 through a Biometric Verification Taskforce. Photocopying or visually inspecting a Ghana Card for a transaction is now an offence; institutions must verify through the authority's verification platform. Fines run from GH¢6,000 to GH¢24,000 for organisations and GH¢600 to GH¢6,000 for individuals.

2026-11-01-gha-wb-contract-award-ghana-g.summary: A World Bank notice records that the contract for Ghana's eGovernment digital services platform was awarded on 21 October 2026. C-BRAINS A/S, with Omni Strategies, won at GHS 76,103,721.44. Tata was evaluated at GHS 96.1 million. The project is the Ghana Digital Acceleration Project.

2026-11-01-gin-ixp-tracker-guinea.summary: Internet Society Pulse lists one active internet exchange point in Guinea in November 2026, with 10 members. The country scores 39 out of 100 for resilience. The exchange serves one of the two cities with over 300,000 people.

2026-11-01-mli-ixp-tracker-mali.summary: Internet Society Pulse lists one active internet exchange point in Mali in November 2026, with seven members. The country scores 46 out of 100 for resilience.

2026-11-01-mus-cloud-innovation-statemen.summary: Cloud Innovation rejected AFRINIC's demand, made through the receiver's notice of 29 October 2026, to remove it from the company register. It cites a Mauritius Supreme Court order of 11 June 2025 directing AFRINIC to record it as a member. It asks that every resource member be entered in the register with the rights company law gives members.

2026-11-01-mus-essaimer-plutot-que-centr.summary: An opinion column in L'Express argues for a decentralised data model in Mauritius. Each ministry would keep its own data and share it through a secure exchange layer. It cites Estonia's X-Road and Singapore's shared government platform.

2026-11-01-rwa-risa-national-dpi-guideli.summary: Rwanda's ICT ministry and RISA published the National DPI Guidelines, Version 1.0, in November 2026. The RISA-owned guidelines set a DPI classification framework and the Rwanda Stack building blocks. They cover interoperability, registries, identity, consent and procurement, with a seven-step roadmap ending in mandated instruments.

2026-11-01-sdn-sudan-council-of-minister.summary: Sudan's Council of Ministers approved three draft laws from the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications on 1 November 2026. They are a Cybersecurity Regulation Bill, a Data and Artificial Intelligence Regulation Bill and a Digital Transformation Regulation Bill. The bill texts were not published.

2026-11-01-tcd-ixp-tracker-tchad.summary: Internet Society Pulse lists one active internet exchange point in Chad in November 2026, N'Djamena IX, with nine members. It counts 11 active networks and scores the country 28 out of 100 for resilience.

2026-11-01-xaf-afreximbank-afpay-cips-ro.summary: Afreximbank is running roadshows across Africa, including in Abidjan and Harare. They promote its AfPAY trade settlement service and its direct access to China's CIPS renminbi clearing system. AfPAY links more than 400 banks and settled US$32 billion of trade in 2024.

2026-11-01-xaf-african-union-calls-for-a.summary: African Union envoys called at a New York dialogue during WPS Week 2026 for AI-driven threats and online abuse of women to be written into national Women, Peace and Security action plans. Ambassador Liberata Mulamula set out four priorities, including early warning and survivor-centred accountability. No mechanism, timeline or funding was announced.

2026-11-01-xea-east-africa-just-approved.summary: An analysis of the East African Community decisions of 31 October 2026, when ministers adopted regional AI, digital transformation and biotechnology strategies. Ministers approved a foundational AI module for all undergraduates, which partner states are asked to consider adopting. The Inter-University Council for East Africa is to write an implementation framework; no funding or deadline was announced.

2026-11-02-airtel-kenya-secures-100mhz-5.summary: ITWeb Africa reported Airtel Kenya's purchase of 100 MHz of 3500 MHz spectrum for KES8.4 billion, about US$65 million. It adds that Jamii Telecommunications has challenged the Communications Authority's 2025 spectrum pricing framework in the High Court, with Safaricom joining, and that the revised fees were suspended in April 2025. Kenya's 5G subscriptions reached 2.1 million in June 2026.

2026-11-02-alibaba-cloud-ai-dakar-youth-.summary: Alibaba said on 2 November 2026 that the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games run on a private cloud built on its Apsara Stack. The cloud hosts ticketing and e-visa processing. It is to pass to Senegal after the Games as a national cloud platform. The ticketing system covers over one million tickets across seven venues.

2026-11-02-bdi-penurie-de-cash-et-si-on-.summary: A Yaga Burundi opinion piece argues that mobile and merchant payments could ease Burundi's cash shortage. It cites the chief executive of Banque de Crédit de Bujumbura saying in early October 2026 that banks lack liquidity. The author says high transaction fees, power cuts and habit slow adoption of BurundiPay.

2026-11-02-ben-benin-comment-fonctionne-.summary: Nasuba described Benin's national services portal, service-public.bj, as it stood on 2 November 2026. Its home page showed 1,208 listed services, 131 of them online, and over 2.5 million requests. Services are grouped by life event, theme and administration. Online ones include criminal-record extracts, tax certificates and first vehicle registration. The portal shows a new business mode and an AI assistant, Yèmi; a mobile app is to follow.

2026-11-02-ben-communique-de-mtn-mobile-.summary: MTN Mobile Money Bénin said its interoperable e-money transactions run through the BCEAO's PI-SPI from 2 November 2026. National interoperable transfers are free up to FCFA 8,000 a day. Above that they cost 0.5%. The wallet ceiling rises from FCFA 2 million to 4 million. The cap on an interoperable transfer rises from FCFA 500,000 to 2 million.

2026-11-02-ben-digitization-in-benin-cri.summary: Benin's Ministry of Justice and Legislation is the first ministry to apply the government's "Tell us once" directive. Since 1 November 2026 a criminal record certificate is issued instantly on service-public.bj with no supporting documents, for a fee of FCFA 1,900. The applicant's identity is checked against the personal identification number and civil-registry records.

2026-11-02-bfa-burkina-faso-le-projet-di.summary: A four-year research project on the digital transition of university work in Burkina Faso, Kenya and Nigeria was launched in Ouagadougou on 2 November 2026. Called Digit OACS, it is led by the Africa Multiple pole of excellence at Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo. German development cooperation provides about FCFA 200 million.

2026-11-02-bfa-lafiako-plateforme-numeri.summary: Burkina Faso's Ministry of Health has launched Lafiako, a digital platform for complaints, information requests and suggestions, leFaso.net reported on 2 November 2026. It covers public and private health facilities. Each request is logged and passed to the responsible body, with a target of an answer within ten days. The platform works alongside 108 reception services, the toll-free line 3535 and a WhatsApp number.

2026-11-02-cameroon-users-protest-poor-m.summary: Cameroonian content creators, influencers and digital-rights campaigners organised a Friday boycott of MTN and Orange. They cite dropped calls, outages, slow internet and data bundles that deplete without clear usage tracking. ITWeb Africa said it could not verify the scale of the protest.

2026-11-02-cmr-cameroon-finds-3-914-fint.summary: Cameroon's ANTIC reported 3,914 security vulnerabilities across 108 audits of fintech operators, presented at the Digitise Cameroon Forum on 28 October 2026. A November 2025 announcement had counted more than 6,500 vulnerabilities in 119 audits. ANTIC has not said how many of the latest findings are critical or have been corrected.

2026-11-02-cod-senat-examen-mercredi-des.summary: The DRC Senate adopted on 31 October 2026 the joint committee report on a bill amending the 2023 digital code to protect minors online. Twenty-two senators' amendments go to the joint committee, which has 72 hours to examine them before the sitting of 4 November. Senators raised age bands for minors, access to digital content and age verification.

2026-11-02-com-draft-country-programme-d.summary: UNDP has published a draft country programme document for Comoros for 2027 to 2030. It goes to the UNDP Executive Board's session of 25 to 28 January 2027. The programme includes a digital and AI accelerator, interoperability work and support for the 2026 to 2030 statistics strategy.

2026-11-02-cpv-cabo-verde-altera-regime-.summary: Cabo Verde's interim President promulgated the third amendment to the decree-law on the entry, stay, exit and expulsion of foreigners. Nationals of countries that need a prior visa may now apply through a digital platform. The amendment also changes the Airport Security Tax and its exemptions for the diaspora.

2026-11-02-dji-ami-assistance-technique-.summary: The African Development Bank issued a call for expressions of interest on 2 November 2026 from firms to advise Djibouti's Cour des Comptes. The work covers internal control and risk management, and the digitisation and modernisation of its control processes and information systems. It falls under the PAIC-GEP project.

2026-11-02-dza-fadaeldjazair-livret-fonc.summary: Algeria's national property directorate, DGDN, launched a new version of the Fadaeldjazair land geoportal on 1 November 2026. Users can request land booklets, negative certificates, copies of deeds and cadastral extracts remotely and follow requests online. The portal has existed since March 2024.

2026-11-02-egy-6-million-new-lines-and-f.summary: Egypt's telecoms regulator NTRA plans to upgrade 6 million more fixed internet lines over three years. Fibre-backed lines would then pass 90% of the fixed network. Spokesperson Mohamed Ibrahim put fixed internet users above 13 million, with more than 5.5 million lines already on fibre. He gave 38,000 cell towers, with 40,000 targeted by end-2026. He said 450 MHz has been released to mobile operators.

2026-11-02-eth-mekelle-city-set-to-join-.summary: Ethiopia's MESOB chief executive said preparations have begun to open a one-stop service centre in Mekelle. There are 114 such centres nationally, which have served more than 2.7 million citizens. A head for the Mekelle centre has been appointed from 27 October 2026.

2026-11-02-fcmb-mastercard-agropass-smal.summary: First City Monument Bank (FCMB) and Mastercard launched AgroPass in Lagos, built on Mastercard's Community Pass. It links Nigerian smallholder farmers to input suppliers, buyers and lenders and builds a digital record of their business activity. FCMB said it provided more than ₦364.6 billion in agricultural financing last year and supported over 196,000 smallholders.

2026-11-02-gha-opening-remarks-by-govern.summary: Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Pandit Asiama opened the reconstituted Payment Systems Advisory Committee on 2 November 2026. He named low GhQR adoption, no agent interoperability and growing bilateral arrangements as sources of fragmentation. He put GhIPSS volumes at about 530 million transactions worth over GH¢1.73 trillion in 2025.

2026-11-02-gha-sensitive-data-must-be-ho.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Sam George, spoke at the Africa Virtual Asset Summit 2026. He said providers licensed under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act 1154) should verify customers biometrically against the NIA register. Sensitive data, he said, must sit on secure sovereign infrastructure such as G-Cloud. He put One Million Coders at more than 140,000 registered and over 10,000 trained.

2026-11-02-ghana-la-police-deploie-des-c.summary: Ghana Police's TraffiTech-GH camera enforcement system went live on 1 November 2026, starting with speeding on crash-prone routes. The Motor Traffic and Transport Department reviews offences captured by fixed, vehicle-mounted and laser devices and notifies drivers by SMS. Drivers have 14 days to pay by mobile money or card, or to contest the fine.

2026-11-02-gin-connectivit-en-afrique-la.summary: The 24th FRATEL annual meeting met in Conakry from 28 to 30 October 2026 on the connectivity gap between cities and rural areas. A Guinean telecoms official gave the national target: fibre from 4,350 km to 10,000 km by 2030. The plan names 857 priority rural localities and a one-stop shop for infrastructure sharing. An ITU speaker said 2.2 billion people remained offline in 2025.

2026-11-02-gmb-gambia-to-enforce-tighter.summary: The Gambian government signed an agreement on 30 October 2026 with InTouch Solutions Gambia for a centralised payment monitoring platform covering pooling, betting and gaming. InTouch will deploy, operate and maintain it under a Build, Operate and Transfer partnership before handover. The Gambia Revenue Authority expects better visibility of transactions and less tax evasion.

2026-11-02-google-skilling-africa-with-g.summary: Google launched Skilling Africa with Google, a free continent-wide learning hub that bundles more than 15 of its training programmes. It targets 3 million people trained in digital and AI skills by 2030. The hub has offline and low-bandwidth modes and an AI study assistant.

2026-11-02-horn-economic-review-uganda-m.summary: Uganda's parliamentary Committee on Foreign Affairs said only Uganda and Rwanda have both signed and ratified the EAC Protocol on ICT Networks, Horn Economic Review reported on 2 November 2026. The protocol was adopted in 2013. The committee asked Uganda's members of the East African Legislative Assembly to press the other partner states to ratify it. It covers infrastructure sharing, cross-border connectivity, cybersecurity and common ICT policy.

2026-11-02-inecs-ai-photo-problem-runs-d.summary: An analysis of Nigeria's preliminary voter register, which lists more than 103 million voters against about 93 million in 2023. On 30 October 2026 the Independent National Electoral Commission's ICT director said registration officers with authorised access had entered some suspect records, including AI-generated photographs. The final register is due on 15 December 2026.

2026-11-02-ken-birth-registration-e-serv.summary: Kenya's online birth registration service won gold at the Estonian Design Awards. Nearly 300,000 births had been registered through it by October 2026. Estonia's development agency ESTDEV funded the service, and one in five Kenyan births is currently unregistered each year.

2026-11-02-ken-kenswitch-wibmo-3ds-acces.summary: Kenswitch, Kenya's domestic payment switch, announced on 2 November 2026 a partnership with Wibmo, a PayU company. Banks connected to Kenswitch gain an EMV 3-D Secure access control server for online card payments. It checks risk in real time and may ask for a one-time password, biometrics or a push approval.

2026-11-02-ken-state-to-strengthen-cyber.summary: Kenya's National Cybersecurity Agency Board, chaired by Martin Koyabe, was inaugurated at Harambee House. Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen directed it to build the real-time detection and response capacity of the National Cybersecurity Operations Centre. Communications Authority data put DDoS attacks at 72.16 million in the year to June 2026, up 114.3%.

2026-11-02-lbr-liberia-lrrrc-sets-novemb.summary: Liberia's refugee commission, the National Identification Registry and Immigration Service will register undocumented migrants, mainly Burkinabe nationals, in four counties. A launch ceremony is set for 4 November 2026, and registration runs from 5 November to 31 December. Enrolment is into the national biometric ID system.

2026-11-02-lbr-national-id-deal-under-sc.summary: The Liberia Information Technology Consortium challenged the proposed US$52 million National Identification Registry concession with Austria's OeSD International GmbH. It cited a 65–35 revenue split in OeSD's favour: about US$69.5 million of a projected US$107 million in fees over ten years, against US$37.4 million for Liberia. It also raised unanswered questions on data hosting, encryption-key control and local participation.

2026-11-02-mli-cybercriminalite-l-apdp-p.summary: Mali's data protection authority, the APDP, proposed a digital age of majority for the Confederation of Sahel States. It made the proposal at Burkina Faso's second national anti-cybercrime week, held from 27 to 30 October 2026. The APDP wants a legal age for independent use of digital services written into the Confederation's texts.

2026-11-02-mli-mali-nouvelles-regles-pou.summary: New BCEAO rules on interoperable transfers took effect in Mali on 2 November 2026, APAnews reports. Orange Finances Mobiles Mali raised the balance cap on identified wallets from two to four million CFA francs. Transfers between individuals are free up to 8,000 CFA francs a day, and 14 Malian institutions are authorised on PI-SPI.

2026-11-02-moz-mozambique-advances-respo.summary: Mozambique held its first training of trainers on artificial intelligence in electoral administration, in Macaneta from 19 to 23 October 2026, with UNDP support. Twenty-six professionals came from six institutions. They were the electoral commission, its technical secretariat, the Constitutional Council, the Supreme Court, the police and the Attorney General's office. Sessions covered cybersecurity, data protection, risk management and spotting deepfakes.

2026-11-02-mwi-ppda-warns-public-institu.summary: Malawi's procurement regulator, the PPDA, says government will not fund procurement done outside the MANePS e-procurement system from 1 January 2027. It plans regional support hubs for institutions.

2026-11-02-nga-banks-fintechs-face-n1bn-.summary: A bill before Nigeria's House of Representatives, sponsored by Lanre Okunlola, would set up a National Payment Data Protection and Sovereignty Commission. Institutions moving payment data abroad would face a minimum fine of N1 billion. Individuals would face 10 years in prison and a minimum fine of N500 million.

2026-11-02-sdn-sudanese-journalists-synd.summary: The Sudanese Journalists' Syndicate counted 673 violations against journalists from April 2023 to end June 2026, including 34 killings. It recorded 64 prosecutions, among them Cybercrime Act complaints against 47 journalists and outlets, after which 18 were declared wanted. The syndicate demanded repeal of restrictive laws, Dabanga reported on 2 November 2026.

2026-11-02-sen-lesoleil-bank-to-wallet-s.summary: Banks in Senegal stopped their bank-to-wallet and wallet-to-bank services from 2 November 2026, Le Soleil reported. They sent customers to the BCEAO's PI-SPI instead; the Launch Base Africa entry covers the rollout. Customers, told a few days ahead, said no reason was given. Using PI-SPI requires an updated banking app and an alias. Its transfers are instant and cannot be reversed.

2026-11-02-sen-senegal-dcssi-nouveau-por.summary: Senegal's cybersecurity directorate, the DCSSI, put online a new institutional portal. It incorporates the national single window for reporting cybersecurity incidents. The portal is open to administrations, businesses, organisations and citizens at jokkocyber-dcssi.sn.

2026-11-02-somalia-puts-hubiye-national-.summary: Somalia's National Identification and Registration Authority announced in late October 2026 that its Hubiye ID verification platform is in operation. Service providers check credentials against the national database by one-time-password consent. Integration is free for now, though the authority says some providers may eventually pay. UNDP put Hubiye at 25 integrated services and about 1.2 million citizens in May 2026.

2026-11-02-swz-eswatini-standards-author.summary: The Eswatini Standards Authority and AICE Africa launched an AI Safety and Standards Center of Excellence, under a partnership formalised in September 2026. It will build the authority's EswasaOne AI platform, train standards officers, auditors and regulators, and develop a proposed AI testing laboratory. A summit is planned for Mbabane in July 2027.

2026-11-02-syc-seyalert-seychelles-gover.summary: Seychelles soft-launched the SeyAlert emergency app on 30 October 2026, after weeks of flooding and landslides. It sends warnings by district through the app and SMS. Users can report their location, and a route-alert feature follows them. The government expects full operation within the week.

2026-11-02-tgo-ecobank-togo-cips-payment.summary: Ecobank signed an agreement with China's CIPS payment system in Beijing on 10 October 2026. The head of Ecobank Togo says the aim is direct access across its 34 African markets, with renminbi payments through fewer banks. Guinea has had indirect access via Bank of China since March 2026.

2026-11-02-uga-questions-swirl-over-inte.summary: Uganda's talks with Samanga Utilities now centre on a 1,775 km fibre line run by the Uganda Electricity Transmission Company, the Daily Monitor reported on 2 November 2026. A Samanga and Liquid Telecommunications joint venture is being evaluated for a $4.6 million contract. The paper says it is unclear whether it would add Tanzanian capacity. It might only operate the existing fibre.

2026-11-02-xaf-only-usd-2-billion-of-afr.summary: Space in Africa released its African Satellite Manufacturing and Launch Market Report 2026 on 2 November. It tracks 113 satellites African operators could build and launch over the next decade, worth USD 7.94 billion. Only 21 of them, worth USD 2.00 billion, are firmly committed. Since 1998, 69 African satellites have reached orbit. None was launched from African soil.

2026-11-02-xaf-smart-africa-itu-telecom-.summary: Smart Africa and the ITU partnered to train African policymakers and telecom regulators in pro-competition broadband and telecommunications regulation. Through the Smart Africa Digital Academy and the ITU Academy, three accredited e-learning courses in English, French and Portuguese were released as digital public goods. The partnership aims to reach more than 3,000 policymakers.

2026-11-02-za-ezar-rand-stablecoin-publi.summary: eZAR, a rand-backed stablecoin, opened to the South African public after almost a year as a pilot. It is run by eZAR Ltd, Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services. R303 million of tokens were in circulation on 30 October 2026. Reserves sit mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. The issuer states that eZAR is a crypto asset, not legal tender or a bank deposit.

2026-11-02-zmb-chief-justice-opens-train.summary: Chief Justice Mumba Malila opened a training-of-trainers workshop for Zambia's Electronic Case Management System, Diamond Media reported on 2 November 2026. Malila said the system should allow electronic filing, real-time case tracking and remote access for lawyers. Malila added that some litigants had travelled long distances only to learn their files could not be found.

2026-11-03-achpr-call-inputs-continental.summary: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights published its draft Continental Study on Digital Violence Against Women in Africa for stakeholder review. The study covers 20 countries and finds that none has enacted comprehensive gender-responsive legislation on digital violence against women. Inputs are due by 4 December 2026, and an online consultation is set for 11 November.

2026-11-03-africas-ai-ambitions-depend-o.summary: In an interview with Biometric Update, Cameroonian AI-governance lawyer Remy Takang argued that African governments should build reliable digital public infrastructure before drafting national AI strategies. He called for a rights-based framework for high-impact AI systems, with a right to redress. He argued that amending existing sector laws could serve in place of a single comprehensive AI law.

2026-11-03-ago-africell-reforca-presenca.summary: Africell is preparing a satellite services company with Angola's government and United States backing, aimed at mining, oil, gas and farming clients. Africell had earlier secured US$99.6 million from the US EXIM Bank for mobile network equipment. The amounts for the satellite venture have not been disclosed.

2026-11-03-bayobab-east-west-fibre-south.summary: Bayobab, an MTN Group company, said on 22 October 2026 that civil works and fibre deployment are complete on the Kenya and South Sudan segments of Northern Route 1 of its East-to-West Connectivity Project. The segments carry 2,038km of fibre, and service activation is the next step. The company gave no activation date, customers or cost.

2026-11-03-ben-modernisation-des-service.summary: Benin's national identification agency says 98% of the population is enrolled. It delivered 10.5 million services in 2025, 75% of them remotely. A pilot for late birth registration starts on 2 November 2026, and 165 more tablets are going to local districts.

2026-11-03-benin-casier-judiciaire-insta.summary: Since 1 November 2026, Benin's Ministry of Justice and Legislation has issued the criminal-record certificate (bulletin n°3) instantly on service-public.bj, for 1,900 FCFA. The certificate is generated from the personal identification number (NPI) and civil-status data the administration already holds, with no supporting documents. Beninese citizens abroad can also apply.
