2026-11-03-businessday-775bn-savings-poo.summary: The sixth African Financial Industry Barometer, presented in Luanda on 3 November 2026, found 11% of surveyed financial institutions connected to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System and 45% with no plans to connect. Only 7% reported tangible progress under the AfCFTA. About 66% reported a rise in digital fraud, and 88% of banks and fintechs.

2026-11-03-businessday-adesina-proposes-.summary: Former African Development Bank president Akinwumi Adesina proposed a $10 billion African AI fund to anchor $50 billion of investment over ten years. He spoke at the 2026 Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference. Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani told the same conference that AI depends on connectivity, compute, data, skills and institutions.

2026-11-03-bwa-southern-africa-s-ai-ambi.summary: A 2026 skills survey by South Africa's IITPSA attributes 24% of the reported skills gap to missing workplace experience and 20% to education and training. ICT body presidents from five countries discussed it in Johannesburg. In Botswana, 60% of unemployed graduates are reported to hold ICT degrees.

2026-11-03-citinewsroom-connecting-afric.summary: Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko, chairman of the Africa Prosperity Network, argued in an opinion piece for linking Africa's mobile money wallets across borders. He made the case at the Africa Internet Governance Forum in Accra on 2 November 2026. The network estimates that this and visa-free travel could lift intra-African trade from 16% to over 25%.

2026-11-03-cmr-sant-num-rique-le-camerou.summary: Health IT stakeholders met in Kribi from 27 to 31 October 2026 on Cameroon's national health interoperability platform. A server hosted at CAMTEL runs the OpenHIM and OpenFn exchange tools. The workshop pre-validated a revised framework and worked on accreditation for health software.

2026-11-03-cod-cybers-curit-un-atelier-d.summary: The DRC digital economy ministry and the telecoms regulator ARPTC opened a workshop on 3 November 2026 to validate seven ministerial orders on cybersecurity. The orders cover incident notification, audits, registers for AI systems and critical infrastructure. The workshop runs to 5 November.

2026-11-03-comesa-world-bank-back-region.summary: COMESA and the World Bank held a validation workshop for the IDEA digital inclusion programme in Chongwe, Zambia, from 3 to 5 November 2026. Participants reviewed a draft regional digital inclusion strategy and action plan. The programme has an indicated envelope of about US$2.48 billion and aims to connect some 180 million people.

2026-11-03-cote-divoire-and-gabon-explor.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister Djibril Ouattara and Gabon's Mark-Alexandre Doumba discussed cooperation on AI, digital public services and data infrastructure in Libreville. They met at the sixth session of the African Union's Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT. The avenues named include reuse of public-service algorithms, cross-data backups and shared computing capacity.

2026-11-03-cpv-nova-plataforma-digital-d.summary: Cabo Verde launched an online portal for its labour inspectorate on 3 November 2026. Workers and employers can file complaints, request interventions and submit declarations on it. The minister said the portal includes AI features and accessibility tools.

2026-11-03-cybersecurite-le-niger-sollic.summary: A Nigerien delegation led by Mohamed Ghadfi, deputy secretary-general of the communications ministry, visited Burkina Faso's information-security agency ANSSI-BF from 2 to 6 November 2026. The study mission prepares Niger's national Security Operations Centre. Niger's government created its Centre national de cybersécurité by decree in October 2025.

2026-11-03-dza-high-commission-for-digit.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitization trained information system officials in verifying documents issued through the national government services portal. Administrations can then accept those documents without asking citizens for new paper copies.

2026-11-03-dza-mesrs-sixieme-reunion-mul.summary: At the sixth follow-up meeting on Algeria's national AI strategy, the higher education minister heard that the data and infrastructure plan starts on 11 November 2026. Some 98% of the tax-law documents for a specialised language model have been collected. Forty-six universities have bid to join the AI doctoral school.

2026-11-03-eac-moves-to-slash-cross-bord.summary: A proposed EAC regulation would cut the retail voice roaming cap from 10 to 5.9 US cents a minute. Retail data would be capped at US$2.72 per GB. The Council of Ministers has yet to approve it. Six of the eight Partner States apply the 2014 One Network Area framework; DRC and Somalia do not.

2026-11-03-ecowas-strengthens-the-harmon.summary: The ECOWAS Commission and the West African Monetary Agency opened an experts' meeting on monetary and financial statistics in Lomé on 2 November 2026. Central bank statisticians are reviewing a draft regional metadata framework until 7 November. They are also assessing a regional action plan adopted in January 2025.

2026-11-03-egy-almasryalyoum-data-classi.summary: Egypt's government will send parliament a bill on classifying and sharing data between state bodies within weeks, the chair of the ICT committee said on 3 November 2026. It will be the first law the committee studies. He tied it to the one-stop service file.

2026-11-03-egy-youm7-egypt-plans-dedicat.summary: Youm7 reported that Egypt is in the final drafting stage of a dedicated law to regulate AI applications and their governance. The report names no official as its source. AI is governed at present under existing laws, including the Personal Data Protection Law 151 of 2020, cybercrime law 175 of 2018 and a 2022 fintech law.

2026-11-03-gha-bawumia-calls-for-laws-to.summary: Mahamudu Bawumia, flagbearer of Ghana's New Patriotic Party, called for laws to protect workers from job losses caused by AI. Speaking to the Trades Union Congress, he proposed that government, organised labour, employers and technology experts draft the rules together. He said the framework should provide for retraining and reskilling.

2026-11-03-gha-gender-ministry-swears-in.summary: Ghana's Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection swore in a Data Review Committee for the Ghana National Household Registry. The committee will review and validate the registry's analytical reports before they go to stakeholders and the public. The registry holds about three million enrolled households across all 16 regions.

2026-11-03-gha-no-new-ghana-cards-requir.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority said on 2 November 2026 that L.I. 2523 requires no new Ghana Cards or fresh biometric registration. The regulation extends mandatory biometric checks to private deals such as land sales and bars photocopying or visual inspection of the card. An NIA mobile app will give individuals a yes-or-no check.

2026-11-03-icasa-takes-aim-at-dormant-te.summary: South Africa's regulator ICASA published a Discussion Document on 30 October 2026 in its inquiry into individual network service licences. It found most of its 470 such licences dormant and proposes that new operators apply to it directly instead of buying existing ones. It is weighing a use-it-or-lose-it rule; comments are due within 45 working days.

2026-11-03-ken-group-raises-alarm-over-d.summary: The Grassroots Disability Agenda launched a survey report in Nairobi on digital exclusion of persons with disabilities in Garissa, Kajiado and Marsabit counties. It cites device and data costs, inaccessible services, limited skills, online safety risks and weak policy implementation. The report sets out ten policy actions for government, regulators and technology providers.

2026-11-03-mar-justice-minister-parliame.summary: Morocco's justice minister told parliament on 2 November 2026 that about MAD 2.5 billion is needed to finish digitising the courts. He named the electronic case file, digital notification and an enforcement platform among the priorities.

2026-11-03-mdg-lexpress-jonah-andrianant.summary: Economist Jonah Andrianantoanina of the CREM think tank said Madagascar's 2005 digital-sector law is obsolete. He backed bill 040/2026 on electronic communications and digital infrastructure, filed in late August 2026. He projected that it and related reforms could add about MGA 4,000 billion to GDP and 330,000 digital jobs by 2031.

2026-11-03-mli-mali-releases-202324-agri.summary: FAO reported on 3 November 2026 that Mali published results of its 2023–24 agricultural survey, the first under the 50x2030 Initiative. The survey puts cultivated area at about 7.45 million hectares and cereal output at 8.84 million tonnes. Interactive tables are on Mali's national open data portal.

2026-11-03-mus-cloud-innovation-four-ste.summary: Cloud Innovation Ltd says it will act against AfriNIC's Receiver. A legal notice of 29 October 2026 sought its removal from the members' register. It will seek the Receiver's removal, file an insolvency complaint and notify the Registrar of Companies. It will also ask the Prime Minister to investigate more than 2,000 members it says were left off.

2026-11-03-mwi-ppda-tough-on-registratio.summary: Malawi's procurement regulator says vendors not registered on the MANePS e-procurement system by 31 December will be barred. By October 2026, 7,704 suppliers had registered, 9% of them small and medium enterprises.

2026-11-03-rwa-res-synesis-and-rwandas-m.summary: RES Synesis, part of Gruppo RES, signed a memorandum with Rwanda's ICT ministry. It covers IT modernisation, AI, cybersecurity and training. The memorandum is exploratory, and any project needs a separate agreement.

2026-11-03-sdn-governance-sector-discuss.summary: The governance sector of Sudan's cabinet met on 3 November 2026 and backed authenticated electronic correspondence as the state's only official channel. Paper circulation would become a restricted exception that needs justification.

2026-11-03-sle-spectrum-monitoring-syste.summary: In an opinion piece, lawyer Joseph Fitzgerald Kamara argued that Sierra Leone's new spectrum monitoring system can locate transmitters and so could serve surveillance. Sierra Leone has no data protection law in force and no independent privacy regulator, he noted. He called for that law, judicial warrants, parliamentary oversight and donor conditions.

2026-11-03-stp-tribunal-de-contas-vai-la.summary: The president of Sao Tome and Principe's Court of Auditors announced an electronic system for public entities to file their accounts instead of paper. A new instruction will follow. He expects the system to be operating by 30 April 2027.

2026-11-03-swz-digital-company-registrat.summary: Eswatini's commerce ministry reports 632 online company registrations in the second quarter of 2026/27, against 2,127 a year earlier. The report cites network connectivity problems and manual processes. Total registrations fell from 952 to 790.

2026-11-03-syc-bill-no-20-companies-amen.summary: Seychelles gazetted a bill on 3 November 2026 that adds section 10A to the Companies Act. It allows electronic filing, service, record-keeping and fee payment at the Registrar. Regulations are to follow.

2026-11-03-syc-bill-no-21-registration-o.summary: Seychelles gazetted a bill on 3 November 2026 that adds section 6(1A) to (1D) to the business names law. It allows electronic filing, records and fee payment for business names. Regulations are to follow.

2026-11-03-tgo-un-supercalculateur-pour-.summary: UNDP says Togo has had a GPU server at the Lomé Data Centre since July 2026, run by Togo AI Lab. It handled 50,200 requests between August and October, and the data stays in Togo.

2026-11-03-tza-tanzania-strengthens-pers.summary: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Commission reports that by October 2026 more than 15,000 institutions had registered with it. It had received over 445 complaints and issued 121 permits to transfer data abroad. The commission was set up on 1 May 2023 under the 2022 data protection act.

2026-11-03-xaf-bundestag-drucksache-21-8.summary: The CDU/CSU and SPD parliamentary groups tabled a motion in the Bundestag on 3 November 2026 on digitalisation in German development cooperation (Drucksache 21/8912). It calls for digital aid led by partner interests. It also calls for reuse rights for software that German funds pay for, and for data centres in Africa.

2026-11-03-xaf-undp-african-ai-companies.summary: At a UNDP-backed event in Rome on 3 November 2026, the AI Hub and Moroccan firm DeepLeaf launched a food-security AI model for seven countries. Cyber4Africa backs 49 start-ups in 13 countries. Datapizza and Zindi also announced a partnership.

2026-11-03-xwa-anp-bceao-pi-spi-obligato.summary: Agence Nigérienne de Presse relayed a BCEAO statement of 2 November 2026 on mandatory PI-SPI routing; the Launch Base Africa entry covers the rollout. It sets a FCFA 100 million ceiling on instant business-to-business payments, which banks may lower. The same rules are to cover cross-border WAEMU transfers from 1 June 2027.

2026-11-03-xwa-launchbaseafrica-pi-spi-r.summary: From 2 November 2026 the BCEAO required interoperable e-money transfers across WAEMU to route through its PI-SPI platform. In the first days, users in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire reported Orange Money-to-Wave transfers debited but not credited, and alias conflicts. Wave added a 1% cash-withdrawal fee, outside the BCEAO's transfer-fee cap; the BCEAO had not commented.

2026-11-03-xwa-pressafrik-pi-spi-obligat.summary: PressAfrik reported failed bank-to-wallet transfers as mandatory PI-SPI routing began on 2 November 2026; the Launch Base Africa entry covers the rollout. Economist Souleymane Astou Diagne said coverage is incomplete, as microfinance has until 30 June 2027 to connect. He named fraud, platform outages and state use of payment data as risks.

2026-11-03-zaf-fake-sims-hold-sa-to-rans.summary: In The Citizen, Johan van Graan argued that SIM cards registered in bulk to false identities hamper police work on ransom kidnappings. Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi promised tougher RICA enforcement from 1 July 2026; by 9 October no results had been reported, he wrote. He cites 27 SIM-crime investigations since 2020, with one arrest.

2026-11-04-afr-smart-africa-and-e-crime-.summary: Smart Africa and e-Crime Bureau signed a three-year memorandum of understanding on cybersecurity, reported on 4 November 2026. It covers workforce skills, governance, risk management, harmonised law and policy, and the securing of critical cybersecurity infrastructure. No signing date or funding is stated.

2026-11-04-ago-agt-pretende-integrar-doi.summary: Angola's tax administration AGT aims to bring two million taxpayers onto electronic invoicing in 2027. More than 80,000 already issue e-invoices. On 4 November 2026 AGT met taxpayers and specialists in Luanda to assess the system before its second phase.

2026-11-04-bdi-alertes.summary: Burundi's meteorological institute, IGEBU, issued a moderate-severity heavy rain alert on 4 November 2026 for parts of the country, including Mugamba and Buyenzi. It had issued a similar alert on 27 October 2026. Both appear on its page as expired.

2026-11-04-ben-code-du-num-rique-l-upmb-.summary: Benin's media union UPMB and Amnesty International Bénin agreed on 3 November 2026 to seek a review of articles 550 onward of the Code du numérique. They cite the effects on journalists, bloggers and citizens. They plan training, awareness campaigns and advocacy with the authorities and legislators.

2026-11-04-ben-compte-rendu-conseil-des-.summary: Benin's Council of Ministers authorised a pilot of two "Innobox" innovation houses, in Parakou and Porto-Novo, on 4 November 2026, according to the government secretariat's record. The houses are modular centres for fabrication and experimentation, intended in time for every commune. Each is to collect national-language corpora for artificial intelligence, as a local relay of the national AI strategy.

2026-11-04-bfa-aes-cinq-chantiers-pour-a.summary: Experts from Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger met in Ouagadougou on 3-5 November 2026 to prepare digital cooperation accords for the Confederation of Sahel States (AES). Topics include shared infrastructure, an NGSO satellite hub, joint bandwidth purchase, regional incident response and postal services. Signing is announced for 24-27 November 2026.

2026-11-04-bfa-communiqu-dgi-facturation.summary: Burkina Faso's tax directorate (DGI) announced that from 1 January 2027 large and medium enterprises must issue every invoice through a certified electronic invoicing system (SECeF). The rule rests on article 564-2 of the Code général des impôts. Suppliers face fines per invoice and possible closure; clients may lose their VAT deduction.

2026-11-04-businessday-afis-2026-savings.summary: A Deloitte-AFIS survey presented in Luanda found that 11% of African financial institutions surveyed were connected to PAPSS, and 45% had no plans to join. Of respondents, 69% judged AfCFTA implementation too slow, and 7% reported tangible progress. 53% said the same of the African Exchanges Linkage Project.

2026-11-04-bwa-huawei-orange-partner-to-.summary: Orange Botswana and Huawei Technologies Botswana signed a memorandum of understanding that extends their cooperation to intelligent networks, AI, cloud, enterprise solutions and data infrastructure. It builds on Orange Botswana's Tier III-certified data centre. No sum is stated.

2026-11-04-civ-l-anp-et-l-anssi-s-accord.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's press regulator ANP and cybersecurity agency ANSSI agreed on 21 October 2026 to prepare a joint roadmap against disinformation and digital threats. It covers prevention capacity and the protection of the ANP's information systems.

2026-11-04-civ-mtn-c-te-d-ivoire-inaugur.summary: MTN Côte d'Ivoire opened its first QG Digital centre at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny on 30 October 2026. It is the first of the digital spaces planned at 20 Ivorian universities under a FCFA 500 million programme.

2026-11-04-cod-du-03-au-05-novembre-2026.summary: DR Congo's digital economy minister opened a review of seven draft cybersecurity orders under the Code du numérique on 3 November 2026. The regulator ARPTC said a diagnostic report and a 2026-2030 digital governance framework are validated. Sixty-three minimum requirements await validation; a government SOC and national CSIRT are still being designed.

2026-11-04-cod-telecoms-kinshasa-concent.summary: DR Congo had 77 million active mobile subscriptions in the second quarter of 2026, the regulator ARPTC's observatory reported, as carried by ACP on 4 November. Penetration rose from 66.8% to 68.6% and sector revenue rose 5.3% to USD 665.6m. Kinshasa held 19.59m subscriptions and about a third of revenue.

2026-11-04-egy-foreign-minister-first-ph.summary: Egypt's foreign ministry said on 4 November 2026 that the first phase of the Unified National System for International Cooperation is complete and its official launch is being prepared. The e-government platform tracks development financing and projects from negotiation to implementation. It links ministries and beneficiary bodies with development partners.

2026-11-04-egy-mts-seeks-chinese-technol.summary: MTS chair Hesham Kandeel said the Egyptian company seeks approval for a data-centre equipment plant with Inspur. Preliminary investment is estimated at US$100 million. MTS is also building an AI platform with China's UCloud, giving access to about 1,787 AI providers.

2026-11-04-eri-integrating-skills-for-di.summary: Shabait, the Eritrean information ministry's outlet, published an interview on 4 November 2026 with pharmacist Nuru Abdu Ahmed and computer engineer Bilal Adem Shelogay. The two have developed an Android application for healthcare and describe it and their plans. Ahmed works on the national formulary at the Ministry of Health.

2026-11-04-eth-au-eu-senior-officials-me.summary: African Union and European Union senior officials met in Addis Ababa on 4 November 2026 to follow up the Luanda summit of November 2025. They are to adopt an implementation plan covering digital and AI governance, among other fields; adoption is not reported. Ethiopia presented the AU position on digital and AI.

2026-11-04-eth-oromia-supreme-court-part.summary: The Oromia Supreme Court and the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute reviewed their joint projects on 4 November 2026. The Institute is building Smart Court systems for the court's operations. The two bodies set frameworks to extend the partnership.

2026-11-04-fibre-cuts-and-nigerias-digit.summary: A TechCabal analysis argues that Nigeria's Critical National Information Infrastructure Order of June 2024 has not reduced fibre cuts. It cites over ₦2.2 billion in repair costs for 5,934 cuts in the first half of 2026. Its figure of over 44,000 cuts in nine months of 2026 has no named source.

2026-11-04-gha-africa-urged-to-unite-on-.summary: The 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum opened in Accra, reported on 4 November 2026. Vice President Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang called for a common African digital governance agenda and cited Ghana's work on a National AI Strategy. Digital minister Samuel Nartey George listed priorities including connectivity, cybersecurity, data protection, child online safety and national language models for AI.

2026-11-04-ken-e-citizen-royalty-system-.summary: Kenya's Directorate of eCitizen told the National Assembly's Sports and Culture Committee that copyright royalty collection now runs fully through eCitizen. The National Treasury remits collections twice a week to licensed collective management organisations, split 70% royalties and 30% administration. PAVRISK was named the only fully compliant organisation; the hearing date is not stated.

2026-11-04-ken-ipf-and-treasury-review-k.summary: Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi told a partners' meeting with the Institute of Public Finance on 4 November 2026 that Kenya's eGP system has onboarded over 1,500 procuring entities and 45,000 suppliers. Contracts worth about KSh 18.3 billion have been processed through it. He set four priorities for the next phase of the reform.

2026-11-04-ken-nyota-agpo-digital-traini.summary: Kenya's State Department for MSMEs launched the NYOTA AGPO Digital Training Programme, reported on 4 November 2026. The free 10-week self-paced course targets more than 600,000 young entrepreneurs and teaches registration and bidding on the government's IFMIS and e-GP procurement systems. Enrolment is by USSD, with a subsidised Safaricom data bundle.

2026-11-04-ken-postbank-opens-600-agent-.summary: Kenya's Postbank joined the Pesalink network, reported on 4 November 2026, so customers of other participating banks can deposit cash at its more than 600 agent and branch points. Withdrawals are not yet available.

2026-11-04-ken-regulators-need-to-talk-t.summary: An opinion piece argues that Kenya's competition and data protection regulators should coordinate on mergers where data is the main asset. It cites the Competition Authority of Kenya's approach to data segregation, which would keep an acquirer from reading rivals' information on a shared payments platform. It refers to the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026.

2026-11-04-lbr-senator-momo-t-cyrus-seek.summary: On 3 November 2026 Senator Momo T. Cyrus of Lofa County asked Liberia's Senate to summon government agencies over the country's cybersecurity preparedness. He named laws and policies, staffing, incident response and the protection of government databases and critical infrastructure. The plenary sent his communication to Senate leadership.

2026-11-04-lby-vetogate-attorney-general.summary: Khalifa Ashour coordinates the Libyan Public Prosecution's digital transformation unit. Ashour told Vetogate on 4 November 2026 that 34,000 civil registry entries are suspected of forgery. Ashour said 1.2 million cases have been entered into the digital system. The remarks came at the third Public Prosecution international book fair in Tripoli.

2026-11-04-le-mali-lance-une-plateforme-.summary: Mali's computer incident response centre ML-CERT launched a web platform for reporting cyber incidents and sharing threat information. The launch came at the fourth National Cybersecurity Days, held by the regulator AMRTP in Bamako on 26-30 October 2026. The national cybercrime unit recorded 1,338 cases in 2025, of which 1,130 were complaints.

2026-11-04-mar-495109-ouahbi-8-millions-.summary: Morocco's justice minister told a House of Representatives committee on 4 November 2026 that about 8 million of some 160 million court files had been indexed in three years. He said the ministry and the judicial authority had each funded similar software. They have since agreed a single digitisation budget with the finance ministry.

2026-11-04-mar-hespress-wahbi-banks-elec.summary: Morocco's justice minister criticised the banks on 4 November 2026 for not responding to a ministry proposal to pay court dues electronically. He said court cashiers leave with sums of up to millions of dirhams in cash. Payment would instead go through the Caisse de Dépôt et de Gestion. Most banks have not responded; one or two raised no objection.

2026-11-04-mar-ministere-de-lia-symptome.summary: A LeBrief opinion piece answers two tribunes by Imad Rochd on Morocco's new ministry of AI, digital transformation and administrative reform. Ahmed Rahhou has headed it since 16 October 2026. The author argues the ministry is chiefly an act of political communication, and that Rochd's indicators sidestep democratic legitimacy.

2026-11-04-mdg-identite-numerique-pres-d.summary: Madagascar's interior minister said on national television on 1 November 2026 that just under seven million adults have completed biometric enrolment under Izaho Tokana, the unique digital identifier project. Phase 2.0 resumed in September 2026 under the DECIM project, after PRODIGY closed in June. It begins in 16 districts and aims for 10 million enrolled by July 2027.

2026-11-04-mdg-le-ministre-du-developpem.summary: Madagascar's Minister of Digital Development, Posts and Telecommunications, Mahefa Andriamampiadana, resigned on health grounds, and the Presidency accepted the resignation on 3 November 2026. The Higher Education Minister is interim minister. The electronic communications bill 040/2026 and the cybersecurity bill 042/2026 remain pending.

2026-11-04-moz-how-ai-is-helping-mozambi.summary: Mozambique announced in September 2026 that it is extending its PAAD immunisation analytics platform from 15 districts to more than 80 across six provinces. The Ministry of Health and Zenysis developed it with Gavi support. It links more than a dozen health systems without replacing them.

2026-11-04-nam-cabinet-briefs.summary: Namibia's Cabinet announced on 3 November 2026 that it had approved a revised National Broadband Policy and delayed the e-ID card launch. The ICT ministry is to tackle gaps in access, usage, affordability and skills. The e-ID launch, set for September 2026, now awaits regulations under a 2024 Act.

2026-11-04-namelok-wireless-launches-com.summary: Namelok Wireless announced on 4 November 2026 a community internet network in Kimuka, on Kenya's Ngong-Suswa Road. It serves public schools, government offices, health facilities and small businesses. No subscriber, coverage or price figures were published.

2026-11-04-nga-africas-fragmented-data-l.summary: At the Data Protection Africa Summit in Lagos on 4 November 2026, regulators from over 15 countries discussed conflicts between national data laws. Teki Akuetteh of the Africa Digital Rights Hub announced a planned Centre of Excellence for data protection research. Nigeria's data protection commissioner Vincent Olatunji called for cooperation across sectors.

2026-11-04-nga-google-org-backs-helium-h.summary: Google.org gave Nigerian health-technology firm Helium Health a US$2.5 million grant to scale HeliumMum, its AI maternal-health tool. The aim is to digitise 150 health facilities and enrol 300,000 women. Helium Health is one of 15 recipients of Google.org's US$30 million AI for Government Innovation Impact Challenge; the award date is not stated.

2026-11-04-nga-how-fg-selects-beneficiar.summary: The Federal Government says beneficiaries of the N50,000 relief under NERSI are chosen from verified national identity records and the National Social Register. The register holds data on more than 70 million people. Enrolment in both is required, payment goes to a mobile wallet linked to the NIN, and people cannot apply to be added.

2026-11-04-nga-nigeria-targets-90-local-.summary: The Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN) marked its 20th year with a goal of 90% local traffic by 2046. Chief executive Muhammed Rudman said up to 70% of traffic is now local, against 1% in 2006. The exchange has over 130 connected networks and plans 1.6T capacity trials in 2033-2036.

2026-11-04-nga-nin-fraud-arrests-data-sc.summary: NIMC's Identity Crime Enforcement Unit arrested suspected illegal NIN enrolment operators in Gwagwalada, Abuja, and elsewhere, and seized their equipment. The investigations covered illegal enrolment, unauthorised changes to identity records and extortion. NIMC has not said how many people were arrested or whether any records were affected; the arrest date is not stated.

2026-11-04-rwa-rwanda-advances-horizon-1.summary: Rwanda's health minister said Horizon 1000 will add AI support to eBuzima, the digital platform frontline health workers use, with a focus on primary health facilities by 2028. The tools are to be tested for safety and effectiveness before they inform patient care. He had recently met the Gates Foundation and OpenAI about the initiative.

2026-11-04-sen-sante-numerique-le-vide-j.summary: A Transform Health Senegal consultation found 65.8% of respondents unaware that Senegal has no specific health data law. The non-representative sample also found 44.7% saying their consent is never sought before their medical data is shared. A draft digital health bill remains under government review, the coalition says.

2026-11-04-sle-sierra-leone-establishes-.summary: Sierra Leone's communications ministry set up a .SL ccTLD Stakeholder Working Group, reported on 4 November 2026. It is to guide the move of the .sl registry, run abroad by a private operator since 2007, onto national infrastructure and its redelegation through IANA. The World Bank funds the work through the SLDTP.

2026-11-04-sle-sierra-leone-s-data-prote.summary: Sierra Leone's Data Protection and Right of Access to Information Bill, 2026 was due before Parliament on 5 November 2026. The rights group CHRDI, which sits on the bill's steering committee, gave the date.

2026-11-04-switch-al-maghrib-on-future-o.summary: Hanae Ben Driss, head of Morocco's national payment switch Switch Al-Maghrib, told TechCabal that each country needs its own switch first. She said it is in talks with the national switches of Nigeria, Ghana and Rwanda on an African association. No date is given.

2026-11-04-syc-sma-successfully-passes-s.summary: The Seychelles Meteorological Authority said on 4 November 2026 that it passed an annual surveillance audit by the British Standards Institution, held on 3 and 4 November. The audit confirms its ISO 9001:2015 certification for aeronautical meteorological services. The authority plans to extend certification to its non-aviation services.

2026-11-04-tun-justice-le-tribunal-admin.summary: Tunisia's Administrative Tribunal held its first pleading hearings in the central first-instance chambers on the Sélim electronic justice system (reported 4 November 2026). The tribunal says Sélim already runs in the regional first-instance chambers. It now covers all chambers and every stage of procedure.

2026-11-04-tun-ministry-of-finance-1-8-m.summary: Tunisia's Finance Minister told parliament's finance committees on 3 November 2026 that the electronic invoicing platform had received about 1.8 million invoices. Nearly 37,000 of them were settled. The 2027 budget also plans a unified tax account from the first quarter of 2027.

2026-11-04-tza-korea-edcf-tanzania-secur.summary: Tanzania's Ministry of Finance and Korea Eximbank signed a concessional loan of US$167.4 million (TSh441.12 billion) on 3 November 2026, from Korea's Economic Development Cooperation Fund. It finances a technology institute in Dodoma offering advanced training, including in AI. Korea Eximbank said it was the first EDCF project approved in 2026 and the first with support for AI.

2026-11-04-tza-tanzania-accelerates-digi.summary: Tanzania's Universal Communications Service Access Fund (UCSAF) and the Tanzania Institute of Education signed a memorandum of understanding in October 2026. It covers investment in digital educational content and training for teachers. Daily News gives no signing day, terms or sum.

2026-11-04-tza-ucsaf-to-improve-mobile-n.summary: Tanzania's UCSAF said on 3 November 2026 that it is preparing a project to fix mobile coverage along the Dar es Salaam-Dodoma railway within a year. Of 2,324 planned towers, 2,199 are complete, reaching 2,053 of 2,306 targeted wards. A further 82 sites are due for tender in January-February 2027.

2026-11-04-uga-mtn-uganda-unaudited-resu.summary: MTN Uganda reports profit after tax of Ush571.2 billion for the nine months to 30 September 2026, up 21.2%. Mobile money transaction value was Ush166.6 trillion, up 18.3%. It had 26.4 million subscribers. Third-quarter data revenue growth slowed to 7.8%, from 17.5% in the second quarter, which MTN attributes to unauthorised public Wi-Fi resellers.

2026-11-04-uga-uganda-east-african-commu.summary: Uganda's EAC Affairs minister Rebecca Kadaga told Parliament on 3 November 2026 that the East African Payment System links only four countries' RTGS systems. These are Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. She set out how an EAC cross-border payment masterplan, adopted in 2025, is to reduce use of the US dollar.

2026-11-04-xaf-google-empowering-educato.summary: Google DeepMind and Fab AI will build open Gemma-based AI tools for teachers in Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, Google announced. Google.org and the Gates Foundation fund the work, which first targets up to 500 teachers and 15,000 students. Google also opened its AI Educator Series in South Africa with SACE.

2026-11-04-xca-cemac-la-beac-engage-une-.summary: The central bank BEAC opened an international selection, funded from its own resources, for a firm to assist with AI project management. The firm would run a maturity diagnostic, draft an internal AI adoption strategy and identify priority processes and use cases. Bids are due on 23 December 2026.

2026-11-04-xwa-ecowas-community-sectoral.summary: ECOWAS statisticians are meeting in Lomé from 3 to 6 November 2026. They are reviewing the first draft of the Commission's Yearbook of Sectoral Statistics. The workshop checks the indicators and fills data gaps. The draft then goes to the Regional Technical Committee. The World Bank funds the work through the PHASAO and PHASAOC projects.

2026-11-04-zambia-first-regional-validat.summary: Zambia, COMESA and the World Bank held the first regional validation workshop of the IDEA programme in Chongwe on 3-5 November 2026. Member states reviewed a draft regional digital inclusion strategy and action plan; validation is not reported. Zambia put its fibre backbone at over 42,000 km, against about 15,000 km in 2021.

2026-11-04-zmb-ict-sector-key-to-grow-za.summary: Zambia's Minister of Technology and Science Felix Mutati set out five ICT pillars for the Grow Zambia Agenda at the ZDA Zambia-Germany ICT Business Forum in Lusaka. They are trusted digital identity, interoperability, intelligence, digital infrastructure and inclusivity. He said digital infrastructure is being imported duty-free.

2026-11-04-zwe-government-to-scale-artif.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera tasked the ministry's new AI Unit with identifying, testing and scaling AI applications. She spoke at a strategic plan review workshop in Bulawayo. The plan names inaccurate responses, bias and poor data quality as risks.

2026-11-05-africa-digital-leapfrogging-o.summary: A journal study by Enock Mwakalila of Mzumbe University uses panel data on African countries to test whether digitalisation changes economic structure. It finds that higher internet penetration lowers agriculture's share of output and raises that of services. The effect is stronger in slower-growing economies.

2026-11-05-air-botswana-probes-suspected.summary: Air Botswana activated incident-response procedures after a suspected ransomware attack on 3 November 2026. Unauthorised access reached internal systems holding employee information. The airline said booking and flight-operations systems were unaffected and that it had begun meeting its Data Protection Act 2024 obligations.

2026-11-05-bfa-burkina-economie-la-dgi-r.summary: Burkina Faso's tax directorate began training more than 400 agents on 4 November 2026 in three digital systems: e-filing, certified e-invoicing and the online cadastre. Sessions are held in four cities. The DISMEFIP project, co-funded by Swiss cooperation and the government, pays for it.

2026-11-05-bfa-compte-rendu-du-conseil-d.summary: Burkina Faso's Council of Ministers adopted two decrees on 5 November 2026. One creates the foundational identification system and a national register of the unique identifier. The other designates the Ministry of Digital Transition to enrol people and issue the identifier until the competent body is operational. The council also approved CFA 15,463,900,000 of state-funded ministry projects, including a new administration network in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso.

2026-11-05-civ-banques-fintech-monnaie-e.summary: The National Assembly's economic and finance committee unanimously adopted a banking-regulation bill on 4 November 2026. It brings FinTechs and electronic-money operators into the banking law for the first time. The 258-article text also covers Islamic finance, BCEAO licensing powers, customer protection and bank resolution.

2026-11-05-civ-cote-divoire-aip-le-minis.summary: Côte d'Ivoire named 32 digital firms on 4 November 2026 for 24 months of state support: 14 start-ups and 18 small and medium enterprises. Each is bound by a performance contract measured on revenue, jobs and regional expansion.

2026-11-05-civ-cote-divoire-aip-le-vote-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Senate voted electronically for the first time on 5 November 2026, on four bills in Yamoussoukro. Digital attendance and tallying replaced the roll call, and results were declared in under three minutes.

2026-11-05-civ-cybersecurite-abidjan-qg-.summary: Cybastion and Cisco inaugurated a Security Operations Centre in Abidjan on 5 November 2026, described as a regional hub for West Africa. A related programme aims to train 200,000 learners in cybersecurity, networking and AI by 2030. A US State Department official attended and cited USD 170 million of new US investment in Côte d'Ivoire in 2026.

2026-11-05-cod-ue-pnud-digitalisation-ju.summary: DR Congo's Ministry of Justice launched digital collection of court fees on 5 November 2026, with the courts, prosecutors' offices and prisons to be interconnected. UNDP provides technical support and the EU funds it. The first digital nationality certificate was issued at the launch, and a second phase is planned for early 2027.

2026-11-05-comesa-introduces-new-rules-t.summary: COMESA's competition commission said on 5 November 2026 that digital mergers worth at least USD 250 million now fall within its jurisdiction. The rules come from regulations adopted in December 2025, which replaced those of 2004. They also set a general financial threshold of USD 60 million and add market inquiry powers. Guidelines are being revised.

2026-11-05-digify-africa-brings-digital-.summary: Digify Africa launched the Didi Mobile Academy, a WhatsApp digital-skills course for South Africans aged 18 to 35. The Trevor Noah Foundation's R50 million Kulaninati Innovation Fund pays for it. The first course has five modules of about 15 minutes each.

2026-11-05-dji-digital-2027-djibouti.summary: DataReportal published its Digital 2027 report for Djibouti on 5 November 2026. It counts 786,000 internet users at the end of 2026, a penetration of 65.3 per cent. It also counts 649,000 mobile connections, equal to 53.9 per cent of the population, and 266,000 social media identities.

2026-11-05-dza-echorouk-digital-platform.summary: Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb launched a digital platform on 5 November 2026 to track the daily prices and availability of basic goods in every wilaya. It is meant to trace goods along the national supply chain. He announced it to the walis by videoconference.

2026-11-05-eth-digital-2027-ethiopia.summary: DataReportal published its Digital 2027 report for Ethiopia on 5 November 2026. It counts 31.1 million internet users at the end of 2026, a penetration of 22.3 per cent. It also counts 105 million mobile connections, equal to 75.3 per cent of the population, and 10.2 million social media identities.

2026-11-05-eth-ethiopia-suspends-the-rep.summary: Ethiopia's Media Authority suspended the publisher of The Reporter indefinitely on 2 November 2026, covering its print editions and digital platforms. The regulator cited reports harming national interests but named no specific article, CPJ reported on 5 November. CPJ called for the suspension to be lifted.

2026-11-05-eth-ifc-invests-in-kifiyas-ai.summary: Kifiya Financial Technology announced on 4 November 2026, at the Africa Financial Summit in Luanda, an investment agreement with IFC, its first investment in the company. The release says it will scale Kifiya's agricultural fintech and rural reach work. No amount was disclosed.

2026-11-05-ethio-telecom-zte-deploy-ethi.summary: Ethio telecom and ZTE announced on 5 November 2026 a pre-commercial AI-driven radio access network in Ethiopia, which they describe as the first. They report 11% more 4G capacity and 40% higher peak-hour user throughput than the conventional solution. The deployment date was not stated.

2026-11-05-gab-gabon-technologie-trois-p.summary: Gabon's government and Huawei signed three memoranda of understanding and a donation agreement in Shanghai on 4 November 2026, with President Oligui Nguema present, AGP reported. The memoranda cover public security, digital infrastructure and teaching platforms in public universities. The donation is AI teaching equipment for the university named after the president.

2026-11-05-gha-bank-of-ghana-announces-s.summary: The Bank of Ghana said on 5 November 2026 that it and the Monetary Authority of Singapore had completed the first proof of concept under Project DESFT (Digital Economy Semi-Fungible Token). The bank says the pilot demonstrated digital credentials for international trade and cross-border payment. The one-paragraph release names no participants, scope or next phase.

2026-11-05-gha-false-91-of-ghanaians-hav.summary: Dubawa Ghana rated false, on 5 November 2026, the Communication Minister's claim that 91% of Ghanaians hold a Ghana Card. National Identification Authority data at 30 October 2026 show 20,610,948 enrolled and 19,575,078 cards issued. That is about 57% of the projected 2026 population.

2026-11-05-gha-ghana-must-protect-its-da.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission proposed on 28 October 2026 that a copy of health, financial, energy and natural-resource data be kept in Ghana. Its executive director said Ghana has eight data centres and Africa fewer than 200, against more than 5,000 in the United States. He spoke at a lecture at GIMPA.

2026-11-05-gnq-gobierno-avanza-negociaci.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Vice-President chaired a government review on 3 November 2026 of the fees US firm Securiport proposed to modernise border control. He asked for its earlier contracts to compare terms. He recommended a pilot at the Malabo and Bata airports before any wider extension.

2026-11-05-helios-towers-raises-2026-gui.summary: Helios Towers added 3,435 tenancies in the nine months to 30 September 2026, its highest year-to-date total, bringing the portfolio to 35,379 tenancies. Revenue rose 13% to US$718.8 million. The company raised its full-year guidance to about 4,000 additions.

2026-11-05-iec-tool-flags-misinformation.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission reported 34 complaints on its Real411 platform ahead of the November 2026 municipal elections. X accounted for 58.8% of them and TikTok for 23.5%. The chief electoral officer cited videos of commission staff posted without context.

2026-11-05-interswitch-deepens-uganda-s-.summary: Housing Finance Bank joined Interswitch's Quickteller agency banking network in Uganda on 4 November 2026. Customers can deposit, withdraw by card and check balances at more than 23,000 agents. The bank said its pilot had processed over UGX49 billion.

2026-11-05-ken-ca-consumer-complaints-re.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya reported 479 consumer complaints escalated to it between July and September 2026. It resolved 422, a rate of 88.1%, and 57 remain under follow-up. Data services drew 140 complaints (29.2%), and the authority also logged 47 on fraud and scams and 49 on cybercrime.

2026-11-05-ken-kenya-moves-to-operationa.summary: ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo named operationalising the National Cybersecurity Agency a priority at the Africa Cyber Defense Forum in Nairobi on 4 November 2026. The agency was established in 2026 to run the National Cybersecurity Operations Centre. He also cited closer coordination with other national cyber bodies and the Data Protection Commissioner.

2026-11-05-ken-kenya-seeks-chinese-suppo.summary: Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo and Chinese Ambassador Guo Haiyan discussed a proposed US$180 million grant for Phase One of an AI Cloud Data Project in Eldoret, reported on 5 November 2026. They also discussed AI capacity building and faster government digitisation. The grant was under discussion and not committed.

2026-11-05-lbr-digital-2027-liberia.summary: DataReportal published its Digital 2027 report for Liberia on 5 November 2026. It counts 1.90 million internet users at the end of 2026, a penetration of 32.2 per cent. It also counts 5.88 million mobile connections, equal to 99.9 per cent of the population, and 1.20 million social media identities.

2026-11-05-lbr-gcf-sap018-liberia-climat.summary: The Green Climate Fund approved project SAP018 on 13 November 2020, with the African Development Bank as accredited entity. It funds climate information and early-warning services in Liberia, aiming to reach 7.7 million people. The grant is USD 10 million of a USD 11.4 million total, and completion is set for October 2027.

2026-11-05-lby-wahda-bank-picks-backbase.summary: Libya's Wahda Bank selected Backbase to build its digital banking platform, reported on 5 November 2026. Business banking goes live first in 2027, with online account opening by electronic identity verification. Retail banking for more than 500,000 customers follows, with links to the LYPay and OnePay instant payment systems.

2026-11-05-mdg-telecommunications-les-re.summary: L'Express de Madagascar reported on 5 November 2026 that the resignation of Minister Mahefa Andriamampiadana, accepted on 3 November, comes as the telecoms sector awaits regulatory reform. Bill 040/2026 aims to ease entry for new operators in a market of three. See the Madagascar entry on the minister's resignation for the main account.

2026-11-05-moz-digital-2027-mozambique.summary: DataReportal published its Digital 2027 report for Mozambique on 5 November 2026. It counts 7.57 million internet users at the end of 2026, a penetration of 20.5 per cent. It also counts 18.4 million mobile connections, equal to 49.9 per cent of the population, and 4.39 million social media identities.

2026-11-05-mtn-uganda-profits-rise-as-da.summary: MTN Uganda's profit after tax rose 21.2% to Ush571.2 billion in the nine months to 30 September 2026, as a one-off tax settlement in the prior year dropped out. Data revenue growth slowed to 7.8% in the third quarter, which the company attributed partly to unauthorised Wi-Fi resellers. It now expects full-year service revenue growth near 8.5%.

2026-11-05-nedbank-gears-up-for-smart-id.summary: Nedbank announced a phased rollout of Home Affairs smart-ID services at its branches. It begins with its own staff in November 2026, then nine pilot sites, and reaches all nine provinces in early 2027. Integration with Home Affairs systems is under test, and the fee is waived during the pilot.

2026-11-05-ner-numerique-dans-lespace-ae.summary: The Alliance of Sahel States adopted the digital deliverables of its Confederation's Year II roadmap in Ouagadougou on 5 November 2026. Sixteen of 18 deliverables were finalised. A confederal network operations centre is due by 31 December 2028. Interconnection legal and tariff frameworks are to be harmonised by 30 June 2027. National cybersecurity response teams are to be funded from universal-service funds and regulatory fees.

2026-11-05-nga-cbn-regulations-operation.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria issued regulations for non-security virtual assets on 5 November 2026. Issuers of naira-referenced stablecoins need NGN 10bn of paid-up capital and foreign-currency-referenced issuers NGN 15bn, through Nigerian-incorporated entities. Algorithmic stablecoins are banned, other virtual-asset services need NGN 1bn, and the commencement date is not yet set.

2026-11-05-nga-why-unverified-phones-cou.summary: Nigeria's Communications Commission urged buyers to check a phone on its Device Checker platform before paying, Vanguard reported on 5 November 2026. The NCC says about 231 million devices already on Nigerian networks were verified automatically before the framework took effect in October 2026. Zonal Controller Tunji Jimoh said the platform reads no personal data. The technical presentation, however, described linking a device's IMEI to subscriber identification.

2026-11-05-nigeria-seeks-digital-id-proj.summary: Nigeria has asked the World Bank for a third extension of its ID4D project, to 31 December 2027, according to a restructuring paper. The priority is the new MOSIP-based identity system, whose contract was signed on 15 September. The paper also records unpaid enrolment partners and about 145 million enrolments at 14 September.

2026-11-05-numerique-les-pays-arabes-mis.summary: A UN commission session in Tunis on 4 and 5 November 2026 discussed a second Arab Digital Agenda. Plans include a mid-term review by 2028, a regional digital-development report and an Arab observatory. ESCWA's executive secretary said networks cover about 95% of the Arab population, but only 70% use the internet.

2026-11-05-paga-expands-direct-debit-acc.summary: Paga now lets businesses collect direct debits from customers of other Nigerian financial institutions through Paga Engine, using existing interbank rails. TechCabal reported it on 5 November 2026. Central Bank of Nigeria data show 157.4 million direct-debit transactions worth about ₦23.3 trillion in 2024.

2026-11-05-paratus-lesotho-opens-for-bus.summary: Paratus Group launched Paratus Lesotho, a joint venture with Real Image Lesotho, on 5 November 2026. It is an authorised Starlink reseller. It offers satellite connectivity to businesses outside fibre coverage.

2026-11-05-revenue-sharing-data-sovereig.summary: Liberian lawmakers are reviewing a draft concession, valued at USD 52 million to 54.7 million, with OeSD International to upgrade the national biometric ID system. Reports say the company would take 65% of specified revenues and the government 35%. Critics also question where biometric data would be stored and who would hold the encryption keys.

2026-11-05-robotique-et-ia-le-gabon-expl.summary: President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema visited a robotics park in Shanghai on 4 November 2026, during a state visit to China. The presidency named training, technology transfer and public-service uses as possible areas of cooperation. Gabon's first national AI strategy has not yet been adopted.

2026-11-05-safaricom-h1-profit-jumps-36-.summary: Safaricom's net income rose 35.9% to KES 58.2 billion in the six months to 30 September 2026. M-PESA revenue grew 13.6% to KES 100.1 billion. Safaricom Ethiopia raised service revenue 71.6% and narrowed its EBITDA loss to KES 434.4 million.

2026-11-05-safaricom-makes-more-from-m-p.summary: Safaricom said Fuliza, its M-PESA overdraft service, earned KES 4.9 billion in the six months to September 2026, up 86%. Borrowers reached 17.2 million, while the average advance fell 24.6% to KES 192. Fuliza supplied about 71% of revenue from Safaricom's six lending products.

2026-11-05-samsung-pay-launches-in-moroc.summary: Samsung Pay launched in Morocco on 5 November 2026 using Mastercard's tokenisation service. Eligible Mastercard cardholders at participating banks can pay with compatible Samsung devices. The banks were not named.

2026-11-05-sas-ict-sector-records-larges.summary: The National R&D Survey for 2024/25 puts South Africa's ICT research spending at R5.7 billion, up R853 million, the largest rise of any field. Total R&D spending was R44.2 billion, and intensity fell from 0.62% to 0.60% of GDP. Business R&D fell by R742 million.

2026-11-05-sen-escroqueries-par-intellig.summary: Senegal's data protection commission (CDP) warned on 5 November 2026 of rising AI scams using voice cloning and deepfakes. It says a person's voice and image are personal data under Law 2008-12. Copying them with AI without consent is unlawful processing, it says. It advises people to call back on a known number.

2026-11-05-sen-protection-des-donn-es-pe.summary: Senegal's digital and health ministries said on 4 November 2026 that they are jointly setting up an infrastructure to secure and host patients' health data, SenePlus reported. They spoke at a Digital Health Week meeting, where Enabel described its digital-health support. No timetable was given.

2026-11-05-somalia-to-establish-ai-acade.summary: Tabaarak ICT Solutions and the Somali National Artificial Intelligence Centre signed an agreement to set up an AI academy in Mogadishu. It is to offer continuous training, courses, research and internships. No funding, start date or intake has been stated.

2026-11-05-ssd-central-bank-and-national.summary: The Bank of South Sudan and the National Communication Authority signed an updated memorandum on digital financial services on 4 November 2026. It revises their 2018 agreement. It provides for information sharing, joint supervision and enforcement, and stronger consumer protection and cybersecurity.

2026-11-05-syc-digital-2027-seychelles.summary: DataReportal published its Digital 2027 report on Seychelles on 5 November 2026. It counts 119,000 internet users, 87.8% of the population, and 228,000 mobile connections, equal to 168% of the population, in late 2026.

2026-11-05-tcd-la-strategie-nationale-de.summary: Chad began drafting a National Digital Transformation Strategy on 4 November 2026, at a framing meeting chaired by the digital economy director-general. UNDP is funding an international consultancy. Chad's data governance strategy has been validated and its AI strategy pre-validated.

2026-11-05-tgo-ia-jusqua-262-millions-de.summary: The Ayre Think Tank published an AI readiness index at the Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda, reported on 5 November 2026. Togo scored 42.6 out of 100, against a readiness threshold of 53, and ranked 37th of 56 countries. The study puts the ten-year economic gain from AI at 83 to 262 million dollars, using IMF scenarios.

2026-11-05-tgo-togo-instant-payment-plat.summary: BCEAO said on 5 November 2026 that its PI-SPI instant payment platform had processed nearly CFAF 15 billion in 163,000 transactions in Togo by the end of October. The platform has 3.9 million users in Togo and 17 connected providers. The bank spoke at the start of a student awareness campaign in Lomé.

2026-11-05-tun-ministere-de-la-famille-7.summary: Nessma and the TAP news agency reported on 5 November 2026 that Tunisia's family ministry has started drafting a bill to protect children online. The minister announced it at a national forum. Officials cited internet use of 77.7 per cent among people aged 10 and over. The ministry launched a national pact on children's online safety in November 2025.

2026-11-05-tun-passeports-des-tre-une-no.summary: Tunisia's Foreign Minister told parliament on 5 November 2026 that the ministry has begun a pilot putting passport issuance and renewal for Tunisians abroad into its electronic consulate system. Roll-out across consular centres is planned during 2027. He did not say which steps will be online. New passport production units are to be installed in Jakarta, Beijing and Montreal.

2026-11-05-tun-sijil-al-mu-assasat-yadkh.summary: Tunisia's National Business Registry announced two AI services on 5 November 2026. Nawarni is a chatbot that guides founders through company creation and the choice of legal form. A second bot checks and reserves trade names. The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law built them, with funding from the Dutch embassy.

2026-11-05-tza-bunge-laridhia-azimio-la-.summary: Tanzania's Parliament passed a resolution for the country to accede to the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention, 2014), reported on 5 November 2026. ICT minister Angellah Kairuki tabled it, with the backing of the Standing Committee on Infrastructure. The report does not give the sitting date.

2026-11-05-uga-ucc-considers-registering.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission is considering asking parents to declare SIM cards used by their children. Operators would then keep databases of minors' SIMs for online-safety measures. No instrument or timetable has been named.

2026-11-05-uga-ursb-launches-mobile-app-.summary: Uganda's Registration Services Bureau launched URSB Connect, a mobile app, on 5 November 2026. It covers company and business-name registration, name searches, annual returns, trademarks and the SIMPO chattels registry. It runs alongside the bureau's eRegistry platform.

2026-11-05-xaf-circleid-the-february-cas.summary: CircleID reports that the Supreme Court of Mauritius is expected to hear Cloud Innovation's petition to wind up AFRINIC again in February 2027. No published order fixes that date. The Technology Service Providers of Kenya has reportedly retained a barrister said to have acted for the petitioner.

2026-11-05-xaf-ipinfo-afrinic-addresses-.summary: IPinfo published an article by Oliver Gasser and João Tomé on 5 November 2026 on the WHEREIS study. The study compares where IP addresses are used with where they are registered. The authors say AFRINIC is the exception among the five regional registries. Most of its space used outside Africa sits in four blocks registered to one company, 80% of the total.

2026-11-06-abidjan-opens-regional-cybers.summary: Cybastion opened a Cisco cybersecurity centre in Abidjan on 5 November 2026, with a security operations centre and an incident response team. Ivorian digital minister Djibril Ouattara said it supports the country's aim to serve West and Central Africa. The centre follows a memorandum signed in October 2025 and the Africa DigiEmpower programme, which targets 200,000 learners by 2030. See the Côte d'Ivoire entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-afcfta-digital-inclusion-prog.summary: The AfCFTA Secretariat closed phase 1 of its Digital Inclusion and Entrepreneurship Programme, run with Google's Hustle Academy, and reported on 6 November 2026 that it had reached more than 7,000 SMEs in 16 African countries. The programme began in November 2025. Phase 2 is in preparation.

2026-11-06-african-judiciary-pushes-for-.summary: African judges held their first judicial dialogue on internet governance at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum. It was held in Accra and closed on 5 November 2026. Egyptian Court of Cassation vice-president Adel Maged said courts must know where sensitive digital data is stored. He said they must also know who can access it. Participants agreed unanimously to his proposal to develop African guidelines on the use of AI in courts.

2026-11-06-ago-governo-quer-cartoes-inte.summary: Angola's Minister of State for Economic Coordination, José de Lima Massano, urged the interbank operator EMIS and Visa to extend their partnership of more than ten years. He wants international-brand cards accepted across the whole national payment network. He spoke at the opening of Visa's Angola office, reported on 6 November 2026. About 60,000 mainly small and medium establishments accept Visa cards. Visa aims to double that by the end of next year.

2026-11-06-ben-benin-8-millions-de-dolla.summary: La Marina BJ reported on 6 November 2026 that Benin's PReM-Benin programme attaches EUR 6.9 million to linking tax numbers (IFU) with personal identification numbers (NPI). The paper cites a finance ministry figure: 439,333 of 1,077,679 tax numbers (40.76%) were linked to an NPI on 25 October 2023. It also cites a TADAT assessment of November 2023. That rated the taxpayer register's accuracy D, down from C in 2019.

2026-11-06-ben-pag-2026-2033-feuille-de-.summary: Benin's Council of Ministers approved the government action programme (PAG) for 2026-2033 on 4 November 2026, La Nation reported. The programme names technology one of two cross-cutting levers. It is to modernise public services, raise productivity and widen market access. The programme targets 7.7% average real growth with 55% private financing. Its projects, overall cost and monitoring indicators were not presented.

2026-11-06-bfa-burkina-44-2-milliards-de.summary: Burkina Faso's draft second national inclusive finance strategy, for 2027 to 2031, went to a validation workshop in Ouagadougou on 6 November 2026. It is costed at 44.2 billion CFA francs and targets 90% financial inclusion by 2031. ANPFI says inclusion reached 79.04% in 2023, above the 75% first target, and 81.8% at end 2025.

2026-11-06-bfa-sahal-tech-old-rock-group.summary: Sahal Tech Innovation Labs of Burkina Faso signed an agreement with Old Rock Group in Ouagadougou on 2 November 2026 to build the Sahal African Language Data Platform. It starts with datasets and AI for Mooré, Dioula, Fulfuldé and Bambara. Old Rock is to support project structuring, infrastructure and training.

2026-11-06-cbn-new-rules-foreign-stablec.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria released regulations on non-security virtual assets on the evening of 5 November 2026. Issuers of foreign-currency stablecoins must set up a licensed Nigerian entity with at least ₦15 billion in paid-up capital, and issuers of naira-backed stablecoins need ₦10 billion. Algorithmic stablecoins are banned, and existing operators have 180 days from the effective date to apply for a licence. See the Nigeria regulations entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-cbn-sec-divide-crypto-oversig.summary: Under the Central Bank of Nigeria's regulations released on 5 November 2026, the bank oversees stablecoins used for payments, transfers and settlement. The Securities and Exchange Commission keeps trading and securities. A firm licensed by the Commission needs a separate central bank authorisation. It also needs at least ₦1 billion in additional capital for payment services, and the same capital cannot count twice. The Commission has raised the minimum capital for digital asset exchanges from ₦500 million to ₦2 billion. June 2027 is the deadline for existing operators. See the Nigeria regulations entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-cbn-tightens-crypto-p2p-rules.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's regulations of 5 November 2026 require peer-to-peer crypto platforms to route naira payments through banks or approved channels. Platforms must also verify traders' identities. A platform may not release a token until the name and Bank Verification Number on the paying account match its verified customer. Platforms must keep records linking each payment to its token transfer. Travel Rule information is required for transfers of $1,000 or more. See the Nigeria regulations entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-civ-cisco-cybersecurity-centr.summary: Cybastion announced the Cisco Cybersecurity Center in Abidjan on 6 November 2026, serving West and Central Africa. It houses a security operations centre and offers technology demonstrations and skills training. The Africa DigiEmpower programme, run by Cisco, Cybastion and the Ivorian government, aims to train 200,000 young people and women by 2030. See the Côte d'Ivoire entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-cod-justice-en-rdc-digitalisa.summary: UNDP published its account of the launch in Kinshasa of the digitalisation of court fee collection and the interconnection of courts, prosecution offices and prisons, reported on 6 November 2026. The Congolese government leads the reform, with UNDP technical support and European Union funding under the 2025-2029 joint justice programme. It replaces manual collection of court fees. See the DRC entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-dpi-map-2026-11-12.summary: UCL's Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose released its DPI Map dataset on 6 November 2026. The African extract holds 1,843 indicator rows on digital ID, payments and data exchange across 54 states. Each row carries its own check date, from October 2024 to October 2026, and a source link.

2026-11-06-egy-sczone-telecom-egypt-sign.summary: The Suez Canal Economic Zone and Telecom Egypt signed a co-operation agreement, reported on 6 November 2026. Telecom Egypt will build multi-route telecommunications networks and deploy digital, IoT and data-analytics services across the zone's industrial areas, ports and affiliated facilities. The signing date was not stated.

2026-11-06-egy-social-registry-13m-house.summary: Assabah reported on 6 November 2026 that Egypt's national social registry holds 13 million households, about half the country's total. Raafat Shafik, assistant to the social solidarity minister, said it links to 27 government databases. He spoke at an Arab conference in Tunisia and described its use in the Takaful and Karama cash programme.

2026-11-06-eth-insa-national-cyber-drill.summary: Ethiopia's Information Network Security Administration held a National Cyber Drill Competition, reported on 6 November 2026, during the country's 7th National Cyber Security Month. Seventeen institutions each fielded a team of four. They used a drill platform the agency says its own experts developed.

2026-11-06-gab-allocation-de-rentree-sco.summary: Gabon's civil-service pension and family fund (CPPF) opened collection of school certificates for the 2027-2028 school allowance on 5 November 2026. Parents and heads enter them online on the BAANA platform. Greater Libreville goes paperless, and the campaign closes on 1 February 2027. The previous round covered 71,412 beneficiaries and XAF 4.36 billion.

2026-11-06-gab-gabon-taps-huawei-st-digi.summary: ST DIGITAL Gabon and Huawei Technologies Gabon signed a memorandum of understanding in Shanghai on 4 November 2026 to set up a National Talent Training Centre. It will train Gabonese technicians and instructors in networking, cybersecurity, cloud computing, AI, 4G mobile networks and fibre optics. The signing took place during President Oligui Nguema's visit to China.

2026-11-06-gha-financial-inclusion-expan.summary: Ghana's Ministry of Finance inaugurated a National Technical Working Committee on 5 November 2026. It will draft the second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy for 2027 to 2031. Launch is targeted for the first half of 2027, and a Financial Inclusion Council is proposed. The deputy minister cited account ownership above 80% (Global Findex 2025). He also cited 22% of adults financially healthy (FinScope 2021).

2026-11-06-gha-only-61-of-ghanaian-child.summary: About 61% of Ghanaian children hold a birth certificate, UNICEF's representative Andy Brooks said on 4-5 November 2026, 3News reported. He partly blamed weak telecommunications and digital registration that remote communities find hard to use. The Births and Deaths Registry registered 588,972 births by the end of 2025. That is 73.4% of the expected total for the year.

2026-11-06-gin-a-bakou-le-gabon-et-la-gu.summary: Gabon's public service minister Laurence Ndong and her Guinean counterpart Faya François Bourouno agreed on 5 and 6 November 2026, at a UN governance innovation summit in Baku, to organise working visits between Libreville and Conakry. Topics are career management, staff training and simplified administrative procedures. No dates for the visits were given.

2026-11-06-gmb-eoi-gambia-capacity-devel.summary: The African Development Bank posted an expression of interest on 6 November 2026 for a consultancy to build the capacity of Gambian institutions to oversee fintech. The assignment follows the Gambia's validated fintech policy. No award has been announced.

2026-11-06-gmb-eoi-gambia-digital-litera.summary: The African Development Bank posted an expression of interest on 6 November 2026 for a consultancy to formulate a National Digital Literacy Policy and a five-year strategy plan for the Gambia, covering 2027 to 2032. The scope includes an implementation roadmap, a financing plan and a monitoring framework. No award has been announced.

2026-11-06-gmb-gov-t-launches-d40m-digit.summary: The Point reported on 6 November 2026 that The Gambia launched a D40 million digital skills programme under the World Bank-funded WARDIP. Contracts were signed with three training institutions to train 1,280 young people over three years. Courses include software development, cybersecurity and data analytics, and the programme includes three-month internships.

2026-11-06-ken-amaco-and-arise-iip-advan.summary: Kenya Engineer reported on 6 November 2026 that AMACO Energy and ARISE IIP Kenya signed an MoU on HERCULES. It is a proposed power and AI data centre project at Dongo Kundu, Mombasa. AMACO puts the investment at a minimum of US$700 million, with about 250 MW of LNG-based generation rising to 1 GW.

2026-11-06-ken-from-paper-files-to-finge.summary: Vihiga County held its first ICT Day and Digital Innovation Expo, reported on 6 November 2026. Governor Wilber Ottichilo said procurement, job applications and payments are now fully online and that the health workforce is integrated into digital systems. He said the county Land Information System is 70 percent complete.

2026-11-06-ken-kenha-lvbcdp-general-proc.summary: Kenya intends to seek USD 1 billion of World Bank financing for a Lake Victoria Basin connectivity project. KeNHA's notice of 6 November 2026 covers about 815 km of road upgrades with fibre-optic cable along them. The roads fall into five design-build packages across eight counties.

2026-11-06-ken-kenyas-ai-ambitions-face-.summary: The Star reported on 6 November 2026 that Seacom's chief technology officer, Prenesh Padayachee, expects its US$2 billion Africa-to-Asia subsea cable to be complete in 2030. He spoke on BBC Africa Enterprise. Mombasa is a key landing point for East African traffic. Seacom is also exploring post-quantum encryption for data in transit.

2026-11-06-ken-kica-amendment-bill-onlin.summary: ITWeb reported on 6 November 2026 that Kenya's Information and Communications (Amendment) Bill 2026 would add a Section 85C. It would require online platforms serving Kenyan users, foreign ones included, to register with the Communications Authority and report unlawful activity. A separate draft Online Safety Bill 2026 proposes a duty of care, parental consent for children and age verification. Its fines run up to KES 500 million or 10% of global turnover.

2026-11-06-ken-state-turns-to-chiefs-e-c.summary: The Daily Nation reported that Kenya's immigration department told a National Assembly committee on 5 November 2026 that at least 557,000 national ID cards are uncollected. Nearly 400,000 have waited over ten years. Chiefs and e-Citizen text alerts will be used to trace owners before voter registration opens in January 2027.

2026-11-06-lagos-directs-isps-to-clean-u.summary: The Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency told internet service providers in three areas of Lagos, in a notice dated 2 November 2026, to clear and secure their cables and installations. Enforcement begins on 9 November 2026, with possible sanctions. General Manager Prince Oyekanmi Elegushi signed the notice. See the Lagos regulator entry for the full account.

2026-11-06-lagos-orders-isps-to-secure-c.summary: Lagos State's infrastructure regulator LASIMRA ordered internet service providers to rearrange dangling fibre cables, secure loose installations and clear obstructions in Ilasan/Ikate, Allen Avenue and the Customs Office area of Ikeja. The notice is dated 2 November 2026, and enforcement with sanctions begins on 9 November 2026. The Nigerian Communications Commission regulates the sector federally.

2026-11-06-lby-house-speaker-draft-law-s.summary: Libya's House of Representatives speaker Saleh Abdelnabi met the executive director of the Ruya Foundation for Digital Development in Benghazi on 6 November 2026. They discussed a draft law to establish a national science and technology authority. The spokesman said the meeting also covered the foundation advising on governance of the digital space. No text, filing or vote was reported.

2026-11-06-le-zimbabwe-veut-sinspirer-de.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera and the head of the investment agency ZIDA discussed co-operation with India in a podcast episode published on 2 November 2026. Priorities named were Indian investment in ICT, business and knowledge process outsourcing, and local processing of critical minerals. A memorandum of understanding has not been concluded.

2026-11-06-lso-lesotho-mobile-data-cost.summary: Data Matrix reported on 6 November 2026 that one gigabyte of mobile data in Lesotho cost M32.75 on average across the flagship 30-day bundles of Vodacom and Econet. Vodacom charged M660 for 20 GB and Econet M650. Per gigabyte, the smallest bundle costs 24% more than the largest. The site has tracked prices since 13 October 2023.

2026-11-06-mar-morocco-korea-advance-cus.summary: Morocco World News reported on 6 November 2026 that Moroccan customs (ADII) and the Korea Customs Service have entered the final phase of a joint project. It began in May 2026 and is run by the Korean firm Okestro. It covers big data and AI for revenue management and digital governance, according to an ADII statement.

2026-11-06-mauritius-telecom-launches-fr.summary: Mauritius Telecom and AWS launched the myt Learning Hub, a free online portal for digital and AI skills, reported on 6 November 2026. It opens with 16 courses. It forms part of the government's target to train 50,000 Mauritians.

2026-11-06-moz-mozambique-new-e-auction-.summary: Mozambique's Asset Management Office launched an e-auction platform for assets seized from crime, Finance Minister Carla Loveira said at a Maputo seminar reported on 6 November 2026. The first auction offers 14 seized vehicles at starting prices of 70% of appraised value. The platform also has an asset-management module, a business-intelligence tool and a public monitoring portal.

2026-11-06-moz-study-projects-us-324m-bo.summary: The 2026 Ayre Index, reported on 6 November 2026, ranks Mozambique 44th of 56 Commonwealth countries on youth readiness for AI. It scores 38.9 out of 100 against a threshold of 53. The study projects AI could add US$324 million to GDP over ten years. It cites electricity access of 36.9% and internet use of 35% among young people.

2026-11-06-mrt-telecommunications-l-auto.summary: Mauritania's regulator ARE fined Mauritel, Mattel and Chinguitel a combined MRU 421,259,757 on 5 November 2026 for poor voice and data service quality. Each fine is 3% of turnover: Mauritel MRU 262.1 million, Mattel 108.8 million and Chinguitel 50.4 million. ARE also ordered a technical and financial network audit and a permanent performance-monitoring platform.

2026-11-06-mus-mauritius-explores-digita.summary: Mauritius's Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation held a workshop on digital public infrastructure with the Centre for Open Societal Systems of India. It took place at the Mauritius Telecom campus in Ebène and was reported on 6 November 2026. Minister Avinash Ramtohul said the proposed infrastructure would include digital identity, a digital wallet and electronic payments. He said citizens' information is held across separate government institutions.

2026-11-06-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet agreed on 6 November 2026 that the ICT ministry will sign a cybercrime memorandum with India's Ministry of Home Affairs. It covers removal of unlawful content, legal cooperation, operational support and threats to critical information infrastructure. Cabinet also approved an Indian memorandum on a cell-broadcast disaster early-warning system, to be deployed by C-DOT.

2026-11-06-mwi-airtel-malawi-invests-mwk.summary: Airtel Malawi told Parliament's communications committee on 3 November 2026 that it had invested nearly MWK81 billion in the network over ten months. It reported 275 new towers in twelve months, 5G on 123 towers, about 2,800 km of fibre and 87% population coverage (company figures). It named foreign-exchange shortages and diesel for 315 off-grid sites as constraints.

2026-11-06-nam-namibian-cybersecurity-ri.summary: Namibia's NAM-CSIRT, housed at the regulator CRAN, recorded 506,143 vulnerabilities and 163,053 cyber events in July to September 2026, according to its newsletter reported on 6 November 2026. Vulnerabilities fell about 1.5% from 513,921 in the second quarter. Events rose 0.93% from 161,547. Exposed Open CWMP services were the most detected, at 320,664.

2026-11-06-nigeria-data-protection-commi.summary: Vincent Olatunji, head of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, opened the 8th Data Protection Africa Summit in Lagos on 6 November 2026. He urged data protection authorities to form public-private partnerships. He said the approach had helped the Commission create more than 27,000 jobs and raise certified data protection officers from under 1,000 to over 10,000 (his figures).

2026-11-06-nigeria-is-rewriting-its-cybe.summary: TechCabal reported on 6 November 2026 that Nigeria is reviewing its cybersecurity laws. It is considering a national cybersecurity architecture with baseline standards. It says the Cybercrimes Act of 2015 was amended in February 2024 and the 2021 national strategy is due for review. A House committee chair gave January to June 2027 as the expected enactment window for the bills.

2026-11-06-rdc-deux-chantiers-numeriques.summary: The Congolese justice ministry launched a programme in Kinshasa on 5 November 2026, with UNDP technical support. It will digitise court revenue collection and link courts, prosecutors' offices and prisons. The report adds that a Cour des comptes report of May 2024 found USD 8.8 million of anomalies in a Kinshasa sample for 2021 and 2022. It also cites UNDP's June 2026 statement that USD 53.9 million was being mobilised for the 2025 to 2029 joint justice programme.
