2026-11-06-rwa-miss-baza-when-rwanda-fou.summary: James Kaliisa, co-founder and chief technology officer of the Rwandan firm Nexus Inc., wrote in KT Press on 6 November 2026 about MTN Rwanda's Miss Baza voice assistant. It is run with Viamo on short code 845. He asks who owns the Google Gemini model, the intellectual property and the call data behind it. The service gives 30 free minutes a month, then RWF 45 a minute.

2026-11-06-sdn-suna-digital-transformati.summary: Sudan's Digital Transformation Authority told the UN Governance Innovation Summit in Baku on 6 November 2026 that the Baladna platform carries 134 digital services from more than 46 government institutions (SUNA). It described a services-first, legislation-second approach. It presented digital transformation as part of post-war reconstruction.

2026-11-06-sdn-supporting-sudan-s-bankin.summary: Dr Marwa Qabbani, a strategic planning and digital transformation specialist, wrote in Sudan Horizon on 6 November 2026 about a Central Bank of Sudan meeting chaired by Sovereignty Council member Ibrahim Jaber. She lists its outcomes as the National Payments Switch, banking applications, links to the Baladna platform and stronger bank capital by the end of 2026. She argues that the government should support the banks with a rebuilding fund. The meeting is undated in the article.

2026-11-06-sen-cloud-le-s-n-gal-envisage.summary: Senegal's digital minister Samba Diouf met an Alibaba Cloud delegation on 3 November 2026. They discussed reusing the cloud built for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games for public administration. No new agreement or investment was announced. Alibaba says more than 10,000 Senegalese under 35 had enrolled in its free online training by 2 November. The target was 1,000 (La Tribune Afrique, 6 November 2026).

2026-11-06-sen-recrutement-d-un-cabinet-.summary: Senegal's telecoms and digital ministry published a notice on 6 November 2026 recruiting a firm to evaluate Year 1 of the New Deal Technologique, covering February 2025 to the first half of 2026. The Council of Ministers ordered the evaluation on 17 June 2026. The two-month mission is financed by World Bank IDA credit 72690 through the PAENS project. It is to report on results by axis and on the financing gap.

2026-11-06-senum-and-univers-telecom-gro.summary: Senegal's state digital company SENUM signed a partnership agreement with Univers Telecom Group, reported on 6 November 2026. The stated aims are a more resilient state digital infrastructure and the digitisation of the administration. The work is already under way through the PRODAP programme on the national backbone.

2026-11-06-sle-communication-minister-ex.summary: Sierra Leone's National Investment Board showed its new Online Business Registration System to Communication Minister Salima Bah, SierraLoaded reported on 6 November 2026. Applicants can reserve a name, upload identification and download certificates online. The Board is working with the National Civil Registration Authority to bring the National Identification Number into registration.

2026-11-06-sle-information-minister-tabl.summary: Sierra Leone's Minister of Information tabled two bills in Parliament, SierraLoaded reported on 6 November 2026. They are the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2026 and the National Records and Archives Bill, 2026. Both have completed Introduction and First Reading and go next to Second Reading.

2026-11-06-som-simad-university-breaks-g.summary: SIMAD University laid the foundation stone on 5 November 2026 for a building to host Somalia's National AI Hub. The hub links four universities; the minister of communications and technology laid the stone with the rector, Dawan Africa reports. Hadiid Group is building the ground-plus-five steel structure.

2026-11-06-ssd-juba-high-court-summons-m.summary: The High Court in Juba summoned MTN South Sudan to answer Petition No. 455/2026 on 18 November 2026, The Dawn reported on 6 November. The subscriber petition concerns deleted unused data bundles and network outages. It also concerns an alleged SSP 10 billion held in MTN Mobile Money.

2026-11-06-stp-mnecc-launches-sydoc-docu.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's foreign ministry launched SYDOC, an electronic document-management system built by the Agência de Gestão e Administração. It also launched SYDOC-PASS for diplomatic and service passport requests (ministry release, 6 November 2026). The minister said a digital-signature legal framework, digital identity and a Citizen Portal are still to come.

2026-11-06-swz-eswatini-risks-missing-e1.summary: The Ayre Index, launched at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting and reported on 6 November 2026, ranks Eswatini 52nd of 56 countries. It scores 36.9 out of 100 against a benchmark of 53. The study puts the AI opportunity at about E1.23 billion over a decade. It records youth unemployment of 52.6%, the highest of the 56.

2026-11-06-swz-home-affairs-goes-digital.summary: Eswatini's Home Affairs Minister Pholile Shakantu told the portfolio committee that passport applications are moving online. She said eVisa issuance and scanning at points of entry are ready (Eswatini Positive News, 6 November 2026). She cited lower costs and shorter queues under budget constraints.

2026-11-06-tun-passeport-carte-didentite.summary: Business News reported on 6 November 2026 that Communication Technologies Minister Sofiene Hemissi promised remote administrative services before the end of the year. Citizens would be able to apply for passports, renew identity cards and driving licences, and pay municipal and personal taxes online. He spoke at a parliamentary hearing on his ministry's 2027 budget. The same hearing is covered in the Tunisian AI projects item.

2026-11-06-tun-tunisie-six-projets-gouve.summary: Tunisia's ICT minister told parliament on 6 November 2026 that his ministry plans six AI-based government projects in 2027, against two in 2026. It aims to move from tier 3 in 2024 to tier 2 of the Global Cybersecurity Index by 2027. He presented a 2027 mission budget of about TND 1.074 billion, 80% from supervised enterprises' own resources. He promised remote ID-card, passport and driving-licence requests before the end of 2026.

2026-11-06-tza-digital-transformation-cu.summary: Tanzania's National Health Insurance Fund cut its average claims settlement time from 120 to 50 days in FY2024/25, according to its briefing of 6 November 2026. It credits digitised claims processing and AI. It reports paper claim forms down 75% and card costs down 80%, with systems linked to NIDA and RITA.

2026-11-06-tza-enabel-tender-womens-digi.summary: Enabel published tender TZA25001-10032 on 6 November 2026 for technical assistance on gender-disaggregated data on women's entrepreneurship and digitalisation. The work includes a women's digital entrepreneurship barometer methodology for Tanzania and Uganda, under a 730-day contract. Bids close on 27 November 2026 at 16:00 East Africa Time.

2026-11-06-tza-m-mama-emergency-referral.summary: Tech Africa News reported on 6 November 2026 on Tanzania's M-Mama emergency referral platform, which the African Union Commission has cited as an example. It gives a cost of USD 170.40 per referral with community drivers. State ambulances alone cost USD 472, from a PLOS Global Public Health study of a pilot in Shinyanga. Drivers are paid by mobile money once delivery is verified.

2026-11-06-tza-tanzanias-smallholder-far.summary: Smallholders in Dodoma region told Al Jazeera on 6 November 2026 that they have not registered for, or get late answers from, the agriculture ministry's M-Kilimo and e-Kilimo services. A 2024 study counted about 7.2 million registered M-Kilimo farmers and some 400,000 incomplete registrations. The ministry did not respond.

2026-11-06-uganda-considers-tracking-chi.summary: Nyombi Thembo, executive director of the Uganda Communications Commission, said at a hackathon in Nakawa that the regulator is considering requiring parents to disclose SIM numbers used by minors (ITWeb Africa, 6 November 2026). Operators could then keep dedicated databases of child-held devices. The commission cites an undated survey in which 88.5% of students face digital risks.

2026-11-06-wayawaya-partners-choice-bank.summary: Kenyan fintech WayaWaya announced a partnership with Choice Bank on 6 November 2026 to offer AI-personalised banking. The microfinance bank provides the regulated accounts, multi-currency holding and transfers. WayaWaya's AI reads customers' transaction patterns to shape the interface.

2026-11-06-xaf-digital-earth-africa-docs.summary: Digital Earth Africa's own documentation, retrieved on 6 November 2026, lists ten continental services, from Cropland Extent to Water Quality, plus external datasets. The page is undated and matches the programme's Annual Report 2024 count of ten. An AWS blog post of 19 August 2026 counted seven.

2026-11-06-xaf-koalition-will-deutsche-k.summary: Germany's CDU/CSU-SPD coalition put a motion to the Bundestag asking the government to back African-owned data centres and digital infrastructure (Fokus Afrika, 6 November 2026). It also asks that digital development funding go preferentially to German, European or local firms. The motion was first debated on 5 November and referred to committee. It has not been adopted.

2026-11-06-xna-escwa-arab-region-advance.summary: The UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia held the sixth session of its Committee on Technology for Development in Tunis on 4 and 5 November 2026. It reported that networks cover 95% of the Arab region's population while 70% use the internet. Arabic accounts for about 1% of websites. The session discussed a second Arab Digital Agenda and a common Arab AI framework with the League of Arab States, both in preparation.

2026-11-06-zaf-ayre-index-commonwealth-y.summary: ITWeb reported on 6 November 2026 that South Africa ranks 13th of 56 Commonwealth countries, with 56.8 points. The ranking is in the inaugural Ayre Index of youth AI readiness from the Ayre Think Tank. South Africa is second among African members after Mauritius, which ranks eighth. In the index's evidence, 88.2% of young South Africans expected to use AI for education or work in the next year.

2026-11-06-zaf-lekkeslaap-booking-data-b.summary: South African booking platform LekkeSlaap told guests on 6 November 2026 that their names, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and booking references were accessed through its calendar-syncing system. It says no payment data, ID numbers or passwords were taken and warns of phishing. The notice follows a separate breach at accommodation-technology provider NightsBridge days earlier.

2026-11-06-zmb-zambia-govt-seeks-tangibl.summary: At a farewell meeting with Zambia's Ministry of Technology and Science in Lusaka, reported on 6 November 2026, a German business delegation named an AI software platform as its key project. It would be built through joint ventures with Zambian companies. The delegation said it had trained 50 Zambians in AI development and would open a permanent contact office.

2026-11-06-zmb-zambia-plans-10-million-m.summary: Zambia's Technology and Science Minister Felix Mutati set a target of 10 million additional smartphones over five years, towards broadband access for 80% of the population. He spoke at a meeting with Airtel Zambia on 5 November 2026. Airtel cited ZICTA figures of 12.4 million smartphone connections out of about 27 million (reported 6 November 2026).

2026-11-06-zmb-znphi-and-cidrz-validate-.summary: Zambia's National Public Health Institute and CIDRZ validated a One Health Digital Landscape Assessment covering ten public institutions, reported on 6 November 2026. It found a strong but fragmented digital landscape, with gaps in governance, cross-sector data sharing and interoperability. The work was funded by Ireland under the ZISSP programme.

2026-11-06-zwe-home-affairs-minister-adm.summary: Zimbabwe's Home Affairs Minister Kazembe Kazembe told the National Assembly that the Smart Traffic Management System makes errors when it captures vehicle registration details, NewZimbabwe reported on 6 November 2026. He accepted motorists' complaints of misidentification and a lapse in police validation before tickets are issued. The number-plate system runs at 20 sites in Harare.

2026-11-06-zwe-three-year-free-internet-.summary: ITU's Bureau for Telecommunication Development director Cosmas Zavazava said ten Zimbabwean schools connected by satellite will get free internet for three years (reported 6 November 2026). The schools are in ITU's Partner2Connect programme with SES. Nine are connected and the last is due online by 10 November.

2026-11-07-ben-terra-benin-ppmec-ii-secu.summary: Benin's land agency ANDF launched the TERRA BÉNIN and PPMEC II programmes in Cotonou on 6 November 2026, Fraternité reported. They extend the national cadastre, which holds 643,993 registered parcels in 12 communes. TERRA BÉNIN's first phase (2025-2030) has USD 100 million from the World Bank and targets 1.5 million parcels in 14 communes. PPMEC II (2026-2031) has EUR 20 million from the Netherlands. It covers six more communes and the e-Foncier Bénin platform.

2026-11-07-cmr-missole-les-etats-unis-se.summary: The Port Autonome de Douala plans a two-hectare modular data centre, built for AI and with its own power plant, at its Dibamba industrial-port zone. It was shown to US chargé d'affaires John G. Robinson on a visit reported on 7 November 2026. The port says the site would keep hosted data under Cameroonian sovereignty. It names no builder, financier or timeline.

2026-11-07-egy-cairo-ict-2026-fra-chairm.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority reported over 1.727 million e-KYC verifications in non-bank finance by late October 2026, against 354,000 at the end of 2025. It put registered digital contracts at 862,000, against 190,000. Presenting at Cairo ICT 2026 on 7 November 2026, it said its sandbox had taken 67 applications and moved two to live testing.

2026-11-07-egy-fintechgate-fra-ekyc-1-7-.summary: Fintechgate reported on 7 November 2026 that the head of Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority, Islam Azzam, cited over 1.727 million e-KYC verifications and about 862,000 digital contracts by the end of October 2026. The figures compare with 354,000 verifications and 190,000 contracts at the end of 2025. He spoke at Cairo ICT 2026.

2026-11-07-egy-wazir-al-ittisalat-al-siy.summary: Egypt's ICT minister, Raafat Hindy, called digital sovereignty a main state priority at Cairo ICT on 7 November 2026, Youm7 reported. He said artificial intelligence had extended sovereignty from networks to data centres and control of data. He also named less reliance on outside parties for critical technology. Diversified technology supply chains were his third aim.

2026-11-07-egy-youm7-cairo-ict-ministers.summary: Youm7 reported on 7 November 2026 from the opening session of Cairo ICT 2026. The ICT minister, Raafat Hindy, said the ministry is working with the electricity ministry to supply up to 1 GW of power at designated data-centre sites. Several ministers set out their digital transformation and artificial intelligence plans at the session.

2026-11-07-egy-youm7-ict-minister-hindy-.summary: Youm7 published an interview on 7 November 2026 with Egypt's ICT minister, Raafat Hindy. The minister said the sector grew 24.5 per cent and aims for 8 per cent of GDP by 2030. The minister also described a plan for seven hyperscale data centres and a target of 400 national e-services.

2026-11-07-gab-gabon-agriculture-agri-tr.summary: Gabon's agriculture and digital-economy ministries signed a cooperation protocol on 3 November 2026 to deploy AGRI-TRACK 241, a platform for agricultural data. AGP reported it on 7 November 2026. Its first module, SYSTEP, will support 150 poultry farms, starting with a cohort of 79. This is ahead of a halt to broiler imports set for 1 January 2027.

2026-11-07-gha-eight-in-10-ghanaian-adul.summary: Ghana's Ministry of Finance opened work on a 2027–2031 financial inclusion strategy on 5 November 2026, 3News reported. Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem cited 81% account ownership in 2024, from the Global Findex. The 2021 FinScope survey found 22% of adults financially healthy. The ministry expects to launch the strategy in the first half of 2027.

2026-11-07-gha-mahama-queen-maxima-discu.summary: President John Mahama disclosed plans for a digital wallet linked to Ghana's national identification system on 5 November 2026, MyJoyOnline reported. He spoke at a meeting in Accra with Queen Máxima, the UN Secretary-General's Special Advocate for Financial Health. He also described a planned upgrade of rural telecoms from 2G to 4G. He gave no timeline, operator or cost.

2026-11-07-gha-travelling-to-ghana-new-m.summary: Ghana will require every arriving traveller to file an online Mandatory Health Declaration Form from 12 November 2026, Graphic Online reported on 7 November. Travellers must complete it on the Ghana Health Service portal before embarking, for public-health surveillance. The announcement says nothing on how the data are kept, shared or protected.

2026-11-07-ken-redtech-plans-a-kenya-nig.summary: Redtech, a Nigerian payments company, plans a payments link between Nigeria and Kenya, its chief executive Emmanuel Ojo told Techweez in a report of 7 November 2026. A Kenyan launch is planned by the first quarter of 2027, through partners. Ojo says some African markets settle within 24 hours while others take three or four days.

2026-11-07-mus-pas-de-censure-des-reseau.summary: Mauritius's ICT ministry and regulator ICTA launched a three-month campaign on social-media use on 6 November 2026, L'Express reported. Amendments to the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 have gone to the State Law Office, the ministry said. New regulations are being prepared under the ICT Act. CERT-MU recorded 5,754 incident reports between 1 January and 5 November 2026.

2026-11-07-sdn-pakistan-sudan-to-strengt.summary: Pakistan and Sudan agreed to widen cooperation on security, cybercrime, police training and civil registration after interior ministers met in Islamabad, The News reported on 7 November 2026. They agreed in principle to sign a cybercrime memorandum. Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said Nadra support had helped Sudan issue 36 million citizenship cards and nine million national identity cards.

2026-11-07-tgo-conseil-des-ministres-du-.summary: Togo's Council of Ministers met on 6 November 2026 and authorised submission for adoption of a national postal-sector policy for 2026-2029. Its five orientations include digital transformation, digital financial services and e-commerce. The council also took a first reading of a bill amending the 2018 land and property code to digitalise land management and create a national land observatory.

2026-11-07-tgo-vladimir-poutine-conseill.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin urged African countries to join the A7 cross-border payment network in October 2026, Togo-Presse reported on 7 November. He spoke at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow and called A7 impossible to block. Finance Minister Anton Siluanov put its fee at 0.3%. The paper says A7 opened offices in Nigeria and Zimbabwe in 2025.

2026-11-07-tun-terres-domaniales-11-000-.summary: Tunisia's minister of state domains, Wajdi Hedhili, briefed a joint parliamentary committee on 6 November 2026. Hedhili said 24 state farmland plots, over 11,000 hectares, have been given to community companies. 3,000 hectares are reserved for renewable energy projects, and a second list of plots is in preparation. State farmland totals 500,000 hectares, 38% of it leased.

2026-11-07-zaf-mk-party-wants-ethekwini-.summary: South Africa's MK Party lodged a formal objection with the Electoral Commission on 6 November 2026, The Citizen reported. It alleges a failure in live results capture at the eThekwini Results Operations Centre. Leaderboard figures, it says, differ from party-signed results slips. The party wants affected voting districts quarantined and an independent forensic audit of the results backend.

2026-11-08-algeria-council-ministers-min.summary: At the Council of Ministers on 8 November 2026, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune told ministers to load their statistics onto a national digital platform. The platform belongs to the High Commission for Digitization. The meeting also ordered a statistics department for agriculture.

2026-11-08-ben-justice-au-benin-les-etat.summary: Benin's justice ministry received equipment worth $2.3 million funded by the United States in Cotonou on 6 November 2026. The equipment is meant to modernise courts in the north of the country. Minister Yvon Détchénou said the criminal record certificate has been available online in three clicks since 1 November and that all jurisdictions are connected to the internet.

2026-11-08-civ-cote-divoire-32-entrepris.summary: Côte d'Ivoire has picked 32 digital companies for 24 months of support, Minister of Digital Transition Djibril Ouattara announced on 4 November 2026. They come under the Ivoire Tech Next 15 and Ivoire Tech Scale Up programmes. More than 150 firms applied. The government aims to raise 5 to 10 billion FCFA from banks, funds and donors.

2026-11-08-congo-ins-mtn-digitalise-nati.summary: Congo's statistics institute and MTN Congo agreed to form a joint working group, La Breve Online reported on 8 November 2026. The group is to diagnose the institute's digitalisation needs and draft a roadmap for a memorandum. Its scope includes SIM-based field collection, data-centre hosting and SMS dissemination, under SDMX standards.

2026-11-08-dza-asharq-bloomberg-ouadah-w.summary: Algeria is in advanced talks with the World Bank on a start-up financing initiative, minister Noureddine Ouadah told Asharq Bloomberg on 8 November 2026. Launch is planned at the African Start-up Conference in Algiers on 5–7 December. Some Algerian start-ups are to raise over US$10m each. The minister said a 2026 research levy now has implementing texts: 1% of profits for firms with revenue above DZD 2bn.

2026-11-08-egy-council-of-state-expands-.summary: Mahmoud Ibrahim Abu al-Dahab, president of Egypt's Council of State, said on 8 November 2026 that the electronic litigation pilot is widening. It will now cover the administrative court for education and its annexes, and the disciplinary court for health. The announcement came during a session of the administrative judiciary court's ninth circuit.

2026-11-08-egy-eg-darwish-egypt-needs-a-.summary: Ahmed Darwish, a former Egyptian Minister of State for Administrative Development, said on 8 November 2026 that Egypt needs a law on data disclosure and circulation. He said it should set which information can be obtained from government bodies and how it may be reused. He saw no need for a criminal law specific to artificial intelligence.

2026-11-08-egy-telecom-egypt-e-finance-m.summary: Telecom Egypt and e-finance signed a memorandum at Cairo ICT 2026, held from 7 to 10 November. It covers joint telecoms, cloud and digital services for government and companies. At the same event, 20 cybersecurity and AI startups graduated from Telecom Egypt's WE Innovate Star programme. The programme is run with the telecoms regulator's EG-CERT.

2026-11-08-eth-digital-sovereignty-prior.summary: Ethiopia aims to host its national data on its own infrastructure, State Minister Solomon Soka said on 8 November 2026. He put that data at about 600 petabytes by 2030, under the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy. He also called for African-owned data centres and cloud. He spoke at the Second African Political Parties Summit in Addis Ababa.

2026-11-08-ethiopia-farmers-profile-regi.summary: Ethiopia's Agricultural Transformation Institute has enrolled nearly one million farmers in its Fayda-linked profile register, Capital reported on 8 November 2026. It targets four million by 2028, out of about 20 million farmers. Data is shared with lenders only with the farmer's consent.

2026-11-08-gha-afenyo-markin-calls-for-r.summary: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin called for repeal of Section 208 of Ghana's Criminal Offences Act on 7 November 2026, GNA reported. The section covers false news likely to cause alarm. The Minority is also weighing repeal of Section 76 of the Electronic Communications Act. The Minority Leader said defamation should be handled through civil action.

2026-11-08-gha-traffitech-gh-protect-mot.summary: Security analyst Richard Kumadoe warned on Channel One TV on 7 November 2026 that data from Ghana's TraffiTech-GH traffic cameras could expose motorists to privacy breaches if criminals obtained it. He said the data includes motorists' movements and facial identities, and that it must be protected. The warning is his opinion, not a report of a breach.

2026-11-08-ken-sh500m-fines-parental-con.summary: The Daily Nation reported on 8 November 2026 that Embakasi West MP Mark Mwenje tabled the Online Safety Bill, 2026 in the National Assembly. The bill requires parental consent for under-18s and age verification on regulated services. Fines reach KES 500 million or 10 per cent of turnover.

2026-11-08-lbr-lra-commissioner-general-.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority showed a public revenue dashboard and an AI virtual taxpayer assistant, Fatu, at the African Tax Administration Forum meetings in Cairo, reported on 8 November 2026. The dashboard gives monthly collections by revenue category and tax type. Commissioner General James Dorbor Jallah said collections rose from US$612 million in 2023 to US$848 million in 2025.

2026-11-08-lby-lana-369567-labour-minist.summary: Libya's Ministry of Labour and Rehabilitation said on 8 November 2026 that its digital platform is ready for web use, with iOS and Android versions to follow. The minister ordered staff data registration to be completed so that the platform's unified database can go live. The implementer is Nasr Global IT.

2026-11-08-mli-aes-frequences-militaires.summary: Maliweb reported on 8 November 2026 that Bamako hosted the second coordination meeting on military frequencies at the borders of the Alliance of Sahel States, to 4 November. Mali's telecoms regulator AMRTP organised it, with delegations from Burkina Faso and Niger. Mali's deputy defence minister, General Oumar Diarra, chaired the opening.

2026-11-08-nga-nigeria-s-internet-capaci.summary: The link between Digital Realty's Medallion data centre and Equinix in Lagos has reached 1 terabit per second. Medallion's link to Rack Centre runs at 500 gigabits per second. Muhammed Rudman, head of the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria, gave the figures at its 20th anniversary event. BusinessDay reported them on 8 November 2026.

2026-11-08-rwa-raia-agentic-ai-poc.summary: The Rwanda AI Agency invited bids for agentic-AI proofs of concept on three government platforms, as reported on 8 November 2026. They are Mbaza for complaints, IremboAI for licensing and Kubaka for building permits. The World Bank finances the work, due to start in late March 2027.

2026-11-08-tun-paiement-mobile-ouverts-d.summary: African Manager analysed the Central Bank of Tunisia's 2025 banking supervision report on 8 November 2026. At end-2025 payment institutions held 113,739 accounts, 44% more than a year earlier. Only 12,843 (11.3%) were active, against 23,830 at end-2024. Transactions rose from 1,632m to 3,775m dinars, about 60% of it inflows from abroad.

2026-11-08-zaf-technology-streamlines-20.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission used 56,000 voter management devices in the 2026 Local Government Elections, Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said on 8 November 2026. That is 16,000 more than its 2021 fleet. Of the new devices, 8,000 were bought and 8,000 donated by Gauteng. The results API took 14.3 million requests. 1,149 users joined the new Virtual Results Operating Centre.

2026-11-08-zmb-zambia-efisp-digital-farm.summary: A University of Zambia study, reported on 8 November 2026, examined the electronic Farmer Input Support Programme in Chongwe District. In the study, 81% of farmers reported timely fertiliser access and 78% saw more transparent allocation. It also found late activation, identity mismatches and slow payments to agro-dealers.

2026-11-09-administration-numerique-djib.summary: Djibouti's Ministry of Labour signed an MoU with Azerbaijan's ASAN Service in Baku on 5 November 2026 on sharing expertise in digitalising public services on ASAN's one-stop-centre model. It follows a September 2025 study visit and an October 2025 inventory in which Djibouti listed 503 administrative procedures. Of these, 83 were prioritised for first-phase digitalisation.

2026-11-09-algeria-ensia-ai-data-centre-.summary: Algeria's higher-education minister, Kamel Baddari, met a Chinese delegation on 9 November 2026 about an AI data centre. The centre would sit at the National Higher School of Artificial Intelligence in Sidi Abdellah. The statement names no Chinese firm, cost or completion date.

2026-11-09-ben-les-nouveaux-membres-de-l.summary: The eight members of Benin's data protection authority (APDP) took their oath before the Supreme Court on 6 November 2026. The swearing-in opens the authority's fourth term. The members then re-elected Luciano Hounkponou as president unanimously.

2026-11-09-ben-numerique-dans-les-mairie.summary: Benin's association of communes, ANCB, counted 35 software applications from 27 providers across 13 functional areas in municipal administrations. Its digital commission reported this at a session in Dassa-Zoumè on 5 and 6 November 2026, citing interconnection failures, duplication and maintenance costs. It weighed the integrated communal software package PIAC as the remedy.

2026-11-09-benin-higher-education-ai-ins.summary: Benin's higher education minister, Sèdami Medegan Fagla, said Benin plans an AI Institute for Higher Education by 2027. She spoke at the rectors' conference in Cotonou on 5-6 November 2026. The institute is to offer dual degrees with partner universities.

2026-11-09-bfa-burkina-faso-semaine-du-n.summary: The organising committee announced at a press conference in Ouagadougou on 9 November 2026 that the 21st Semaine du numérique will run from 24 to 27 November 2026 at the SIAO site. The theme is technological sovereignty and secure, inclusive digital transformation. The programme includes conferences, a start-up village, robot demonstrations, the RoboKids competition and free ICT training.

2026-11-09-bfa-intelligence-artificielle.summary: A panel at the second Le Faso Digital in Burkina Faso, reported on 9 November 2026, discussed whether AI can handle Mooré, Dioula and Fulfuldé. The speakers said translation, transcription and voice tools exist but remain approximate. They named the shortage of digitised data, spelling harmonisation, and the need for computer scientists, linguists and public authorities to work together.

2026-11-09-civ-cote-d-ivoire-ce-que-la-n.summary: The economic and finance committee of Côte d'Ivoire's National Assembly unanimously adopted the banking regulation bill on 4 November 2026. The bill transposes the UMOA uniform banking law of 16 June 2023 and places fintechs, payment institutions and electronic-money issuers in one framework with banks. It also admits Islamic finance and adds an early-intervention mechanism. The bill still has to complete its passage before promulgation.

2026-11-09-cod-lancement-du-recensement-.summary: Maniema province in the DRC began a digitalised census of plots in Kindu on 9 November 2026, Radio Okapi reported. The firm THE WIN is building a provincial taxpayer file for land, rental-income and vehicle taxes. Payments are due to start in January 2027.

2026-11-09-cod-wacs-cable-repairs-enter-.summary: Congo Telecom said a repair vessel was due on 11 November 2026 at the WACS fault between the two Congos. A disruption on 29 October cut its primary circuits. The operator said failover to backup links kept customers connected. It listed earlier WACS outages in 2020, August 2023 and January 2026.

2026-11-09-dza-iso-member-ianor.summary: The ISO membership page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists the Institut Algérien de Normalisation as a member body. It sets out the institute's tasks, including national standards development, the WTO TBT information point and the Algerian conformity mark. It shows participation in 27 technical committees and observer status in 50.

2026-11-09-econet-burundi-invests-6-5-mi.summary: Econet Wireless Burundi broke ground in Bujumbura on 5 November 2026 on solar power for its network. The USD 2.5 million first phase of a USD 6.5 million programme covers about a third of its sites by July 2027. GEFI Solutions SEZ arranged the financing under a CRDB Bank guarantee. The company targets renewable power across the network by December 2028.

2026-11-09-egy-22-electronic-notarial-an.summary: Vetogate reported on 9 November 2026 that Egypt's Digital Egypt platform offers about 22 notarial and real estate registry services. Of these, 16 are notarisation services and 6 are real estate registry services, including official powers of attorney and declarations. The Ministry of Justice is expanding the mechanisation of these transactions to cut crowding at notary offices.

2026-11-09-equatorial-guinea-sigef-biome.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Treasury presented the SIGEF civil-servant management system on 9 November 2026. Built with Morocco's M2M, it rests on a single biometric register of state employees. A multiservice identity card can also carry payroll payment, to help control the wage bill.

2026-11-09-eth-techafricanews-gdp-rebase.summary: Ethiopia's rebased national accounts put 2024/25 GDP at 24.03 trillion birr, against 15.09 trillion under the previous series, Tech Africa News reported on 9 November 2026. The reference year moved from 2015/16 to 2024/25 with IMF technical assistance, and digital financial services and ride-hailing platforms entered the count. Preliminary 2025/26 GDP is 31.86 trillion birr.

2026-11-09-ethiopia-eaii-ai-hub-2030-med.summary: Ethiopia's AI Institute opened a residency for 51 AI start-up founders from 12 African countries on 9 November 2026, ENA reported. Its director general set a goal of a leading African AI hub by 2030. Japan's ambassador put Japanese support for the Addis Ababa AI UniPod at about US$1m a year.

2026-11-09-gabon-huawei-three-accords-ga.summary: Gabon Infos reported on 9 November 2026 three memoranda between the Gabonese state and Huawei, signed in Shanghai. They cover fibre, Wi-Fi 6 and 5G for public universities, and AI training centres. The security accord covers smart urban surveillance, border-zone systems and linked security infrastructure.

2026-11-09-gha-techafricanews-ghana-us-d.summary: Ghana's Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, met a US Embassy delegation led by incoming Ambassador Faris Asad, reported on 9 November 2026. They discussed investment in data centres and cloud infrastructure through Amazon Web Services, cybersecurity and skills. The report records no commitment.

2026-11-09-gmb-ministry-updates-public-o.summary: The Gambia's lands ministry briefed the press on National Land Policy implementation on 9 November 2026. Dr Samba Sowe heads the Land Policy Implementation Unit. Sowe said work began in January 2026, after President Adama Barrow launched the policy in December 2025. The alpha version of a National Land Information System is complete and in testing. A contractor is setting up a centre to digitise historical land records.

2026-11-09-gnq-camara-aprueba-ley-impren.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Chamber of Deputies unanimously passed a digital communication bill and a copyright bill on 9 November 2026. The government says the first sets obligations for digital platforms and protects minors online. The second covers computer programs and databases and creates a collective-management body.

2026-11-09-govstack-built-to-evolve-what.summary: GovStack published an account on 9 November 2026 of HUSIKA, a platform that passes climate and early-warning information from producing institutions to media, authorities and communities. It lists active deployments in 11 countries, across web, SMS and Telegram. South Sudan's Meteorological Service used it in a journalist training and an official said it replaced door-to-door printed posters.

2026-11-09-gsma-innovation-fund-for-ai-e.summary: The GSMA launched an Innovation Fund for AI-Enabled Financial Health on 9 November 2026, funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. It offers grants of GBP 100,000 to 250,000 to small and growing enterprises in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia. Applications close on 17 December 2026.

2026-11-09-ipris-tenth-cohort.summary: The iPRIS project opened its tenth cohort in Sweden on 9 November 2026, for regulators from six African countries. In three years it has involved 34 African countries and 56 country-led change initiatives. Five lusophone countries are due to join in February 2027.

2026-11-09-ken-how-kenya-s-digital-birth.summary: Immigration PS Belio Kipsang told Kenyan MPs that birth and death certificate fees will be waived by Gazette notice, the Daily Nation reported on 9 November 2026. Within 30 days, civil registration is to link to the hospital system. Every newborn would then get a Unique Personal Identifier. Electronic birth notification is piloted in Nairobi and Bomet and is due to reach over 7,500 public hospitals.

2026-11-09-lbr-liberia-regains-atu-votin.summary: Liberia has regained its voting rights in the African Telecommunications Union, the telecoms regulator's chair Clarence K. Massaquoi said on 9 November 2026. A waiver of more than US$400,000 and a government payment of the balance ended its observer status. He gave neither the amount paid nor the date the rights were restored.

2026-11-09-mar-moroccans-abroad-can-now-.summary: Morocco's General Directorate of National Security opened its Epolice portal on 9 November 2026 to Moroccans abroad applying online for criminal-record certificates. Each request can be tracked online and the certificate is collected at the chosen diplomatic mission. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccan Expatriates built the service with the directorate.

2026-11-09-mdg-cybercriminalite-les-etat.summary: Madagascar and the United States signed a judicial cooperation agreement against cybercrime on 6 November 2026 in Washington. Madagascar's justice minister signed with Jeanine Pirro, US prosecutor for the District of Columbia. Pirro heads the Scam Center Strike Force. A US Justice Department report credited FBI cooperation with dismantling 13 scam centres in Madagascar.

2026-11-09-mdg-madagascar-lapmf-lance-un.summary: Madagascar's port and maritime agency, APMF, launched the second phase of INTEGRATE-Madagascar on 9 November 2026. Indonesia is giving technical assistance to set up a Maritime Single Window under the IMO FAL Convention. Experts from both countries are to draft a roadmap by 17 November.

2026-11-09-mli-modernisation-de-la-justi.summary: Mali's Justice Minister, Mamoudou Kassogué, said on 5 November 2026 that an e-justice platform is going into operation. Its first services are digital criminal-record extracts and nationality certificates. UNDP handed over equipment and penal codes worth USD 493,193 under its Netherlands-supported PROSMED programme.

2026-11-09-moz-mocambique-e-portugal-ref.summary: Mozambique's parliament and Portugal's parliament signed a cooperation memorandum in Maputo on 9 November 2026. It adds artificial intelligence, archive management and digital system resilience to their exchanges. Delegation visits, committee exchanges and staff training are also covered.

2026-11-09-moz-mozambique-estevao-pale-u.summary: Mozambique's energy ministry launched the National Geospatial Least-Cost Electrification Plan 2026-2030 and the Integrated Electrification Platform in Maputo on 6 November 2026. The plan uses geospatial data to choose between grid extension and off-grid solutions for each settlement. The platform pools sector data from MIREME, ARENE, EDM and FUNAE. The World Bank funded the work, with technical assistance from SEforALL.

2026-11-09-mrt-build-once-use-across-gov.summary: GovStack reported on 9 November 2026 on two years of work with Mauritania, ITU, GIZ and the digital transformation ministry. In 2025 more than 30 officials from four ministries prototyped a company-registration service for the social security fund. In March 2026, 118 officials from 34 departments agreed a reference framework for shared architecture and service design.

2026-11-09-mrt-mattel-lance-commercialem.summary: Mattel launched commercial 5G in Mauritania on 9 November 2026, starting in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou. It also opened a Tier III redundancy and network-supervision centre. The operator presented its e-money subsidiary Mattel Money and the Mechili wallet.

2026-11-09-mtn-group-earnings-outpace-re.summary: MTN Group's update for the nine months to 30 September 2026 put service revenue at R176.2 billion, up 17.2% in constant currency, and EBITDA at R86.0 billion, up 22.9%. Nigeria and Ghana led the growth. The group counted 323.0 million customers and 70.3 million active Mobile Money users, with fintech transaction value up 36.9% to US$512.5 billion.

2026-11-09-mus-iso-member-msb.summary: The ISO membership page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists the Mauritius Standards Bureau as a member body. It describes a bureau that develops standards, provides testing, calibration and certification, and keeps national measurement standards. It shows participation in 34 technical committees and observer status in 28.

2026-11-09-mus-transport-osman-mahomed-m.summary: Mauritius awarded the overhaul of the National Land Transport Authority's IT system to State Informatics Ltd. The land transport minister's second annual report says so (reported 9 November 2026). GPS tracking of about 2,000 buses was delayed by an Independent Review Panel challenge and re-evaluation. Bids for a cashless e-ticketing consultancy were still under evaluation.

2026-11-09-mwi-malawi-s-nzika-digital-id.summary: Some Malawian banks are refusing the Nzika digital ID wallet, Zodiak Online reported on 9 November 2026. The wallet launched on 16 September 2026. The Bankers Association of Malawi says it is still a pilot with one bank. The National Registration Bureau promised it the card's validity but set no compliance deadline.

2026-11-09-mwi-ubuntu-in-action-maren-an.summary: The research and education networks of Malawi (MAREN) and Uganda (RENU) signed a memorandum of understanding at UbuntuNet-Connect 2026 in Lilongwe. The chief executives, Solomon Dindi and Nicholas Mbonimpa, signed it. It covers institutional collaboration and the sharing of knowledge and experience.

2026-11-09-nam-namibia-russia-to-share-c.summary: The Namibia Revenue Agency signed a customs data agreement with Russia in Moscow, as reported on 9 November 2026. The two sides are to exchange customs information and trade statistics, treated as confidential. Implementation awaits the completion of both countries' procedures.

2026-11-09-netherlands-dgis-mli-2026-jus.summary: UNDP handed Mali's Ministry of Justice IT equipment and new penal codes worth USD 493,193 on 5 November 2026. The Netherlands supports the PROSMED programme behind the gift. Laptops, tablets and internet modems are to equip the ministry's e-justice platform.

2026-11-09-nga-nitda-srap-dashboard.summary: Nigeria's NITDA launched a public dashboard tracking its Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2.0, as reported on 9 November 2026. It shows implementation updates and digital-economy indicators. GIZ's Digital Transformation Center Nigeria built it, with co-funding from the EU and Denmark.

2026-11-09-nigeria-s-telecom-operators-s.summary: ALTON and four Nigerian operators filed a summons at the Federal High Court in Abuja on 4 November 2026, TechCabal reported. They ask whether the Constitution lets the House of Representatives investigate their network quality and summon their chiefs. The House says each operator holds its own licence and must account for its performance.

2026-11-09-proparco-cashi-sudan.summary: Proparco announced on 9 November 2026 a EUR 600,000 investment in Cashi, a fintech serving Sudan. It is Proparco's first financing in Sudan. Proparco says Cashi's MyCashi wallet has 2.2 million registered users.

2026-11-09-rdc-un-systeme-connecte-pour-.summary: The DR Congo Ministry of Health announced on 8 November 2026 that the Etoile Bleue emergency medical response system will be inaugurated by the President, after a postponement in June 2026. It starts in Kinshasa and Matadi with a free 199 number, a mobile app, a regulation centre, 130 ambulances and 300 medical motorbikes. No launch date was given.

2026-11-09-sdn-cbs-full-week-clearing.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan resumed interbank electronic clearing every day of the week from 8 November 2026. It also lifted the ceiling on cheque values, Sudan Tribune reported. A circular of 9 November cancelled the earlier caps set in January and March.

2026-11-09-sdn-cbs-restoring-banking-sys.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's director general of policies spoke to Sudan Horizon on 9 November 2026. He said payments were restored by reactivating the Siraj RTGS and partly reinstating the national switch. He put inflation at 28.3% in September 2026, against 68% in December 2025.

2026-11-09-sdn-iso-member-ssmo.summary: The ISO membership page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists the Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organization as a member body. It describes a government body set up in 1993, with headquarters in Khartoum, state offices and 15 laboratories, and lists its memberships of regional and international standards bodies. The page carries no date of its own.

2026-11-09-sdn-zain-sudani-mtn-internet-.summary: Rtmediasd reported on 9 November 2026 that Zain, Sudani and MTN raised internet bundle prices in Sudan. The companies cite the rising dollar and the cost of fuel for towers. Zain's 100 GB bundle went from 68,900 to 115,000 pounds, up 67%, and its 300 GB bundle from 93,000 to 137,000, up 47%. Zain increases range from 44% to 130%.

2026-11-09-sen-wave-precise-l-acces-a-pi.summary: Wave announced on 6 November 2026 that its customers in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire can use the PI-SPI instant-payment system from its app. Sending is free up to 8,000 FCFA a day and costs 0.8% plus taxes above that. Receiving is free. Withdrawing PI-SPI funds at an agent costs 1%.

2026-11-09-sierra-leone-begins-training-.summary: Sierra Leone's Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation began training ICT officers from ministries, departments and agencies on website management and security, reported on 9 November 2026. Under its Website Standardisation Framework the ministry builds and hosts official sites on shared gov.sl infrastructure, and the officers maintain content. The first phase ran two days, and further phases are planned.

2026-11-09-sle-eu-wfp-school-feeding-dat.summary: The EU is giving EUR 2 million over two years through WFP for Sierra Leone's school feeding data, WFP said on 9 November 2026. More than 80 government staff are to be trained in monitoring and evaluation. Open Data Kit and School Connect are being introduced for school-feeding data.

2026-11-09-swz-iso-member-eswasa.summary: The ISO membership page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists the Eswatini Standards Authority as a correspondent member of ISO. It describes a body that opened on 2 April 2007, has sixteen staff and is governed by a ten-member Council. Its technical department holds an information centre, a standards development unit and a testing unit.

2026-11-09-tcd-chad-health-digital-commi.summary: Chad's technical committee on digital health met in N'Djamena on 9 November 2026, MEDD TV INFO reported. A recent ministerial order widened its members and missions, including patient records and telemedicine. It works under the 2025-2030 digital health plan and is to meet every two months.

2026-11-09-this-tech-firm-built-the-geos.summary: A profile published on 9 November 2026 describes the location data behind Nigeria's digital postcode system. The system launched on 1 October 2026 and gives codes to buildings or delivery units. Milsat chief executive Taslim Salaudeen says the firm supplies location data and is not an addressing company.

2026-11-09-tun-tunisia-356m-digital-tran.summary: Tunisia's communication technologies minister presented a 2027 budget of TND 1.07 billion on 6 November 2026, up 9.3%, Agence Ecofin reported. The ministry aims for 150 services on the Khadamet app, from over 40 now. It also plans 1.5 million active digital identities and 200 interoperability services.

2026-11-09-tza-tanzania-bot-payment-fram.summary: The Bank of Tanzania is reviewing its National Payment System regulatory framework, UNCDF reported in November 2026. In October 2026 it sent a ten-member delegation to the Central Bank of the UAE for a peer exchange. Further sessions, including on tiered licensing for payment providers, are planned.

2026-11-09-uga-uganda-nita-u-telecentres.summary: Uganda's NITA-U invited bids on 9 November 2026 for telecentre infrastructure and connectivity in refugee-host communities. The contract, under the World Bank-financed Uganda Digital Acceleration Project, has three regional lots. Bids close on 3 December 2026.

2026-11-09-xaf-af-ix-african-ixp-list.summary: The African IXP Association's page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists Internet exchange points by country and city with the year each opened. Entries include Angola-IXP in Luanda (2006), Benin IX in Cotonou (2013) and the Kinshasa exchange KINIX in the DRC (2012). The page carries no date of its own.

2026-11-09-xaf-african-union-concludes-6.summary: African Union ministers of education, science and technology met in Addis Ababa on 6 November 2026. They cleared five sectoral AI publications for national adaptation. They asked AUDA-NEPAD and an advisory group for a continental semiconductor strategy to 2034. They also asked the AU Commission for a reporting portal on 60 CESA indicators.

2026-11-09-xaf-call-for-stakeholder-inpu.summary: AUDA-NEPAD and the Science for Africa Foundation invited stakeholders, in a notice on file under 9 November 2026, to comment on a draft Vision for Open Research in Africa. The draft sets an ambition for an African-led open research ecosystem by 2034, aligned with STISA-2034. The consultation asks for views on relevance, challenges and priorities.

2026-11-09-xgl-ai-satellites-spectrum-ta.summary: The ITU Plenipotentiary Conference opened in Doha on 9 November 2026, with 194 member states meeting over three weeks. Delegates elect the Union's leadership from 12 November, along with 12 Radio Regulations Board members and 48 Council members. They also approve the ITU's 2028-2031 strategic and financial plans, amid contests over spectrum, satellite coordination and AI.

2026-11-09-xwa-ecowas-heads-of-immigrati.summary: ECOWAS Heads of Immigration adopted the Freetown Declaration on 4 November 2026. Member states commit to accept any valid ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card at official border crossings from 1 January 2027, whether or not the issuing state has started its own rollout. National rollout plans are due to the Commission by December 2030.

2026-11-09-zaf-icasa-gn4249-high-demand-.summary: ICASA published a questionnaire on assigning high-demand spectrum in the Government Gazette on 9 November 2026. It asks whether 80 MHz no longer reserved for a wholesale open access network should be included. Responses are due by 30 November 2026.

2026-11-09-zaf-south-africa-participates.summary: South Africa is seeking re-election to the ITU Council at the Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, which runs from 9 to 27 November 2026. Its delegation is led by the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies. For the 2027-2030 term it pledges to support digital public infrastructure, submarine-cable resilience and the safe use of AI.

2026-11-09-zmb-zambia-china-ai-data-cent.summary: Zambia's Ministry of Technology and Science asked China, including Huawei, to help build an AI-enabled data centre on 9 November 2026. It said existing Chinese-built data centres were designed for storage. The two sides agreed to meet again within weeks on a roadmap.

2026-11-09-zmb-zambia-national-ict-surve.summary: Zambia released its 2025 national survey on access and use of ICTs on 9 November 2026. Individual internet access was 29.7% in 2025, up from 25.2% in 2022. Only 7.7% of respondents knew of ZamPortal.

2026-11-09-zwe-iso-member-saz.summary: The ISO membership page, on file under 9 November 2026, lists the Standards Association of Zimbabwe as a member body. It describes a non-profit body formed in 1957 that publishes national standards, runs testing and certification, and serves as the WTO TBT enquiry point. It shows participation in 39 technical committees and observer status in 35.

2026-11-10-afdb-backs-local-tech-assembl.summary: Nicholas Williams manages the African Development Bank's ICT operations division. He said in November 2026 that African tech investment should extend to local hardware manufacturing and assembly. He gave the bank's tech portfolio as 47% digital entrepreneurship and skills, 23% connectivity and data infrastructure, 18% tech hubs and 12% digital policy and regulation. He named Ethiopia's device assembly base as an example, ITWeb Africa reported.

2026-11-10-africa-technology-policy-trac.summary: The Carnegie Endowment's Africa Technology Policy Tracker, as fetched on 10 November 2026, lists 595 digital laws, policies and regulations. It covers 36 countries and the African Union, with instruments dated from 1988 to 2025.

2026-11-10-ago-angola-apresenta-a-uit-pr.summary: Angola's telecommunications minister, Mário Oliveira, addressed the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha in November 2026. He described the national fibre backbone, the ANGOSAT-2 satellite and the Cloud Nacional government cloud. He said an electronic signatures regime, a national cybersecurity strategy and a national cybersecurity council had been approved. An AI law and a national AI strategy are in preparation with no completion date given, Portal de T.I. reported.

2026-11-10-ago-angola-seeks-stronger-tec.summary: Angola's minister Mário Oliveira invited Qatari investors into Angola's technology sector in November 2026. He spoke in an interview at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, The Peninsula reported. He said the Conecta Angola programme involves 71 small internet service providers, and ANGOSAT-2 serves Mozambique, Namibia, Zambia and South Africa. He added that the SADC Shared Satellite Programme, led by Angola, has secured eight ITU orbital positions.

2026-11-10-bog-governor-asiama-banking-e.summary: Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama addressed the 30th National Banking and Ethics Conference, held 9–10 November 2026. Communications Director Bernard Otabil delivered the text. It said the bank's security operations centre, FICSOC, supplies threat intelligence to 23 banks. It also said AI in credit assessment needs safeguards against bias and unfair outcomes.

2026-11-10-bwa-botswanas-ai-paradox-rich.summary: The Ayre Index of youth AI readiness was launched at the November 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. It ranks Botswana 45th of 56 Commonwealth states, scoring 38.9 out of 100 against a benchmark of 53. Botswana scores 7.2 of 10 for access to technology and 2.9 for decent work and enterprise. Weekend Post reported the study's moderate estimate of AI's possible GDP gain after ten years: USD 289 million.

2026-11-10-caf-developmentaid-pgnsp-acct.summary: An award notice under the World Bank-funded Public Sector Digital Governance Project in the Central African Republic was posted on 10 November 2026. It covers works to fit out the ACCT server room and rehabilitate the Sim-Ba experts' offices, under bid reference 137. The listing names no contractor, value or award date.

2026-11-10-civ-cote-divoire-gsma-mou-sma.summary: Côte d'Ivoire and the GSMA signed a memorandum of understanding on smartphone affordability at MWC Doha 2026, Tech Review Africa reported on 10 November 2026. The universal-service agency ANSUT will lead implementation under the GSMA Handset Affordability Coalition. The report gives no targets, prices or funding, and no signing date.

2026-11-10-civ-wb-padci-barometre-servic.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital ministry seeks a firm to digitise its National Public Service Quality Barometer, in a call closing 17 November 2026. The work falls under the World Bank-financed PADCI project. The barometer's 2024–2025 survey was run largely by hand. PADCI targets 12 public dashboards and 80% user satisfaction by 2030.

2026-11-10-civ-wearetech-artci-cadre-fib.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's regulator ARTCI drafted fibre-optic deployment standards and a quality-of-service measurement protocol for fixed networks at a seminar in Assinie on 4–6 November 2026. A third draft sets conditions for activating VoLTE and VoWiFi. The three drafts go to the ARTCI regulatory council for adoption, WeAreTech reported.

2026-11-10-cmr-art-communique-166-contro.summary: Cameroon's regulator ART reported on 10 November 2026 on its quality-of-service control of 13 July to 10 August 2026. It found 93 breaches of licence obligations: 41 for CAMTEL, valued at FCFA 8.2 billion, 29 for Orange Cameroun at FCFA 5.8 billion and 23 for MTN Cameroon at FCFA 4.6 billion. Each operator received a 15-day formal notice. An audit of CAMTEL's national fibre network found significant degradation.

2026-11-10-cmr-cemac-a-call-for-financia.summary: Pierre Kam is secretary general of Cameroon's banking association APECCAM. At APIDE 2026 in Douala on 9–10 November 2026, he proposed a common merchant identification system across CEMAC. He said a six-month work programme with the regional central bank BEAC is envisaged on merchant payment interoperability. A feasibility report and a pilot framework are expected by the end of June 2027, Season Media reported.

2026-11-10-cmr-gtai-kfw-pmsi-dgi-it-trai.summary: Cameroon's tax directorate has issued a tender for technical IT training for its IT staff, financed by KfW under the programme to modernise the directorate's information system. The training covers networks, security, virtualisation, backup, data centres and programming. Bids close on 10 December 2026, and no value is stated, according to the GTAI notice.

2026-11-10-cod-augustin-kibassa-maliba-a.summary: The DRC's digital economy minister, Augustin Kibassa Maliba, opened the second Journées des DSI in Kinshasa on 9 November 2026. The event is for public-sector IT directors. He listed his ministry's instruments, including the digital economy sector policy, the national data governance strategy, work on a national AI strategy and a plan to digitise the administration. Actu7.cd reported that he set the IT directors strategic, technical and transformational responsibilities.

2026-11-10-cod-nation-digitale-2030-a-ki.summary: The DRC's Agence pour le Développement du Numérique organised the second Journées des DSI in Kinshasa on 9–11 November 2026. GIZ and Huawei Technologies RDC were among its supporters. The first day's sessions covered the national fibre backbone and the universal connectivity strategy for 2026–2035. The agency's deputy coordinator named digital identity, e-government and a sovereign data-hosting space among its priorities.

2026-11-10-comesa-regional-digital-inclu.summary: Fifteen COMESA member states validated a Regional Digital Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, with a Situational Analysis Report, at a workshop in Lusaka on 3–5 November 2026. Zambia hosted the workshop, with World Bank support under the IDEA programme. COMESA said on 10 November 2026 that the outcomes will guide the documents' finalisation, adoption and implementation.

2026-11-10-dfc-wiocc-equity-approval.summary: Jim Kelly of the US International Development Finance Corporation briefed the press on 9 November 2026. He said DFC's equity investment in the West Indian Ocean Cable Company is its largest to date. He expects the deal to mobilise up to USD 400 million of private capital and expand networks in more than 30 African countries. DFC's commitments across Africa exceed USD 14.5 billion, Nexus Media reported.

2026-11-10-dr-luciano-hounkponou-re-elec.summary: The eight councillors of Benin's Personal Data Protection Authority (APDP) were sworn in before the Supreme Court. At their first elective plenary of the authority's fourth term, they unanimously re-elected Luciano Hounkponou as president. Tech Review Africa reported this on 10 November 2026.

2026-11-10-egy-cairo-ict-digital-records.summary: A Cairo ICT 2026 panel on 9 November 2026 discussed medical AI in Egypt. Health Care Authority chairman Ahmed El Sobky cited about 6.2 million electronic health files. Hospital automation in the authority exceeds 85%, the chairman said. Noha Adly of the Applied Innovation Center called for sensitive health data to stay in Egypt.

2026-11-10-egy-health-minister-cairo-ict.summary: Egypt's health ministry will send parliament a draft law bringing health databases into one system, minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said on 8 November 2026. The minister spoke at Cairo ICT 2026. The Nephro Egypt platform follows about 60,000 dialysis patients. Automated state-funded treatment decisions now take at most 24 hours.

2026-11-10-egy-pm-opens-cairo-ict-ai-tar.summary: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly opened Cairo ICT 2026 on 7 November 2026. ICT Minister Raafat Hendy set 2030 targets of 200,000 jobs, 250 AI start-ups and US$12bn in digital exports. Digital Egypt offers 261 services in 29 packages, with 13.7m active users against 10.4m a year earlier. A National Data Centre Strategy is expected before the end of 2026.

2026-11-10-enabel-di4e-call-eoi-tanzania.summary: Enabel, Belgium's development agency, invited expressions of interest on 10 November 2026 in running its Innovation Hub and Toolkit model for teachers in Tanzania and Uganda. The model sits in the Digital Innovation for Education Scaling Project, funded by the EU and Belgium. The call is a mapping exercise and awards no funding. Responses are due by 11 January 2027, ahead of a call for proposals planned for March 2027.

2026-11-10-ethiopia-presses-public-insti.summary: Ethiopia's Innovation and Technology Minister, Frehiwot Tamru, ordered faster completion of the National Cloud Data Center at the Addis Ababa ICT Park, Tech Review Africa reported on 10 November 2026. She repeated federal directives that public institutions move from their own server rooms onto shared national infrastructure. The centre is still under construction.

2026-11-10-gha-itu-pp26-policy-statement.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, addressed the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha in November 2026. He said 5G will reach more than 70% of Ghanaians by March 2027. He cited 2,016 rural telephony sites being completed, 5G spectrum licensing and a National AI Compute Centre under construction. Ghana is standing for re-election to the ITU Council and has nominated NCA Director-General Edmund Yirenkyi Fianko for the Radio Regulations Board.

2026-11-10-gha-nca-hosts-helios-towers-d.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority met a Helios Towers Ghana delegation on 3 November 2026. The tower company raised delays in environmental permits, community approvals for towers and the disconnection of sites from the electricity grid. The NCA's Director-General offered to broker talks with the environmental regulators, according to the authority's release.

2026-11-10-gin-mojaloop-nimbapay-launch-.summary: The Mojaloop Foundation said on 10 November 2026 that NimbaPay went live on 22 July 2026. NimbaPay is Guinea's national instant payment system, built on the foundation's open-source software. It reported 24,064 transactions worth GNF 19.151 billion between June and August 2026, rising from 5,542 in July to 18,459 in August. The central bank BCRG and the national switch GuiM run the system.

2026-11-10-global-cyberlaw-tracker-2026-.summary: UNCTAD's Global Cyberlaw Tracker, as fetched on 10 November 2026, records the position of 54 African states on five kinds of law. These are e-transactions, consumer protection, data protection, cybercrime and indirect taxation.

2026-11-10-google-skilling-africa-offlin.summary: Google's Skilling Africa with Google platform aims to train three million Africans in digital and AI skills by 2030. It targets 250,000 graduates by the end of 2026. It offers more than 15 programmes, with materials that can be downloaded over Wi-Fi for offline use. The figures come from a Google West Africa statement, the Independent Newspaper Nigeria reported on 10 November 2026.

2026-11-10-gov-za-home-affairs-launches-.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs opened the first phase of its Digital Asylum System to test cases on 10 November 2026. The portal on Myhomeaffairsonline records intentions to apply for asylum, with facial biometrics, personal details and documents. Public intake follows the next weekend software release. The department says later phases will add biometric checks and AI tools for the appeals backlog.

2026-11-10-ict-regulatory-tracker-2026-1.summary: The ITU's ICT Regulatory Tracker, as fetched on 10 November 2026, gives 2024-round values for 54 African states. Its 50 indicators cover the regulatory authority, its mandate, the regulatory regime and competition, and all are self-reported by governments.

2026-11-10-ken-where-did-my-bundles-go-d.summary: Data services drew 140 of the 479 consumer complaints escalated to the Communications Authority of Kenya in July to September 2026, or 29.2%, Daily Nation reported on 10 November 2026. Mobile money followed with 57. Billing and premature bundle depletion made up 44 complaints, of which the authority resolved 37.

2026-11-10-kenya-nominates-lydia-sitiene.summary: President Ruto nominated Lydia Sitienei, director of legal services at the Communications Authority of Kenya, as the country's second Data Commissioner, Tech Africa News reported on 10 November 2026. The nomination has gone to the National Assembly for approval. She would succeed Immaculate Kassait, the first commissioner, at the end of her six-year term.

2026-11-10-kenya-securke-konza-sovereign.summary: Kenya's ICT Principal Secretary, John Tanui, launched the SecureKE/Konza Sovereign Security Operations Centre, reported on 10 November 2026. The centre is a partnership between the Konza Technopolis Development Authority and SecureKE. It offers public and private institutions continuous monitoring, threat detection, incident investigation and coordinated response, according to the ICT ministry.

2026-11-10-lbr-iso-member-lisa.summary: The International Organization for Standardization lists the Liberia Standards Authority (LiSA) as a correspondent member, as read on 10 November 2026. ISO's page says LiSA was established by law in 2022 and began operating in 2024.

2026-11-10-lby-launch-of-national-trade-.summary: Libya's Ministry of Economy and Trade launched the National Trade Facilitation Enquiry Point platform after its pilot phase, reported on 10 November 2026. It is run with the Libya Trade Network. It covers 53 import, export and transit procedures, 140 laws and decisions, 32 international agreements, 1,030 standards and 10 customs ports, and takes online enquiries and complaints.

2026-11-10-liberia-rwanda-five-year-mou-.summary: Rwanda Cooperation and Liberia's Ministry of Local Government signed a five-year memorandum of understanding in Kigali on 10 November 2026. Its first area is digitising Liberia's 15 County Service Centers, drawing on Rwanda's Irembo experience; it also covers local revenue administration and tax registries. Focal persons are due within 30 days and a joint implementation plan within 90.

2026-11-10-m-pesa-pesalink-pricing-gaps.summary: Postbank's entry to PesaLink brings Kenya's interbank payments network to 80 institutions, including all 38 licensed commercial banks. PesaLink says it processes an average of KES 4 billion a day, up 24% on a year earlier. TechCabal compares bank tariffs, with 19 banks on a flat KES 20 fee, and asks whether lower fees can draw users from M-PESA.

2026-11-10-mar-ahmed-rahhou-annonce-une-.summary: Morocco's minister for AI, digital transition and administrative reform, Ahmed Rahhou, presented his department's AI projects to a parliamentary committee on 10 November 2026. Reports by Al3omk and Alyaoum24, relayed by TelQuel, list voice services in Darija, a first open-source national language model and a speech-recognition model built with Mistral. The ministry expects to launch the programme in 2027.

2026-11-10-mar-al3omk-ai-simplify-2800-a.summary: Ahmed Rahhou is Morocco's Minister of AI, Digital Transition and Administrative Reform. On 10 November 2026 he presented his ministry's 2027 sub-budget to the House of Representatives' Interior Committee. He said the ministry is using AI to find which of about 2,800 administrative procedures can be simplified. Al3omk reports he also said the 1918–2026 Official Gazette archive will be opened to AI tools to speed legal drafting and research.

2026-11-10-mar-morocco-develops-national.summary: Morocco's AI, Digital Transition and Administrative Reform Ministry presented its 2027 budget to the House of Representatives' Interior Committee on 10 November 2026. For sovereign AI services, it is structuring about 2,800 administrative procedures, nearly 10,000 legal texts and a first national corpus of 85,000 documents. Its data programme covers 10,000 hours of transcribed Darija audio and the roughly 90,000-text Adala legal base. It has opened four Jazari institutes.

2026-11-10-moz-governo-apresenta-em-doha.summary: Mozambique's Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation, Américo Muchanga, spoke at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, held from 9 to 12 November 2026, AIM reports. He set out the country's digital priorities: broadband expansion, 5G, cybersecurity and data protection. He also named AI and big data for disaster prevention and management. He met Saudi and Estonian representatives on cooperation in communications and digital transformation.

2026-11-10-mrt-luniversite-de-nouakchott.summary: Université de Nouakchott launched a blockchain-based platform on 10 November 2026 to issue and verify its diplomas and certificates electronically. It was built with UNDP support and the Tunisian firm Kalis. AMI reports that it is meant to curb forgery and let employers and institutions in Mauritania and abroad check qualifications.

2026-11-10-mrt-mauritania-cybashon-cyber.summary: Mauritania's Ministry of Digital Transformation signed a memorandum of understanding with the US company Cybashon in Nouakchott on 10 November 2026. It covers protection of state systems and networks, digitisation of administrative procedures, and public services in remote areas. It also covers skills training through the Africa Digi Empower programme, with Cisco Networking Academy certification, Taqadoumy reports.

2026-11-10-nam-itu-pp-26-doha-namibia-re.summary: Namibia's ICT ministry told the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha on 8 November 2026 that it will connect all public schools and clinics by 2030. It put mobile broadband population coverage above 89% in 2026. It named affordability, digital literacy, device access and local content as the remaining gaps, TechReviewAfrica reports.

2026-11-10-nam-when-technology-outpaces-.summary: Dr Etuna Simon argues in The Brief, in November 2026, that Namibian higher education lags behind AI. The article points to curricula, lecturer readiness and unequal student access. It calls for sustained training for lecturers, assessment that tests judgement as well as recall, and continuous curriculum work with industry. It also asks for wider use of labour-market data, such as vacancy trends and graduate destination studies.

2026-11-10-namibia-could-gain-us-219-mil.summary: The Ayre Think Tank's 2026 Commonwealth Youth AI Readiness Index ranks Namibia 36th of 56 countries, with 42.7 out of 100, Namibia Daily News reported on 10 November 2026. The index estimates AI could add US$219m to GDP over ten years in a moderate scenario. It records youth unemployment of 47% and electricity access of 59.3%.

2026-11-10-nga-active-telecom-lines-hit-.summary: Nigeria's active telecom subscriptions passed 200 million for the first time since the 2024 NIN-SIM disconnections, reaching 200,337,097 in September 2026, on data from the Nigerian Communications Commission. Teledensity stood at 92.41% and broadband subscriptions at 128 million, or 59.05% penetration. 5G made up 5.05% of mobile connections.

2026-11-10-nga-cbn-fiscal-data-collectio.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria is moving its Sub-National Fiscal Survey of the 36 states, the FCT and 774 local governments from paper to a digital platform. Its Statistics Department said returns will be quarterly instead of twice a year. Training had reached 16 states by 6 November 2026. The remaining states are due by 4 December, and the FCT on 9 and 10 December 2026.

2026-11-10-nga-migration-records-integra.summary: Nigeria's Interior Ministry said on 10 November 2026 that more than 17 billion migration records had been moved into an integrated system, Vanguard reports. The system is used to verify the nationality of returnees. The ministry said this as it closed negotiations with the EU on a readmission agreement, which had run for about a decade.

2026-11-10-nga-national-single-window-ex.summary: Nigeria's National Single Window will open export processing on 14 December 2026, its secretariat said on 10 November 2026. A first group of permit-issuing agencies goes live then: NAQS, SON, NAFDAC, NACCIMA, FPIS and REX. CBN, Customs, NEPZA and four ministries follow in the first quarter of 2027. Customs' regulatory HS-code list is due by 1 December 2026 and will be enforced from 1 January 2027.

2026-11-10-nga-thefact-nigeria-integrate.summary: Nigeria's Interior Minister, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said on 10 November 2026 that over 17 million migration records had been integrated into the automated migration management system. TheFact Daily reported this and compares it with over 15 million in October. He spoke at a meeting in Abuja with EU Commissioner Magnus Brunner on the readmission agreement. An EU delegate there said almost EUR 100 million in additional funding had been made available.

2026-11-10-nigeria-biometric-election-cl.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission, INEC, said it had removed more than 1.6 million invalid voter records after screening with its automated biometric identification system. Biometric Update reported this on 10 November 2026. Of 268,000 records adjudicated, 217,722 were confirmed invalid. INEC also identified 54 staff in 10 states implicated in registration irregularities, including AI-generated photographs, ahead of certifying the final register on 15 December 2026.

2026-11-10-nigeria-hybrid-cloud-postcode.summary: NIPOST said Nigeria's digital postcode database is hosted in the country on Galaxy Backbone, under the Level 3 controls of the National Digital Cloud Policy of August 2026, TechCabal reported on 10 November 2026. AWS serves only the public website. NIPOST said its data protection impact assessment with the NDPC is still in progress.

2026-11-10-nigeriastartupact-google-ai-n.summary: Data Science Nigeria, with Google support, opened registration for contributors to a National AI Glossary Project, reported on 10 November 2026. The project builds AI language resources in Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa and Nigerian Pidgin. The call states no payment or grant.

2026-11-10-osun-uk-digital-access-progra.summary: The Osun State governor's office announced on 10 November 2026 an agreement on SPRIRET, a project of the UK-funded Digital Access Programme. It covers digital-economy policy, connectivity, digital public infrastructure and civic technology, and will be implemented by the Initiative for Digital Inclusion. No amount was stated.

2026-11-10-ria-bringing-more-voices-into.summary: Research ICT Africa reports on its ten sessions at the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum in Accra, held from 2 to 5 November 2026. They covered an African AI safety agenda and the gap in implementing data policy. They also covered exclusion when ID is linked to SIM cards, banking and health insurance. RIA says it has supported validation of national data policies for The Gambia, Somalia and the Comoros.

2026-11-10-sen-audit-biometrique-agents-.summary: Senegal launched a physical and biometric audit of local-government staff on 10 November 2026, installing the bodies that will govern it, APS reported. The aim is a secure database of agents, interoperable with territorial HR information systems, with lists certified by local executives. Minister Moussa Balla Fofana cited a 2022 diagnostic counting 18,716 agents in 601 local authorities.

2026-11-10-sen-justice-apix-business-reg.summary: Senegal's Justice Minister, Moussa Sarr, agreed on 10 November 2026 to deploy APIX's online company-creation platform in the courts, APAnews reports. The court registries that keep the RCCM trade and movable-credit register would be interconnected with other agencies, so that a company can be created in hours. He asked for a governance framework that brings together the institutions involved.

2026-11-10-sen-pidsm-mining-platform.summary: Senegal's Ministry of Mines and Geology validated its integrated mining-sector data platform, PIDSM, Le Marché Finance reported on 10 November 2026; the workshop date is not given. The one-stop portal shows mining perimeters in real time, publishes geological data and takes title applications online. It links LandFolio, SIGEOS, E-Gouv, SenTax and SenTrésor through APIs.

2026-11-10-senate-passes-bill-to-regulat.summary: Nigeria's Senate passed SB. 959 on third reading on 10 November 2026. The bill amends the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act 2020 so the Central Bank can designate and register fintechs and other non-bank institutions as Systemically Important Institutions. It requires stress tests, data-integrity assessments, cybersecurity safeguards and a public register of designated institutions.

2026-11-10-sle-data-protection-records-b.summary: Sierra Leone's Minister of Information and Civic Education, Chernor Bah, tabled two bills in Parliament on 5 November 2026. Both completed First Reading. The Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2026 would set up one independent authority for data protection and access to information. The National Records and Archives Bill, 2026 would replace colonial-era records laws, Sierra Leone Monitor reports.

2026-11-10-sle-unipod-fintech-lab.summary: A FinTech Innovation Lab has been set up at Sierra Leone's University Innovation Pod (UniPod) by UNCDF, the EU and the Bank of Sierra Leone, The Spear News SL reported on 10 November 2026. It gives early-stage fintech startups acceleration support and access to the central bank's regulatory sandbox. The date it was set up is not stated.
