2026-11-10-som-ministry-of-finance-feder.summary: The Federal Government of Somalia's Ministry of Finance website, captured on 12 November 2026, carries a transparency portal of budget, debt, procurement and audit publications. Its Open Budget Initiative section promises open data and machine-readable releases. A fiscal dashboard puts the public debt stock at US$1.48bn in Q2 2026, figures the ministry says are still being checked.

2026-11-10-south-africa-yoco-secures-100.summary: South African fintech Yoco secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors to expand its Yoco Capital merchant financing, Tech Africa News reported on 10 November 2026. Offers are pre-approved on merchants' sales data and repaid from daily takings. Yoco says it has provided more than R6.5 billion to over 40,000 merchants since 2018.

2026-11-10-techcentral-vodacom-eyes-sa-a.summary: Vodacom Group CEO Shameel Joosub spoke to TechCentral on 10 November 2026 about a sovereign AI data centre in Egypt. Vodafone Egypt plans it with Elsewedy Electric and Cassava Technologies, at a total cost of about US$1 billion. It will be built in modules, and Vodafone Egypt will own about 30%. He named South Africa and Kenya as further AI data centre hubs, with planning there at a very early stage.

2026-11-10-tgo-togo-harc-content-creator.summary: Togo's communication regulator, HARC, called on content creators, bloggers and influencers to register in its database, in a communiqué of 9 November 2026. A QR-code form collects identity, residence, field of activity, and electronic and telephone contacts. The regulator says it wants an up-to-date directory of people active on digital platforms, the government portal reported on 10 November 2026.

2026-11-10-tun-paiement-mobile-en-tunisi.summary: Tunisie Numérique reported Central Bank of Tunisia data showing 719,000 e-wallets at end-September 2026, up 53.3% on a year earlier. Wallet transactions rose 20% to 7.1 million, 64.2% of them payments. Twenty payment providers processed 1,354.9m dinars, up 6.6%.

2026-11-10-tza-tanzania-mwinyi-ai-public.summary: Zanzibar President Hussein Ali Mwinyi told the 11th annual meeting of the Africa Public Service Human Resource Managers Network in Unguja on 9 November 2026 that AI should remain a tool under human judgement and accountability. First Vice-President Othman Masoud Othman read the speech for him. The Citizen reports 1,140 participants from 21 African countries.

2026-11-10-uga-uganda-new-ict-permanent-.summary: President Museveni appointed Prof Stephen Akandwanaho, a professor of artificial intelligence, as Permanent Secretary for ICT and National Guidance, the Daily Monitor reported on 10 November 2026. In an interview on 9 November he named his priorities. They are digital services, connectivity and digital skills in every sub-county, a Uganda-first approach to AI and sovereign technology, and cybersecurity.

2026-11-10-uga-what-dr-aminah-zawedde-le.summary: Uganda's President moved ICT Permanent Secretary Aminah Zawedde to the Office of the Prime Minister on 9 November 2026, PML Daily reported. The profile relays ministry figures. The Government Digital Registry listed about 743 systems in May 2026. The ICT budget rose from about UGX 104bn in FY2022/23 to about UGX 490bn this year.

2026-11-10-wb-kenya-lake-victoria-basin-.summary: Kenya's KeNHA issued a procurement notice for the Lake Victoria Basin Connectivity and Development Project, The Eastleigh Voice reported on 10 November 2026. It seeks US$1bn (Sh129.92bn) in IDA financing. The money covers about 815 km of roads and a similar length of fibre across eight counties. Procurement is expected in October–December 2026.

2026-11-10-xaf-uneca-health-information-.summary: The UN Economic Commission for Africa called on governments to treat health information systems as public infrastructure. The call came at the opening of the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi on 10 November 2026. Chief of Staff Aboubakri Diaw spoke for Executive Secretary Claver Gatete. Diaw said Africa spends about $145 billion a year on health, yet planning often rests on incomplete population and mortality data.

2026-11-10-xaf-who-afro-his-maturity-fun.summary: WHO's Regional Office for Africa launched a report on health information systems on 10 November 2026. In a 2024 assessment, systems in 40 of its 47 member states scored 59 of 100 for maturity. Of the 40, 19 notify at least 80% of deaths. 18% hold a dedicated budget line and 20% run digital patient records. The report was released at the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi.

2026-11-10-xaf-why-africa-is-struggling-.summary: A news report of 10 November 2026 covers the WHO report on health data systems presented at the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi. WHO regional director Mohamed Janabi said the 2024 assessment gave the region a maturity score of 59 out of 100. Of 52 countries assessed, 49 had well-developed capacity to review health performance. None had reached sustainable capacity in using data for policy and action.

2026-11-10-zaf-pmg-nw5534-dpsa-applicant.summary: South Africa's public service minister told Parliament on 10 November 2026 that no central portal stores job applicants' data (reply NW5534). A shared HR system depends on National Treasury's IFMS project, now in abeyance. The department and the CPSI are exploring links between existing recruitment platforms.

2026-11-10-zaf-south-africa-icasa-high-d.summary: ICASA opened a stakeholder questionnaire on 10 November 2026 on the second phase of licensing high-demand IMT spectrum. It covers the IMT750, IMT800, IMT1500, IMT2300, IMT3300 and IMT3500 bands. It may also cover the 80 MHz once reserved for the Wireless Open Access Network. Responses are due by 16h00 on 30 November 2026, before an Information Memorandum and an Invitation to Apply.

2026-11-10-zaf-techafricanews-vodacom-h1.summary: Vodacom Group reported revenue of R102.5 billion for the six months to 30 September 2026, up 25.6% after it consolidated Safaricom, Tech Africa News reported on 10 November 2026. Financial services revenue rose 99% to R15.9 billion, with 108 million financial services customers. Transactions worth US$575.5 billion passed across Vodacom and Safaricom, and smartphone penetration reached 69.8%.

2026-11-10-zaf-vodacom-interim-results-s.summary: Vodacom Group reported 250 million customers, up 11.8%, in its interim results for the six months to 30 September 2026, published on 10 November. It holds 55% of Safaricom. Kenya's High Court declared the acquisition null and void, but the Court of Appeal ordered the status quo kept pending an expedited appeal. The interim dividend is 355 cents a share, up 7.6%.

2026-11-10-zmb-zambia-world-bank-ict-sur.summary: Zambia launched its National ICT Survey in Lusaka on 9 November 2026. World Bank representative Luke Mate said at the launch that internet access had risen from 25.2% to 29.7%. Individual use of financial services rose from 49% in 2022 to 60% in 2025. Technology and Science Minister Felix Mutati said the Government Service Bus recorded 1.2 million transactions last year and hosts 532 services.

2026-11-10-zwe-zimbabwe-citizen-feedback.summary: Zimbabwe's Minister of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare, Edgar Moyo, called for citizen satisfaction surveys to set a baseline for AI in government services. He spoke at the UN Governance Innovation Summit in Baku, Zim Now reported on 10 November 2026. He named welfare case management and forecasting demand for assistance as uses. The ministry named no specific AI platform or programme.

2026-11-10-zwe-zimbabwe-smart-traffic-da.summary: Engineer Jacob Kudzayi Mutisi argues in ZimEye, on 10 November 2026, that Zimbabwe's Smart Traffic Management System needs accurate vehicle ownership records before it relies on camera fines. He proposes free online ownership transfers through the Central Vehicle Registry. He also proposes driver identification with privacy safeguards. He calls for an independent vulnerability assessment and penetration test of the whole system.

2026-11-11-bdi-paperless-comesa-trade-ce.summary: Burundi and the COMESA secretariat met in Bujumbura on 9–12 November 2026 to prepare Burundi's connection to the regional electronic certificate of origin platform. The meeting feeds a national implementation action plan. No timetable or cost has been published.

2026-11-11-bdi-saudi-support-digital-id-.summary: Burundi's finance and digital economy minister, Alain Ndikumana, asked Saudi Arabia to consider backing a national digital ID card and data centre, Lionweek reported on 11 November 2026. The talks took place in Doha on the sidelines of ITU PP-26, and the ministry's statement mentions no agreement, pledge or timetable. Both projects sit in the World Bank's US$92m PAFEN project, 61% committed by March 2026. The biometric card still awaits a law on its use.

2026-11-11-ben-protection-des-donnees-pe.summary: Benin's data protection authority, APDP, warned content creators on 11 November 2026. Recording or publishing identifying data on Facebook, WhatsApp or TikTok needs the person's consent under the Code du numérique. It cited penalties of up to seven years in prison and a fine of FCFA 100 million. It said it may act without a complaint.

2026-11-11-bfa-operation-d-enregistremen.summary: Burkina Faso's President launched mass enrolment in the electronic unique identifier register in Ouagadougou on 11 November 2026. Each person receives a free, random 12-digit number after photograph, fingerprint and iris capture at 160 sites and by mobile teams. The digital transition ministry says it replaces no existing identity document.

2026-11-11-bfa-registre-identifiant-uniq.summary: Burkina Faso launched mass enrolment in its Unique Identifier Register on 11 November 2026, Lefaso.net reported. Every resident, including foreigners in transit, is to receive an electronic identifier. Enrolment captures ten fingerprints and both irises. A pilot enrolled over 16,000 people, and a first count is due at the end of December 2026.

2026-11-11-businessday-google-600k-niger.summary: Google.org committed US$600,000 to the TechSocietal Development Foundation for Nigeria's first nationwide study of teenagers' online risks, Businessday reported on 11 November 2026. The sum is US$550,000 in funding and US$50,000 in Ad Grants. The study will survey 2,000 adolescents and train 5,000 teachers, alongside a child online-safety pilot in four states.

2026-11-11-bwa-statistics-botswana-strat.summary: Acting President Ndaba Gaolathe launched Statistics Botswana's 2026–2030 corporate strategic plan in Tlokweng, the Daily News reported on 11 November 2026. The plan has four pillars: statistical excellence and leadership, data use and impact, institutional resilience, and innovation. The Acting President tied it to monitoring the Botswana Economic Transformation Programme.

2026-11-11-citinewsroom-ghana-infrastruc.summary: Ghana's proposed Dig Once Policy is before Cabinet, minister Samuel Nartey George told an ITU session in Doha. Citi Newsroom reported the remarks on 11 November 2026. A National Emergency Telecommunications Plan is being developed. Ghana proposed an ITU Programme of Action on Resilience with timelines and measurable indicators.

2026-11-11-civ-guichet-unique-numerique-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Tourism and Leisure launched a digital one-stop shop for tourism operators on 10 November 2026. Operators can file and pay for administrative procedures online and track them against a 45-day maximum processing time. It is the first component of the tourism activity management system, piloted in four regional directorates (Linfodrome, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-civ-semafor-distant-wars-pose.summary: Yango users in Côte d'Ivoire had intermittent booking and delivery failures in October 2026 after the company moved operations between data centres. Its Dubai-based spokesperson told Semafor on 11 November 2026 that a partner said in September that Gulf infrastructure hit by Iranian attacks could no longer support it. The partner and new location were not named.

2026-11-11-civ-undp-centre-national-ia-e.summary: UNDP in Côte d'Ivoire tendered on 11 November 2026 for a national firm to run lot 1 of a feasibility study for a national AI and innovation centre. The lot covers the centre's positioning, service offer, virtual hub, use cases, institutional model and data governance. The tender documents require a UNDP supplier login.

UNDP in Côte d'Ivoire tendered on 11 November 2026 for a national firm to run lot 2 of a feasibility study for a national AI and innovation centre. The lot covers computing, hosting and connectivity options, cybersecurity and the technical requirements of the centre's first IT purchase. A first lot covers the centre's positioning and governance.

2026-11-11-cod-nation-digitale-2030-coll.summary: DR Congo's digital economy minister, Augustin Kibassa, closed a meeting of state IT directors in Kinshasa on 11 November 2026, ACP reported. Augustin Kibassa cited a USD 510 million World Bank and AFD digital project and a presidential pledge of about USD 1 billion. A donor group set up in July 2026 aligns funders to avoid duplicate projects.

2026-11-11-cod-recrutement-sae-akili-dig.summary: DR Congo's digital transformation project unit, UG PTN, is recruiting a body to incubate and accelerate start-ups under the Akili Digital pilot in Kinshasa. An addendum of 10 November 2026 gives 25 points to knowledge of the Kinshasa ecosystem, Congo Quotidien reported. The World Bank finances the project under credit 7602-ZR, with AFD co-financing.

2026-11-11-cpv-cvtelecom-restabelece-ser.summary: A fire at CVTelecom's Mindelo station on São Vicente on the night of 10 November 2026 disrupted telecommunications on several Cabo Verde islands. On 11 November the operator reported services fully restored on Fogo and Brava, and mobile and fixed internet restored on Sal and Boa Vista. Other services remained affected (A Nação, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-digitalisation-des-attestatio.summary: Mali's trade directorate, the DGCC, launched the pilot phase of digital import certificates for private vehicles on 9 November 2026. The first certificate, no. 2026000001001, was entered and printed in the new system. Customs, the tax services and licensed customs brokers are taking part before the system is extended.

2026-11-11-dza-portail-numerique-les-doc.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitisation said all public administrations now accept documents issued on the Dzair Digital Services portal. A decision of Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb requires it. The portal has grown from 21 services at its July 2026 launch to 68. It had over two million registered users on 10 November 2026.

2026-11-11-eac-eac-digital-recruitment-s.summary: The East African Community Council of Ministers approved an electronic recruitment system, according to a Council report from Mombasa cited by The Citizen on 11 November 2026. The report estimates a saving of USD 495,624 against USD 955,257 for recruiting 88 posts by the paper process. The first phase covers 69 priority positions in the 2026/27 financial year.

2026-11-11-ednews-africa-ai-education-dr.summary: AI Research Foundations, a Google.org-funded programme training lecturers to teach advanced AI, launched at Stellenbosch University on 9 November 2026. It targets 30 universities in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa, ten of them South African, and aims to reach 30,000 students. FATE Foundation holds the grant and AIMS South Africa is the academic partner, ednews.africa reported.

2026-11-11-egy-prosecution-launches-pers.summary: Egypt's Public Prosecution opened a training course on 8 November 2026 for 22 staff of the Personal Data Protection Centre. It is held at the Institute of Criminal Research and Training and runs to 12 November. It trains them as judicial officers, with 60 per cent given to practical work.

2026-11-11-egy-prosecution-opens-ai-data.summary: Egypt's Public Prosecution announced on 11 November 2026 that it will open an AI data centre at the Prosecutor-General's office in Rehab on 14 November. It has invited journalists to register to attend.

2026-11-11-egy-remote-power-of-attorney-.summary: Egypt's remote general power-of-attorney service on the Digital Egypt platform checks a face scan from the digital identity app against state biometric records. It then issues a one-time remote e-signature certificate for each transaction, on infrastructure built by ITIDA, Youm7 reported on 11 November 2026. The launch date has not been stated.

2026-11-11-enabel-haut-katanga-classe-mo.summary: Enabel, GIZ and the Centre de Ressources du Haut-Katanga presented a mobile digital classroom, Njia ya Ujuzi, to provincial authorities in Lubumbashi, Enabel reported on 11 November 2026. The truck carries computers and an internet connection under the Edubase project. It will travel the Lobito corridor offering digital-skills training, ICB certification preparation and solar-technology courses.

2026-11-11-gab-restoring-social-media-ac.summary: An analysis published on 11 November 2026 reviews the end of Gabon's social media ban. The media regulator HAC suspended Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube on 17 February 2026. It lifted the suspension on 24 October, after 248 days. The author says access came with identity rules and cooperation agreements with platforms. The author raises concerns for free expression and privacy.

2026-11-11-gha-ghana-petroleum-commissio.summary: Ghana's Petroleum Commission introduced a Digital Permit Application Platform to replace paper permit applications in the upstream petroleum sector. Chief executive Emeafa Hardcastle announced it at the Commission's 2026 Local Content Conference in Takoradi (MyJoyOnline, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-gha-national-identification-a.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority says L.I. 2523 ends the practice of photocopying or scanning the Ghana Card. Institutions must now verify identity biometrically against the National Identity Register under a direct service agreement with the Authority, and a taskforce has begun monitoring compliance.

2026-11-11-gnb-guinea-bissau-data-portal.summary: The terms of use for Guinea-Bissau's data on the African Development Bank's High Fives application allow free copying and reuse, commercial or not, with attribution in the metadata. The Bank gives no warranty and may withdraw access at any time. No standard licence is named (checked 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-google-africa-applied-ai-lab-.summary: Google named the ten start-ups in the first cohort of its Africa Applied AI Lab on 11 November 2026. They include Crane AI Labs (Uganda), Intron, Termii and Vendy (Nigeria), Satlyt (Kenya) and Tolbi (Senegal). Entrants came from more than 45 African countries, and a demo day is set for December 2026 in Accra.

2026-11-11-inforpress-fogo-telecoms-inte.summary: Fogo island in Cabo Verde lost telephone and internet services overnight on 10 November 2026, Inforpress reported. A CVTelecom source blamed a fire at its São Vicente station, which also cut Brava and Santo Antão. Since March, Fogo has used a backup submarine cable after a fault on the Santiago–Fogo link, due for repair in late November.

2026-11-11-ken-airtel-kenya-partners-pes.summary: Airtel Kenya and Integrated Payment Systems Limited, which operates Pesalink, signed an agreement on 10 November 2026. It lets Airtel Money users send funds from their wallets to accounts at 30 banks, SACCOs and microfinance banks on the Pesalink network. An account-confirmation check runs before each transfer (reported 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-ken-new-konza-centre-to-boost.summary: Kenya's government launched a security operations centre at Konza Technopolis that monitors networks with AI and coordinates responses to incidents. Private firms pay an annual fee based on the assets monitored. The Communications Authority reported 2.7 billion detected threat events from July to September 2026, up 14.45 per cent on the previous quarter (reported 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-ken-telkom-opposes-proposed-i.summary: Telkom Kenya addressed the National Assembly communication committee on 10 November 2026. It said the Kenya Information and Communications (Amendment) Bill should set a billing-transparency standard, not one metering model. Chief executive Mugo Kibati warned that persistent subscriber identifiers could expose personal data. Telkom backed Kenya's proposed accession to the Budapest Convention, with safeguards on foreign requests.

2026-11-11-lby-gia-open-data-platform-te.summary: The terms of Libya's open data platform, run by the General Information Authority, allow reuse of its data for lawful purposes with attribution to the platform and dataset. They bar re-identification of individuals, provide the data without warranty, and allow datasets to be changed or withdrawn without notice. The page names no standard licence (checked 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-lso-lesotho-startup-funding-h.summary: An analysis published on 11 November 2026 draws on the Lesotho Entrepreneurship Hub's October 2026 newsletter. It reports 260 enterprises incubated, including 144 women-owned and 174 youth-owned, and a co-investment fund of more than M45 million announced. The author says no public record shows how much private equity has reached these businesses.

2026-11-11-mar-morocco-is-making-propert.summary: Morocco's land conservation agency, ANCFCC, has opened an online service for ownership certificates (reported 11 November 2026). Owners of registered property can request and download them without visiting a registry office. The agency says it aims to cut waiting times and protect personal information.

2026-11-11-mwi-dpa-reviews-proposed-data.summary: Malawi's Data Protection Authority, MACRA, reviewed proposed registration fees for major data controllers and processors at a workshop in Blantyre, reported on 11 November 2026. The proposal weighs annual revenue and the number of data subjects, replacing a revenue-only model. Fees of K50,000 to K7 million are expected to take effect on 4 January 2027.

2026-11-11-nga-10-states-get-mobile-cent.summary: Nigeria's Humanitarian Affairs ministry, UNHCR and Germany handed mobile one-stop-shop vehicles to 10 states (reported 11 November 2026). The vehicles bring NIN enrolment, birth registration, BVN and SIM registration to displaced people. Nigeria has 3.7 million of them.

2026-11-11-nga-doro-mobile-one-stop-shop.summary: Nigeria's humanitarian affairs minister, Bernard Doro, handed ten Mobile One-Stop Shop vehicles to state governments in Abuja on 11 November 2026. The units, provided through UNHCR with German funding, offer NIN enrolment, birth, SIM and BVN registration, and bank accounts. Bernard Doro said the scheme should later reach all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

2026-11-11-nga-fmcide-3mtt-delivery-netw.summary: Nigeria's digital economy ministry opened the 3MTT Delivery Network to training organisations and experts on 11 November 2026. About ₦4 billion is earmarked for results-based funding of Cohorts 5 and 6, and applications close on 30 November 2026. The EU and Denmark fund Cohort 5 through GIZ, HAUS and ESTDEV, with a MacArthur Foundation grant.

2026-11-11-nga-mobile-subscriptions-200-.summary: Nigeria's active mobile subscriptions reached 200.3 million in September 2026, Nigerian Communications Commission data show. That is up 29 per cent in two years. MTN had 104.6 million and Airtel 68 million, about 86 per cent of the total. In 2024 lines fell from 224.7 million to 164.9 million when SIMs without a verified NIN were cut off.

2026-11-11-nga-nigeria-opens-4-billion-f.summary: Nigeria opened applications on 11 November 2026 for about ₦4 billion of outcome-linked funding for delivery partners of 3MTT Cohort 5. The EU and Denmark fund it through GIZ, HAUS and ESTDEV, with a MacArthur Foundation grant. Applications close on 30 November 2026.

2026-11-11-nga-nitda-review-digital-stra.summary: Nigeria's NITDA opened a stakeholder review of its Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2.0 (2024–2026), Voice of Nigeria reported on 11 November 2026. The review, held at DNICE in Abuja, prepares a new strategy for 2027. SRAP 2.0 has eight pillars, 37 aggregate success indicators and about 78 initiatives.

2026-11-11-nga-nitda-tech-outlook-report.summary: NITDA launched the Nigeria Tech Outlook Report 2026 as an annual digital-economy baseline, Voice of Nigeria reported on 11 November 2026. The report finds that 86.5% of adults hold a financial account and 12% used digital credit. It finds 40.6% personally use a smartphone and 17.9% used government services online in the previous 12 months.

2026-11-11-rwa-rwandas-skills-first-path.summary: An opinion piece by Moses Mugisha, published on 11 November 2026, reviews Rwanda's 2023 National AI Policy. Mugisha says about 70 per cent of it concerns skills. Mugisha argues that rules should now cover physical AI, such as humanoid robots, because the policy's principles are not statutory duties.

2026-11-11-sdn-baldna-portal-home-and-lo.summary: Sudan's Baldna portal is run by the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications. Users log in with the national digital identity, SudaPass. On 11 November 2026 its home page showed 48 government institutions and 141 digital services. It reported more than 265,000 completed transactions.

2026-11-11-sen-ansd-accord-licence-donne.summary: The open data licence of Senegal's national statistics agency, ANSD, grants a free, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to copy, adapt and distribute its data, including commercially. Users must carry a prescribed source statement (checked 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-sen-cartes-consulaires-system.summary: Senegal's foreign ministry (MIAAESE) and the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations signed a convention on 9 November 2026 to build a secure system for issuing and tracking consular cards for Senegalese abroad, Seneweb reported. The CDC's digital subsidiary, Synapsys Conseil, will deliver it. The stated aim is simpler procedures and traceable, authentic consular documents.

2026-11-11-sen-starlink-suspended-in-sen.summary: Senegal's Supreme Court rejected the State's appeal on 3 November 2026. The suspension of Starlink's licence stays in place. It is the State's second loss in the case in two months. A final ruling is still to come (The Point, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-sle-business-registration-75p.summary: Sierra Leone's online business registration system, launched on 10 November 2026, puts 66 National Investment Board services on one platform, Ecofin Agency reported. The NIB's director set an eight-working-hour target for complete applications. At an October 2026 roundtable, a Finance Ministry official cited World Bank 2025 estimates that about 75% of enterprises are unregistered.

2026-11-11-sle-online-business-registrat.summary: President Julius Maada Bio launched Sierra Leone's Online Business Registration System in Freetown on 10 November 2026, Sierra Leone Monitor reported. The President pledged to process complete, lawful applications within 24 hours and to deliver related registration services within seven days. The National Investment Board runs the system and says earlier records have been moved into it.

2026-11-11-som-somalia-plans-central-sec.summary: Somalia's internal security ministry has begun designing a Data Analysis Centre to pool police, intelligence and immigration data, Dawan Africa reported on 11 November 2026. Director General Mohamed Shire said the system will replace paper filing. The ministry did not say who funds it, when it will operate or how personal data will be protected.

2026-11-11-southwood-chad-landlocked-one.summary: An analysis by Russell Southwood of Balancing Act, dated November 2026, describes Chad's telecoms market. It reports an Airtel and Moov mobile duopoly and a single international transit route through Camtel to Kribi in Cameroon. It also covers Starlink licensing and Moov's first fibre-to-the-home offer.

2026-11-11-ssd-eservices-portal-ministri.summary: South Sudan's eServices portal listed 14 ministries and agencies on 11 November 2026. The National Communication Authority offered 22 online services, including licence and type-approval applications, and the Revenue Authority's customs division offered permit and licence applications.

2026-11-11-syc-blue-economy-department-s.summary: Seychelles' Department of Blue Economy signed two open-ended data-sharing memoranda of understanding on 10 November 2026, Seychelles Nation reported. The partners are the Seychelles Revenue Commission and the Registration Division. Principal Secretary Veronique Nibourette, Acting Commissioner General Fred Morel and Registrar General Suleiman Athanasius signed them.

2026-11-11-tcd-chad-pp-26-policy-stateme.summary: Chad's statement to the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, posted by 11 November 2026, says 4,400 km of a planned 14,000 km fibre network is built. A further 2,700 km is under way and 6,900 km has no financing. Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat cited 15 million mobile subscriptions (79%) and 5.6 million internet subscriptions (30%) at end-2025.

2026-11-11-tgo-opendata-gouv-tg-cgu-lice.summary: The terms of use of Togo's open data platform, opendata.gouv.tg, make registration free. Published data is under an open licence unless stated otherwise. The page names no specific licence and carries no date (checked 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-tgo-togo-rallies-digital-sect.summary: Togo's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCy) announced on 10 November 2026 that it will hold the first Togo Cyber Arena in Lomé on 19 and 20 November. Government agencies, businesses and cybersecurity specialists are invited. The programme includes talks, a national student contest and a live security demonstration (Togo First, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-tun-bancarisation-en-tunisie-.summary: The Central Bank of Tunisia's banking supervision report shows bank accounts fell 1.8% in 2025 to 10.5 million, Challenges TN reported on 11 November 2026. The branch network grew by 17, from 2,064 to 2,081. Special savings accounts fell 5.9% and current accounts rose 1.2%; the Global Findex puts adult account ownership at 37.8% in 2024.

2026-11-11-tun-world-bank-findex-account.summary: The World Bank's Global Findex series shows that 26.6% of Tunisian women aged 15 and over held an account at a financial institution or mobile-money provider in 2024. The share was 28.7% in 2021, 28.4% in 2017 and 20.7% in 2014. The World Bank updated the series on 11 November 2026.

2026-11-11-uga-itu-pp26-policy-statement.summary: Uganda's ICT minister told the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha on 11 November 2026 that network coverage reached 96% of the population (GSMA, 2025). The minister cited digital-skills training for over 100,000 young people in three years and over 10,000 free smartphones in a trial. Uganda stood for re-election to the ITU Council for 2027–2030.

2026-11-11-uga-uganda-highlights-digital.summary: The Uganda Communications Commission reported that ICT minister Justine Kasule Lumumba delivered Uganda's policy statement at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha on 11 November 2026. The minister cited 96% population network coverage (GSMA, 2025) and digital-skills training for over 100,000 young people in three years. The minister also cited the UCC's e-Booster Programme for homegrown ICT solutions.

2026-11-11-uga-ursb-defends-system-failu.summary: The Uganda Registration Services Bureau answered Parliament's COSASE committee on 10 November 2026. The Auditor General had found long downtime in its online business registration system from August 2023 to September 2025. The audit also found personal data exposed in business records. The Bureau said it had raised storage to about 50 TB and added backup power and a second internet provider. It put availability at 99 per cent (Nile Post, 11 November 2026).

2026-11-11-xaf-itu-pp-26-doha-african-un.summary: African Union Commissioner for Infrastructure and Energy Lerato Mataboge spoke at MWC Doha (reported 11 November 2026). Mataboge said energy, digital infrastructure, skills and capital must be planned together for Africa's role in the AI economy. Mataboge spoke with the GSMA's John Giusti, alongside the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference.

2026-11-11-xaf-itu-pp-26-doha-cofie-afri.summary: Technology policy expert Ethel Cofie sits on the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference working group on public policies in Doha. Cofie urged African countries to press for firm wording on financing, cybersecurity, AI and connectivity (reported 11 November 2026). Cofie said the choice between shall and may decides whether commitments bind. Draft resolutions include 130 on ICT security and 179 on child online protection.

2026-11-11-xaf-kenya-backs-50-african-pr.summary: Kenya said it would back the 50 African Common Proposals at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha. They were adopted in Abidjan in September 2026. Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo spoke to African Telecommunications Union heads of delegation (reported 11 November 2026). Africa has put forward Dominic Ooko of the Communications Authority of Kenya to chair Committee 3 on Budget Control.

2026-11-11-xaf-lu-heng-note-77-openness-.summary: An essay by Lu Heng, dated 11 November 2026, criticises the participation requirements for candidates in the five regional internet registries. It argues that the claim of openness does not give those bodies a mandate over people outside their meetings. It notes that the AFRINIC co-chair slate has one candidate.

2026-11-11-xaf-souverainete-numerique-l-.summary: A commentary published on 11 November 2026 asks whether Africa should build a separate national internet, as North Korea did with Kwangmyong, or seek sovereignty through control of digital resources. It cites the filtering systems of China and Russia and India's public digital infrastructure as other approaches. The author is Mariama Salifou.

2026-11-11-xwa-ecowas-etls-task-force-th.summary: TradeMark Africa gave IT equipment to Benin's customs directorate in Cotonou. It is meant to cut downtime on the SIGMAT customs node. The handover came beside the first meeting of the third ECOWAS ETLS Task Force, on 5 and 6 November 2026.

2026-11-11-zaf-beyond-access-closing-sou.summary: Policy Brief No. 246 by Luke Boyle, published in November 2026, says about 17 million people in South Africa remain unconnected. It argues that private providers' consumption-driven models risk reinforcing inequality. It makes the case for community-centred connectivity projects, backed by supportive regulation and finance.

2026-11-11-zaf-home-affairs-smart-id-753.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs had Smart ID replacement services running at 753 bank branches by 11 November 2026, past its target of 750 branches by end-March 2027. Smart ID service points have risen from 214 offices to 967 locations. Home Affairs says more than one million South Africans have been served since 9 March 2026.

2026-11-11-zaf-transparency-portal-beta-.summary: South Africa's National Treasury runs a beta Transparency Portal of eTender procurement data, last updated on 11 November 2026. It counts 169,559 tenders published, 73,447 awards and 8,366 contracts, a subset of eTender data. Monthly OCDS data from May 2021 is downloadable under a CC BY 4.0 licence, with a REST API.

2026-11-11-zmb-mutati-reaffirms-signific.summary: Zambia's government has asked Hobbiton Investments Limited to form a Ministerial Technology Advisory Panel, minister Felix Mutati said (reported 11 November 2026). The panel joins public and private stakeholders. It is to speed the digitisation of public services under the Grow Zambia Agenda.

2026-11-12-a-doha-le-mali-defend-un-nume.summary: Mali's digital economy minister, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, spoke for Mali and the Sahel confederation at the ITU conference in Doha, Malijet reported on 12 November 2026. The minister listed infrastructure, cybersecurity, online services and rural access as priorities. The minister asked the ITU for more support to African states, in particular those of the Sahel confederation.

2026-11-12-acces-a-internet-madagascar-v.summary: A COMESA consultation on financing digital infrastructure met in Antananarivo from 10 to 13 November 2026. GSMA estimates cited there put 3G and 4G coverage at about 81% of Madagascar's population in 2026. Yet 66% of people live in covered areas without using mobile internet. 4G reaches an estimated 67% of rural people against 96% in towns.

2026-11-12-afd-afdb-partnership-renewal-.summary: The African Development Bank Group and the Agence française de développement signed a memorandum of understanding for 2026-2031 in Paris on 10 November 2026. Its areas include digital infrastructure, data governance and the responsible use of AI. Energy and transport are also covered. No sum is attached; the two lenders have co-financed 17 projects in 14 countries since 2021.

2026-11-12-ben-unctad-transit-digitalisa.summary: UNCTAD and Benin's trade ministry held a workshop in Cotonou on 11-12 November 2026 for Benin's National Trade Facilitation Committee. It covered a single customs transit guarantee for Benin, Burkina Faso, Niger and Togo, and links between national Single Windows. The work falls under the EU-funded Global Gateway programme for the Cotonou-Niamey corridor.

2026-11-12-botswana-positions-data-as-di.summary: Statistics Botswana launched its Corporate Strategic Plan 2026-2030 in Gaborone, ITWeb reported on 12 November 2026; the launch date is not stated. The plan, themed 'From Data Producer to Data Leader', covers data governance, modernised information systems and the use of AI and machine learning. Vice President and Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe launched it.

2026-11-12-cod-donnees-ouvertes-itie-rdc.summary: The DRC's Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative office publishes its sector data in open formats. Files in CSV, Excel and JSON, and a public API, cover revenue, mining output and the active mining-rights register. The mining, oil and forestry contracts are listed too.

2026-11-12-comesa-central-bank-governors.summary: The bureau of COMESA's central bank governors met in Lilongwe on 11 November 2026 to review revised charters for the COMESA Clearing House and the COMESA Monetary Institute. COMESA said its Digital Retail Payment Platform, a cross-border retail system in local currencies, was nearing user trials. Live transactions are to be piloted between Malawi and Zambia.

2026-11-12-cote-d-ivoire-un-guichet-nume.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Tourism and Leisure launched a digital one-stop shop for tourism businesses in Abidjan on 10 November 2026. The US firm Cybastion built it. Operators can file applications, pay online and track requests, and the ministry sets a 45-day maximum for processing. A pilot runs in four regional directorates: Abidjan Nord, Abidjan Sud, San Pedro and Grand-Bassam.

2026-11-12-cran-develops-regulatory-fram.summary: Namibia's Communications Regulatory Authority is developing a regulatory sandbox, The Brief reported on 12 November 2026. It would let operators, start-ups, universities and government projects test AI, satellite broadband, direct-to-cell, drones, blockchain and digital-identity services under set conditions. A steering committee would recommend changes to regulation; the framework is still at stakeholder consultation.

2026-11-12-egy-fra-approves-10-companies.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority approved 10 companies to run non-bank financial activities through fintech, in a release of 12 November 2026. They include the start-ups Nice Deer, for factoring, and Dayra Microfinance, as well as insurers, brokers, asset managers and custodians such as MNT-Halan. Each approval is tied to a named e-KYC provider, chiefly VLens.

2026-11-12-egy-hyperscalers-want-clear-r.summary: Lawyers quoted by Enterprise say Egypt's data rules deter hyperscalers. Each transfer of data abroad needs its own permit, and limits on state access are unclear. Egypt has an estimated 15-60 MW of installed data-centre capacity against an ambition of 400-500 MW. The government plans a national data-centre strategy by the end of 2026 but has set no date for new rules.

2026-11-12-ehealth-africa-using-tech-to-.summary: TechCabal profiles eHealth Africa, a non-profit that maps settlements and plans and tracks vaccination campaigns in Nigeria. Its 2026 Mid-Year Report says campaigns it supported reached over 23 million children in the first half of 2026. In Kebbi State, missed settlements fell from over 20% to about 6% with a digital microplan, eHealth Africa says.

2026-11-12-eu-egypt-electronic-signature.summary: The European Commission said on 12 November 2026 that Egypt's electronic signature and seal framework is technically aligned with the EU's eIDAS Regulation. Egypt is the first country outside Europe to reach this. It will join the EU Third Countries Trusted List, so EU member states can validate its signatures and seals. The step was a deliverable of the EU-Egypt Summit of 22 October 2025.

2026-11-12-eu-kenya-ruto-global-gateway-.summary: President William Ruto asked EU heads of delegation in Nairobi for jobs and investment, Y News reported on 12 November 2026. President Ruto said the EU takes 21% of Kenya's exports. The president asked for Global Gateway finance on concessional terms. The next Kenya-EU Digital Dialogue, later in November, is to take up fibre links and the Blue Raman cable.

2026-11-12-facephi-and-egypttrust-partne.summary: Egypt Trust is adding Facephi's identity-verification and fraud-detection technology to its locally hosted platform. Egypt Trust was among the first electronic signature and e-seal providers licensed by ITIDA. The partnership was announced at Cairo ICT and reported by Biometric Update on 12 November 2026.

2026-11-12-gimpa-uestc-digital-governanc.summary: Ghana's public-administration institute GIMPA announced a partnership with China's University of Electronic Science and Technology to set up a Ghana-China Centre for West African Studies, the Ghana News Agency reported on 12 November 2026. The proposed centre would do research and capacity-building in digital governance, e-government, AI and data systems. No timetable or funding is stated.

2026-11-12-gnq-ejecutivo-aprueba-moderni.summary: Equatorial Guinea's government approved on 11 November 2026 the second of three investment options to modernise CNEDOGE, which issues national identity documents and passports. The plan renews servers, storage, security, networks, power supply and biometric capture and issuing equipment, much of it in service since 2017. The initial invoice was revised 40% downward; the amount is not stated.

2026-11-12-itu-emerging-technologies-clo.summary: ITU reports a ministerial discussion on emerging technologies and digital divides at its Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha on 11 November 2026. Rwanda's ICT minister, Paula Ingabire, called for a move from universal connectivity to universal capability. The Global Satellite Operators Association said terrestrial mobile networks cover only about 20% of the Earth's landmass. No decision came from the session.

2026-11-12-kenya-ai-governance-fragmenta.summary: Lawyers at Bowmans, writing in CIO Africa on 12 November 2026, warn that Kenya's AI rules risk overlapping mandates. They list the National AI Strategy of March 2025 and a draft AI policy published for comment in July 2026. A draft data governance policy and a private member's AI Bill are also in play. The Central Bank of Kenya published draft guidance on AI in banking in September 2026.

2026-11-12-kenyan-fixed-internet-outpace.summary: Communications Authority of Kenya figures show 2.84 million fixed internet subscriptions in June 2026, up 32.4% in a year. Safaricom held 1.02 million of them, or 36.1%. nPerf user tests from November 2025 to October 2026 put Kenya's average fixed latency at 29ms, ITWeb reports. That ranks Kenya second of 16 English-speaking countries; South Africa recorded 71ms.

2026-11-12-lbr-lacc-anti-corruption-dash.summary: The Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission launched a public accountability dashboard on 11 November 2026, due to become operational in 2027. It is to bring together audit findings, procurement compliance, investigations, prosecutions and asset declarations. The work sits under the World Bank-supported GREAT Project. The PPCC, the General Auditing Commission and the Public Accounts Committee are to be trained to feed it.

2026-11-12-lesotho-itu-pp26-affordable-c.summary: Lesotho's ICT minister, Nthati Moorosi, asked the ITU to prioritise affordable connectivity for landlocked states, the government reported on 12 November 2026. The minister spoke at the ITU conference in Doha. Lesotho has approved a digital transformation strategy, an AI policy and a data policy. With ITU support, it is building an emergency telecoms plan and a farmers' registry.

2026-11-12-libya-gia-government-reports-.summary: Libya's General Information Authority began training public bodies on its Government Reports Platform on 11 November 2026, starting with the Ministry of Culture and Knowledge Development. The authority describes the platform as a central tool for periodic reports to the Prime Minister's Office. It says the platform tracks performance indicators in real time.

2026-11-12-mnt-halan-lists-egyptian-busi.summary: MNT-Halan listed its Egyptian business on the Cairo Stock Exchange, Egypt's largest IPO since 2021, Tech Africa News reported on 12 November 2026. The retail tranche was more than 43 times oversubscribed and the institutional tranche more than 19 times. Norfund says the fintech grew from 400,000 customers in 2018 to 10 million across four countries.

2026-11-12-mrt-unctad-launch-national-e-.summary: UNCTAD says Mauritania's digital transformation ministry was to launch its National E-commerce Strategy 2026-2030 on 12 November 2026. The strategy builds on a 2023 eTrade Readiness Assessment and was funded by GIZ and UNCTAD's core donors (Australia, Switzerland and the Netherlands). A development partners' roundtable was set for 13 November.

2026-11-12-mrt-wearetech-cybastion-mou-c.summary: Mauritania's digital transformation ministry signed a memorandum with the US firm Cybastion in Nouakchott on 10 November 2026, We Are Tech Africa reported. It covers network protection, digital infrastructure and training through Cybastion's Africa DigiEmpower programme with Cisco Networking Academy. A separate World Bank-funded WARDIP tender for a national CSIRT and SOC closes on 17 November 2026.

2026-11-12-mwi-paratus-launches-malawi-s.summary: Paratus Group has launched in Malawi, its 16th market in sub-Saharan Africa, Tech Africa News reported on 12 November 2026. Paratus will first sell Starlink enterprise connectivity to businesses and organisations in Lilongwe, Blantyre and Mzuzu. Local technical partners are to install within 24 to 48 hours.

2026-11-12-nga-nitda-cbn-national-sovere.summary: NITDA and the Central Bank of Nigeria held a dialogue on the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative, NITDA reported on 12 November 2026. Director General Kashifu Inuwa said the two bodies want the financial sector to comply first.

2026-11-12-nga-nitda-us-chamber-partners.summary: NITDA Director General Kashifu Inuwa received a U.S. Chamber of Commerce delegation led by Kendra Gaither, NITDA reported on 12 November 2026. Inuwa said the federal government invested more than NGN 4.5 trillion in IT between June 2023 and June 2026. Inuwa said NITDA is working with the Central Bank of Nigeria on an assurance framework for data localisation.

2026-11-12-nigerian-fintech-raenest-acqu.summary: Nigerian fintech Raenest has acquired Remitise, a UK payments company registered with the Financial Conduct Authority, Connecting Africa reported on 12 November 2026. The terms were not disclosed. Raenest says the deal adds UK payments infrastructure to its Nigerian and Canadian licences.

2026-11-12-nigerias-tap-to-pay-adoption-.summary: TechCabal reported on 12 November 2026 that contactless payment works on some Nigerian cards and terminals but few consumers use it. On 28 October 2026 Mastercard and Interswitch launched Google Pay for eligible Mastercard holders in Nigeria. TechCabal tested a contactless Verve card from Wema Bank's ALAT at a point-of-sale agent, and it worked.

2026-11-12-nitda-and-nbs-launch-nigeria-.summary: NITDA and the National Bureau of Statistics launched the Nigeria Tech Outlook Report at Digital Nigeria 2026 in Abuja, Tech Africa News reported on 12 November 2026. The two bodies present it as a source of technology-sector data for policy and investment. The account gives none of the report's figures.

2026-11-12-norfund-backed-fund-mnt-halan.summary: MNT-Halan listed its Egyptian business on the Cairo Stock Exchange in Egypt's largest IPO since 2021, Innovation Village reported on 12 November 2026. The retail tranche was more than 43 times oversubscribed and the institutional tranche more than 19 times. Norfund committed USD 40m in 2019 to the DPI fund that invested in MNT-Halan in 2021.

2026-11-12-rwanda-explores-ai-and-scienc.summary: Rwanda's Ministry of Justice met two institutes to discuss AI in the justice sector, Tech Review Africa reported on 12 November 2026. The institutes are the Institute of Legal Practice and Development and the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences. The talks covered case management, delays and access to legal resources. They build on a recent memorandum between the two institutes; no project was named.

2026-11-12-sdn-bankak-app-hack-traders-l.summary: More than 50 Bank of Khartoum customers in Kordofan say thieves took money through the Bankak app, Radio Dabanga reported on 12 November 2026. The Dar Hamar Emergency Rooms put losses at SDG 18-45 million each, from thefts on 14 October and 3 November. The group accuses the bank of not freezing accounts and is preparing legal action.

2026-11-12-sdn-civil-registry-restores-d.summary: Sudan's General Directorate of Civil Registry says its engineers have restored the registry database in full. The war damaged its archives and offices in Khartoum, Gezira and Sennar. The directorate is widening electronic registration and will take applications for children online.

2026-11-12-sen-fonction-publique-cadre-i.summary: Senegal's Minister of the Civil Service, Mamadou Lamine Dianté, proposed on 12 November 2026 that the State, employers and unions draw up a national framework on AI at work, APS reported. The minister made the proposal at a workshop held with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation. The framework would cover changes in jobs and skills, training and workers' rights.

2026-11-12-tcd-itu-pp-26-doha-chad-and-r.summary: Chad's telecoms minister, Haliki Choua Mahamat, met Rwanda's ICT minister at ITU PP-26 in Doha on 10 November 2026. The Chadian minister asked ADETIC and ARCEP Chad to prepare a study mission to Rwanda. ARCEP Chad is looking at cooperation with RURA on spectrum management, quality of service, competition and consumer protection.

2026-11-12-tun-e-payments-gain-momentum-.summary: Central Bank of Tunisia data show 18 million online payments worth TND 1.229bn in January-September 2026, up 27%. In-store card payments rose 18.6% to 41.3 million, worth TND 5.143bn. At 30 September 2026 there were 1,552 active merchant websites and 45,900 POS terminals, African Manager reported on 12 November.

2026-11-12-uga-bou-calls-for-safeguards-.summary: Bank of Uganda Deputy Governor Augustus Nuwagaba spoke at a financial inclusion forum in Kampala on 12 November 2026. The deputy governor said AI, open banking and open finance need privacy, security, fairness and accountability safeguards from the start. Virtual assets, stablecoins and tokenisation also need examination. The bank became vice-chair of the African Financial Inclusion Policy Initiative in July 2026.

2026-11-12-undp-sudan-digital-financial-.summary: UNDP published an assessment of digital financial literacy in Sudan on 5 November 2026. It surveyed 152 people in River Nile, Kassala and Gedaref; the sample is not nationally representative. Of these, 78% own a phone but only 44% have a bank account, 36% a mobile payment app and 10% a digital wallet. UNDP found that wallets from different providers often cannot pay one another.

2026-11-12-workonline-extends-into-ugand.summary: Workonline Communications opened its first Ugandan point of presence at Raxio's UG1 data centre in Kampala, the company announced on 12 November 2026. Workonline sells 100GE IP transit under a new Ugandan licence, over two separate routes to Nairobi. UG1 hosts 25 carriers and ISPs and the Uganda Internet Exchange Point, where Workonline plans to peer.

2026-11-12-zaf-biometricupdate-asylum-re.summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs has begun testing a digital asylum platform, Biometric Update reported on 12 November 2026. The platform records an intention to apply for asylum with facial biometrics, personal details and supporting documents. Later phases are to add appointments, records checks and machine-learning tools for adjudication.

2026-11-12-zaf-etenders-transparency-por.summary: South Africa's National Treasury publishes eTender procurement data in the Open Contracting Data Standard, says the portal's policy, read on 12 November 2026. Bulk files run monthly from May 2021, with an API; the stated scope starts on 1 April 2022. Municipalities and state-owned entities are not obliged to share their data.

2026-11-12-zaf-itweb-electron-intelligen.summary: Electron Intelligence forecasts that South African data centres will add 7.77 TWh of power demand by 2035, ITWeb reported on 12 November 2026. The firm projects Africa's data centre use rising from 2.55 TWh in 2025 to 12.60 TWh in 2035. It finds that only 337 MW of 647 MW announced has a commissioning date by 2035.

2026-11-12-zaf-itweb-icasa-new-network-l.summary: ICASA published a discussion document on 30 October 2026, ITWeb reports. It takes the preliminary view that licence transfers have not promoted competition well, and that new network licences could be considered. The inquiry drew 33 responses to its first phase, including from ISPA, Cell C and Vodacom. Amatole Telecommunications put the cost of a licence pair at over R1 million; comments are due by 6 January.

2026-11-12-zaf-sanews-president-silicon-.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa will lead a South African delegation to Silicon Valley from 15 to 21 November 2026, Presidential Spokesperson Vincent Magwenya said on 12 November. The programme includes Stanford University, Alphabet and Google, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks and Microsoft. The stated aims include AI policy, investment, cyber resilience and digital sovereignty.

2026-11-12-zaf-techreviewafrica-china-ai.summary: South Africa and China are advancing plans for an AI Talent Development and Innovation Centre in South Africa, Tech Review Africa reported on 12 November 2026. Deputy Minister Nomalungelo Gina and Vice Minister Zhang Guangjun discussed it at a China-Africa innovation forum in Wuhan. A Chinese technical team is to visit for a preliminary assessment.

2026-11-12-zambia-deploys-751-starlink-k.summary: Smart Zambia Institute has begun deploying 751 Starlink kits to health facilities in all 10 provinces, Tech Africa News reported on 12 November 2026. The Global Fund pays for the kits through the Ministry of Health, and UNDP supports the rollout. The first 90 kits went to the Western Province health office.

2026-11-12-zwe-potraz-puts-zimbabwe-on-a.summary: POTRAZ, Zimbabwe's telecoms regulator, won the PICCASO Africa 2026 award for most outstanding data protection authority in Lagos on 5 November, the Post On Sunday reported. The paper says POTRAZ has licensed more than 2,500 data controllers and certified over 1,500 data protection officers. It also credits POTRAZ with more than 195 enforcement notices.

2026-11-12-zwe-transforming-public-servi.summary: In a Herald column of 12 November 2026, Louis Mondo argues that Zimbabwe should connect its existing government systems so citizens submit information once. The column names TaRMS, ZimConnect, the e-Cadastre and the Digital Land Administration Platform as the base. It says TaRMS already links to the company registrar, the deeds office and civil registry.
